Title: Video: Machete-wielding Florida man arrested during traffic stop after bolting from sheriff’s office
description: During an incident in Lehigh Acres, Florida, deputies with the Lee County Sheriff’s Office arrested 60-year-old Leodan Gallo after a violent confrontation following a traffic-related pursuit. Authorities said Gallo chased victims through streets, wielded a machete, and smashed a vehicle window during the encounter. The victims drove to a sheriff’s office substation for help, where Gallo continued causing a disturbance in the parking lot and inside the lobby. When deputies attempted to detain him, he tried to flee, entered his vehicle, and struck officers with the driver’s door before being stopped nearby. A search of the vehicle reportedly uncovered two machetes within reach. He was arrested and charged with aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, aggravated battery, criminal mischief, disturbing the peace, and fleeing and eluding law enforcement. The incident began after an altercation at an apartment complex though the motive remains unclear. No serious injuries were reported in total.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon; aggravated battery; criminal mischief; disturbing the peace; fleeing and eluding law enforcement

Title: BWC: Ohio man flees traffic stop with officer inside his vehicle
description: During a traffic stop in Dayton, Ohio, a 46-year-old man identified as Gary L. Pullen allegedly fled while an officer was partially inside his pickup truck. According to police reports, officers stopped Pullen late Thursday night for traffic violations including illegal window tint and expired tags. During the stop, the officer observed the driver manipulating a black bag and requested he exit the vehicle for a pat-down. As the officer attempted to detain him, Pullen re-entered the truck and suddenly accelerated, causing the officer to be carried along as the vehicle drove away. Body and dash camera footage later showed the truck traveling about 1,500 feet before crashing into a snowbank, where additional officers approached with weapons drawn and removed Pullen from the vehicle. He was taken into custody and evaluated at a hospital before being booked. No injuries were reported for the officer involved in the incident.
Charges: Abduction; failure to comply with an order or signal of a police officer; obstructing official business; three weapons-related charges

Title: Suspect Flees from Traffic Stop with Two Young Children in Vehicle During Violent Crime Reduction Initiative in Cleveland
description: During a violent crime reduction initiative in Cleveland, Ohio, on November 6, 2025, officers from the Cleveland Division of Police and troopers with the Ohio State Highway Patrol conducted a traffic stop on a white Jeep for a traffic violation. The driver, later identified as Javion Griffie, allegedly failed to stop and fled, prompting a coordinated response involving aviation support. Authorities tracked the vehicle as it moved through the city, at one point leaving two young children at a gas station before continuing to flee at high speed. The pursuit was later terminated on the ground, but aerial units continued tracking the Jeep until a tire deflation device was deployed. The vehicle eventually stopped, and Griffie fled on foot, hiding in a dumpster where he was taken into custody without further incident. He was transported to the Cuyahoga County Jail. The children were safely recovered and released to family members.
Charges: Fleeing and eluding law enforcement; traffic violation; active misdemeanor warrant

Title: Sheriff: Man arrested after traffic stop leads to pursuit, crash in Butler County
description: During a traffic stop in Butler County, Ohio, a police chase began after deputies pulled over a Kia SUV on Interstate 75 for having no visible license plate. According to the Butler County Sheriff’s Office, after the vehicle stopped, deputies asked the driver to exit while the passenger, 18-year-old Ja’Toin Lamont Jackson, moved into the driver’s seat and fled the scene in the vehicle. The pursuit continued along Butler Warren Road, where Jackson struck another vehicle carrying occupants but continued driving. He later jumped out of the moving vehicle and fled on foot. Law enforcement, including aerial support from a sheriff’s helicopter and assisting agencies, eventually located and arrested him in a nearby neighborhood. Authorities confirmed Jackson had active warrants for failure to comply and theft at the time of the incident. He was charged with multiple offenses including felonious assault, grand theft auto, failure to comply, obstruction of official business, and leaving the scene of an accident.
Charges: Felonious assault; grand theft auto; failure to comply; obstructing official business; leaving the scene of an accident; outstanding warrants (failure to comply, theft)

Title: Fleeing felon arrested after leading deputy on high-speed chase
description: A 31-year-old Ohio man was arrested in Washington County, Florida, after leading deputies on a high-speed chase on Dec. 19, 2025. A deputy attempted to stop his vehicle at an intersection after it was flagged in a BOLO linked to multiple felony warrants from Kentucky, including violent offenses such as assault, strangulation, intimidation of a witness, unlawful imprisonment, and rape. When emergency lights were activated, the driver immediately accelerated and fled, reaching speeds around 100 mph in a 30 mph zone. The pursuit continued through multiple roadways as the driver ignored stop signs and traffic signals, creating a serious public safety risk. Law enforcement said the chase ended when the driver lost control of the vehicle in Bay County. He was taken into custody without further incident. He was charged in Washington County with felony fleeing and eluding, aggravated fleeing causing injury or property damage, and resisting an officer without violence, along with additional Florida Highway Patrol charges.
Charges: Felony fleeing and eluding police; aggravated fleeing with injury or property damage; resisting an officer without violence; additional Florida Highway Patrol charges

Title: Man in custody after leading police on chase through Columbus for nearly 40 minutes
description: A 21-year-old man, Sayvion Lewis, was arrested after leading Columbus police on a nearly 40-minute pursuit on February 6, 2024. Officers initially observed a black Dodge Challenger engaging in reckless behavior in a residential area near Leckner Avenue. When police attempted a traffic stop, the driver fled, initiating a high-speed chase through multiple city streets. During the pursuit, the suspect drove through stop signs and red lights, increased speed on residential roads, and struck multiple vehicles, including a Columbus City Schools bus and other civilian and law enforcement vehicles. Spike strips were eventually deployed on a highway by sheriff’s deputies, which helped stop the vehicle. Lewis was taken into custody shortly after the stop. Authorities stated the chase involved dangerous driving conditions that put multiple motorists and officers at risk. The incident ended without any reported fatalities, though significant vehicle damage occurred. The suspect was arrested and transported into custody for processing and court proceedings.
Charges: Aggravated fleeing and eluding; failure to comply with police orders; reckless operation; traffic violations; property damage involving vehicles including a school bus

Title: Orlando police officer back on the job after fleeing traffic stop in Seminole County
description: An Orlando Police Department officer, Alexander Shaouni, was pulled over in Seminole County, Florida, after a deputy observed him driving 80 mph in a 45 mph zone while operating a marked police SUV incident. During the traffic stop, Shaouni reportedly refused to provide his driver’s license to the deputy. He then re-entered his vehicle and drove away from the scene, prompting a criminal investigation. Body camera footage showed the interaction and the moment he left the stop. Shaouni was later arrested and faced charges including reckless driving, fleeing and eluding law enforcement, and resisting an officer without violence. He was relieved of duty while internal and criminal investigations were conducted. Prosecutors later declined to pursue the case after he completed a pretrial intervention program. The officer was allowed to return to duty following resolution of the criminal matter, though an internal affairs review continued within the department the time of reporting.
Charges: Reckless driving, fleeing and eluding law enforcement, resisting an officer without violence

Title: Man Arrested After Striking Patrol Vehicle and Fleeing Scene
description: A Tampa man was arrested after striking an unmarked patrol vehicle during an early-morning incident and fleeing the scene before being stopped by deputies. According to the Hillsborough County Sheriff’s Office, the incident occurred on January 3, 2026, at approximately 3:01 a.m. on Adamo Drive near Orient Road. A deputy was conducting an unrelated traffic stop with emergency lights activated when a vehicle traveling eastbound collided with the driver’s side of the patrol unit. The driver did not stop after the crash and continued driving for about one mile before deputies conducted a traffic stop. Once the vehicle was stopped, the driver, identified as Amin Williams, showed signs of impairment. He was arrested at the scene without further incident. Authorities reported no injuries, though both the patrol vehicle and the suspect’s vehicle sustained minor damage. Williams was taken into custody following the stop and processed on multiple charges related to the crash and suspected impairment.
Charges: Leaving the scene of a crash with property damage, driving under the influence with property damage or personal injury, refusal to submit to testing

Title: Fort Myers man bails on court hearing after fleeing and eluding arrest
description: A Fort Myers man is wanted after fleeing a traffic stop, leading police on a high-speed chase, crashing into a tree, and later failing to appear for a court hearing, according to Southwest Florida Crime Stoppers. Authorities say Jon Degrande, 28, initially attempted to evade Fort Myers Police when officers tried to conduct a traffic stop. He reportedly drove away at speeds exceeding 75 mph through a residential neighborhood while fleeing law enforcement. The pursuit ended when Degrande crashed into a tree. After the crash, he fled on foot but was later located and arrested by officers the same night. Officials also reported that he was in violation of probation conditions after failing to notify authorities about a change of address. Despite his arrest, Degrande later failed to appear for a scheduled court hearing, prompting law enforcement to issue a wanted notice. He is now being actively sought by authorities and remains at large.
Charges: Fleeing and eluding law enforcement, probation violation, failure to appear in court

Title: Man accused of fleeing from deputies in stolen Cadillac in northwest Miami-Dade faces judge
description: A 26-year-old man was arrested after leading law enforcement on a vehicle pursuit in a stolen Cadillac SUV through northwest Miami-Dade County. Authorities said Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office robbery intervention detectives first spotted the stolen vehicle, which had been reported by Miami Gardens Police. When officers attempted a traffic stop near Northwest 22nd Avenue and 151st Street, the suspect continued driving and briefly stopped in the roadway before fleeing again, prompting a continued chase. Florida Highway Patrol later joined the pursuit and used a PIT maneuver near Northwest 152nd Street to disable the vehicle. The driver then exited the SUV and ran into nearby bushes along train tracks in Miami Gardens, where he was taken into custody. Court records show the suspect was already on probation at the time of the incident and had prior criminal involvement. The arrest involved charges related to fleeing law enforcement and vehicle theft, according to authorities.
Charges: Fleeing and eluding a police officer Resisting an officer without violence Grand theft of a vehicle

Title: Man accused of abandoning car with child inside after police chase in Miramar
description: A Miramar man was arrested after leading police on a brief vehicle pursuit and then fleeing on foot while allegedly leaving his 3-year-old child inside the car. Officers first attempted a traffic stop after noticing the suspect driving a red BMW with a license plate registered to another vehicle. The driver initially pulled over but then sped off, prompting a short chase through local streets. Police were able to stop the vehicle again a few blocks away. As officers attempted to take him into custody, the suspect allegedly ran from the scene a second time. During this second escape attempt, he reportedly left his young child in the backseat of the car with the engine off. After a roughly 30-minute search, officers located and arrested him. Authorities also noted he has a prior criminal history involving fleeing law enforcement. The child neglect charge was added following the investigation into the incident.
Charges: Fleeing and attempting to elude law enforcement Child neglect (originally listed as desertion of a child)

Title: Traffic stop in Jupiter escalates into foot chase, ends with drone-assisted arrests
description: A traffic stop conducted by the Jupiter Police Department on July 31, 2025, escalated into a foot chase involving three vehicle occupants near the intersection of South Central Boulevard and Toney Penna Drive in Jupiter, Florida. At approximately 8:20 p.m., officers initiated the stop, but all three occupants exited the vehicle and fled on foot. Police quickly established a perimeter and launched a coordinated search operation using aerial support from a department drone. The suspects were identified as Obed J. Godines Perez, Erick R. Mateo-Perez, and Enrique Diego Andres. Officers eventually located all three individuals and took them into custody. During the arrest process, Andres allegedly resisted officers and was subdued with a Taser before being safely detained. Following their apprehension, the suspects were transported to the Palm Beach County Jail. Authorities stated that the arrests were the result of coordinated ground and aerial efforts, which helped officers locate the fleeing suspects and bring the incident to a safe conclusion.
Charges: Fleeing to Elude  Resisting Arrest

Title: Taser used on Florida driver accused of fleeing traffic stop
description: Charles Lavon Williams, 36, was arrested after fleeing a traffic stop in Summerfield, Florida, on May 21, 2024. A Marion County Sheriff's Office deputy attempted to stop Williams after observing him driving a sedan towing a wooden trailer without a license tag and running a stop sign on Sunset Harbor Road. Instead of stopping, Williams accelerated and led deputies on a brief pursuit. During the chase, he abandoned the moving vehicle and attempted to escape on foot. Deputies repeatedly ordered him to stop, but he ignored their commands and continued running. A deputy then deployed a Taser, which successfully subdued Williams, allowing officers to take him into custody without further incident. While being transported to jail, Williams allegedly kicked the patrol vehicle doors and made threats toward law enforcement officers. Authorities stated that what began as a routine traffic violation escalated into a dangerous pursuit and arrest. Williams was booked into jail and held on a $9,000 bond.
Charges: Fleeing and Eluding Resisting Without Violence Failure to Register a Motor Vehicle Operating a Motor Vehicle Without a Valid License Resisting Arrest With Violence

Title: Man arrested after vehicle chase on I-75 in Lee County
description: A stolen black Hyundai SUV led law enforcement officers on a high-speed pursuit along Interstate 75 from Collier County into Lee County, Florida. The vehicle was reported stolen from Regent Circle at approximately 8:30 a.m. Deputies located the SUV about two hours later and attempted a traffic stop, but the driver allegedly fled, initiating a pursuit. The Florida Highway Patrol joined the chase, while the Lee County Sheriff's Office helicopter monitored the vehicle from the air. Authorities stated that the pursuit lasted more than 45 miles along the interstate. During the chase, multiple motorists moved onto the shoulder to allow emergency vehicles to pass safely. The pursuit ended when the SUV struck the rear of a Florida Highway Patrol patrol vehicle. A trooper then performed a PIT (Precision Immobilization Technique) maneuver, causing the SUV to spin and stop. No injuries were reported. The driver was arrested and taken into custody in Lee County.
Charges: Four counts of reckless driving One count of fleeing police

Title: Man who led police on car chase offers deputies a vodka spritzer, asks if they ‘had fun’ during pursuit
description: A man was arrested in Highlands County, Florida after leading deputies on a vehicle pursuit that began when he allegedly stole items from a convenience store in Miami. Deputies were alerted that the suspect was driving a black minivan and circling the store before fleeing the area. When law enforcement attempted to intervene, the suspect accelerated and led officers on a chase that continued for several miles. During the pursuit, the suspect allegedly behaved erratically, including offering deputies a vodka spritzer through his vehicle window while still driving. The chase ended near Sebring Airport in a parking lot after spike strips were deployed and the vehicle’s tires were disabled. The suspect attempted to exit the vehicle and walk away before being taken into custody by deputies. He was later arrested on multiple felony and misdemeanor charges, including assault on law enforcement officers, resisting arrest, DUI-related offenses, and petit theft.
Charges: Two counts aggravated assault on law enforcement officer Battery on law enforcement officer Two counts resisting arrest DUI Refusal to submit to DUI test Petit theft

Title: Man accused in intense police chase caught on camera facing dozens of charges
description: Kevin Prater was arrested in Miami-Dade County after allegedly attempting to evade law enforcement during two separate traffic stops tied to an ongoing investigation. Officers with the Homeland Security Bureau Priority Response Team initially attempted to pull him over on West 56th Street near the Palmetto Expressway. According to police, Prater refused commands to exit his vehicle and drove away, initiating a pursuit. A second traffic stop was later attempted on Southwest 41st Street near Southwest 72nd Avenue, where authorities say he escalated the situation by backing his vehicle into a police unit and driving toward officers. During the incident, Prater also struck additional vehicles before being taken into custody. Video footage reportedly shows a chaotic scene with officers surrounding the vehicle. He was arrested and remains in custody awaiting bond. Authorities stated he was already on probation and facing additional outstanding charges at the time of the pursuit.
Charges: Fleeing and eluding, reckless driving, aggravated assault on a law enforcement officer, aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, and additional related charges (nearly three dozen total)

Title: Florida man charged with leading police on chase reaching speeds over 100 mph in stolen car
description: Omar Castro, a Florida man, was arrested in Villa Park, Illinois after allegedly leading police on a high-speed chase in a stolen vehicle through suburban areas near Route 83 and North Avenue. According to authorities, an Elmhurst police officer initially located the stolen car and attempted a stop, but Castro fled the scene. During the pursuit, he reportedly accelerated to speeds exceeding 100 mph, including approximately 107 mph in a 45 mph zone, and ignored multiple traffic signals. He also performed a U-turn and continued driving at high speeds through a construction zone before officers lost sight of the vehicle. The car was later found abandoned in a school parking lot, and Castro was located nearby on foot. He was taken into custody after resisting arrest. Officials stated the chase posed significant danger to officers and the public, though no injuries were reported.
Charges: Two counts of aggravated fleeing and eluding a police officer, aggravated speeding in a construction zone, reckless driving, driving with a suspended license, and multiple misdemeanors

Title: After woman from viral traffic stop clip leaves jail, cops cuff her driver for same offense
city and state: Sunny Isles Beach, Florida, United States
description: Cecilia Selina Mercado, a 32-year-old woman, was arrested in Sunny Isles Beach, Florida after police stopped a vehicle allegedly displaying fake diplomatic license plates. Officers initially pulled her over on Sunny Isles Boulevard after observing a car with counterfeit registration that claimed diplomatic status. During the traffic stop, Mercado was removed from the vehicle after a confrontation with police, who said the plates and claimed diplomatic immunity were not valid. She was arrested and later released on bond. Shortly after her release from jail, police also stopped the car she was riding in and arrested the driver for similar violations involving fake plates and driving offenses. Mercado claimed the plates were legally registered under a private trust and insisted she was entitled to use them, which police rejected. The incident went viral due to bodycam footage showing the confrontation and her unusual claims about citizenship and diplomatic status. Authorities confirmed the investigation was ongoing.
Charges: Counterfeit license plate / registration Driving with invalid license plate Resisting officer without violence (driver case mentioned in follow-up stop)

Title: Florida woman flees traffic stop because she couldn't 'afford to go to jail': deputies
description: Lake County deputies attempted a traffic stop on Corin Perkins after she was observed driving with a revoked license and other vehicle registration issues in Bassville Park, Florida. According to authorities, Perkins initially failed to stop for law enforcement and continued driving away from the attempted stop. Deputies did not pursue the vehicle directly, but later located her abandoned vehicle nearby. A K-9 unit was deployed and a track led investigators to information about her whereabouts, resulting in her eventual arrest. During a post-arrest interview after being read her Miranda rights, Perkins reportedly told deputies she fled because she “couldn’t afford to go to jail.” Officials stated the vehicle she was driving was unregistered and her license had already been revoked. She was taken into custody without further incident and transported to the Lake County Jail for processing and booking on multiple charges related to fleeing and vehicle compliance violations under Florida law.
Charges: Felony fleeing and attempting to elude law enforcement, driving while license revoked, failure to register motor vehicle

Title: I hadn't done anything:' Pregnant woman arrested in Boca Raton traffic stop
description: Nerillia Laurent, a pregnant woman, was arrested in Boca Raton, Florida, following a traffic stop that initially began as a domestic disturbance call at a gas station where her car had broken down. According to police reports, officers arrived after Laurent and her boyfriend were involved in an argument. Officers attempted to identify Laurent during the encounter, but she allegedly refused to provide her driver’s license and information. Police stated she was warned she could be arrested if she continued to refuse. She was eventually removed from her vehicle, handcuffed, and placed under arrest. Laurent later claimed she was five months pregnant and experienced difficulty breathing while in the back of a hot patrol car, stating she was not given adequate ventilation. She was charged with resisting an officer without violence, along with outstanding warrants for failure to appear, driving with a canceled license, and providing a false name during detention. Her boyfriend was also charged separately.
Charges: Resisting an officer without violence; failure to appear warrant; driving with canceled/suspended license; giving a false name upon arrest or detention

Title: Officer brings pregnant woman to ground in arrest; history using force brought to light
description: Tamara Hatcher, a 38-year-old pregnant woman, was arrested in Palm Bay after a traffic stop escalated when she allegedly refused to exit her vehicle. According to police reports, she was initially stopped for driving without insurance. Officers stated that when she did not comply with commands, an officer broke her car window with a baton in an attempt to remove her from the vehicle. Hatcher then allegedly drove away from the scene, reportedly speeding and driving on the wrong side of the road before later being located at her residence and taken into custody. She faces charges stemming from resisting arrest and fleeing law enforcement at high speed. The incident gained attention after body-camera footage was released, raising public debate about the level of force used during the arrest. Officials stated the officer’s actions were within policy, while critics and former law enforcement personnel questioned the force applied during the arrest of a pregnant suspect.
Charges: Resisting Arrest, Fleeing and Eluding at High Speed, Driving Without Insurance

Title: Woman arrested after fleeing Flagler traffic stop into Volusia at 110+ mph, deputies say
description: Barbara Ray, 59, allegedly fled a Flagler traffic stop in Bunnell, Florida, early Thursday while driving a Ford Mustang. Deputies said she refused to stop and accelerated at speeds exceeding 100 mph, traveling southbound U.S. 1 and entering Interstate 95 northbound. Law enforcement attempted stop sticks but was initially unsuccessful as the vehicle continued at high speed. Deputies later deployed stop sticks near the Flagler Courthouse, damaging two tires, yet Ray continued fleeing on State Road 11 toward Volusia, reaching speeds over 110 mph. The pursuit ended when she lost control and crashed into a ditch in Volusia. She was located and taken into custody without further incident. She faces charges in Flagler for reckless driving, fleeing and eluding law enforcement with disregard for safety, resisting an officer without violence, and failure to obey lawful orders, plus additional fleeing and eluding charges in Volusia. No drug involvement was reported.
Charges: Reckless driving; fleeing and eluding law enforcement with disregard for safety; resisting an officer without violence; failure to obey lawful orders; additional fleeing and eluding (Volusia County)

Title: Missing child found with ‘pervert’ during chaotic traffic stop in Flagler County, sheriff says; additional charges filed
description: Darnell Hairston, 60, was arrested in Flagler County, Florida, after a chaotic traffic stop that escalated into a violent incident involving a missing child case. Deputies conducted a stop on a Ford F-150 along U.S. Highway 1 near Whiteview Drive after reports of suspicious activity. Inside the vehicle were Hairston, a registered sex offender, and two juveniles, one of whom had been reported missing from St. Johns County. During the stop, the missing child told deputies he had been kidnapped and was unsafe. As deputies investigated, Hairston suddenly fled on foot and attempted to grab a deputy’s firearm before being tackled and arrested. While officers were detaining him, one of the juveniles re-entered the truck and fled, nearly striking a deputy, leading to a pursuit and crash. The juvenile rammed a patrol vehicle during the chase. Hairston now faces kidnapping, child abuse, and additional violent felony charges in Flagler County Florida USA.
Charges: Kidnapping of a child under 13; aggravated child abuse; battery by strangulation; robbery with a deadly weapon; resisting an officer with violence; attempting to deprive a law enforcement officer of a firearm

Title: Video: Woman tries to stab deputies with Fix-a-Flat tool while attempting to resist arrest
description: On May 11, 2023, Flagler County deputies responded to reports of a woman riding a bicycle erratically along East State Road 100 near Aviation Drive in Bunnell, Florida. According to the Flagler County Sheriff’s Office, the woman was allegedly swerving into traffic and had reportedly damaged or keyed multiple vehicles before deputies arrived. When officers attempted to detain her, she fled into a grassy area and resisted arrest. During the confrontation, the woman became physically aggressive and attempted to stab a deputy in the leg using a Fix-a-Flat tire repair tool. Deputies used a Taser to gain control of her after she continued resisting. No deputies were seriously injured during the incident. The suspect was ultimately restrained and taken into custody after multiple officers assisted in securing her in a patrol vehicle. Authorities described her behavior as violent and dangerous during the encounter, and she was arrested following the incident.
Charges: Fleeing with intent to elude law enforcement; resisting an officer with violence; aggravated battery on a law enforcement officer; two counts of criminal mischief

Title: Police: Trumann woman led officers on a chase, attempted to use Taser on officers
description: A Jonesboro police officer assisted Craighead County deputies and a Bay officer in pursuing a vehicle driven by Amanda Ellen Lewis after she allegedly fled during a traffic stop. Officers conducted a tactical vehicle intervention to stop the car, successfully disabling it. After the vehicle came to a halt, Lewis reportedly refused to comply with commands and remained inside while speaking with dispatch on the phone. Officers observed her holding a Taser inside the vehicle. When she did not drop the weapon, police broke a window to gain entry. A struggle followed as officers attempted to disarm her. According to the affidavit, Lewis discharged the Taser multiple times in an effort to strike officers before being overpowered. She was eventually removed from the vehicle and taken into custody. Authorities charged her following the incident, and she is being held in jail on a $200,000 bond awaiting arraignment.
Charges: Aggravated assault on a police officer; fleeing a police officer

Title: 19-year-old Arkansas woman arrested after colliding with semi-truck during police chase
description: A 19-year-old woman led Arkansas State Police on a high-speed pursuit in West Memphis after allegedly driving recklessly on Interstate 40 during morning rush hour traffic. According to authorities, Kyla Morrow reached speeds exceeding 100 miles per hour while weaving through traffic, passing vehicles on the shoulder, and endangering other motorists. As the chase progressed toward the I-40 and I-55 interchange, she changed direction and entered Interstate 55 southbound before reversing course and driving northbound in the wrong direction against traffic flow. Police said she attempted to evade a PIT maneuver before colliding head-on with a commercial 18-wheeler, disabling both vehicles. After the crash, Morrow exited her vehicle and fled on foot but was quickly apprehended by officers a short distance away. Emergency responders evaluated both drivers, with the truck driver reporting no injuries. The suspect was taken into custody following the incident.
Charges: Fleeing; aggravated assault; leaving the scene of an accident; reckless driving

Title: Man arrested during Arkansas State Police altercation on I-49 takes plea deal
description: A traffic stop on Interstate 49 in Rogers, Arkansas escalated into a physical confrontation between a driver and an Arkansas State Police trooper. The driver, identified as 26-year-old Angel Zapet-Alvarado, was initially stopped for allegedly traveling at 114 mph. During the stop, authorities reported that he refused to exit his vehicle when ordered by the trooper. The trooper attempted to remove him from the vehicle, and a struggle occurred during which Zapet-Alvarado allegedly wrestled away a Taser and threw it onto the interstate. As the situation intensified and a passerby stopped to assist, the trooper drew her firearm and shot Zapet-Alvarado in the right temple. He was later treated at a hospital and taken into custody. Prosecutors later reduced or dropped several original felony charges, and he ultimately pleaded guilty to misdemeanor DWI and reckless driving, receiving credit for time served in jail and being ordered into rehabilitation.
Charges: Original: battery, resisting arrest, failure to yield, speeding, driving without license; Final plea: driving while intoxicated, reckless driving

Title: Man arrested in Ohio after dragging Waukegan police officer with car during traffic stop: police
description: Darius Mingo was involved in a traffic stop in Waukegan where police attempted to detain him after allegedly detecting the smell of marijuana coming from his vehicle. Officers reported that when they asked Mingo to exit the car, he initially complied but then pushed past them and tried to re-enter the vehicle. As officers attempted to stop him, Mingo allegedly drove away while an officer was partially outside the vehicle, resulting in the officer being dragged approximately 10 feet. The officer sustained bruises and cuts and was taken to a hospital for treatment. Mingo fled the scene and was not immediately apprehended, but he was later arrested the following day in Ohio during a separate traffic stop by local authorities. The case led to multiple serious felony charges related to violence against law enforcement and fleeing.
Charges: Aggravated battery to a police officer (2 counts), obstruction of justice, aggravated fleeing and resisting arrest

Title: Toledo police tase, hit passenger who allegedly had open container in car and resisted arrest
description: John Dorn was arrested in Toledo, Ohio following a traffic stop on West Manhattan Boulevard. Police reported that Dorn was the front-seat passenger in a vehicle stopped for a traffic violation. During the stop, officers allegedly observed an open container near his feet. When officers attempted to identify him, Dorn refused to provide his name and allegedly threw the container out of the vehicle window. Officers then ordered him to exit the car, but he reportedly resisted by holding onto the door frame and refusing to comply with commands. According to police, multiple attempts were made to remove him from the vehicle, including the use of a Taser three times, which was not effective. Officers ultimately struck Dorn in the face twice before successfully removing and arresting him. During the struggle, a police sergeant sustained hand injuries including lacerations and bruising. Dorn was taken into custody and charged with multiple misdemeanor offenses.
Charges: Resisting arrest, obstructing official business, failure to disclose personal information, open container violation, littering

Title: Man facing charges after deputy injured during chase, arrest in downtown Cincinnati
description: Garrett Monroe was arrested in downtown Cincinnati following a traffic stop that escalated into a foot pursuit and physical struggle with law enforcement. According to police reports, Monroe was initially stopped by the sheriff’s office due to an outstanding warrant. During the stop, he allegedly attempted to flee, prompting officers to pursue him on foot in the area near Central Parkway. During the chase and subsequent arrest attempt, Monroe was tased multiple times by officers. Prosecutors stated that during the struggle, a deputy was “slammed to the ground” and rendered unconscious, requiring hospital treatment. The incident was described in court as a chaotic melee involving multiple officers. Monroe was eventually subdued and taken into custody. Authorities charged him in connection with the injuries to the deputy and his resistance to arrest. The case involved both active warrant enforcement and allegations of violent resistance during apprehension in a busy downtown area.
Charges: Felonious assault, resisting arrest, driving under suspension, obstructing official business

Title: Defiance PD: Man with active felony warrant escalates traffic stop into pursuit, assault on officers
description: Matthew Kiessling was arrested in Defiance, Ohio after a traffic stop escalated into a violent confrontation involving multiple officers and a brief vehicle pursuit. Police said the incident began when officers stopped a 2007 Ford F-150 at a gas station due to an active felony warrant for attempted burglary. When officers informed Kiessling he was under arrest, he allegedly refused to exit the vehicle and actively resisted commands. During the struggle at the driver’s side door, Kiessling reportedly shifted the truck into reverse and accelerated, striking two officers with the open door and injuring them. He then allegedly rammed two marked police cruisers before fleeing the scene at high speed. After abandoning the vehicle, he fled on foot but was later located hiding beneath another vehicle and taken into custody with the help of a police K-9 unit. Both officers were treated and released from the hospital.
Charges: Assault on officers, failure to comply, vehicular assault (plus outstanding felony warrant for attempted burglary)

Title: Woman arrested for DUI after refusing sobriety test, injuring police officer in Gainesville
description: Officers in Gainesville, Florida, conducted a traffic stop around midnight after observing a vehicle without headlights that also ran a stop sign. The driver, identified as Woantavia Shaquan Culler, allegedly delayed pulling over and told officers she was stopping to use the bathroom. Police reported finding open containers of whiskey inside the vehicle and noted signs of impairment. Culler refused to complete field sobriety exercises, stating she did not need to prove sobriety. She was taken to the station for breath testing, where she recorded a 0.15 blood alcohol level. During the process, she allegedly became aggressive and pulled on the breath test equipment, causing minor injury to an officer. Her license was confiscated after refusing a second test. She was arrested and charged with DUI and battery on a law enforcement officer, then later released on her own recognizance after court appearance. No further injuries reported. case remains pending
Charges: Driving under the influence (DUI), battery on a law enforcement officer

Title: Woman attempts to get gas during DUI traffic stop in Marion County
description: Deputies in Marion County, Florida arrested Christina Bermudez after a high-speed reckless driving incident that reached over 100 miles per hour. Officers attempted a traffic stop after observing her vehicle swerving across the roadway. Instead of stopping immediately, she continued driving before eventually pulling into a gas station where she attempted to refuel her car. Officers reported she appeared unaware that law enforcement had been pursuing her with emergency lights activated for an extended period. During questioning, she stated she did not realize she was being pulled over and claimed it was dark. She denied drinking alcohol at the scene, but deputies observed signs of impairment and arrested her for DUI. At the jail, she later provided a breath sample registering 0.191, more than twice the legal limit. The case involved reckless driving and suspected intoxication, with no injuries reported by deputies in Marion County law enforcement authorities said report
Charges: Driving under the influence (DUI), reckless driving, speeding over 100 mph

Title: Anything for you, daddy': Hooters waitress attempts to charm police during DUI stop
description: A 22-year-old woman identified as Sophia Ross was arrested in Sarasota, Florida after officers observed her vehicle driving erratically, including stopping at green lights and striking curbs along the roadway. According to police reports, she showed signs of impairment when approached, including slurred speech and lethargic movements. Officers stated she admitted to drinking at a bar prior to the traffic stop. During the DUI investigation, bodycam footage reportedly showed Ross making repeated inappropriate and flirtatious remarks toward a responding officer, including attempts to avoid or delay sobriety testing. She identified herself as a Hooters waitress during the interaction and continued making advances despite repeated refusals from law enforcement. Officers ultimately determined she was impaired and placed her under arrest after she refused to complete field sobriety testing. She was charged with driving under the influence. No injuries were reported during the incident, and the case proceeded to court with a not guilty plea entered and a pretrial hearing scheduled.
Charges: Driving under the influence (DUI)

Title: Florida Woman Claims Husband Was Driving During DUI Arrest. He Wasn't There
description: Kristian Beall, Florida Highway Patrol officers arrested a woman after a wrong-way driving incident on Interstate 4 that required a PIT maneuver to stop the vehicle. Authorities reported the driver was traveling dangerously and allegedly driving in the wrong direction on the interstate, creating a serious risk to other motorists. After the stop, officers observed clear signs of impairment and determined she was intoxicated. Breath test results reportedly showed extremely high alcohol levels, with readings of 0.099 and 0.202, both significantly above the legal limit of 0.08. During questioning, the woman attempted to blame her husband for driving the vehicle the wrong way, despite officers confirming she was the only person in the car. Fortunately, no injuries were reported in the incident. She was taken into custody on suspicion of DUI and reckless driving-related offenses. The case involved a high-risk traffic stop on a major highway and is being handled by Florida Highway Patrol authorities.
Charges: Driving under the influence (DUI), reckless driving, wrong-way driving

Title: Driver arrested for DUI after traffic stop in Port St. Lucie
description: Officers in Port St. Lucie, Florida conducted a traffic stop on 40-year-old Fernanda Duque early Friday morning after observing her driving carelessly on U.S. 1 near Southeast Jennings Road. During the stop, officers suspected impairment and noted two open bottles of wine inside her black Infiniti SUV. The driver underwent field sobriety testing and failed, according to police reports. Authorities determined she was under the influence of alcohol and placed her under arrest for driving while intoxicated. Her vehicle was subsequently towed, and she was transported to the St. Lucie County Jail for booking. Police emphasized ongoing enforcement efforts targeting impaired driving during late-night and early-morning hours. No injuries or crashes were reported in the incident, and no other occupants were involved. The case remains part of local DUI enforcement efforts aimed at reducing roadway risks and preventing alcohol-related accidents in the community. No additional charges were reported by authorities.
Charges: Driving under the influence (DUI)

Title: ‘I'm not crazy, I'm sober': Video shows Miami Gardens Police sergeant's DUI arrest
description: A Miami Gardens Police sergeant identified as Andrea Rhodesia Smith was arrested in Florida after officers observed her driving a Mercedes that allegedly sped through traffic signals, including rolling through a red light and accelerating through another intersection. A traffic stop was conducted by her own department, during which officers reported signs of impairment, including bloodshot eyes, slurred speech, and the odor of alcohol. She was asked to complete sobriety exercises, which were reportedly initiated but then halted during the investigation, and she also refused a breath test according to reports. Smith was taken into custody and booked on traffic-related charges including DUI and reckless driving. Body camera footage captured portions of the arrest, including her statements during transport to jail. She was later relieved of duty by the Miami Gardens Police Department following the incident. No injuries were reported, and the case remained pending trial proceedings after she pleaded not guilty.
Charges: Driving under the influence (DUI), reckless driving

Title: South Fort Myers woman accused of DUI after hitting deputy’s car, refusing sobriety test
description: A 65-year-old woman identified as Julie Biffar was arrested in Fort Myers, Florida after allegedly driving under the influence and striking a deputy’s patrol vehicle during a traffic stop investigation. According to the Lee County Sheriff’s Office, deputies were initially responding to a hit-and-run crash involving a stationary patrol car conducting a traffic stop when the suspect vehicle hit the cruiser and continued driving away. Deputies later located the registered owner’s residence and conducted a traffic stop when the vehicle was seen returning. Officers reported signs of impairment, including watery eyes, slurred speech, and a strong odor of alcohol. A small bottle of alcohol reportedly fell from the vehicle during the encounter. After failing field sobriety tests, she was taken into custody for driving under the influence. She was later transported to a hospital for medical clearance before being booked into the Lee County Jail. No serious injuries were reported in the incident.
Charges: Driving under the influence (DUI), hit-and-run

Title: Florida woman arrested for DUI after having 'three sips of wine': police
description: A 42-year-old woman identified as Britaine Schmer was arrested in Leesburg, Florida after being stopped by police on suspicion of driving under the influence. Officers reported observing her vehicle swerving within its lane on U.S. Highway 27 before initiating a traffic stop. During the investigation, the driver allegedly showed signs of impairment, including glassy and watery eyes and the smell of a strong air freshener inside the vehicle. She told officers she had only consumed “three sips of wine” earlier at her boyfriend’s house. Schmer agreed to perform field sobriety tests but was later arrested after failing to properly follow instructions during the evaluation. She provided breath samples that reportedly showed no alcohol, but a subsequent urine test suggested possible impairment. She was taken into custody and transported to the Lake County Jail. The case involved DUI suspicion despite conflicting chemical test results, and no injuries were reported.
Charges: Driving under the influence (DUI)

Title: Florida woman arrested for DUI during Hurricane Debby blamed storm winds for failed sobriety test
description: A 38-year-old woman identified as Candace Wisecup was arrested in Citrus County, Florida during severe weather conditions as Hurricane Debby impacted the area. According to the Citrus County Sheriff’s Office, the sheriff himself observed the driver behaving erratically at a traffic signal, including spinning her tires and repeatedly activating hazard lights. A traffic stop was initiated, and deputies reported signs of impairment such as slurred speech and the odor of alcohol. Officers also discovered multiple open and empty alcohol containers inside the vehicle, including liquor shooters and an open can of beer. During field sobriety testing, Wisecup allegedly performed poorly and blamed strong hurricane winds for her inability to maintain balance. She refused to submit to a breathalyzer test and was also found to be driving with a suspended license. She was arrested for DUI-related offenses and taken into custody without any reported injuries or collisions during the incident.
Charges: Driving under the influence (DUI), driving on suspended license, refusal to submit to breath test
Comments: Citrus County Sheriff's Office was not utilizing dash or body cameras at the time of this incident.

Title: Cape Coral woman arrested for DUI, accused of causing more than $4K in damages
description: On July 12, 2024, Layla Martinez, 22, was involved in a series of crashes in a Cape Coral neighborhood before being stopped by law enforcement. A deputy was alerted by a resident who reported that a blue sedan had struck multiple vehicles and property and that the driver might be experiencing a medical issue. When officers located the vehicle, they observed significant front-end damage. Martinez reportedly showed signs of impairment, including bloodshot and watery eyes, slurred speech, poor coordination, and the odor of alcohol. Officers attempted to have medical personnel evaluate her, but she allegedly refused to cooperate and had to be removed from the vehicle. Investigators later determined that she struck several vehicles, city water access covers, a drainage pipe, and a mailbox, causing approximately $4,700 in property damage. She was arrested for DUI and additional offenses. At the hospital, authorities reported that she remained uncooperative and had to be restrained before being transported to jail.
Charges: DUI (1 count) Property Damage (7 counts) Hit-and-Run / Leaving the Scene of a Crash Involving Property Damage (7 counts) Battery on Law Enforcement Officer (2 counts) Battery on a Registered Nurse (1 count) Resisting Officers Without Violence (1 count)

Title: Monroe County Woman Blames Driving Infraction on Dog, Results in DUI and Felony Charge
description: On October 2023, Michele Lee Burke, 54, was stopped by deputies in Key Largo, Florida, after failing to comply with Florida’s Move Over Law while passing officers conducting a traffic stop on the Overseas Highway. Deputies initiated a stop after she failed to move over or sufficiently slow down. During the encounter, Burke reportedly blamed the traffic violation on her Yorkshire Terrier, which was sitting on her lap. Deputies detected a strong odor of alcohol and observed signs of impairment. Burke admitted to having consumed alcohol and participated only partially in field sobriety exercises before refusing further cooperation. When officers attempted to arrest her, she allegedly became hostile, used profanity, grabbed a deputy’s finger, threatened an officer, and later kicked a deputy multiple times while restrained. After being transported to jail, she reportedly admitted she had consumed too much alcohol and refused a breathalyzer test. The incident escalated from a traffic violation into criminal charges due to her conduct during the arrest.
Charges: Driving Under the Influence (DUI) Resisting an Officer with Violence (Felony)

Title: Just take me away': DUI stop on golf cart leads to arrest, unpleasant exchanges, deputy says
description: David Clifford Roach, a 71-year-old man, was arrested in Lady Lake, Florida, after a deputy observed him appearing unsteady and confused before entering and operating a golf cart. The deputy watched Roach drive through a flashing red signal without coming to a complete stop and drift across lane dividers multiple times. Concerned that the driver might be impaired or experiencing a medical emergency, the deputy initiated a traffic stop. After stopping the golf cart, the deputy observed bloodshot and watery eyes, detected the odor of alcohol, and noticed Roach swaying while standing. Roach admitted to consuming alcoholic beverages earlier in the evening. During the investigation, he participated in field sobriety exercises, which the deputy determined he performed poorly. Roach was arrested for driving under the influence and transported to jail. During the encounter, he made several argumentative and threatening remarks toward the deputy. He was later released from jail after less than twelve hours.
Charges: Driving Under the Influence (DUI)  Written Warning for Failing to Stop for a Flashing Red Signal

Title: Venice Police find DUI suspect parked at police headquarters
description: Officers with Venice Police Department discovered a woman asleep in a running Toyota sedan parked in the police headquarters lot. Inside the vehicle, they observed several partially consumed wine bottles, suggesting alcohol use. When officers attempted to wake her, she refused to roll down the window or communicate. As police investigated, she remained uncooperative and later drove away despite stop sticks being deployed. A pursuit followed through multiple streets while the vehicle continued on a deflated tire and ignored traffic signals. The driver eventually stopped near Venice City Hall, where officers safely removed her from the vehicle after forced entry due to continued noncompliance. Field sobriety tests were administered, and she was arrested. She faces charges related to DUI, fleeing to elude law enforcement, and resisting an officer without violence. The incident highlights dangerous impaired driving behavior and escalation during a routine welfare check that became a pursuit incident escalation
Charges: DUI; fleeing to elude law enforcement; resisting an officer without violence

Title: Shoreview woman accused of drunk driving in Florida and seriously injuring deputy
description: A Shoreview woman was involved in a serious DUI-related crash in the Florida Keys after striking a deputy’s cruiser during an active traffic stop. According to the Monroe County Sheriff’s Office, the incident occurred near Mile Marker 87 on U.S. 1 when a deputy was standing between his patrol vehicle and another stopped car. The driver, identified as 26-year-old Alexandra Marlene Baraga, collided with the deputy’s cruiser, pinning the deputy between vehicles and causing severe injuries. Emergency responders had to assist in freeing the deputy, who was then airlifted to a Miami hospital for treatment. Authorities reported that Baraga had a blood alcohol concentration of 0.310, nearly four times the legal limit. She was arrested by the Florida Highway Patrol and taken into custody. The crash was treated as a major DUI incident involving serious bodily harm to a law enforcement officer during a roadside traffic stop operation.
Charges: DUI (suspicion/expected formal charges not specified); DUI causing serious injury (implied from report)

Title: Florida man claiming to be ICE Agent arrested for DUI with children in vehicle: deputies
description: A 42-year-old man, Scott Thomas Deisroth, was arrested in Monroe County, Florida, after deputies received a report from another motorist about reckless driving. Deputies conducted a traffic stop and found two children, ages 7 and 9, inside the vehicle. During the investigation, officers detected a strong odor of alcohol coming from Deisroth. According to authorities, he identified himself as a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent. Deputies administered standard field sobriety exercises, which he reportedly failed. As a result, he was taken into custody and charged with driving under the influence. The incident raised additional concerns because young children were present in the vehicle while he was allegedly impaired. The case originated from a reckless driving complaint rather than a crash. No injuries or fatalities were reported. The arrest followed the roadside DUI investigation conducted by deputies, and Deisroth was placed in handcuffs after failing the sobriety tests.
Charges: DUI (Driving Under the Influence)

Title: Body camera footage shows woman fleeing from traffic stop, striking officer with her car
description: Police in Lauderhill, Florida, released body camera footage showing a DUI traffic stop that escalated into a brief chase and crash. Officers attempted to stop a vehicle driven by 26-year-old Crystalee Tennant-Parnther after suspecting impairment during a traffic encounter. According to authorities, during the stop an officer tried to gather information, but the driver attempted to flee the scene. As she drove away, she struck the officer with her car door, which was open at the time. The vehicle then traveled a short distance before crashing into a tree. Body camera footage shows officers responding immediately, assisting the injured officer, and approaching the crashed vehicle. One officer used a knife to cut Tennant-Parnther’s seatbelt to safely remove her from the car. She was taken into custody and later charged with multiple offenses related to DUI and resisting law enforcement. At a court appearance, she was ordered not to drive under any circumstances pending further proceedings.
Charges: DUI Resisting law enforcement Driving with expired license (over 6 months) Fleeing/attempting to flee traffic stop Property damage (crash-related)

Title: Doctor on Hurlburt arrested for DUI, resisting officer in Tiger Point
description: A periodontist and active-duty Air Force lieutenant colonel stationed at Hurlburt Field was arrested in Tiger Point, Florida, after a traffic stop for suspected DUI. According to the Santa Rosa County Sheriff’s Office, deputies observed a BMW SUV traveling above the posted speed limit, reaching about 73 mph in a 55-mph zone and later continuing at high speed into a construction area. When a traffic stop was initiated near Tiger Point Park, the driver, identified as Michelle Bongiovi, allegedly refused to cooperate with officers. She did not provide requested documents and repeatedly declined commands to exit the vehicle. Deputies reported that she continued to argue and resist compliance, prompting officers to forcibly open the vehicle and remove her. She was arrested after allegedly failing field sobriety tests and showing signs of impairment such as unusual statements and dilated pupils. She was booked into jail and later released.
Charges: Driving Under the Influence (DUI) Resisting an officer Failure to obey lawful police instructions

Title: North Fort Myers woman charged with DUI with children in the car
description: Officers with the Cape Coral Police Department arrested a North Fort Myers woman after a report that she was driving under the influence with children inside her vehicle. According to authorities, the incident began when a young teen caller alerted emergency dispatchers that an adult driver appeared intoxicated and was “swerving all over the road” while transporting minors. Officers located a vehicle matching the description on Country Club Boulevard and initiated a traffic stop. During the stop, police reported observing multiple signs of impairment, including a strong odor of alcohol coming from the driver. Two children under the age of 10 were found in the back seat of the vehicle. Officers conducted standardized field sobriety tests, during which the driver allegedly showed numerous indicators of impairment. Based on their observations and test performance, she was taken into custody on suspicion of DUI. The children were later released to a legal guardian following the arrest.
Charges: Driving under the influence (DUI) with a person under 18 in the vehicle DUI refusal to submit to testing

Title: Taylors woman sings gospel songs and urinates on herself after DUI arrest following police chase, officials say
description: Courtney Epps, 41, was arrested in the Florida Keys after authorities reported she drove the wrong way on U.S. Route 1 at high speeds, creating a serious hazard for oncoming traffic. Troopers stated she traveled between 90 and 120 mph while heading north in southbound lanes and ignored emergency lights and sirens during the pursuit. Law enforcement deployed spike strips, which damaged her tires, but she continued driving at dangerous speeds. Eventually, she crashed into a construction area and was taken into custody. During medical evaluation, officers reported unusual behavior including singing gospel songs loudly, periods of confusion, and incoherence. She later underwent breath testing, which showed 0.000 BAC readings, but she refused a urine test. Despite this, she was charged with DUI and felony fleeing or eluding law enforcement with disregard for safety. Officials emphasized the severity of the chase due to oncoming traffic and the presence of runners during a marathon event nearby.
Charges: DUI Fleeing or Eluding Law Enforcement with Disregard for Safety (Felony)

Title: Watch: 2 violent arrests after deputy's discussion with 'sovereign citizen' driver on following laws
description: Authorities in Volusia County, Florida, responded to a traffic stop involving a pickup truck after a deputy observed irregular license documentation and registration concerns. During the stop, the driver, Detry Wogerman, refused to provide a valid driver’s license and instead presented paperwork while engaging in “sovereign citizen” style arguments. The situation escalated when deputies determined he was failing to properly identify himself and ordered him out of the vehicle. After he refused, multiple deputies physically removed him from the driver’s seat and placed him in handcuffs. A second suspect, Laralynne Nabozny, later arrived at the scene and became involved in the confrontation. She refused commands from officers, remained uncooperative, and was forcibly removed from her vehicle after deputies broke the driver’s side window. Both individuals were detained following resistance to law enforcement. The incident resulted in multiple charges related to resisting arrest and driving violations. Sheriff’s officials described the situation as a highly uncooperative traffic stop requiring physical enforcement actions by deputies.
Charges: Detry Wogerman: Driving unregistered motor vehicle; driving with suspended/revoked license (habitual); resisting officer without violence Laralynne Nabozny: Battery on law enforcement officer; resisting officer with violence

Title: Navarre woman arrested after driving under the influence with children in car: Arrest Report
description: Santa Rosa County deputies arrested a Navarre woman after she was observed driving recklessly and suspected of operating a vehicle under the influence while transporting children. According to the Santa Rosa County Sheriff’s Office arrest report, deputies attempted to initiate a traffic stop after noticing erratic driving behavior on Highway Boulevard. The driver allegedly initially refused to pull over, continuing for a short distance before stopping. When deputies made contact, they reported detecting a strong odor of alcohol coming from her breath along with bloodshot eyes, both consistent with impairment. Two prepubescent children were found in the back seat of the vehicle at the time of the stop. Officers conducted their investigation and determined probable cause for DUI. The driver was taken into custody and charged with driving under the influence and child abuse due to the presence of minors during the alleged impaired driving incident. She was booked into the county jail and later released.
Charges: Driving under the influence (DUI) Child abuse (DUI with children in vehicle)

Title: Man accused of driving 118 mph drunk with wife, young children in car, authorities say
description: Juan Espinosa was arrested in Brevard County, Florida after deputies with the Brevard County Sheriff’s Office observed him driving at extremely high speed on Interstate 95, reportedly reaching 118 mph shortly before stopping in the center median. A deputy initiated a traffic stop around 2:20 a.m. and, upon approaching the vehicle, detected signs of alcohol consumption, including the smell of alcohol coming from inside the SUV. Authorities reported that Espinosa’s wife was in the passenger seat and two young children, ages 1 and 8, were in the back seat. Law enforcement stated that Espinosa showed indicators of impairment while interacting with deputies and was subsequently arrested. He was charged with driving under the influence and child neglect due to the presence of minors during the dangerous high-speed incident. Officials emphasized the risk posed to all occupants and other motorists due to the excessive speed and suspected intoxication.
Charges: DUI, child neglect

Title: Florida woman accused of biting deputy after her arrest for DUI
description: Deborah Odom, a 60-year-old woman, was arrested in the Florida Keys after deputies stopped her for suspected drunk driving. Law enforcement reported receiving complaints that she was driving recklessly and swerving on US-1 near mile marker 82. During the traffic stop, deputies observed signs of intoxication, including an odor of alcohol. She was arrested for driving under the influence and transported to jail. While in custody, authorities say Odom became combative and bit a corrections deputy, escalating the situation into a battery on a law enforcement officer charge. The incident began as a DUI traffic stop but continued after arrest when her behavior allegedly turned violent inside the detention setting. She was ultimately booked into jail facing multiple charges related to DUI and assaulting a deputy. Officials did not report any injuries requiring hospitalization, but confirmed the deputy was bitten during the encounter inside the jail facility following her arrest.
Charges: Driving under the influence (DUI), battery on a law enforcement officer

Title: Do you understand I'm a deputy?': Sarasota deputy arrested for DUI, found slumped over
description: Former Sarasota County Sheriff’s Office deputy Tracy Bell, age 49, was arrested for DUI after Sarasota police found her slumped over in her personal vehicle on the shoulder of Ringling Boulevard at the intersection with S. Osprey Avenue. Officers reported that her vehicle was idling and obstructing part of the roadway when they approached. Bell allegedly showed clear signs of impairment, including slurred speech, bloodshot eyes, confusion, and difficulty standing without support. She initially told officers she had stopped to text her boyfriend and admitted to drinking alcohol earlier in the evening at Siesta Key. She refused field sobriety tests and a breathalyzer. A plastic cup smelling of alcohol was reportedly found inside her vehicle. Bell was arrested for DUI and later bonded out of jail. She resigned from the sheriff’s office following the incident and was found in violation of agency policies during an internal investigation into her conduct and behavior.
Charges: Driving under the influence (DUI), reckless driving

Title: Florida deputies, officer gashed while arresting ‘combative’ DUI driver, officials say
description: Richard Lakin, a 56-year-old man, was arrested in Flagler County, Florida, after a DUI traffic stop escalated into a violent confrontation with law enforcement. Deputies and a Bunnell police officer initiated the stop after Lakin made an illegal U-turn and showed signs of impairment. Officers reported slurred speech, bloodshot and glassy eyes, and the odor of alcohol. Lakin allegedly admitted to drinking four beers earlier at a bar. During field sobriety testing, he became argumentative and agitated, then resisted arrest. Deputies said the situation escalated into a physical struggle in which officers sustained minor injuries, including abrasions and gashes. While being taken into custody, Lakin continued to resist and was eventually subdued and placed in handcuffs. A search of his vehicle reportedly revealed a half-full beer. He was later transported to jail and charged after the incident, which involved multiple law enforcement agencies responding to the scene.
Charges: DUI, resisting with violence, three counts of battery on law enforcement officer, refusal to submit to breath test

Title: Video shows Cape Coral councilwoman walk away during DUI stop
description: Rachel Kaduk, a 36-year-old Cape Coral councilwoman, was arrested on December 16, 2025, following a report of reckless driving in Cape Coral, Florida. Authorities responded after a concerned citizen called 911 and reported that a driver appeared to be intoxicated while traveling along Del Prado Boulevard. The caller stated that the driver seemed “definitely drunk.” Body camera and police footage released later showed Kaduk interacting with officers during the traffic stop. According to reports, she was uncooperative during the investigation, failed to answer several questions from law enforcement, and did not comply with field sobriety testing procedures. Video footage also showed her walking away from officers during the encounter. Based on the observations made by responding officers and the circumstances surrounding the incident, Kaduk was taken into custody and charged. The arrest attracted public attention because of her position as an elected city council member. The case was handled by local law enforcement authorities.
Charges: Driving under the influence (DUI)

Title: Boca Raton Woman Accused of Leading Police in Late-Night DUI Chase
description: Fernanda Blanco, 35, was arrested in Boca Raton after police said she led officers on a late-night DUI pursuit following a disturbance call at a bowling and sports lounge. Officers reported seeing her stumble into a Volkswagen SUV before driving over a curb and heading south on Plaza Real. According to the police report, she ran a stop sign, swerved within her lane, and continued driving despite multiple attempts by officers to stop her vehicle using lights and sirens. She allegedly refused to pull over and even drove off when officers attempted to open her car door during an initial stop. The pursuit continued into downtown Boca Raton, where she entered a parking garage. Officers ultimately removed her from the vehicle and placed her in custody. She reportedly gave a false name before being identified through credit cards. Police said she appeared confused and disoriented.
Charges: DUI, fleeing and eluding police, resisting an officer

Title: DUI suspect flees traffic stop, tries to escape handcuffs in Flagler County
description: Justin Quintero, a 23-year-old man from Palm Coast, was arrested in Flagler County after deputies said he fled a traffic stop while suspected of driving under the influence. According to the Flagler County Sheriff’s Office, Quintero was observed driving a gray Nissan at approximately 70 mph in a 35 mph zone and appeared impaired, with officers noting unsteady movement, staggering, and a strong odor of alcohol. Deputies attempted to conduct a traffic stop, but he allegedly fled the scene with lights and sirens active. Authorities later took him into custody after the pursuit. During transport, he reportedly tried to escape his handcuffs. He refused field sobriety and breath testing and was uncooperative with detention staff. Officials said his behavior indicated intoxication and reckless disregard for traffic laws. The case resulted in multiple charges tied to DUI, fleeing law enforcement, and resisting arrest without violence.
Charges: DUI, reckless driving, fleeing law enforcement, resisting arrest without violence, refusal of DUI tests

Title: Lake County woman faces DUI charges after driving erratically, dangerously close to the power crews
description: Faith Walker, 33, was arrested in Lake County after deputies responded to reports of a reckless driver operating a white Chrysler in multiple areas along Highway 42 and Highway 450A. According to the Lake County Sheriff’s Office, witnesses reported the vehicle performing dangerous maneuvers, including driving into oncoming traffic, spinning in the roadway, and nearly striking pedestrians and utility workers. Deputies said power line crews working in the area were forced to signal urgently to alert law enforcement after the vehicle drove extremely close to them. When officers located the car, Walker reportedly refused repeated commands to turn off her vehicle and instead ignored deputies, increasing the volume of her radio. She was eventually removed from the vehicle and placed in handcuffs after resisting officers’ instructions. Authorities said she showed signs of impairment, including slurred speech and an odor of alcohol, and an empty alcohol bottle was found in the vehicle. She later refused a breath test at jail.
Charges: DUI, resisting an officer without violence, failure to obey law enforcement

Title: VIDEO: State Police Pursuit Ends In Crash And Foot Chase Arrest In Quitman
description: Arkansas State Police initiated a traffic stop after observing a red Ford traveling above the speed limit near Quitman. The driver briefly entered a parking lot but failed to stop and instead circled back onto the highway, continuing to flee. Troopers activated sirens and pursued the vehicle as it accelerated onto nearby streets. During the chase, the driver lost control on a curve, causing the car to strike a tree and come to a stop. After the crash, the suspect exited the vehicle and fled on foot into nearby woods. Law enforcement conducted a brief search operation and successfully apprehended him. He was identified as Caleb Michael Phillips and taken into custody without further incident. The pursuit involved both a vehicle chase and a foot chase, and it ended when the suspect was located and arrested by Arkansas State Police in the surrounding wooded area.
Charges: Felony fleeing in a vehicle Fleeing on foot First-degree reckless driving Driving on a suspended license Failure to wear seatbelt Speeding (1–15 mph over limit)

Title: Veteran JSO officer faces DUI charge after traffic stop in St. Johns County
description: A veteran Jacksonville Sheriff’s Office officer was arrested in St. Johns County after an off-duty DUI traffic stop on U.S. Highway 1. According to authorities, Raymond Goethe, a 28-year veteran of the Jacksonville Sheriff’s Office, was driving his personal vehicle when a St. Johns County Sheriff’s Office deputy pulled him over for a traffic violation. During the stop, deputies conducted a roadside interview and determined he was impaired, leading to a DUI arrest. Following the incident, the Jacksonville Sheriff’s Office announced that Goethe was administratively reassigned from his patrol duties. The case is notable due to his long tenure with law enforcement and his position as an active-duty officer at the time of arrest. No injuries were reported, and no crash was involved. The arrest initiated internal administrative action within his employing agency. The investigation and any further disciplinary or court proceedings were not detailed in the report provided.
Charges: Driving under the influence (DUI)

Title: Wrong-way DUI stop leads to woman handing over Barnes & Noble gift card instead of license
description: Kami Ellis was arrested after a deputy observed her driving the wrong way on Sheldon Road near West Linebaugh Avenue in Tampa, Florida, at approximately 12:30 a.m. on April 12, 2026. According to authorities, Ellis was seen traveling on the incorrect side of the roadway and driving onto a curb, prompting a traffic stop. During the encounter, the deputy asked for her driver's license. Instead of providing her license, Ellis first handed over a credit card and then a Barnes & Noble gift card. Body camera footage reportedly captured the interaction and showed signs that led deputies to investigate her condition further. After exiting her vehicle, Ellis was detained and placed in handcuffs. Law enforcement determined that she was impaired while operating the vehicle. The incident gained attention because of the unusual exchange involving the gift card during the stop. Ellis was subsequently taken into custody and booked into jail following the investigation.
Charges: Driving under the influence (DUI)

Title: Akron man pleads guilty to shooting at police during March traffic stop
description: Jon Tae Von Angelo Nelson was involved in a traffic stop in Akron, Ohio, where police attempted to pull over his Ford F-150 for an alleged traffic violation. As officers approached the vehicle during the stop, Nelson allegedly fired a gun toward the officers, prompting one officer to return fire. Nelson then fled the scene, initiating a brief pursuit. No officers or bystanders were reported injured during the incident. Authorities later arrested Nelson the following day with assistance from the U.S. Marshals Northern Ohio Violent Fugitive Task Force. Court proceedings show he was originally charged with multiple serious felonies, including felonious assault and weapons-related offenses. However, as part of a plea agreement, he pleaded guilty to reduced charges, including discharging a firearm near prohibited premises, failure to comply with a police order, and improper handling of a firearm in a motor vehicle. He is scheduled for sentencing following the plea deal resolution in court.
Charges: Discharge of firearm near prohibited premises (misdemeanor), failure to comply with police order (felony), improper handling of firearm in vehicle (felony)

Title: Jonesboro woman charged with endangering children, DWI after traffic stop
description: Latrica Marie Upshaw, 30, was arrested in Jonesboro, Arkansas, following a traffic stop conducted by police on February 17, 2026. Officers stopped her vehicle on Church Street after observing defective license plate illumination. During the encounter, police reported that Upshaw displayed signs of intoxication, including bloodshot and watery eyes and a strong odor of alcohol. She allegedly refused to provide proof of insurance and attempted to leave the scene despite being instructed to remain. After a brief struggle, officers placed her in handcuffs. While investigating, officers discovered three young children, ranging from 9 months to 5 years old, inside a nearby residence without adult supervision. Police reported the home was in an unsanitary condition and one child was found in a heavily soiled diaper. Upshaw later attempted to flee while handcuffed but was apprehended after a short pursuit. She was transported to jail and refused a chemical blood-alcohol test.
Charges: Three Counts of First-Degree Endangering the Welfare of a Minor  Third-Degree Escape from Custody  Resisting Arrest  Disorderly Conduct  Driving While Intoxicated (DWI)  Refusal to Submit  Tail Lamps and Reflectors Violation

Title: OSHP, Cincinnati police make multiple arrests after 2 chases Monday night
description: Cincinnati police and the Ohio State Highway Patrol were involved in two separate vehicle pursuits late Monday night, resulting in multiple arrests. The first incident began when Mykez Smith allegedly fled a traffic stop while driving a Ford Escape. During the pursuit, Smith reportedly crashed into two vehicles before exiting the SUV and attempting to flee on foot. He was later apprehended after a Taser was deployed by a Cincinnati police officer. Authorities reported that the vehicle Smith was driving had been stolen and that a stolen firearm was recovered from inside the SUV. A passenger, Madison Stallworth, was also arrested at the scene. The pursuit was part of a broader violent crime reduction operation involving multiple law enforcement agencies. Smith and Stallworth face several charges related to stolen property, firearms violations, and improper handling of weapons in a motor vehicle. The second chase later that night involved additional arrests.
Charges: Reckless driving; receiving stolen property; having weapons while under disability; improper handling of a firearm in a motor vehicle

Title: Man arrested after leading police on a vehicle chase
