description: A 24-year-old Toledo man was arrested after police say he stole a Ford F-150 pickup truck from a dealership and led officers on a multi-route pursuit across Toledo. Officers first observed the suspect doing “donuts” at an intersection before attempting a traffic stop, at which point he fled. Police reported that the pursuit continued through multiple major roads and highways, including I-475, I-75, the Anthony Wayne Trail, and several city streets. The chase ended when the suspect drove off the road near Jeep Parkway and crashed the stolen truck into a ditch. He was taken into custody and transported for minor injuries. While being held in a patrol vehicle, he allegedly damaged the interior cage by kicking it, resulting in additional vandalism charges. Authorities charged him with receiving stolen property, failure to comply with a police order, and vandalism. No serious injuries to officers or civilians were reported during the incident.
Charges: Receiving stolen property; Failure to comply with police order; Vandalism

Title: Officer breaks leg after semitruck driver accused of stalking person at IHOP flees traffic stop
description: A 34-year-old semitruck driver was arrested after allegedly stalking a person at an IHOP restaurant and then fleeing from police during a traffic stop, leading to a dangerous pursuit in Springfield, Ohio. Officers initially responded to reports that the suspect was making threats at the restaurant. When police attempted to remove him from the cab of his semitruck during a traffic stop, he allegedly resisted and drove away, causing an officer to suffer a concussion and a broken leg after clinging to the vehicle. The suspect then led law enforcement on a pursuit across multiple communities, during which he reportedly struck police cruisers and other vehicles. At one point, he attempted to evade capture by continuing to drive the semitruck with a trailer attached. Police later located him again after the pursuit continued, and he was ultimately taken into custody following further confrontation. He faces multiple felony charges related to assault, fleeing, and obstruction.
Charges: Felonious assault; willful fleeing; obstruction of official business; aggravated menacing

Title: Former Saints star Marshon Lattimore arrested on new weapons charges in Ohio
description: Marshon Lattimore, a 29-year-old NFL cornerback, was arrested during a traffic stop in Lakewood, Ohio after police reported weapons-related violations. Officers said the vehicle was initially stopped for expired license plates and other traffic infractions. Lattimore was a passenger in the vehicle. During the stop, officers asked if there were any firearms in the car, and authorities allege that Lattimore did not properly inform them about a firearm inside the vehicle. Police then charged him with carrying a concealed weapon and improperly handling firearms in a motor vehicle. He was booked into jail and later released pending further investigation, with no bond required. The incident drew attention due to his professional football career and previous legal issues involving firearms. Lattimore has had prior arrests related to concealed weapons charges, including a 2021 Cleveland traffic stop case that resulted in a misdemeanor conviction and a suspended jail sentence. The investigation into the 2026 incident remains ongoing.
Charges: Carrying concealed weapon, improperly handling firearms in a motor vehicle

Title: BG Police arrest driver after alleged high-speed car chase, then foot chase into manufacturing plant
description: A 34-year-old Toledo man, Talmadge Thomas, was arrested in Bowling Green, Ohio after a traffic stop escalated into a high-speed pursuit and foot chase. Police initiated the stop after observing Thomas driving without headlights on Poe Road. During the initial interaction, Thomas provided identifying information but allegedly fled as the officer returned to their patrol vehicle. He then led officers on a high-speed chase through multiple roads, including East Poe Road, Dunbridge Road, and Woodbridge Boulevard, entering a business park. Multiple civilian vehicles reportedly had to take evasive action to avoid being struck during the pursuit. Thomas eventually abandoned his vehicle and ran into a manufacturing facility, where officers pursued him on foot and took him into custody inside the Magna plant. Authorities later discovered he was driving with a suspended license and was on federal parole at the time of the incident.
Charges: Failure to comply/fleeing and eluding, non-compliance suspension, driving under OVI suspension

Title: Man arrested after leading Bucyrus Troopers on wild high-speed chase
description: An Upper Sandusky man, Tyler Rowalt, was arrested after leading Ohio State Highway Patrol troopers on a multi-county high-speed chase that reached speeds of up to 120 mph. The incident began when troopers were dispatched for a welfare check related to a domestic dispute, during which Rowalt allegedly took his wife’s vehicle while impaired, emotionally distraught, and reportedly in possession of a firearm. Troopers located the vehicle near Upper Sandusky and attempted a traffic stop, but Rowalt fled, triggering a prolonged pursuit. During the chase, he drove recklessly, including traveling in opposing lanes of traffic and nearly striking a pursuing officer. The pursuit ended when he crashed into a guardrail on State Route 15 in Hancock County. After the crash, he initially refused commands to exit the vehicle and allegedly attempted to ignite gasoline inside the car before eventually surrendering. He was treated for minor injuries and taken into custody.
Charges: Failure to comply/fleeing and eluding (felony), plus related traffic violations (exact full list not specified in article)

Title: Man arrested after chase, gunfire exchange with police
description: Police in Toledo, Ohio attempted a traffic stop near Parkside Boulevard and Hill Avenue around 10:30 p.m. The driver, identified as Henry Goodlow, fled from officers, initiating a short vehicle pursuit through residential streets that lasted about four minutes. The chase ended when Goodlow crashed his vehicle near South Creek Lane in the Country Trail Estates area off Airport Highway. After the crash, he exited the vehicle and ran behind nearby homes. According to police, Goodlow then fired multiple shots at pursuing officers, and one officer returned fire; no injuries were reported and all rounds missed. Goodlow was eventually apprehended after a foot pursuit. Authorities reported that he had multiple active warrants at the time of the incident. He was charged with felonious assault on a police officer, failure to comply with a police order, and having weapons while under disability, in addition to other warrant-related offenses.
Charges: Felonious assault on a police officer; failure to comply with order of a police officer; having weapons under disability; plus pre-existing warrants (two counts of strangulation; tampering with evidence)

Title: Convicted felon from Minnesota arrested in Miami Beach after fleeing from officers, police say
description: Police in Miami Beach, Florida attempted a traffic stop on a black Dodge Durango in the 1000 block of Ocean Drive around 4:45 p.m. The driver did not stop and continued southbound, leading officers to initiate a pursuit. During the incident, police used a drone to track the vehicle. Authorities reported that the driver, identified as Jirell Thomas, eventually left the vehicle on the 700 block of Jefferson Avenue and fled on foot. While being monitored by the drone operator, Thomas allegedly threw a black handgun during the escape. Officers were directed to his location and took him into custody. The firearm was later recovered by investigators. Police confirmed Thomas is a convicted felon from Minnesota. No injuries were reported. He was arrested and charged in connection with firearm possession and fleeing law enforcement.
Charges: Possession of a firearm as a convicted felon; eluding/fleeing police; resisting an officer without violence

Title: Driver charged with fleeing deputies in stolen car in St. Paul, hitting State Patrol car in Minneapolis at 80 mph
description: A 19-year-old Minneapolis man, identified as Thailand Taiwan Hawkins, was involved in a police pursuit in Minnesota after allegedly driving a stolen vehicle. Deputies initially attempted to stop the suspect in St. Paul, but he fled at high speed, leading to a multi-agency pursuit that crossed into Minneapolis. During the chase, the stolen vehicle ran a stop sign at high speed and collided with a Minnesota State Patrol squad car at approximately 80 mph. The crash injured a state trooper, who suffered serious injuries including a broken leg and shoulder blade, and also injured two passengers inside the stolen vehicle, one of whom sustained severe injuries including a compound fracture and brain bleed. The suspect fled on foot but was later arrested nearby. Investigators reported that the suspect admitted he found it “fun” to drive stolen vehicles. The case involved multiple agencies, including the Minnesota State Patrol and Ramsey County Sheriff’s Office.
Charges: Criminal vehicular operation (3 counts); receiving stolen property; fleeing police in a motor vehicle

Title: Repeat DWI Offender Charged After Fleeing Ramsey County Deputies
description: Ramsey County deputies in Saint Paul, Minnesota attempted a traffic stop after observing a Mazda CX-7 linked to a registered owner with an active warrant. When officers activated emergency lights and sirens, the driver accelerated and fled, leading deputies on a short pursuit. The vehicle turned into an alley where it lost traction and slid. The driver then exited the vehicle and attempted to run from officers. He fell during the attempt and was taken into custody. Deputies identified him as Anthony Marquiz Henderson. Investigators reported that the vehicle’s license plates did not belong to the Mazda and were improperly registered. Officers also noted signs of alcohol impairment, including a strong odor of alcohol and visible empty beer cans in the vehicle. Henderson was transported to the Ramsey County Law Enforcement Center, where he refused to provide a breath sample despite multiple requests. Authorities stated he admitted he fled because he did not want to return to jail.
Charges: Felony fleeing a peace officer in a motor vehicle; gross misdemeanor test refusal; additional DWI-related charges (including pending third-degree DWI refusal case)

Title: State trooper fired after ramming wrong car in botched PIT maneuver on I-630
description: An Arkansas State Police trooper was fired after mistakenly using a tactical vehicle intervention (PIT maneuver) on an innocent driver during a high-speed pursuit on Interstate 630 in Little Rock. The incident began when trooper J. Fitzgerald stopped a white Buick Envista for speeding 92 mph in a 60 mph zone. The driver, Johnny Williams, was found to have a suspended license and reportedly smelled of marijuana. When the trooper instructed him to exit the vehicle, Williams fled the traffic stop. During the pursuit, the trooper briefly lost sight of the suspect vehicle and mistakenly identified a different white SUV as the fleeing car. He then rammed the wrong vehicle using a PIT maneuver. The driver of that SUV was an uninvolved woman. No injuries were reported. The trooper later realized the mistake, apologized, and was subsequently terminated by Arkansas State Police for the error.
Charges: Felony fleeing Misdemeanor failure to obey police officer Driving on suspended license Speeding over limit

Title: FOX13 Investigates: ASP dashcam video shows pursuit from Memphis into Arkansas
description: Arkansas State Police and Tennessee Highway Patrol conducted a joint pursuit after a driver allegedly fled law enforcement across state lines from the Memphis area into Arkansas. Dashcam video shows troopers attempting multiple Tactical Vehicle Intervention (TVI) maneuvers to stop the vehicle as it traveled at high speed. The chase continued across the Mississippi River into West Memphis, where officers coordinated efforts to end the pursuit safely. The suspect, identified as Terry Grant, reportedly continued driving despite repeated attempts to stop him. The pursuit ended when the vehicle was successfully brought to a halt near an interstate access point. Grant was taken into custody at the scene and transported to jail. Authorities said the pursuit involved multiple agencies and spanned several jurisdictions, highlighting the risks of high-speed cross-state chases. No fatalities were reported in connection with the incident, though officers emphasized the danger posed to the public and law enforcement during the extended pursuit.
Charges: Charges Fleeing (felony) Expired vehicle tags Fictitious license plates

Title: TPD, WCSO locate and arrest Tallahassee carjacking suspect in joint operation
description: On January 31, 2026, a joint operation involving the Tallahassee Police Department and the Wakulla County Sheriff’s Office led to the arrest of Christopher Kentrell Roberts, a suspect in a Tallahassee carjacking case. Authorities reported that Roberts was driving a stolen gray 2014 Acura SUV and was believed to be traveling south on Wakulla Springs Highway. Deputies located him near Inez Lane and attempted a traffic stop, but he allegedly fled at high speed. During the search, deputies found the stolen vehicle abandoned on Patricia Lane with the engine running and the driver’s door open. A perimeter was established, and a K-9 unit was deployed to track the suspect. Investigators later received information that Roberts was hiding at a residence on Raker Lane in Crawfordville. Deputies entered the residence with the homeowner’s consent and located Roberts. He initially provided a false name before admitting his identity and was arrested without incident.
Charges: Carjacking-related charges (specific charges not listed in the article) Providing a false identity to law enforcement

Title: Osceola County man accused of impersonating officer may have more victims
description: Carlos Barros-Villahermosa, a 59-year-old man, was arrested in Osceola County, Florida, after allegedly impersonating a police officer during a traffic stop involving two teenagers. According to investigators, the incident occurred near Buenaventura Boulevard and Osceola Parkway on a Thursday night. Authorities said Barros-Villahermosa activated flashing blue lights installed in his SUV and pulled over an 18-year-old driver. He allegedly displayed a badge, identified himself as a police officer, and requested the driver's license and registration. The teenagers became suspicious and began recording the interaction while also calling 911. They reportedly asked for another officer to respond to the scene. After the encounter, Barros-Villahermosa left the area, but deputies later located and arrested him. During the investigation, deputies found emergency-style lights and a siren installed in his vehicle. He claimed to be a retired police officer from Puerto Rico, but investigators determined that claim was false. Authorities believe there may be additional victims.
Charges: Impersonating a police officer False imprisonment

Title: Man accused of impersonating law enforcement in North Fort Myers fake traffic stop, DUI
description: Martin Portillo-Lopez, 22, was arrested in North Fort Myers, Florida, after allegedly attempting to impersonate a law enforcement officer during a fake traffic stop. According to investigators, a woman noticed a white SUV resembling a retired patrol vehicle following her closely on Pondella Road. The suspect allegedly used his cellphone to display flashing red and blue lights from a YouTube video and played siren sounds to make the vehicle appear to be a police unit. Concerned for her safety, the woman contacted 911 while continuing to drive. Deputies from the Lee County Sheriff’s Office located and stopped the suspect in a parking lot. During the investigation, deputies determined that Portillo-Lopez was allegedly driving under the influence, with a blood alcohol level reported to be nearly twice the legal limit. An open alcoholic beverage was also found inside the vehicle. He was arrested and later released from jail after posting bond.
Charges: Impersonating a law enforcement officer Driving under the influence (DUI)

Title: Bush spurs and sweat helped deputies link two suspects to a Lehigh Acres car chase
description: Deputies in Lee County arrested two suspects after a late-night high-speed pursuit through a Lehigh Acres neighborhood ended with both individuals fleeing on foot and being tracked down by multiple law enforcement units. According to the Lee County Sheriff’s Office, a vehicle was observed speeding near Leonard Boulevard and failed to stop at an intersection, prompting a traffic stop attempt. The driver refused to comply and led deputies on a dangerous chase through residential areas, driving off-road and between homes. Eventually, the driver and passenger abandoned the vehicle and fled into nearby property. Florida Highway Patrol assisted in the search, and deputies deployed K-9 units, drones, and aviation support. The suspects were later found hiding nearby, covered in sweat and vegetation debris, which helped confirm their involvement. Both individuals were taken into custody after being linked to the abandoned vehicle and charged following the pursuit. Prior criminal histories were also noted by investigators.
Charges: Resisting an officer, fleeing and eluding law enforcement

Title: Palm City manhunt ends with suspect in custody after fighting trooper
description: A 60? no 36-year-old Jaime Alberto Silvabernal of Colombia was arrested after a Florida Highway Patrol traffic stop on Interstate 95 in Palm City escalated into a violent confrontation. Troopers stopped a blue Chevrolet Traverse due to an unregistered vehicle and mismatched license plate. When officers attempted to detain him for an outstanding warrant, the suspect resisted as handcuffs were being applied, striking a trooper and breaking free. He then fled on foot into nearby residential and wooded areas along the I-95 corridor. The Martin County Sheriff’s Office, Florida Highway Patrol, and assisting agencies launched a manhunt using aviation, patrol units, and K-9 teams. Deputies later located him hiding in bushes near a fence line. After refusing repeated commands to surrender, a K-9 named Zoli was deployed and apprehended the suspect by biting his arm. He was taken into custody, treated for injuries, and transported to jail after medical clearance. He faces multiple resisting and fleeing-related charges tied to the arrest incident.
Charges: Resisting an officer with violence, fleeing and eluding, outstanding warrant-related charges

Title: Florida man accused of punching, choking K-9 after fleeing deputies
city and state: Palm Beach County (Lake Worth Beach / West Palm Beach area), Florida
description: A 30-year-old man was arrested in Palm Beach County, Florida, after deputies said he fled multiple traffic stop attempts and later violently resisted arrest while attacking a police K-9. According to the Palm Beach County Sheriff’s Office, deputies initially attempted to stop a gray Nissan Altima for traffic violations including improper lane change and a covered license plate. The driver, identified as Diego Alberto Cisneros, briefly slowed but then fled, running red lights and evading officers. He was later located near his residence after a separate surveillance effort. When deputies boxed in his vehicle, Cisneros refused commands to exit and was eventually Tasered after acting aggressively toward officers. During the arrest struggle, deputies reported he struck a K-9 with closed fists and attempted to choke the dog. He was taken into custody after force was used to restrain him and is being held on multiple felony charges.
Charges: Fleeing and eluding, resisting an officer with violence, offenses against a police K-9, unlawful alteration of a license plate, driving without a valid license

Title: Florida woman said ‘she was ready to fight’ moments before punching trooper, kicking ICE officer: arrest report
description: Jennifer Cruz was arrested in Jacksonville, Florida after a traffic stop on Beach Boulevard escalated into a violent confrontation with law enforcement. According to an arrest report, a Florida Highway Patrol trooper initially stopped Cruz for traffic violations including driving with a suspended license and unsafe driving behavior. During the stop, she reportedly became confrontational, followed the trooper into a parking lot, and refused to comply with instructions to provide proper identification and surrender her keys. The situation escalated when Cruz allegedly stated she was “ready to fight” and then punched a trooper in the face with a closed fist, causing injuries. She also resisted arrest by tensing her body and attempting to kick officers, including a trooper and federal agents during the encounter. Officers used a taser in drive-stun mode before placing her in restraints. She was taken into custody and later booked into jail.
Charges: Battery on officer, resisting arrest, driving with suspended license (and multiple related charges totaling 14 counts)

Title: Naples man accused of running from deputies at traffic stop
description: Cornelious Martin, 21, was arrested in Collier County, Florida, after a traffic stop escalated when he fled from deputies and resisted arrest. Deputies had pulled over a vehicle on US-41 at Palm Drive due to careless driving and an unregistered tag. While the driver cooperated, Martin, a passenger in the back seat, opened the door despite being ordered to stay inside. He then exited the vehicle and ran across multiple lanes of traffic on US-41, prompting deputies to chase and tackle him for safety reasons. According to the arrest report, Martin continued to resist while being restrained, tensing his body and refusing to comply with commands. Deputies eventually used force, including a strike to the face, to gain control and complete the arrest. Both Martin and deputies sustained minor injuries during the struggle and were treated and cleared by emergency medical services. Martin was arrested on a charge of resisting an officer without violence and was already on probation at the time of the incident.
Charges: Resisting an officer without violence

Title: Connersville man found hiding in dumpster following Ohio police chase and crash
description: David Morris was the driver of a 2003 Honda Accord stopped by an Ohio State Highway Patrol trooper in Preble County after officers observed unsafe driving behavior, including improper lane changes and following too closely. When the trooper attempted a traffic stop on Interstate 70, Morris initially slowed on the shoulder but then accelerated away, fleeing the stop and initiating a brief pursuit that was later terminated for safety reasons. Shortly after crossing into Indiana near the state line, Morris was involved in a two-vehicle crash on an on-ramp connecting I-70 and U.S. 40. After the crash, he fled the scene on foot. Law enforcement officers from Indiana State Police and the Wayne County Sheriff’s Department tracked footprints in the snow leading to a nearby area. Morris was ultimately located hiding inside a dumpster at a nearby business and taken into custody without further incident. He was arrested on charges related to fleeing police and driving with a suspended license.
Charges: Failure to comply with police officer, operating a vehicle with a suspended license

Title: Man arrested after traffic stop turns into officer involved shooting during dangerous pursuit in North Miami
description: On March 22, 2026, Miami Beach police attempted a traffic stop on a blue Mercedes driven by Tavaris Palacios after noticing illegal window tint. Officers reported that Palacios initially complied but then suddenly fled, driving through Ocean Drive and swerving into a bike lane, creating a public safety risk due to heavy pedestrian traffic. The pursuit continued onto Interstate 95, where authorities say he collided with another vehicle. A Florida Highway Patrol trooper discharged a weapon at the suspect’s vehicle during the chase, though no one was injured by gunfire. The pursuit eventually ended in North Miami after officers used a pit maneuver to stop the car. Palacios was taken into custody at the scene. A passenger in the vehicle was also detained. The incident involved multiple agencies due to the cross-jurisdictional chase and escalating danger to the public during the high-speed flight from law enforcement.
Charges: Fleeing and eluding police, reckless driving, refusing to obey a lawful order of a police officer

Suspect Name: Summer R. Davis, Harold D. Jenkins
Title: Solon police say they arrested a Parma mother on a menacing charge, then arrested the father after he drove drunk to pick up their children
description: Two linked incidents in Solon, Ohio on Dec 28, 2025: Parma mother Summer R. Davis arrested for aggravated menacing after allegedly threatening to shoot a woman at an apartment complex. Her three children were present. Later the children’s father Harold D. Jenkins arrived to pick them up appeared intoxicated and was stopped by police. Officers found loaded firearms in his vehicle including a rifle near a child seat. Jenkins was arrested for OVI child endangering and improper handling of firearms in a vehicle. Children were placed with grandmother and authorities notified child services. No injuries reported during either incident overall.
Charges: Summer R. Davis: Aggravated menacing (misdemeanor) Harold D. Jenkins: OVI, child endangering, improper handling of firearms in a vehicle (felony), additional traffic-related violations

Title: Cincinnati man arrested, charged with 10th OVI, troopers say
description: Ohio State Highway Patrol arrested Timothy Lyles after troopers observed multiple traffic violations, including running a red light and lane violations in Cincinnati. During the stop, officers reported signs of impairment, leading to his arrest for operating a vehicle under the influence (OVI). Authorities said this was Lyles’ tenth OVI offense, including prior felony convictions, making him a repeat offender with a long history of impaired driving. He was also charged with additional traffic-related violations and taken to the Hamilton County Justice Center. The case highlights ongoing concerns about repeat DUI/OVI offenders and road safety risks posed by impaired driving behavior.
Charges: 10th OVI (Operating Vehicle Impaired), second felony OVI, failure to obey traffic signals, OVI suspension violation, open container

Title: Stamps, Ark. police trainee arrested for allegedly trying to pull someone over in Magnolia
description: On March 22, 2026, a motorist reported that a woman driving a white Lexus with flashing blue lights attempted to pull them over in Magnolia, Arkansas. The victim believed the vehicle was not a legitimate police car because it lacked police markings and feared for their safety. Police said the suspect pursued the victim while the victim remained on the phone with law enforcement. The chase ended at the Columbia County Sheriff’s Office, where Magnolia Police took over. Investigators identified the suspect as Jacqulyn Curry, also known as Jacqulyn Willis, a police trainee with the Stamps Police Department who had not completed law enforcement certification.
Charges: Aggravated Assault Disorderly Conduct Violation of Blue Light Statute No Proof of Liability Insurance

Title: Police: 70-year-old woman arrested for DWI while driving Springdale students on school bus
description: Dawn Russell, a 70-year-old school bus driver, was arrested on March 4, 2026, after allegedly operating a school bus while intoxicated in Springdale, Arkansas. According to police, Russell was transporting approximately 53 students when she turned too wide at the intersection of Holcomb Street and Meadow Avenue, striking a utility pole and a tree. Authorities later determined that she had transported about 150 students earlier that morning. No injuries were reported among the children. Officers located Russell and the bus at the school district’s bus lot following the incident. During their investigation, police observed signs of impairment, including bloodshot and watery eyes, slurred speech, and the odor of alcohol. Field sobriety tests reportedly indicated intoxication, and a subsequent blood alcohol content test showed a BAC of 0.08. The crash caused significant property damage estimated at approximately $30,000, including damage requiring replacement of a utility pole.
Charges: Driving While Intoxicated (DWI)  Second-Degree Endangering the Welfare of a Minor  Criminal Mischief (Damage Over $25,000)  Leaving the Scene of an Accident Involving Property Damage  Careless and Prohibited Driving

Title: 62-Year-Old Arrested on DWI, Child Endangerment Counts After Traffic Stop Near Paragould, Affidavit Says
description: Police in Paragould, Arkansas, arrested Michael D. Orr after responding to a traffic complaint involving a vehicle reportedly driving into oncoming traffic. Officers located the vehicle and observed signs of impairment including bloodshot eyes, slurred speech, and alcohol odor. A 6-year-old child was present in the back seat of the vehicle. Authorities reported the vehicle was still in drive and the suspect initially refused commands to shift into park and exit. After field sobriety testing, Orr was arrested. A breath test later showed a blood alcohol level of 0.18. He was charged with DWI and child endangerment-related offenses.
Charges: First-degree endangering the welfare of a minor, DWI (second offense), obstructing governmental operations, possession of an open container in a vehicle

Title: Liberty traffic stop turns into high speed chase
description: John Buoy, a 49-year-old man from Youngstown, Ohio, was involved in a traffic stop in Liberty that escalated into a high-speed police pursuit. Officers initially stopped Buoy for a red light violation on Belmont Avenue near the Interstate 80 westbound ramp. During the stop, Buoy argued with the officer and disputed the circumstances of the traffic violation. After the officer returned to his vehicle to issue a citation, Buoy allegedly raised his window and fled the scene in his car, entering I-80 at high speed. Police reported that the pursuit reached speeds between 80 and 100 miles per hour and involved dangerous driving behavior, including cutting off other vehicles. The chase was eventually terminated due to weather and traffic conditions. Later, Buoy was located and detained at his residence with assistance from Austintown police and transferred to Liberty officers for custody. He was charged and scheduled to appear in court for the incident.
Charges: Failure to comply with police officer’s order or signal; obstructing official business

Title: Two arrested after police chase from southwest Willmar to Pennock
description: Police in Willmar, Minnesota responded to a reported shoplifting incident at a hardware store, where suspects were seen leaving in a gray Mazda. Officers located the vehicle and attempted a traffic stop, but the driver fled, leading to a pursuit westbound on Highway 40. The vehicle eventually stopped, and the male driver exited and fled on foot while a second suspect took over driving duties. The pursuit continued into Pennock, Minnesota, where the fleeing vehicle struck another car. Law enforcement, including Willmar Police and Kandiyohi County Sheriff’s Office, established a perimeter and used a drone and K-9 unit to search for the suspects. Both individuals were eventually located and arrested without incident. No injuries were reported, though both the suspect vehicle and another civilian vehicle sustained damage during the chase.
Charges: Shoplifting; fleeing police in a motor vehicle; traffic-related offenses (specific formal charges not fully listed at time of report)

Suspect Name: Rep. Elliott Engen, Rep. Walter Hudson
Title: Behavior of two Minnesota lawmakers called into question following DWI arrest
description: Minnesota House Representatives Elliott Engen and Walter Hudson came under review after a March 26, 2026 traffic stop in White Bear Lake, Minnesota. Engen was arrested on suspicion of driving while intoxicated and later charged with misdemeanor DWI after registering a 0.13 BAC. Hudson was a passenger in the vehicle and told police that one of the alcohol bottles belonged to him. He also had a legally carried firearm, though Minnesota law prohibits carrying a weapon with a BAC above 0.04. Neither was initially charged beyond Engen’s DWI. The incident prompted political scrutiny and internal legislative review of their conduct.
Charges: Rep. Elliott Engen: misdemeanor DWI Rep. Walter Hudson: no charges filed

Title: Rochester Man Charged for High Speed Chase That Ended With Squad Car Crashes
description: A 21-year-old Rochester man, Abdikadir Said Mohamed, was arrested after a high-speed police chase that ended in a crash involving a Rochester Police Department squad vehicle. Officers initially found him slumped in a parked car early Saturday morning. After attempting a traffic stop, Mohamed fled at speeds exceeding 90 mph, ran red lights, and nearly struck other vehicles. The pursuit ended when police later located the disabled vehicle, which then struck two squad cars and other property before his arrest. Officers reported signs of alcohol use and found an open bottle in the vehicle. A blood test was collected for analysis.
Charges: Fleeing police (felony), DWI, driving after revocation, open bottle violation (misdemeanor)

Title: Suspect arrested after running from traffic stop, hiding in garage
description: Police in Miamisburg, Ohio attempted to stop a red Chrysler 300 driven by Devion Jackson, but the driver refused to comply and fled, prompting officers to initially disengage from the pursuit. Shortly after, the vehicle crashed in the 700 block of East Pearl Street. Jackson exited the vehicle and ran into a nearby residential neighborhood. Officers established a search perimeter as residents reported sightings. During the search, a neighbor informed police that Jackson was hiding inside a garage. Officers located him there and attempted to take him into custody, but he fled again from the garage. Law enforcement then deployed a Taser to subdue him, successfully taking him into custody. Authorities also reported multiple incidents of vehicle and property damage believed to be connected to Jackson’s driving prior to and during the pursuit. No serious injuries to officers or civilians were reported in the incident.
Charges: Failure to comply with order or signal of a police officer Breaking and entering

Title: Tri-State suspect tracked down after fleeing traffic stop for alleged extreme speeding
description: Whesley Wynn was the driver of a vehicle stopped by Ross Township police after officers observed him allegedly traveling at more than 90 mph in a 45-mph zone. During the traffic stop, officers ordered Wynn to exit the vehicle multiple times. Body camera footage showed Wynn refusing commands and arguing with officers as they attempted to detain him. Wynn told officers he intended to start the car despite instructions to remain still. Officers warned him that continued refusal could result in arrest. Wynn then fled the scene in his vehicle, initiating a brief pursuit. Police reported that he drove at speeds exceeding 100 mph and placed other motorists at risk, including driving in the opposite lane. Officers terminated the pursuit due to safety concerns. The next day, investigators located Wynn with assistance from the United States Marshals Service. He was arrested without further incident. The case escalated from a traffic stop into felony charges due to fleeing and reckless driving behavior.
Charges: Failure to comply, obstructing police, speeding, reckless operation

Title: Chillicothe Man Arrested After Struggle With Officers During Traffic Stop
description: Police observed a black Honda Pilot driving erratically in Chillicothe, Ohio, drifting around corners and nearly striking a parked vehicle. Officers initiated a traffic stop in a nearby parking lot. The driver, Christopher James Radachi, exited the vehicle immediately and began arguing with the officer instead of complying. Despite repeated commands to return to the vehicle, he refused and re-entered the driver’s seat. When officers attempted to detain him, he resisted arrest, resulting in a physical struggle. One officer was able to secure a single handcuff before Radachi actively resisted further restraint. A second officer arrived to assist, and additional force was used to gain control after Radachi continued resisting and kept his hands under his body. The confrontation escalated into a prolonged struggle before officers subdued him. Radachi was later treated at a medical facility for injuries sustained during the arrest. Two officers also suffered minor injuries during the incident.
Charges: Resisting arrest Reckless operation on a public street

Title: Bryant Police Sergeant arrested for DWI after driving wrong direction; Terminated following incident
description: Bryant Police Department Sergeant Brett Carpenter was arrested after a traffic incident in which he was observed driving a Ford F-150 on the wrong side of the road along Interstate 30 North Service Road near Benton in Saline County. A Saline County Sheriff’s deputy conducted a traffic stop after witnessing the vehicle traveling westbound in an eastbound lane. Upon contact, Carpenter appeared confused, unsteady on his feet, and emitted a strong odor of alcohol. He admitted to drinking “a couple of beers” but refused to complete standardized field sobriety tests, including the horizontal gaze nystagmus, walk-and-turn, one-leg stand, and a preliminary breath test. At the detention center, a breath test indicated a blood alcohol concentration of 0.22, nearly three times the legal limit. Three firearms were later discovered in his vehicle during inventory. He was taken into custody, charged, and subsequently terminated from his employment with the Bryant Police Department the following day.
Charges: DWI (First Offense), Driving Left of Center

Title: Palm Coast Woman Arrested for DUI After Hitting Multiple Vehicles and Fleeing
description: Marina Brandon, a 25-year-old woman from Palm Coast, Florida, was arrested after deputies responded to multiple reports of a hit-and-run crash involving several vehicles. According to the Flagler County Sheriff’s Office, witnesses reported a black Toyota Tacoma striking multiple cars before fleeing the scene. Deputies later located the damaged vehicle parked near Ulaturn Trail and Seminole Woods Boulevard. When officers made contact with Brandon, she appeared disheveled, was partially clothed, smelled strongly of alcohol, and had difficulty speaking clearly. She also struggled to maintain her balance and was unable to complete most standardized field sobriety tests. Following her arrest, a breath test showed a blood alcohol concentration of 0.250, more than three times the legal limit in Florida. She was charged with DUI involving property damage, leaving the scene of a crash, and operating a motor vehicle without a valid license. She was later released after posting bond.
Charges: DUI with property damage, Leaving the scene of a crash involving property damage, Operating a motor vehicle without a valid license

Title: Lehigh Acres woman accused of probation violation following third DUI arrest
description: D’nahzai Fletcher, a 26-year-old woman from Lehigh Acres, Florida, was accused of violating probation following a DUI-related traffic stop that led to her arrest and renewed legal issues. According to Southwest Florida Crime Stoppers, Fletcher was pulled over after showing signs of impairment while driving. During the stop, officers reported that she failed field sobriety tests and later registered a breath alcohol level nearly three times the legal limit. Authorities stated that she was already on probation for a prior DUI offense and did not have a valid driver’s license at the time of the incident. Investigators also noted that she had failed to comply with court-ordered drug treatment requirements, which contributed to the probation violation. The case escalated due to repeated DUI behavior and noncompliance with legal conditions. Fletcher’s current status includes being wanted for probation violation related to impaired driving and prior alcohol-related offenses.
Charges: DUI, Probation violation, Driving without valid license

Title: Man Arrested For Impersonating Law Enforcement
description: On January 7, 2026, deputies with the Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office responded to a report from the Pasco County Sheriff’s Office regarding a suspicious black Chevrolet Equinox equipped with red and blue emergency-style lights. Authorities said the vehicle was being used in a manner that caused at least one driver to believe they were being pulled over by law enforcement and to stop their vehicle. Deputies located the SUV later that day in the area of Dale Mabry Highway and Ehrlich Road in Hillsborough County and conducted a traffic stop. The driver, identified as 28-year-old Gamal Said, admitted to activating the lights while driving. He stated he did so in order to get to work faster. Investigators determined the conduct constituted impersonation of law enforcement and improper use of emergency lighting equipment. Said was taken into custody without incident and the investigation remained active following his arrest. No injuries were reported during the incident.
Charges: Unlawful use of blue lights; impersonating a public officer; two out-of-county warrants (probation violation related to burglary of an unoccupied structure)

Title: Port St. Lucie police arrest sparks expert warning on avoiding fake officer traffic stops
description: Daniel Beyzer, a 38-year-old man in Port St. Lucie, was arrested after allegedly impersonating a law enforcement officer and conducting an illegal traffic stop on a black Jeep. Police say Beyzer activated fake emergency-style white lights and pulled the vehicle over while identifying himself as an officer. A passenger in the Jeep became suspicious and called 911, prompting real police response and his arrest. Investigators reported finding several items in his vehicle including a concealed carry badge, handcuffs, a loaded firearm, and an open container of alcohol. Beyzer claimed he worked for the Federal Aviation Administration and used the lights for runway purposes, and said he previously worked as a bounty hunter. Officers determined he had a blood alcohol content of 0.15, nearly twice the legal limit. Authorities emphasized the dangers of fake traffic stops and advised drivers to contact 911 and move to well-lit areas if they suspect impersonation incidents occurring
Charges: Impersonating a law enforcement officer; driving under the influence (DUI)

Title: WATCH: Flagler County K-9 tracks, bites suspect after high-speed chase in stolen vehicle
description: A 33-year-old man, James Myers of DeLand, Florida, was arrested after a violent police pursuit involving a stolen vehicle in Flagler County. Around 2 a.m., a deputy attempted a traffic stop after locating a reported stolen truck near Mahogany Boulevard. The driver had already been observed running stop signs and driving at approximately 92 mph in a 30 mph zone. When the deputy initiated the stop, the driver refused to pull over and accelerated, leading to a high-speed chase. The pursuit ended when the truck crashed into a ditch near the roadway. Myers and a passenger fled on foot after the crash, and deputies temporarily lost sight of them. A K-9 unit later located Myers hiding under a home on Cheryl Elaine Drive. He was apprehended after being bitten by a K-9 and taken into custody. He was later held without bond at the Flagler County Inmate Detention Facility.
Charges: Grand theft of a motor vehicle; Fleeing and eluding; Driving while license is suspended; Resisting arrest without violence; Dangerous excessive speeding; Reckless driving

Title: Tri-State officer hurt when fleeing suspect hits cruiser: Police
description: On Tuesday in Goshen Township, Ohio, officers responded to a reported assault at MeadowView Townhomes. Following the incident, 32-year-old Keon Humphries stole the victim’s vehicle and fled the area. Officers later located Humphries and the stolen vehicle near State Route 28 and Deerfield Road, but when they attempted a traffic stop, he fled, colliding with two civilian vehicles and a police cruiser at the intersection of State Route 28 and Branch Hill–Guinea Pike. Humphries then abandoned the vehicle and attempted to escape on foot before being apprehended after a foot chase. One officer sustained minor injuries during the pursuit, while no other injuries were reported. Humphries is facing multiple charges, including felonious assault, fleeing and eluding, grand theft auto, and domestic violence, with additional charges pending. He was held overnight without bond at the Clermont County Jail and is scheduled for his first court appearance. The incident underscores the dangers posed to both civilians and officers when suspects flee law enforcement.
Charges: Felonious assault, fleeing and eluding, grand theft auto, domestic violence (additional charges pending)

Title: Delray Beach man arrested after shooting at officers serving warrant
description: A Delray Beach man was arrested after a violent standoff with police during the execution of multiple warrants at his home. Officers were attempting to serve an arrest warrant, search warrant, and DNA warrant on Evan Berkowitz, 56, when he allegedly barricaded himself inside his residence. According to police, Berkowitz fired shots at officers outside the home during the standoff, which extended into the afternoon. A SWAT team established a perimeter and used a tactical vehicle to breach the residence after Berkowitz continued firing, including shots directed at the vehicle. He eventually surrendered and was taken into custody. Authorities confirmed that no officers were injured during the incident. Police also noted that Berkowitz had previously fled from an attempted traffic stop the week before. He now faces charges including aggravated fleeing and eluding, reckless driving, and additional charges related to the armed confrontation with law enforcement.
Charges: Aggravated fleeing and eluding Reckless driving Additional weapons/assault-related charges pending

Title: Lady Lake Police arrest man after fleeing traffic stop attempt
description: On March 29, 2026, Lady Lake police attempted a traffic stop on a white Chevrolet Suburban after a license plate reader indicated the vehicle’s owner, Bradley Seymour, 51, had active warrants. Seymour refused to stop, leading officers on a reckless pursuit through multiple streets, private property, and a hotel parking lot. During the chase, tire deflation devices deployed by Lake County deputies struck the vehicle, causing a tire to fly off and leaving a burnt rubber smell. The vehicle eventually slowed near 625 First Ave., where Seymour exited and ran but was apprehended near a fence line without further incident. He was taken to a hospital for evaluation before being transported to the Lake County Jail. Seymour was charged with fleeing with disregard for public safety, reckless driving, and resisting an officer without violence. Authorities praised the use of technology and teamwork in the arrest.
Charges: Fleeing with disregard for public safety, reckless driving, resisting an officer without violence

Title: Suspect dubbed 'Oscar the Grouch' caught hiding in trash can; officer arrests after chase
description: Police in Huber Heights, Ohio initiated a traffic stop involving a 27-year-old driver later identified as Jonathan McMillan on Monday. According to authorities, McMillan exited his vehicle and immediately fled on foot, prompting officers to establish a perimeter and begin a search. During the search, dash camera footage captured a sanitation worker opening a trash bin and discovering the suspect hiding inside. As police units arrived, McMillan emerged from the trash can and attempted to run again, but officers quickly pursued him through nearby apartment areas. The department later nicknamed him “Oscar the Grouch” after the unusual hiding attempt. Officers reported that Officer Perez successfully caught and arrested the suspect after a short chase. McMillan was transported to the Montgomery County Jail. Police confirmed he also had an outstanding warrant from Miami County. The initial traffic violation was resolved with a warning, and no injuries were reported during the incident.
Charges: Obstructing official business; resisting arrest

Title: Orange Park woman’s family alleges excessive force during Jacksonville traffic stop; JSO says arrest was within policy
description: Tiara Young, 34, was stopped by officers in Jacksonville, Florida, while making a DoorDash delivery because her vehicle's taillights were not illuminated. According to the arrest report, officers said Young partially lowered her window, questioned commands, and failed to provide identification when requested. Police ordered her out of the vehicle and later attempted to place her in custody after she allegedly failed to comply with commands. Young and her family claim officers used excessive force during the arrest, causing injuries to her eye and scalp. The Jacksonville Sheriff's Office reviewed the incident and determined the officers acted within policy.
Charges: Resisting an officer without violence

description: Jermell Williams, 22, of Campbell, Ohio, was arrested following a traffic stop in Warren after officers observed multiple traffic violations including improper signaling and failure to yield. During the stop, officers noted Williams was wearing heavy clothing in warm weather and believed he may be concealing a weapon. Title: Turo-Rented Porsche Cayenne Allegedly Hit 170 MPH While Fleeing Arkansas State Trooper

During the stop, he reportedly became noncompliant and fled, leading to a high-speed pursuit that reached approximately 170 mph before officers discontinued the chase for safety reasons. Hours later on December 19, 2025, deputies in Hot Spring County observed Burton exit the same vehicle and enter another car. A felony stop was conducted, and both occupants were detained without incident. Burton was taken into custody and later charged with multiple offenses including felony fleeing, reckless driving, and excessive speeding by Arkansas State Police and local deputies during coordinated enforcement response operation.

Witnesses reported hearing the crash from nearby homes. Emergency responders arrived at the scene, and both the suspect’s vehicle and the deputy’s vehicle were later towed away. Lee was transported to a hospital for treatment following the crash. After receiving medical attention, he was taken into custody and booked into the Turner Guilford Knight Correctional Center. Authorities reported that he faces several charges related to the pursuit, crash, and alleged traffic violations. He was scheduled to appear before a judge following his arrest.

Title: South Side chase leads to 8 felony charges

The driver, later identified as Raheem Satterthwaite, allegedly provided false identification and was observed with a firearm magazine inside the vehicle. When officers ordered him out, he fled, leading to a high-speed pursuit into Boardman and surrounding roads. The chase ended when the vehicle was disabled after losing tires. The suspect fled on foot carrying a package and was reportedly armed. Officers, assisted by a police dog, attempted to detain him as he resisted arrest, struggled with officers, and reached for a weapon. During the confrontation, he bit an officer’s thumb, and stun guns were deployed multiple times before he was subdued. Three firearms were later recovered along his escape route. He was taken to hospital and arraigned on multiple felony charges.

He allegedly behaved erratically, handled an unknown object, and attempted to give instructions to a DUI suspect, disrupting police activity. The chase continued until Williams lost control of the vehicle near the Pollard Harris / Bonifay Gritney Road intersection, where he left the roadway and crashed into several trees in a residential yard. Title: Cable woman charged with OVI on Memorial Day
description: Priscilla Gregg, 42, of Cable, Ohio, was stopped by Urbana Police after officers observed her black Chevy truck crossing left of center on Miami Street. During the traffic stop, Gregg reportedly admitted she had consumed an alcoholic beverage before driving and showed signs of impairment during standardized field sobriety tests, including balance issues and difficulty following instructions. Officers also reported finding multiple alcoholic beverages and drug-related paraphernalia in the vehicle, including a glass pipe with residue and suspected controlled substance tabs. A passenger in the vehicle was taken into custody on active warrants. A dog in the vehicle was removed and taken to a shelter.
Charges: Operating a vehicle under the influence (OVI); marked lane violations

Title: Teen facing DUI charge, accused of hitting motorcycle, home in Lake County
description: An 18-year-old driver was arrested in Clermont after deputies say she drove under the influence and caused a chain of crashes involving a motorcycle and a residential home. Law enforcement reports indicate she was first seen by a deputy responding to complaints of a reckless driver and later observed running a red light. A deputy attempted to initiate a traffic stop, but the driver fled into a neighborhood. Shortly afterward, she allegedly struck a motorcycle and then crashed into a house before attempting to flee on foot. She admitted to drinking alcoholic beverages while driving and failed field sobriety and breath tests.
Charges: DUI (Driving Under the Influence) Fleeing and Eluding Law Enforcement

Title: MCSO: Woman threatened to kill deputy, assaulted detention officer following pursuit in Marathon
description: A 55-year-old woman from St. Cloud was arrested in Marathon after deputies say she led Monroe County Sheriff’s Office deputies on a high-speed chase along U.S. 1. According to reports, her vehicle was clocked at more than 80 mph in a 35 mph zone. She allegedly attempted to evade law enforcement before stopping near a residential area, where she was taken into custody. Authorities further report that after being arrested and transported to jail, she became violent, threatened to kill a deputy, and later kicked a detention officer in the stomach during processing at the detention facility.
Charges: Fleeing and eluding law enforcement Battery on a law enforcement officer Threatening a law enforcement officer

Title: Driver arrested for OVI Thursday night on State Route 117
description: A 40-year-old woman from Waynesfield was arrested after a traffic stop on State Route 117 near State Route 273 in Logan County. Deputies observed her vehicle had only one working headlight and was crossing the fog line. During the stop, Angelica Johnson showed multiple signs of intoxication and admitted to drinking three 12-ounce beers earlier that evening at a bar in Belle Center. She refused to perform field sobriety tests. At the Logan County Jail, her breath test revealed a BAC of 0.189, more than twice the legal limit. She was cited and released to a sober driver.
Charges: Operating a vehicle under the influence (OVI) Failure to drive within marked lanes

Title: Til Arrest Do Us Part: Wife Booked for DUI, Husband Picks Fight with Police
description: During a DUI traffic stop in Coral Springs, officers arrested Felicia Zuniga for impaired driving. Her husband, Alex Roberto Zuniga, remained at the scene and became increasingly aggressive. Police reported he was visibly intoxicated, slurring his speech, and refusing to comply with commands. Alex directed insults and threats at officers, advancing toward them despite warnings. When he stepped toward an officer, deputies used force to subdue him, resulting in a brief struggle before he was handcuffed. Alex was medically cleared at Broward Health Coral Springs and booked into the Broward County Jail. Felicia was separately charged for DUI.
Charges: Assault on a law enforcement officer Corruption by threat against a public servant Resisting an officer without violence

Title: Reckless driver arrested after high speed endangers fellow motorists
description: Chelsea Alonzo, 37, of Summerfield, was stopped by Lady Lake police after driving a red Ram pickup at 75 mph in a 45 mph zone on U.S. Hwy. 27, aggressively changing lanes, and cutting off other vehicles. Officers deemed her behavior reckless and dangerous to other motorists. A check revealed her driver’s license had been suspended in December for unpaid traffic tickets. During the traffic stop, she was arrested for reckless driving and driving with a suspended license, and issued a citation for speeding over 30 mph. She was booked at Lake County Jail and released on $1,000 bond.
Charges: Reckless driving Driving while license suspended Unlawful speeding by 30+ mph

Title: Three sisters wind up in jail after ruckus with police in Fruitland Park
description: Three Leesburg sisters were arrested following a traffic stop in Fruitland Park. Officers initially stopped Dena Tasha Hyppolite for driving with a suspended license and expired registration. Her sisters, Chelsea Shakenna Hyppolite and Joely Joseph, arrived to assist but became combative with law enforcement. Chelsea repeatedly refused to back away, while Joely resisted handcuffing and struck an officer. Officers had to use force to restrain both women. Dena was charged with driving while license suspended, Chelsea with obstructing law enforcement and resisting arrest, and Joely with obstructing law enforcement, resisting arrest, and battery on a law enforcement officer. All were released on bond.
Charges: Dena Tasha Hyppolite: Driving while license suspended or revoked (third offense) Chelsea Shakenna Hyppolite: Obstructing law enforcement, resisting arrest Joely Joseph: Obstructing law enforcement, resisting arrest, battery on law enforcement officer

Title: Driver with canceled license calls 911 to speak with supervisor during traffic stop at Walmart
description: Robin Elizabeth Miller, 35, of Tampa was arrested after a traffic stop at a Walmart in Bushnell. A deputy observed her driving a black sedan in the fast lane at 70 mph despite having a canceled license. Miller became argumentative, refused to exit her vehicle, and called 911 to speak with a supervisor. She resisted the deputy physically by rolling up her window onto his forearm. Backup units arrived, allowing the officer to remove her from the vehicle. Miller was charged with misuse of 911 services, driving while license canceled, battery on officer, and resisting an officer without violence, then posted $4,000 bond.
Charges: Driving while license canceled Misuse of 911 services Battery on officer Resist officer (obstruct without violence)

Title: Urine Trouble: Police Say DUI Suspect Urinated in Patrol Car, Flooded Margate Jail Cell Toilet With T-Shirt
description: Shakeita Latrise Brunson, 42, of Coral Springs was arrested on February 25 after a traffic stop in Margate for making an improper turn. Officers detected alcohol, and Brunson performed poorly on a roadside sobriety test, leading to a DUI arrest. While being transported, she urinated in the patrol car and later clogged a holding cell toilet with her T-shirt, flooding the cell and spreading urine throughout. The biohazard situation required professional cleanup. Brunson was charged with DUI, refusal to submit to DUI testing, and criminal mischief, in addition to the traffic violation, and was released on a $1,150 bond.
Charges: DUI Refusal to submit to DUI testing Criminal mischief Improper turn (traffic citation)

Title: Woman accused of driving away from Collier County deputies during traffic stop
description: Ashlie Soto, 33, was arrested in Collier County after deputies conducted a traffic stop on US-41 for a vehicle operating with only the front headlight illuminated. During the stop, deputies reported smelling marijuana and noted Soto appeared fearful and paranoid. After additional deputies arrived on scene, Soto allegedly fled the traffic stop in her vehicle, prompting a pursuit. Deputies later used a PIT maneuver to bring the vehicle to a stop. A search of the vehicle reportedly uncovered a green leafy substance suspected to be THC. Soto was taken into custody and charged following the pursuit incident.
Charges: Resisting an officer without violence Fleeing and eluding law enforcement

Title: Deputy catches suspected drunk driver who nearly fell down during sobriety exercises
description: Armi Locke Turner, 73, of Ocala was arrested in Lake Panasoffkee after a deputy observed her driving recklessly, including failing to stay in her lane, striking a curb, and nearly hitting a street sign. During the traffic stop, Turner showed clear signs of impairment, including watery eyes, slurred speech, and the odor of alcohol. She initially refused field sobriety exercises but later attempted them, nearly falling multiple times and requiring the deputy to prevent her from hitting the ground. Due to safety concerns, testing was stopped. Turner later refused a breath test and was arrested for DUI and refusal to test.
Charges: Driving under the influence (DUI) Refusal to submit to DUI testing

Title: Woman on pre-trial release charged with fleeing from officer after driving away with parking boot
description: Tia Misel Cooks, 32, was arrested in Gainesville after allegedly driving away with a parking boot attached to her vehicle, damaging it in the process. Police say a tow truck operator initially booted her Toyota Corolla for being parked in a tow-away zone. Cooks then allegedly fled the area, prompting officers to attempt a traffic stop, which she did not immediately obey. She was later located after multiple reports of reckless driving, including speeding and crossing a double yellow line. Cooks admitted she fled because she believed she did not need to stop. She was arrested for fleeing and property damage.
Charges: Fleeing or attempting to elude a police officer Misdemeanor property damage

Title: Elyria Police chase ends in arrest of armed carjacking suspect
description: Desmond Lewis, 28, of Elyria, Ohio, was arrested after leading police on a chase connected to an armed carjacking. The carjacking occurred the previous evening near Lorain Boulevard, where Lewis allegedly flashed a gun and stole a vehicle. Elyria Police located the stolen car the following morning near West Avenue and Oberlin Road and attempted a traffic stop. Lewis fled, traveling south on State Route 301 and entering the eastbound ramp to U.S. Route 20, before turning westbound in the eastbound lanes. The vehicle experienced apparent engine failure, stopping in U.S. Route 20 lanes. A high-risk traffic stop was initiated, and Lewis initially refused commands, requiring 30 minutes of negotiation before surrendering. Lewis has a history of violent offenses involving firearms. He was taken into custody without injuries to anyone and faces multiple charges including receiving stolen property, failure to comply, obstructing official business, and operation in willful or wanton disregard of safety.
Charges: Receiving Stolen Property (Vehicle) – Felony 4, Failure to Comply with a Lawful Order – Felony 4, Obstructing Official Business – Felony 5, Operation in willful or wanton disregard of the safety of persons or property – Misdemeanor 4

Title: Sheriff: Man fled from police
description: Jeffrey L. Clemens, 63, of Huron Township, Ohio, was arrested after leading police on a pursuit that began following a traffic stop in Berlin Heights. Clemens fled northbound on Ohio 61 to Ohio 2, maneuvering through multiple roads including Rye Beach Road, U.S. 6, Center Street, and Bogart Road, apparently attempting to return home. Erie County deputies followed him cautiously without lights or sirens. A spike strip was deployed at Bogart and Camp roads, puncturing both driver-side tires of Clemens’ Chevy SUV, but he continued driving to his garage. Deputies entered the garage and arrested him after he resisted. He faced a fourth-degree felony for failure to comply, plus three misdemeanors: obstructing official business, resisting arrest, and reckless operation. Clemens also had an outstanding warrant from Ottawa County. During the chase, officials noted that he drove at reasonable speeds and observed traffic devices, and his SUV was towed following the arrest.
Charges: Failure to comply (4th-degree felony) Obstructing official business (misdemeanor) Resisting arrest (misdemeanor) Reckless operation (misdemeanor) Outstanding warrant (Ottawa County)

Title: Sheriff: Woman fled from traffic stop
description: On January 5, 2026, Stormie S. Chinn, 46, of Vermilion Township, Ohio, was arrested after allegedly fleeing from two separate traffic stops on U.S. 6. The first stop occurred around 11:30 a.m. when an Erie County sheriff’s deputy observed her driving nearly 30 mph over the speed limit. While the deputy explained the speeding citation, Chinn reportedly rolled up her window and fled, kicking up debris. A second traffic stop was initiated near Volunteer Bay, and despite being informed she was not free to leave, Chinn fled again, traveling between 65 and 75 mph in a 50 mph zone for approximately a mile. She eventually turned onto Poorman Road and parked. The deputy ordered her out of the vehicle at gunpoint. Chinn was unarmed, made vulgar comments, and was arrested. She faces one felony count of failure to comply with an officer and three misdemeanors: improper starting, reckless operation, and speeding. She is held in Erie County Jail on a no-bond order.
Charges: Failure to comply with an order or signal of a police officer (felony); improper starting, reckless operation, speeding (misdemeanors)

Title: Man on pre-trial release arrested for pushing his way into his previous victim’s apartment
description: Nathan John Zudoffsky, 41, was arrested after allegedly violating a court order by entering the apartment of the victim in his pending domestic battery case. He had previously been arrested for domestic battery and released on his own recognizance with a strict no-contact order issued by the court. Despite this, he allegedly went to the victim’s residence wearing dark clothing and a mask, knocked on the door, and forced his way inside after the victim answered. The victim reported that he attempted to hug and kiss her while she repeatedly told him to leave. Deputies later located him nearby and detained him following a traffic stop. Post-Miranda, he did not verbally respond to questioning. He was charged with burglary with battery and violation of pre-trial release conditions. The court later ordered him held without bail pending trial due to the seriousness of the violation and prior domestic case.
Charges: Burglary with battery, violation of pre-trial release conditions

Title: Deputy pulls car over, finds 16-year-old girl who has been missing for a month
description: A 16-year-old girl reported missing from North Carolina was found during a traffic stop in Putnam County, Florida. Deputies stopped a speeding vehicle on U.S. Highway 17 near Crescent City and discovered the teen passenger inside. The driver, identified as Joshua Magraff, initially told law enforcement the girl was his cousin, but the teen later said she was 12 before correcting her identity and confirming her real name. Investigators learned she had been missing for about a month. Magraff later changed his story, claiming she was a friend and saying he believed she was 19. A search of the vehicle revealed counterfeit $100 bills, synthetic marijuana, and drug paraphernalia. The teen’s mother confirmed she did not know Magraff. The girl was taken into protective custody by the Department of Children and Families and arranged for reunification with her family. Magraff was arrested on multiple charges including interference with child custody and drug-related offenses.
Charges: Interference in child custody, possession of counterfeit currency, contributing to the delinquency of a minor

Title: Olympian Sha’Carri Richardson pleads not guilty to excessive speeding charge
description: Sha’Carri Richardson, a 25-year-old Olympic sprinter, was arrested in Orange County, Florida, after being accused of driving at 104 mph in a 65-mph speed zone. According to the arrest affidavit, she was allegedly weaving through traffic, making unsafe lane changes, and flashing her lights at other drivers in an attempt to get them to move out of her way. During the traffic stop, body camera footage captured Richardson apologizing to the deputy and stating she did not realize how fast she was driving, also mentioning a possible mechanical issue with her vehicle. Authorities charged her under a Florida law that criminalizes driving over 100 mph in a manner considered dangerous to others. The case is categorized as “excessive speeding” with criminal implications due to the high speed and alleged reckless behavior. Richardson later pleaded not guilty to the charge and is awaiting further legal proceedings in court.
Charges: Excessive speeding (driving over 100 mph in a dangerous manner under Florida law)

Title: Man arrested for punching trooper during I-95 traffic stop, FHP says
description: On May 12, 2026, an 18-year-old man identified as Luis Angel Gomez Lopez was arrested following a traffic stop on Interstate 95 in Brevard County, Florida. A Florida Highway Patrol trooper observed a white Ford Transit van driving erratically, weaving in the center lane, and nearly colliding with a semi-truck. After the stop was initiated, seven occupants reportedly fled from the passenger side of the van into nearby wooded areas. Gomez Lopez attempted to escape on foot despite repeated commands from law enforcement to stop. During the struggle with officers, a Taser was deployed twice, and both the suspect and trooper went down an embankment. The suspect then allegedly punched the trooper in the face while resisting arrest. Multiple agencies, including county sheriff’s offices and specialized aviation and drone units, assisted in searching for the remaining individuals. Six other fleeing suspects were not located. The arrested suspect faces multiple charges related to violence and resisting arrest.
Charges: Battery on a law enforcement officer, resisting arrest

Title: Teen arrested in Indiantown with loaded gun during traffic stop
description: On May 9, 2026, in Indiantown, Martin County, Florida, a 16-year-old male was arrested during a traffic stop conducted by the Martin County Sheriff’s Office. Deputies stopped a vehicle and asked the teenager to exit. During a pat-down search, officers discovered a loaded 9 mm handgun and a loaded magazine concealed in his waistband. Authorities also reported finding a clown mask and a hoodie inside the vehicle, which were collected as evidence. The sheriff’s office stated that the arrest is part of proactive policing efforts aimed at reducing illegal firearms possession and preventing potential violent crimes in the community. Investigators also noted that the teen had a prior criminal history, including burglary of a conveyance and grand theft auto. He was charged with unauthorized carrying of a concealed firearm, a felony offense. The State Attorney’s Office will determine whether the case will be handled in juvenile or adult court proceedings.
