Title: Video shows moment semitrailer driver arrested after bomb scare shuts down I-4
description: On April 4, 2026, a traffic stop on Interstate 4 near Lake Mary in Seminole County, Florida, escalated into a major law enforcement response after authorities were alerted to a possible explosive threat involving a commercial truck. The Florida Highway Patrol stopped a white semitrailer after receiving information that the driver may have claimed there were bombs inside the vehicle. As a precaution, eastbound lanes of I-4 were shut down for over an hour while troopers, deputies, and a K-9 unit searched the truck. Traffic was heavily impacted, with long backups reported. After investigation, no explosives were found inside the vehicle. The driver, identified as 49-year-old Kelvin Harp of Clarksville, Tennessee, was arrested at the scene. He was charged with making threats involving an explosive device and making written or electronic threats to kill. Authorities booked him into the Seminole County Jail, and his bond was set at $105,000. The case remains under court proceedings following arrest.
Charges: Threatening to discharge an explosive device, making written or electronic threats to kill

Title: Suspect Arrested After Paragould Police Say He Fled Traffic Stop, Parked at Home
description: Paragould police responded to a traffic incident after an officer observed a vehicle making unsafe turns and nearly causing a collision at an intersection. The driver continued through multiple streets, reportedly failing to stop at a stop sign and attempting to evade a traffic stop after emergency lights were activated. The vehicle eventually stopped at a residence where the driver exited and initially tried to avoid identification. Officers found personal items in the vehicle and later made contact with individuals at the home. A man identified as Kaireik Burgess was recognized by the officer as the driver. He initially denied being involved and refused to give his name but was later identified and taken into custody. Authorities arrested him at the scene after confirming his involvement in the traffic stop. The incident did not involve injuries, but it led to multiple traffic-related and obstruction charges after the attempted evasion and failure to comply with law enforcement during the stop.
Charges: Fleeing in a vehicle Obstructing governmental operations Driving on a suspended license Failure to obey a stop sign Operating a vehicle without a license plate

Title: Video shows toddler emerging from overturned car after trooper pursuit crash
description: On May 2, 2026, in Joiner, Arkansas, a state trooper attempted to stop a Dodge Charger for speeding. The driver, later identified as 23-year-old Thalia Jones, refused to pull over, leading to a police pursuit along State Highway 118. During chase, trooper performed PIT maneuver that caused the vehicle to spin out and overturn onto its roof. After the crash, officers held the scene at gunpoint until backup arrived. A 3-year-old child, identified as Jones’ son, exited the overturned vehicle and was immediately assisted by the trooper, who ensured the child’s safety. The mother then crawled out of the wrecked car and was taken into custody. Authorities confirmed both were medically cleared after the crash. Jones was charged with speeding, reckless driving, driving with a suspended license, endangering the welfare of a child, and unauthorized use of another person’s vehicle to commit a crime. Incident was reported to child protection authorities officials
Charges: Speeding; reckless driving; driving with a suspended license; endangering the welfare of a child; unauthorized use of another person’s vehicle to commit a crime

Title: Moorhead man arrested after allegedly fleeing traffic stop, barricading inside home
description: On March 4, 2026, in Moorhead, Minnesota, police attempted a traffic stop in the 3900 block of 28th Street North involving a 40-year-old male driver. After exiting the vehicle, James Moher entered a nearby residence and refused to comply with officers’ commands to come out. Law enforcement later entered the home and detained him without incident following a brief barricade situation. He was identified as James Moher and charged with driving after revocation, obstructing justice, and fleeing police. He was taken to Clay County Jail for processing and custody. The incident began as a traffic enforcement action and escalated when the driver left the vehicle and entered a home, prompting police response and eventual arrest by Moorhead Police Department in Minnesota. No injuries were reported during the incident and no weapons or drugs were mentioned in the report. Charges are pending court proceedings following the arrest in Clay County Minnesota.
Charges: Driving after revocation, obstructing justice, fleeing police

Title: St. Cloud Driver Arrested After Allegedly Fleeing Traffic Stop on Foot; Loaded Gun and Open Containers Found in Car
description: On March 6, 2026, St. Cloud Police attempted a traffic stop on a vehicle near 9th Street South and 11th Avenue South in St. Cloud, Minnesota, after observing it driving without lights. According to police reports, the driver, identified as 21-year-old Abdulaziz Hussein, made a slow turn and struck a fence before exiting the vehicle and fleeing on foot. Officers pursued him and were able to catch him, though he briefly attempted to run again. A taser was used to subdue him after he resisted arrest and failed to comply with commands. Police reported signs of impairment, including slurred speech and alcohol odor. A search of the vehicle revealed a loaded handgun on the driver’s side floorboard, ammunition, and open containers of whiskey. Hussein was arrested and charged with multiple offenses, including DWI, test refusal, firearm possession without a permit, fleeing on foot, obstruction, and open container violations. An additional passenger in the vehicle was also charged separately.
Charges: Second-degree DWI, second-degree DWI test refusal, possession of firearm without permit, fleeing on foot, obstruction, open container violations

Title: Man wanted in Wisconsin arrested after Minnesota chase, linked to missing woman case
description: Robert Chilcote, a 29-year-old man wanted in Wisconsin, was arrested in Monticello, Minnesota, after leading Wright County deputies on a high-speed pursuit. Authorities had been notified that Chilcote was wanted in connection with an aggravated assault investigation and a possible homicide and was believed to be armed. A deputy located the red Toyota Prius he was driving and attempted a high-risk traffic stop. When ordered to exit the vehicle, Chilcote allegedly refused and drove away. Deputies pursued him for approximately 16 minutes over a distance of 17 miles. During the chase, he reportedly drove at speeds exceeding 100 mph, ignored traffic signals and stop signs, and passed vehicles recklessly. Deputies deployed stop sticks, and while attempting to avoid them, Chilcote drove onto a median, struck a stop sign, and became stuck. He was then taken into custody. An AR-15 rifle with an inserted magazine was found in the vehicle. He was also identified as a person of interest in the disappearance of Gabriella Cartagena.
Charges: Fleeing a Peace Officer in a Motor Vehicle  Fugitive from Justice from Another State

Title: 100mph Driver Accused of Threatening State Trooper During Rochester Traffic Stop
description: An 18-year-old Rochester man, Brian Morales-Velazquez, was charged following a high-speed traffic stop and arrest on March 24, 2026, in Rochester, Minnesota. A Minnesota State Patrol trooper observed a vehicle traveling at an excessive speed and weaving through traffic on Highway 52. The trooper measured the vehicle traveling at 103 mph and later accelerating to 117 mph. After activating emergency lights, the trooper followed the vehicle until it exited the highway and stopped on the shoulder. During the stop, the driver allegedly attempted to return to the driver’s seat after being ordered out of the vehicle. The trooper detected the odor of alcohol and learned the driver had consumed alcoholic beverages before driving. Field sobriety tests were unsuccessful, and the suspect refused breath testing. After being arrested, Morales-Velazquez allegedly threatened the trooper and the trooper’s family while being transported to jail. He was booked into the Olmsted County Jail and later appeared in court.
Charges: Felony fleeing a peace officer Felony threats Gross misdemeanor DWI Misdemeanor DWI Careless driving Underage drinking and driving Failure to yield to an emergency vehicle Speeding

Title: Erhard Man Arrested After Using a Fork to Hotwire a UTV and Fleeing Deputies
description: An Erhard man was arrested early Friday morning after deputies in Otter Tail County responded to a report of a stolen UTV allegedly taken from a garage by a family member. Deputies later located the UTV on a county highway around 2:30 a.m. and attempted a traffic stop. The driver, identified as Justin Allen Sheridan, failed to stop and led deputies on a low-speed pursuit, traveling approximately 45 to 50 miles per hour. During the chase, Sheridan turned into the opposite lane of a U.S. highway and later drove into a ditch but continued operating the vehicle. The pursuit ended about an hour later when the UTV stopped and Sheridan surrendered by placing his hands out the window. Deputies discovered a bent fork jammed into the ignition, which investigators believe was used to hotwire the vehicle. Sheridan was taken into custody and later appeared in court on charges related to fleeing law enforcement and tampering with a motor vehicle.
Charges: Fleeing from law enforcement Tampering with a motor vehicle

Title: Man Arrested After Abandoning a Pistol in the Toy Section of a Fergus Falls Gas Station
description: A North Dakota man was arrested in Fergus Falls after a traffic stop led to the discovery of a handgun left inside a gas station. An Otter Tail County deputy initially observed a vehicle driving suspiciously on Interstate 94 east of Fergus Falls and initiated a stop after the driver failed to use a turn signal. The vehicle pulled into a gas station, where the passenger, identified as Jacob Daniel Gilmore, entered the store and was later followed by the deputy. While Gilmore was in the bathroom, the deputy conducted an investigation and reviewed surveillance footage. The video allegedly showed Gilmore dropping an item inside the store. Deputies later found a black shirt wrapped around a yellow plastic bag containing a Walther PPX 9mm pistol in the store’s toy section. The firearm was not loaded but had two loaded magazines. Gilmore was arrested for felony firearm possession due to prior violent convictions and carrying a pistol in public without a permit.
Charges: Felon in possession of a firearm Possession of a pistol in public without a permit

Title: Williston Man Driving Stolen SUV in Otter Tail Discovered for Using His Phone While Driving
description: On May 23, 2026, a Minnesota State Patrol trooper stopped a gray Jeep SUV in Otter Tail County after observing swerving and multiple lane departures. The driver, later identified as Marquis Jerell Charleston of Williston, North Dakota, was initially pulled over for suspected distracted driving when the trooper saw him using a cellphone while operating the vehicle, violating Minnesota’s hands-free law. During the stop, dispatch confirmed the SUV had been reported stolen from North Dakota earlier that same day. Charleston claimed the vehicle belonged to his stepdaughter and said he had been using it for several days. Officers determined the vehicle was unlawfully possessed, and Charleston was taken into custody at the scene without reported injuries or pursuit. He was later booked and appeared in court on charges related to vehicle theft and receiving stolen property. The investigation remains ongoing. No injuries or additional suspects were reported by authorities officials
Charges: Unauthorized use of a motor vehicle, receiving stolen property, violation of hands-free driving law

Title: Three Juveniles Arrested After Short Vehicle Pursuit Sunday
description: On March 29, 2026, Fergus Falls police attempted a traffic stop that led to a short pursuit on East Main Avenue before being terminated due to safety concerns. The vehicle was later found abandoned on East Cherry Avenue. A coordinated search by Fergus Falls Police, Otter Tail County Sheriff’s Office, State Patrol, and DNR established a perimeter. K-9 located a 16-year-old female suspect. Residents reported two juveniles entering a home while fleeing and leaving after confrontation. Officers located two juveniles, ages 14 and 15, in Fergus Falls and took them into custody. Two were transported to detention in Moorhead; one released to family. Case will be reviewed by Otter Tail County Attorney for possible charges including vehicle theft fleeing trespassing and related offenses stemming from incident investigation process ongoing review period continues
Charges: Expected: motor vehicle theft, fleeing in a motor vehicle, fleeing on foot, trespassing

Title: Fergus Falls Man Charged After Fleeing from Police on Motorcycle
description: On May 26, 2026, a Fergus Falls police officer observed a motorcycle traveling at approximately 80 mph on Lincoln Avenue, where traffic conditions were heavy. The rider, later identified as 26-year-old Aldin Saric, was seen speeding, swerving, and nearly striking multiple vehicles. The officer attempted to initiate a traffic stop, but the motorcycle fled, leading to a brief pursuit through city streets. Due to public safety concerns and traffic density, the officer terminated the chase after losing sight of the motorcycle near Vernon Avenue and Court Street. Several days later, on May 29, investigators obtained surveillance footage from a local gas station that helped identify Saric as the rider. Police later located him at a storage facility, where he initially denied involvement. After being confronted with video evidence, Saric admitted to operating the motorcycle during the incident. He was charged in connection with fleeing law enforcement in a motor vehicle. No injuries were reported.
Charges: Fleeing a Peace Officer in a Motor Vehicle

Title: 100mph Driver Accused of Threatening State Trooper During Rochester Traffic Stop
description: Brian Morales-Valazquez, an 18-year-old Rochester man, was arrested following a high-speed traffic stop on Highway 52 in Rochester. A Minnesota State Patrol trooper observed his vehicle traveling at extreme speeds, initially clocked at about 103 mph and later accelerating up to 117 mph while weaving through traffic. The trooper initiated a stop, and Morales-Valazquez eventually pulled over after exiting the highway. During the stop, officers reported signs of intoxication, including the smell of alcohol. The driver admitted to drinking vodka mixed drinks prior to driving and failed field sobriety tests. He also refused multiple breath tests. While being transported to jail, Morales-Valazquez allegedly threatened the trooper and the trooper’s family. The case includes both traffic and criminal charges due to reckless driving behavior, alcohol impairment, and alleged threats made during custody. A passenger was also present in the vehicle at the time of the incident.
Charges: Felony fleeing police Felony threats of violence Gross misdemeanor DWI Misdemeanor DWI Careless driving Underage drinking and driving Failure to yield to emergency vehicle Speeding

Title: Man arrested after allegedly assaulting and disarming officers in Clearwater County
description: On February 4, 2026, a Clearwater County deputy conducted a traffic stop on a vehicle driven by Daniel Johnson of Bagley, Minnesota, after observing erratic driving that included swerving, hitting fog lines, and avoiding deer. During the stop, Johnson reportedly showed signs of alcohol impairment, including watery eyes and a strong odor of alcohol. He initially refused a chemical test but later admitted to drinking alcohol. As officers attempted to place him under arrest, Johnson became aggressive and resisted. He pushed away from officers, struck one officer in the face with a closed fist, and escalated the encounter further when another officer attempted to use a Taser. Johnson allegedly grabbed the Taser and deployed it against the officer’s hand. He was eventually subdued, handcuffed, and taken into custody. He was later transported to a hospital due to chest pain complaints. The incident involved multiple officers and required physical restraint before Johnson was secured.
Charges: Disarming a peace officer, fourth-degree assault, refusal to submit to a chemical test, obstructing the legal process

Title: Arrested Warrant Issued for Rochester Man Accused of Leading Officers on Pursuit
description: Rochester police officers attempted to stop a vehicle belonging to Brent Howard Schad after spotting it at a gas station while confirming his driving status and outstanding warrant for a prior DWI case. Officers observed Schad leave the parking lot and followed him onto a four-lane road, where they initiated a traffic stop using emergency lights. Instead of pulling over, Schad reportedly changed lanes, turned off the main road, and accelerated away from officers. Despite officers activating sirens, the suspect continued fleeing, leading law enforcement to terminate the pursuit for safety reasons. The incident occurred in November 2025 but the arrest warrant and related charges were reported in January 2026. Authorities noted that Schad was already wanted due to a previous DWI-related warrant and had a revoked driver’s license at the time. The pursuit ended without a crash or injuries, and a felony warrant was later issued for his arrest.
Charges: Felony fleeing police; driving after cancellation/inimical to public safety

Title: Rochester Man Accused of Fleeing Traffic Stop at High Speed
description: Justin Wayne Higgins, a 34-year-old Rochester man, was charged after fleeing from a traffic stop at high speed in the Rochester area. An officer initially attempted to stop him for speeding, but Higgins allegedly continued driving, accelerating and committing multiple traffic violations while attempting to evade police. He reportedly ran a red light and then drove through several streets at speeds estimated between 50–60 mph in a 30 mph zone. At one point, officers lost active pursuit due to safety concerns, but another officer later located the vehicle nearby and conducted a traffic stop. Higgins was taken into custody without further incident. The case involves allegations of felony fleeing a police officer and reckless driving behavior. He was later released pending court proceedings and scheduled to return to court the following month. The incident highlights dangerous driving behavior and police pursuit protocols in residential and mixed-traffic areas of Rochester.
Charges: Felony fleeing police

Title: Man arrested after pursuit with law enforcement ends in Zumbro River
description: On May 8, 2026, Olmsted County Sheriff’s deputies in Rochester, Minnesota attempted to stop a vehicle for traffic violations near Country Club Road and 45th Avenue SW. The driver, identified as 28-year-old Aries Candler of Rochester, briefly fled in his vehicle before stopping and then exiting. He attempted to escape on foot and ultimately ran into the Zumbro River during the pursuit. Deputies followed and were able to take him into custody without further incident. The arrest occurred after a short vehicle chase followed by a foot pursuit into the river. Authorities confirmed that the incident began as a traffic stop and escalated when the suspect fled both by car and on foot. Candler was booked into the Olmsted County Adult Detention Center shortly after the incident. Charges are being forwarded to the County Attorney’s Office and include fleeing in a motor vehicle, reckless driving, and fleeing on foot. No injuries were reported.
Charges: Fleeing in a motor vehicle, reckless driving, fleeing on foot

Title: Holiday Woman Charged With Carjacking: Pasco County Sheriff
city and state: Holiday and New Port Richey, Florida
description: Africa Jones was arrested in Pasco County, Florida, after a violent carjacking incident that began in a Winn-Dixie parking lot in Holiday. According to deputies, Jones approached a woman loading groceries into her SUV, asked about push-to-start ignition, then drew a firearm and demanded the keys while stating she did not want to hurt her. The victim complied and fled. Jones then drove the stolen vehicle to a Dollar General on State Road 54 in New Port Richey, where she attempted another carjacking. She allegedly reached toward a woman and her daughter while holding a gun, but the victim resisted, punched her, and escaped. Deputies later located Jones and conducted a traffic stop, taking her into custody without further incident. She reportedly claimed emotional distress and denied intent to steal the second vehicle, saying she was trying to get home and had a tire issue earlier that day as well.
Charges: Two counts of robbery (carjacking with a firearm or weapon), possession of a weapon or ammunition by a convicted felon

Title: Vehicle chase ends at roundabout crash; four suspects arrested in Benton break-in probe
description: Benton Police responded early in the morning to a breaking or entering complaint in a residential subdivision, where witnesses reported suspects leaving the scene in a white vehicle. Officers quickly located a matching vehicle nearby and attempted a traffic stop, but the driver fled at high speed, leading to a police pursuit. The chase ended when the vehicle crashed at a roundabout near a local overpass. One suspect was immediately taken into custody at the scene, while three others fled on foot. Law enforcement established a perimeter and later located and arrested all remaining suspects. The investigation revealed that the group, including three juveniles and one adult, was allegedly involved in multiple breaking or entering incidents and theft-related offenses. Authorities recovered stolen property from the vehicle and are working to identify its owners. Charges were filed against the adult suspect, Dominic Gibson, including fleeing, breaking or entering, theft of property, and contributing to the delinquency of minors.
Charges: Use of another’s property to facilitate a crime Breaking or entering (multiple counts) Theft of property Fleeing Contributing to the delinquency of a minor Endangering the welfare of a minor

Suspect Name: Juan Gabriel Caicedo Chasoy Jhon Alex Riasco Vergara Louis Ramon Monseque
Title: Traffic Stop Leads to the Arrest of Three Unauthorized Aliens Linked to Residential Burglary
description: Hillsborough County deputies conducted a traffic stop on a vehicle linked to multiple residential burglaries after surveillance identified it as being involved in two break-ins. The stop led to the arrest of three men connected to the incidents. Investigators say the driver lacked a valid license and had a final deportation order. One passenger used false identification and was later tied to an armed burglary involving over $100,000 in stolen property. The third passenger also used fraudulent ID and was found to have multiple felony warrants out of Texas and Washington for burglary and kidnapping-related charges. All three were taken into custody.
Charges: No valid driver’s license Fugitive warrants (2 counts) Unauthorized use or possession of fraudulent ID card (2 counts) False information to law enforcement officer Displaying fraudulent ID card Armed burglary of an unoccupied dwelling Grand theft over $100,000 False name to law enforcement officer Possession of cannabis under 20 grams Multiple out-of-state felony warrants (burglary, kidnapping, criminal mischief)

Title: Reading woman arrested after spraying officers with Mace during OVI stop, records show
description: A 39-year-old woman from Reading, Ohio was arrested after a violent confrontation with police during a traffic stop for suspected driving under the influence. Officers from Reading Police Department initiated the stop on the 1000 block of 4th Street after observing signs of intoxicated driving. According to court records, the situation escalated when the suspect refused to exit her vehicle after being ordered to do so. As officers attempted to remove her from the car, she allegedly used Mace against two officers, spraying them directly in the face. The chemical spray caused immediate irritation and injury, and a physical struggle followed. During the altercation, one officer sustained additional injuries. The suspect was ultimately subdued and taken into custody. Authorities charged her with multiple offenses including resisting arrest, obstructing official business, driving under the influence, felonious assault, and assault on officers. She was booked into the Hamilton County Justice Center on bond.
Charges: Resisting arrest; obstructing official business; driving under the influence (OVI); two counts of felonious assault; three counts of assault on an officer

Title: Traffic stop leads to arrest of Warren County man accused of child sex crimes
description: A 56-year-old Warren County, Ohio man, Michael Waldron, was arrested during a traffic stop conducted by law enforcement on March 17, 2026. Prosecutors allege that Waldron groomed and sexually abused multiple elementary-school-aged boys over a period of approximately four years beginning in 2021. Court records state he faces 12 felony charges including gross sexual imposition, importuning, public indecency, and multiple grooming-related offenses. Investigators say at least six victims were involved. The arrest was captured on Hamilton County Sheriff’s Office body camera footage while Waldron was stopped in a vehicle and speaking with his attorney on phone. After the stop, he was taken into custody on sex-related charges. Waldron later posted a $100,000 cash bond but was ordered to remain under GPS monitoring. His defense attorney requested work release, stating he is employed in real estate and can comply with bond conditions. He is scheduled for a bond hearing April.
Charges: 12 felony charges including gross sexual imposition, importuning, public indecency, grooming-related offenses

Title: Gun Found During Traffic Stop Leads To Felony Arrest
description: On May 29, 2026, Jonesboro police conducted a traffic stop on a vehicle for traffic violations including improper lane change and excessively dark window tint. During the stop, officers identified the driver as Rachelle Leigh Drum and a male passenger in the vehicle. Because officers could not see inside the car, a K-9 unit was deployed, which reportedly alerted to the presence of contraband. A search of the vehicle led officers to discover a shotgun located behind the rear seats. Authorities later determined that Drum had a prior felony conviction, making her prohibited from possessing firearms under state law. She was taken into custody without incident. The passenger was also removed from the vehicle but was not reported as charged in connection with the firearm. Drum was charged with possession of a firearm by certain persons, along with traffic violations. Her bail was set at $5,000, and she is scheduled for a court appearance on July 30.
Charges: Possession of a firearm by certain persons (felony); improper lane change; improper window tint
Refrence number: Your request reference number is JPD-2026-671 and your security key is 4FE7D0EA.

Title: Parole Absconder Arrested After Traffic Stop Reveals Loaded Handgun in Vehicle
description: Jonesboro Police Department officers conducted a traffic stop on a blue Hyundai Elantra on February 24, 2026 after observing a failure to signal while turning onto Rogers Street in Jonesboro, Arkansas. During the stop, the driver initially provided false identification under the name “Craig Noble” with a different date of birth. Officers ran the information through law enforcement databases and determined it was not accurate. The driver was then correctly identified as Corbin Dshaun Noble, a 39-year-old parole absconder with a prior felony record and an active warrant. A parole search of the vehicle was conducted, and officers located a loaded .25-caliber handgun inside the glove compartment. Noble was confirmed to be the sole occupant of the vehicle at the time of the stop. He admitted he was aware of his warrant status. He was arrested for providing false information and possession of a firearm by a convicted felon.
Charges: Possession of firearm by certain persons (felon in possession), obstructing governmental operations (false identification)
Refrence number: Your request reference number is JPD-2026-672 and your security key is 91A9BC99.

Title: Dramatic bodycam video captures deputy pulling woman from fiery car wreck: 'I got to her just in time'
description: Richard Younger, a 34-year-old man, was arrested after allegedly carjacking a vehicle and leading police on a pursuit that ended in a violent crash in Jacksonville. During the incident, officers attempted to stop the stolen vehicle, but the suspect fled and later crashed into another car, causing a fire. A woman inside the struck vehicle was rescued by a deputy moments before the car became fully engulfed in flames. Authorities also reported that a 1-year-old child was in the stolen vehicle during the incident but was safely removed by officers. Younger was taken into custody at the crash site and charged in connection with the carjacking, fleeing police, and other felonies
Charges: Carjacking; fleeing law enforcement; multiple felony charges (including related violent incident charges)

Title: Woman accused of threatening authorities after illegal firearms arrest
description: Danielle Marie Whitebird, a 39-year-old woman, was arrested on June 1, 2026, in Clay County, Minnesota, after deputies conducted a traffic stop near the Hawley Airport and a storage unit complex that had experienced previous break-ins. Deputies observed Whitebird leaving the area in a pickup truck that lacked a front license plate. During the stop, officers noticed what appeared to be burglary tools, including bolt cutters and a pry bar. Whitebird reportedly stated that she did not rent a storage unit at the facility. A search of the property allegedly revealed three storage units that had been broken into. Investigators then searched the truck and reportedly found a loaded handgun, a modified short-barreled shotgun, ammunition, wire cutters, and binoculars. Authorities stated that Whitebird was prohibited from possessing firearms because of prior violent felony convictions. After her arrest, she allegedly escaped her handcuffs, threatened deputies and their families, and was subdued with a stun gun.
Charges: Carrying or Possessing a Pistol Without a Permit  Obstructing the Lawful Execution of Legal Process (Misdemeanor)  Owning, Possessing, or Operating a Short-Barreled Shotgun  Possession of Burglary Tools  Possession of a Pistol or Assault Weapon by a Person With a Previous Conviction  Making Terroristic Threats With Reckless Disregard for Causing Terror

Title: Wrong-way driver with flat tires leads Okaloosa County deputies on brief chase
description: Brandon Martinez, a 28-year-old man from Crestview, Florida, was arrested after allegedly leading deputies on a brief pursuit in Okaloosa County on May 3, 2026. Authorities received multiple reports of a red BMW traveling the wrong way on Eglin Parkway in Shalimar. Callers informed dispatchers that they narrowly avoided head-on collisions with the vehicle. Deputies located the BMW and observed that it had two flat tires and visible damage on the driver’s side. Law enforcement attempted to conduct a traffic stop, but Martinez allegedly refused to pull over and continued driving. Deputies pursued the vehicle for a short distance before taking Martinez into custody without incident. Investigators determined that the driver was impaired and charged him accordingly. No injuries were reported during the incident, and no crashes involving other motorists were mentioned by authorities. The case stemmed from dangerous driving behavior that prompted public safety concerns and required intervention by responding deputies.
Charges: DUI  Fleeing and Eluding

Title: Video: Man arrested for driving backward on Flagler County road
description: A 47-year-old man was arrested in Flagler County, Florida after multiple drivers reported a silver sedan traveling backward along State Road 100. Deputies responded after several 911 calls described the unusual and dangerous driving behavior. When law enforcement located the vehicle, they found the driver operating the car in reverse on a public roadway. The suspect later told deputies that his vehicle had a mechanical issue and that he believed driving backward was the safest way to reach a repair shop. However, investigators reported that the claimed mechanical problem appeared to disappear once the traffic stop was initiated. The vehicle was safely stopped in a parking lot near State Road 100 and Airport Road. Authorities also discovered that the driver had an extensive history of license-related offenses, including more than ten prior convictions for driving while his license was suspended. The incident drew strong criticism from officials due to the reckless and unsafe nature of the driving behavior.
Charges: Habitual driving while license suspended

Title: Toledo man accused of hiding in trash can after fleeing on foot from officers in stolen-car chase
description: Toledo police attempted to stop a stolen vehicle driven by 18-year-old Arris Campbell near Detroit and Pinewood in Toledo, Ohio. When officers tried to initiate the traffic stop, Campbell refused to pull over and instead led police on a high-speed pursuit exceeding 100 mph through city streets. The chase ended when the vehicle became disabled and came to a stop. Campbell then fled the vehicle on foot, prompting a ground search by officers. After a brief but extensive search in the surrounding area, officers located him hiding inside a trash can. He was taken into custody without further incident. Authorities stated that the initial stop attempt was related to the stolen vehicle investigation. Campbell was later charged with multiple offenses, including failure to comply with a police order and receiving stolen property. The case highlights a stolen-vehicle pursuit that escalated into a dangerous high-speed chase before ending in a foot pursuit and arrest.
Charges: Failure to comply with police order, receiving stolen property

Title: Bradford County Sheriff’s deputies recover stolen firearms during traffic stop
description: Bradford County Sheriff’s deputies conducted a traffic stop on US Highway 301 near mile marker 1 in Starke, Florida, leading to the arrest of four individuals from Gainesville. During the stop, deputies discovered the group was connected to stolen firearms, including a loaded rifle-caliber AR-style pistol, a loaded handgun, and another stolen handgun from Marion County. One passenger fled the vehicle on foot across the highway while carrying the AR-style pistol, prompting a foot pursuit. When deputies apprehended him, the firearm was no longer in his possession and was later found discarded near a retention pond. Additional responding units, including the Florida Highway Patrol, assisted at the scene. Investigators recovered the remaining stolen weapons from inside the vehicle. Two suspects were juveniles. All four individuals were taken into custody and charged with multiple firearm theft and related offenses. The case remains under investigation as authorities continue ongoing investigation review process
Charges: Two counts grand theft of firearm; resisting law enforcement without violence; attempting to conceal/destroy evidence; possession of handgun under 18 (juveniles)

Title: Man arrested after leading Columbia County deputies on chase ending with PIT maneuver
description: Columbia County Sheriff’s Office deputies conducted a traffic stop attempt after spotting a brown Jeep running a red light at the intersection of U.S. 90 and Southwest Bascom Norris Drive in Lake City, Florida. When deputies tried to initiate the stop, the driver, Robert Cyron, fled westbound on U.S. 90 at high speed, reaching up to 108 mph. During the pursuit, the driver drove into the opposite lane and turned off his headlights in an attempt to evade law enforcement. The chase continued until deputies successfully used a PIT maneuver on County Road 137 to stop the vehicle. After the vehicle was disabled, Cyron attempted to switch seats with a passenger to avoid being identified as the driver. Authorities confirmed he had 24 prior license suspensions. He was arrested at the scene and taken into custody without reported injuries. The case involved reckless fleeing behavior and active evasion of deputies before arrest
Charges: Fleeing and eluding law enforcement; driving with a suspended license

Title: Video shows arrest after driver runs from police, admits to having gun illegally
description: During a coordinated violent crime reduction effort involving Ohio State Highway Patrol troopers, Cincinnati Police, and the Hamilton County Sheriff’s Office, officers conducted a traffic stop in Cincinnati that escalated when the driver fled on foot. Authorities reported that officers initially pulled the vehicle over after spotting alcohol inside. As officers attempted to detain the driver, later identified as 40-year-old Orlando McSwain, he ran from the scene. Officers deployed a Taser in an effort to stop him, but he continued fleeing before being apprehended shortly afterward. After his arrest, McSwain reportedly admitted that he had an illegal firearm inside his vehicle. The incident was captured on video and later shared by the governor’s office as part of ongoing crime reduction initiatives. The case highlights enforcement efforts targeting weapons violations, impaired driving indicators, and resistance to police commands during traffic enforcement operations in the Cincinnati area under multi-agency cooperation.
Charges: Obstructing official business; resisting arrest; carrying a concealed weapon; having weapons while under disability; improper handling of a firearm in a motor vehicle

Title: Suspect allegedly tried to evade arrest by jumping into the Ottawa River
city and state: Toledo Police officers attempted to stop a white sedan around 1 a.m. for a traffic violation when the driver failed to comply and fled the scene. The vehicle sped away, leading officers on a short pursuit before it stopped near Phillips and North Detroit Avenue. The driver, later identified as 21-year-old Victor Leroy-Patrick Eames, exited the vehicle and fled on foot while the passenger remained inside the car. During the chase, Eames ran toward the Ottawa River and jumped into the water in an attempt to evade arrest. Officers observed him in the river and coordinated to take him into custody shortly after. He was arrested and later transported to a hospital for evaluation. The passenger was also detained at the scene. Authorities stated the incident began as a routine traffic stop but escalated due to the suspect’s attempt to flee both by vehicle and on foot into the river area in Toledo.

The vehicle sped away, leading officers on a short pursuit before it stopped near Phillips and North Detroit Avenue. The driver, later identified as 21-year-old Victor Leroy-Patrick Eames, exited the vehicle and fled on foot while the passenger remained inside the car. He was arrested and later transported to a hospital for evaluation. The passenger was also detained at the scene. Authorities stated the incident began as a routine traffic stop but escalated due to the suspect’s attempt to flee both by vehicle and on foot into the river area in Toledo.
Charges: Failure to Comply; Obstruction of Official Business

Title: Man accused of DUI after striking firefighter at crash scene
description: On March 14, 2026, in Jonesboro, Arkansas, Lynal Ray Hardin was involved in a DUI-related incident after police said he struck a firefighter who was responding to a crash at the intersection of Highland Drive and Great Dane. According to Craighead County court documents, Hardin was driving a small Toyota pickup when he hit the firefighter and continued through the intersection before being stopped by officers. Witnesses reported that he appeared to be using his phone at the time of the collision. When officers contacted him, Hardin allegedly showed signs of impairment, including unsteady balance and inability to complete field sobriety tests. He admitted to drinking earlier in the day and later submitted to a breath test, which returned a BAC of 0.09. The firefighter sustained minor injuries. Hardin was arrested and charged with aggravated assault, driving while intoxicated, and reckless driving. The case remains pending in circuit court with bond set by a judge.
Charges: Aggravated assault, driving while intoxicated, reckless driving

Title: WPSO close investigation after the arrest of West Monroe man during traffic stop in Ohio
description: Authorities in Amherst, Ohio conducted a traffic stop on a man identified as Jessy Dean, 25, during an ongoing investigation linked to a Webster Parish, Louisiana warrant. Officers initially stopped Dean for a traffic violation, and upon running his information through the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), they discovered he was wanted in connection with an investigation originating in October 2025. The case involved allegations related to juveniles, including indecent behavior and contributing to the delinquency of minors. Dean was taken into custody at the scene without further reported incident. Law enforcement later confirmed coordination with the Webster Parish Sheriff’s Office, which stated the arrest effectively closed their ongoing investigation after Ohio authorities detained him. Dean is also described as a registered sex offender and is accused of using social media to contact a minor under false identity claims. He is currently held pending extradition and bond proceedings in Louisiana.
Charges: Two counts of contributing to the delinquency of juveniles; two counts of indecent behavior with juveniles

Title: Suspect in wild police chase that hurt officer on the run since 2023
description: Norwood and Cincinnati police pursued a 34-year-old woman, identified as Iesha Harris of Winton Hills, after officers attempted a traffic stop connected to outstanding felonious assault and weapons warrants dating back to 2023. Harris allegedly fled in her vehicle, initiating multi-state pursuit that moved across Hamilton County, Ohio, and into Indiana before returning to Ohio. During the chase, she reportedly struck two Cincinnati police cruisers, causing significant damage and injuring an officer. One cruiser overturned after collision during the pursuit on Lees Creek Road in Harrison. The chase ended when another police cruiser rammed her vehicle, forcing it into a tree where it caught fire. Harris and Cincinnati officer were transported to hospital with minor injuries. Prosecutors stated she had been evading arrest for prior felonious assault charges and admitted she had been on the run since 2023. She now faces multiple felony charges including felonious assault and weapons offenses.
Charges: Felonious assault (4 counts), failure to comply with police, discharging a firearm near prohibited property, illegal gun possession, driving under suspension, running a red light

Title: Toledo man accused of 100+ m.p.h. pursuit, foot chase and gun violation
description: Toledo police arrested a 21-year-old man following an alleged high-speed pursuit on March 30, 2026, that reached speeds over 100 miles per hour. Officers initiated the stop after a traffic violation, but the driver fled, leading police on a chase through city streets involving red lights, sidewalks, and residential yards. The pursuit eventually ended after the suspect was taken into custody following a foot chase. During the incident, police reported that the suspect was illegally carrying a firearm. Authorities later charged him with failure to comply with police orders and tampering with evidence. The chase and arrest were part of an ongoing investigation into dangerous driving behavior and weapons violations. The suspect, identified as Jayden Bryce Gibson, was later indicted on the charges in early June 2026. His bond was set by the court while he awaited further legal proceedings related to the pursuit and firearm offense.
Charges: Failure to comply, tampering with evidence, illegal firearm possession (as reported in incident context)

Title: Man arrested after Elyria police chase ends in crash: Investigators
description: Elyria police attempted to approach a suspect, identified as 25-year-old Denavin Whitman, in a hotel parking lot on Midway Boulevard due to outstanding felony warrants for burglary and domestic violence. As officers moved in, Whitman allegedly entered a 2011 Hyundai Sonata and fled the scene at high speed, nearly striking an officer in the process. This initiated a police pursuit through city streets. During the chase, Whitman continued driving recklessly until the vehicle collided with another car at the intersection of Murray Ridge Road and Lowell Street, bringing the pursuit to an end. Police took Whitman into custody at the crash scene and transported him to University Hospitals for medical treatment. Authorities confirmed that no officers or civilians were seriously injured during the incident. Investigators also noted that Whitman’s driver’s license had already been suspended prior to the pursuit due to earlier violations and legal issues.
Charges: Fleeing/Eluding police, felony burglary warrant, domestic violence warrant, driving with suspended license (as reported)

Title: Teens allegedly stole car, led police on high-speed chase after their cellphones were taken away
description: Bowling Green police pursued a stolen vehicle reported to have been taken from a group home in Dayton, Ohio, driven by two teenage girls aged 13 and 15. Officers located the vehicle after a license plate reader alert and attempted a traffic stop near Route 25 and Demps Road. The driver, a 13-year-old, refused to stop, initiating a high-speed chase that reached speeds up to 100 mph. The pursuit continued through multiple jurisdictions, including passing Perrysburg Police, before ending when the stolen vehicle collided with another car near Route 25 and Interstate 475. After the crash, both juveniles fled on foot but were quickly apprehended by officers. The 13-year-old sustained a shoulder injury and was hospitalized. The 15-year-old was taken into custody and ordered held in juvenile detention. Authorities stated both suspects were involved in stealing the vehicle after their cellphones were taken at the group home.
Charges: Receiving stolen property, failure to comply with police orders

Title: Man arrested after leading Youngstown police on chase to Struthers: Report
description: Youngstown police attempted to stop a vehicle driven by 27-year-old Kevion Bradley after officers recognized him as a wanted individual on U.S. Marshals warrants. Instead of complying, Bradley allegedly fled from West Hylda Avenue, initiating a pursuit through city streets and into Struthers, Ohio. During the chase, he reportedly drove at high speeds reaching approximately 70 miles per hour and engaged in evasive maneuvers, including backing into a yard and driving through residential areas. Police continued the pursuit until Bradley eventually stopped in front of a residence in Struthers, where officers were able to apprehend him. He was taken into custody without further incident. Records indicated that Bradley had a prior failure-to-comply warrant and a criminal history involving firearm-related offenses, including being a felon in possession of a firearm. He is currently being held in the Mahoning County Jail pending arraignment on felony failure-to-comply charges related to the pursuit incident.
Charges: Failure to comply with order or signal of police officer (third-degree felony), prior warrants (including failure to comply), prior firearm-related felony conviction

Title: Toledo man sentenced in high-speed chase with four child passengers that ended in crash
description: On February 20, 2026, Toledo Police Department officers attempted to stop a vehicle near 2501 Lagrange Street after the driver ran a red light. The driver, identified as 20-year-old Kyle Reed of Toledo, Ohio, allegedly fled instead of pulling over, initiating a high-speed pursuit through city streets. Court records state that Reed had four child passengers in the vehicle, including a 2-year-old, a 5-year-old, and two 15-year-olds. During the chase, Reed reportedly ran multiple traffic signals before losing control of the vehicle and crashing. After the crash, he attempted to flee on foot but was quickly apprehended by police officers. During the arrest, Reed physically resisted officers, including pushing and twisting away, which resulted in an injury to one officer’s left thumb. He was later charged in connection with the incident and entered a guilty plea to multiple charges, including failure to comply and endangering children.
Charges: Four counts of endangering children One count of failure to comply Guilty plea entered on five charges

Title: Driver crashes within a minute of fleeing Independence police: Report
description: Independence police attempted to stop a vehicle early Tuesday morning after observing it being driven without headlights and displaying fictitious license plates. When officers initiated the stop, the driver refused to pull over and fled, leading to a brief police pursuit. The chase lasted less than one minute before the driver lost control of the vehicle while attempting a turn on Quarry Lane, striking a curb and coming to a stop after crashing while traveling uphill. After the crash, the driver exited the vehicle and attempted to flee on foot, but officers quickly located and detained her. The suspect was identified as Alecia Finklea, 31, who was found to have multiple active felony warrants at the time of arrest. She now faces additional charges related to fleeing from police and the crash incident. Authorities confirmed that no officers, the suspect, or any bystanders were injured during the short pursuit and crash.
Charges: Fleeing police, driving with fictitious plates, no headlights, plus multiple active felony warrants

Title: Driver arrested after hitting cruiser, nearly striking officer while fleeing Cincinnati police
description: Gatlin Gillespie, 34, was arrested after a police pursuit in Cincinnati, Ohio, on February 13, 2026. Officers with the Cincinnati PIVOT unit were conducting a drug investigation in the West End and Over-the-Rhine neighborhoods when they attempted to stop his black Chevy Colorado. The driver fled, later struck a marked cruiser, and nearly hit an officer during the second encounter. Police deployed drones and received assistance from a bystander to locate the vehicle after it fled again. The pursuit continued into Kentucky, where officers with local law enforcement units stopped and arrested him. He faces charges including DUI, wanton endangerment, criminal mischief, and fleeing from police. No officers were seriously injured during the incident, and the investigation remains ongoing as prosecutors review evidence gathered from body cameras and drone footage. Authorities credited coordinated efforts between Cincinnati police and Kentucky officers for quickly ending the cross-border pursuit safely without further injuries
Charges: DUI; wanton endangerment; criminal mischief; fleeing

Title: Man arrested with child in car had blood alcohol level twice legal limit, police say
description: Police in Paragould, Arkansas arrested Michael Orr after a traffic stop in which officers reported he was driving while intoxicated with a young child inside the vehicle. Authorities said the incident began when dispatchers received reports of a silver SUV traveling into oncoming traffic on Highway 49 North. Officers located the vehicle and found it blocked in a driveway by another truck. When contacted, Orr showed visible signs of impairment including bloodshot eyes, slurred speech, and slow responses. Officers also reported detecting a strong odor of alcohol and observed empty alcohol bottles inside the vehicle. Despite repeated commands, Orr initially refused to put the vehicle in park or exit, and officers had to physically remove him. A field sobriety test was conducted before his arrest. At the station, he later agreed to a blood alcohol test, which reportedly showed a BAC of 0.18. A child was present in the back seat during the incident.
Charges: Endangering the welfare of a minor (1st degree), DWI (2nd offense), open container, obstructing governmental operations

Title: Man accused of driving 100 mph while drunk, hopping away from deputies during stop in Collier County
description: On February 11, 2026, deputies with the Collier County Sheriff’s Office conducted speed enforcement on Vanderbilt Beach Road in Collier County, Florida, when they observed a silver Kia Soul traveling at approximately 96 mph in a 45 mph zone. Deputies initiated a pursuit after the vehicle continued at speeds exceeding 100 mph through multiple roadways, including Logan Boulevard and Islandwalk Boulevard, before the driver eventually stopped on Pristine Drive. The driver, identified as Brent Alma-Francis, was ordered out of the vehicle but initially failed to comply with instructions and was described as behaving erratically on the roadway. Once detained, deputies reported a strong odor of alcohol coming from him. He was transported to the Naples Jail Center, where he failed field sobriety tests and refused a breathalyzer test. Authorities stated he became aggressive during the process. He was arrested for multiple offenses connected to impaired driving and high-speed fleeing from law enforcement.
Charges: Fleeing and eluding police, driving over 100 mph, DUI, refusal to submit to DUI testing

Title: Jury Convicts Rochester Man Accused of Pulling Gun on Landscaper
description: Kyndle Richard Bennett, a 32-year-old man from Rochester, Minnesota, was involved in a criminal incident stemming from a dispute with a landscaper over a completed job at his residence. According to court records, the landscaper visited Bennett’s home after ongoing communication issues. During the meeting, Bennett allegedly demanded that the victim sign an agreement without reading it. When the landscaper refused, Bennett was accused of pulling a handgun from under his shirt and pointing it at the victim. He also allegedly made threatening statements, including warnings about finding the victim and knowing personal details about him. The victim left the residence unharmed and reported the incident to authorities. The Olmsted County Sheriff’s Office later investigated the case, leading to criminal charges. Bennett was ultimately convicted by a jury for felony second-degree assault with a dangerous weapon and terroristic threats following the review of evidence and testimony presented in court proceedings.
Charges: Second-degree assault with a dangerous weapon Terroristic threats

Title: Charges Filed in Rooster’s Parking Lot Shooting, Subsequent Rochester Police Chase
description: On May 25, 2026, a confrontation at Rooster’s Barn and Grill in northwest Rochester escalated into a shooting, leaving two women with non-life-threatening injuries. According to a criminal complaint filed in Olmsted County Court, one victim was speaking with Giwa when a second victim witnessed the interaction, leading to a physical altercation. Giwa allegedly drew a firearm and fired in a sweeping motion, striking the victims—one with grazes to her ankle and upper leg, the other with gunshot wounds to her abdomen and arm. Police tracked Giwa’s vehicle from his residence, initiating a traffic stop that led to a high-speed pursuit through residential areas. The chase ended using a PIT maneuver near 55th Street and Fairway Drive NW. Giwa and an accomplice, Cabdulqaadir Axmed Ciise, were arrested, while a third passenger was released. Giwa faces multiple charges including two counts of second-degree assault, firearm discharge in a municipality, and possession of a firearm as a violent felon.
Charges: Luke Giwa: Two counts of second-degree assault, discharge of a firearm in a municipality, possession of a firearm as a person convicted of a violent crime Cabdulqaadir Ciise: Felony fleeing

Title: Police arrest man after high-speed chase ends in crash
description: Mason C. Markum, a 22-year-old man from Paragould, Arkansas, was arrested after a police pursuit that began following reports of a stolen debit card and possible stolen vehicle use. According to investigators, officers responded to a report that Markum had attempted to use a stolen debit card in the 1300 block of West Kingshighway. Although the transaction was partially successful for a small amount, the suspect left the area before police arrived. The vehicle was later located, and when officers attempted a traffic stop, Markum fled at high speed. The pursuit reached speeds exceeding 110 mph and crossed into Dunklin County, Missouri. The chase ended when the vehicle crashed, after which Markum attempted to flee on foot but was quickly apprehended by officers. Authorities reported no major injuries during the incident. He was taken into custody and charged in connection with fleeing, theft-related offenses, and reckless driving following the investigation.
Charges: Fleeing (felony) Theft of property (felony) Theft of property (misdemeanor) Reckless driving

Title: WATCH: ASP releases dash cam footage of West Memphis ambulance chase
description: A stolen ambulance from Memphis triggered a multi-agency pursuit that crossed into Arkansas and ended in West Memphis. According to reports, Memphis Fire Department crews were treating a patient on Tunica Street when an unknown individual took control of the ambulance and drove away. The vehicle was tracked across state lines into Arkansas, where Arkansas State Police initiated a high-speed chase. Troopers used spike strips and a PIT maneuver to safely stop the ambulance. The pursuit concluded near Baptist Memorial Hospital in West Memphis, where the suspect was taken into custody without further escalation. Authorities identified the suspect as Vanessa Bowen, who was arrested and charged with theft of property. The incident involved emergency medical equipment being unlawfully taken during an active medical response, prompting immediate coordination between Memphis Fire Department and Arkansas State Police. No serious injuries were reported during the chase or arrest.
Charges: Theft of property

Title: Crash Into Business Sign Leads to Felony Fleeing, DWI Arrest
description: Justin Sanders was involved in a police pursuit in Paragould, Arkansas, after officers attempted to stop an ATV being driven at a high rate of speed on February 10, 2026. According to a probable cause affidavit from the Paragould Police Department, Sanders failed to stop for officers and continued driving recklessly through traffic. He reportedly entered the opposite lane, weaved around vehicles, and attempted to evade law enforcement while traveling at speeds higher than the posted limit. The pursuit ended when Sanders entered a business parking lot, struck a parking pole and a store sign, and overturned the ATV. He was ejected from the vehicle during the crash and was later apprehended at the scene. Officers observed signs of intoxication, including slurred speech and the smell of alcohol. An open container and additional alcohol were reportedly found nearby. Sanders admitted to drinking and speeding. He was taken for medical treatment before facing charges related to fleeing and intoxicated driving.
Charges: Felony fleeing (Class C felony) Second-degree criminal mischief Possession of an open container Driving while intoxicated (DWI) Reckless driving Other traffic offenses

Title: Man leads deputies, state police on high-speed chase along I-530
description: Deandre Brothers, a 29-year-old man from Arkansas, led Jefferson County Sheriff’s deputies and Arkansas State Police on a high-speed pursuit along Interstate 530 after being suspected of terroristic threatening, aggravated assault, and resisting arrest. According to authorities, the chase reached speeds of up to 125 mph and created significant danger for other motorists on the highway. During the pursuit, a state trooper executed a tactical vehicle intervention near the Redfield exit, causing Brothers’ vehicle to cross the median into the southbound lanes and collide with a civilian van. No serious injuries were reported, although a passenger in the suspect’s vehicle was transported to a hospital with minor injuries. After the crash, Brothers attempted to flee on foot but was quickly apprehended by deputies. Law enforcement confirmed that multiple additional charges are pending as the investigation continues. Officials described the incident as highly dangerous due to the extreme speeds and risk to public safety.
Charges: Terroristic threatening (suspected) Aggravated assault (suspected) Resisting arrest Additional pending charges related to fleeing and traffic offenses

Title: Cortland man facing weapons charges after Warren traffic stop
description: Warren police conducted a traffic stop on a speeding truck near South Street and West Market Street just before 1 a.m. During the stop, a female passenger exited the vehicle and fled on foot toward Buckeye Street while officers attempted to locate her. The driver, identified as Allen Milleson, told officers he had recently been released from prison and denied that any drugs or weapons were in the vehicle. However, during a search, officers discovered suspected drugs and drug paraphernalia inside the truck, including a plastic bag wedged between the passenger seat and center console. A backpack located on the rear floorboard contained loose bullets and a loaded firearm. Because Milleson had a prior felony conviction prohibiting firearm possession, he was taken into custody. The investigation confirmed multiple violations involving weapons and possible drug possession. The female passenger who fled was also the subject of a search during the incident in Warren, Ohio.
Charges: Having weapons under disability; improper handling of a firearm in a motor vehicle; carrying concealed weapons; speeding

Title: Deputies: Florida man cut off other drivers, pointed gun at them in Walton County
description: Blackie Alvarez, 34, was arrested after a road rage incident in Walton County, Florida. According to the Walton County Sheriff's Office, Alvarez allegedly sped, honked, and aggressively drove around another vehicle on Highway 331 South. Investigators said he cut off the victims, stopped his vehicle in front of them, exited, and pointed a handgun at them. The victims called 911 to report the incident. Deputies quickly located Alvarez and stopped his vehicle. During the stop, Alvarez exited the vehicle and placed a handgun on top of his car. He was taken into custody and booked into the Walton County Jail.
Charges: Two felony counts of False Imprisonment  Two felony counts of Aggravated Assault with a Deadly Weapon  One felony count of Possession of a Firearm by a Convicted Felon  Two counts of Unlawful Carry of a Concealed Weapon  Driving Without a License

Title: Video shows 5 suspects in foot chase during rush hour on I-4 in Central Florida
description: Florida Highway Patrol conducted a traffic stop on Interstate 4 near Altamonte Springs in Seminole County after a vehicle was observed towing an unauthorized trailer in an express lane. During the stop, five passengers fled on foot, triggering a large pursuit captured on video. Four suspects ran along the interstate shoulder while one was initially detained. Two of the fleeing individuals reportedly jumped off the interstate into a nearby structure connected to Cranes Roost Park. Backup units from FHP and the Altamonte Springs Police Department established a perimeter and coordinated a search of the surrounding area. All five suspects were eventually apprehended. Authorities reported the individuals carried Guatemalan identification cards, and a Border Patrol agent placed immigration detainers on them. The suspects were taken to Seminole County Jail and charged with resisting arrest. The incident remains under investigation. No injuries were reported during the incident by authorities at this time
Charges: Resisting arrest, Traffic stop

Title: Court docs: Woman charged with OVI, accused of being three times legal limit with child in car
description: Misty Merida, 38, was arrested in Liberty Township, Ohio after police received a report of a possible drunk driver on Roden Park Drive. Officers located her vehicle on Cold Water Drive, finding her 6-year-old son inside. They detected the smell of alcohol and noted her slurred speech. Merida admitted to drinking, and a breathalyzer test revealed a blood alcohol content of 0.243, over three times the legal limit. Whiskey bottles were also found in the car. She was charged with operating a vehicle under the influence and endangering children for driving while intoxicated with a minor present.
Charges: Operating a vehicle under the influence (OVI) Endangering children

Title: Suspect driving 90 mph in 20 mph zone later crashes in Minneapolis
description: A 20-year-old Minneapolis man was arrested after a dangerous high-speed police pursuit that began when officers observed a vehicle traveling approximately 90 mph in a 20 mph zone on Victory Memorial Parkway. Robbinsdale Police attempted a traffic stop, but the driver refused to pull over, initiating a chase that moved through north Minneapolis and across the Mississippi River into northeast Minneapolis. During the pursuit, the suspect vehicle reached extreme speeds and was significantly ahead of pursuing squad cars. The chase ended when the driver lost control near the 4300 block of Marshall Street Northeast, close to the Minneapolis Water Treatment Plant. The vehicle rolled onto its roof in a rollover crash. After the crash, the driver exited the vehicle and complied with officers at the scene. He was taken to a hospital with non-life-threatening injuries and later booked into Hennepin County Jail. Authorities reported multiple probable cause charges related to the incident.
Charges: "Fleeing Police Possession of Stolen Property Reckless Driving Driving Without a Valid Driver’s License Speeding"

Title: Driver who said he had ‘one beer’ arrested for DUI with child in vehicle, troopers say
description: David Valencia, a 43-year-old man from Lehigh Acres, Florida, was arrested after Florida Highway Patrol troopers observed him committing a traffic violation and later determined he was driving under the influence with a child in the vehicle. According to authorities, his Chevrolet Silverado made an illegal left turn against a red traffic arrow on State Road 82 near Buckingham Road. Troopers conducted a traffic stop and noted signs of impairment, including slurred speech and a strong odor of alcohol. Valencia reportedly told officers he had consumed “one beer,” but a breath test later showed a blood alcohol concentration of 0.233, nearly three times the legal limit. A 9-year-old girl was inside the vehicle during the incident and was later released to a sober family member. The Florida Department of Children and Families was notified due to the presence of a minor. Valencia was arrested and charged with DUI and child neglect following the investigation.
Charges: DUI, child neglect

Title: Incarcerated Cannon Falls Woman Sentenced in Rochester DWI Fleeing Case
description: Ashley Rose McConnell, a 39-year-old woman from Spring Valley, Minnesota, was arrested after allegedly fleeing from a Minnesota State Patrol traffic stop near Rochester on the night of March 10, 2026. A state trooper initially stopped the vehicle because of a malfunctioning taillight near the Game Haven Reservoir area. During the stop, McConnell allegedly identified herself as her sister and provided a license belonging to another person. The trooper became suspicious of her identity and informed her that a fingerprint reader would be brought to the scene for verification. Before officers could confirm her identity, McConnell allegedly drove away from the stop at an estimated speed of 35 miles per hour. Law enforcement officers pursued the vehicle and used a PIT maneuver to bring it to a stop. She was then taken into custody. Authorities stated that McConnell was aware she had an active warrant at the time of the incident and was later charged in court.
Charges: Felony Fleeing a Peace Officer  Misdemeanor Giving a False Name to a Peace Officer

Title: Stewartville Teen Captured After Fleeing Law Enforcement, Crashing in Southeast Rochester
description: Del Dance, an 18-year-old from Stewartville, Minnesota, was arrested after fleeing from law enforcement in southeast Rochester. The incident began around 1:00 a.m. when the Minnesota State Patrol and local deputies attempted to stop a vehicle that was reportedly traveling at a high rate of speed. The driver failed to stop and continued fleeing, leading officers on a pursuit. The suspect vehicle later rolled over in the area of Marion Road and Pearl Court SE in rural Rochester. After the crash, the driver reportedly exited the vehicle and fled on foot before law enforcement arrived. A large search operation involving deputies, Rochester Police Department, and the Minnesota State Patrol was launched. K-9 units and a drone were used to locate the suspect. Officers eventually found and arrested Del Dance. He was taken into custody without further incident and booked into the Olmsted County Jail. Authorities stated that multiple charges are expected following the investigation.
Charges: Fleeing Law Enforcement Expected Multiple Pending Charges (Not yet formally listed)

Title: Sartell Man Jumps from Third Story Window While Fleeing Domestic Assault Arrest
description: Felony Domestic Assault by Strangulation Felony Threats of Violence Misdemeanor Domestic Assault False Imprisonment Providing False Name to Law Enforcement Active Felony Warrant (Fleeing Police in Vehicle)
Charges: Felony Domestic Assault by Strangulation Felony Threats of Violence Misdemeanor Domestic Assault False Imprisonment Providing False Name to Law Enforcement Active Felony Warrant (Fleeing Police in Vehicle)

Title: Rochester Man Charged for Police Pursuit That Ended With Vehicle Hitting Restaurant
description: Sebastijan Mileusnich, a 35-year-old Rochester man, was arrested after a police pursuit that ended when his vehicle crashed into a restaurant in Rochester, Minnesota. The incident began when officers observed him driving through an intersection at Civic Center Drive and 11th Avenue NW, where he ran a red light and stopped in the middle of the roadway, nearly causing multiple collisions. When an officer activated emergency lights and attempted a stop, Mileusnich accelerated and fled westbound at high speed. During the pursuit, he drove recklessly, weaving through traffic and reaching speeds of up to 70 mph. He later lost control while turning onto 16th Street NW, striking a curb, a sign, and a light pole before the vehicle became airborne and ultimately crashed into a restaurant. The vehicle rolled and came to rest upright. He was arrested and transported to a hospital before being booked into jail. Officers reported history.
Charges: Felony Fleeing Felony DWI

Title: 21-year-old faces new charges after fleeing deputies in Northwest Gainesville
description: Derrick Burke, a 21-year-old man, was arrested in Gainesville, Florida, after fleeing law enforcement during and after a domestic-related incident. Deputies initially responded to an armed domestic disturbance at the Quality Inn on Newberry Road, where Burke was taken into custody following the use of a Taser. While being transported for medical evaluation at a hospital, he managed to escape custody and ran away near the Publix area on Northwest 43rd Street and 53rd Avenue. Law enforcement quickly initiated a search and located him a short time later, leading to his rearrest. Authorities stated the incident involved multiple offenses including resisting arrest and fleeing from law enforcement. Burke was booked into the Alachua County Jail following his capture. His bond was set at $110,000. The case involved both domestic disturbance allegations and a subsequent escape from police custody while under arrest. No further injuries to others were reported during the incident.
Charges: Fleeing Law Enforcement Resisting Arrest Gun-related charges (from domestic incident)
Refrence number: Your request reference number is LERR2026-5709 and your security key is 9263279E.

Title: Armed carjacking suspect arrested after 30-mile chase, faces life in prison
description: Authorities say James Yawn was arrested following a violent armed carjacking that escalated into a high-speed pursuit across Central Florida. The incident began in a busy Winter Park parking lot near a restaurant area when Yawn allegedly attacked a woman, grabbing her by the hair and attempting to forcibly take her purse. During the struggle, he escalated the violence by pulling a firearm, threatening the victim, and stealing her vehicle. He then fled the scene, triggering a coordinated multi-agency pursuit involving Florida Highway Patrol and local law enforcement. Troopers reported the suspect drove extremely aggressively during the chase, reaching speeds near 130 mph, weaving through traffic, and attempting to evade stop maneuvers including PIT tactics. The pursuit continued for more than 30 miles along Interstate 4, crossing multiple jurisdictions before officers successfully stopped the vehicle near Deltona and Orange City exits. The suspect was taken into custody after being forcibly stopped and identified through fingerprints.
Charges: Armed carjacking Kidnapping with a firearm Armed robbery Aggravated assault DUI Fleeing and eluding law enforcement

Title: Gainesville police arrest man for breaching fire lines during wildfire response
description: Jeffrey Emminger, a 52-year-old man, was arrested in Gainesville, Florida after reportedly breaching fire lines during an active wildfire emergency. According to police, emergency crews were responding to multiple wildfires in North Central Florida when Emminger entered a restricted area that had been sealed off for public safety. Officials said his presence inside the fire zone interfered with firefighting operations and posed risks to both responders and nearby residents. Gainesville Police emphasized that restricted fire lines are established to allow firefighters safe and unobstructed access to dangerous areas. Despite warnings and active emergency conditions, Emminger allegedly entered the zone and failed to comply with instructions to leave. He was subsequently detained by officers on scene. Authorities charged him with failure to obey, resisting arrest, and fleeing. Police stated that keeping civilians out of active wildfire areas is critical to ensuring emergency operations are not delayed or disrupted during fast-moving fire events.
Charges: Failure to obey; resisting arrest; fleeing
