Title: VIDEO: 3 teens plead guilty after robbing victim at gunpoint, fleeing from police
description: In the summer of 2025, three teens committed an armed robbery at Willo Park Apartments in Willoughby, Ohio. The suspects forcibly took items from a victim at gunpoint around 9 p.m. on July 29. After the robbery, they fled in a vehicle, which was tracked by the Bedford Police Department. When officers attempted a traffic stop, the driver refused to comply, prompting a police chase through local neighborhoods. The pursuit ended when officers rammed the vehicle. Four occupants tried to flee, but two were immediately arrested. A third suspect was later apprehended at a Maple Heights residence, where police found multiple firearms, including a stolen rifle linked to five prior crimes across greater Cleveland. All three teens were charged with aggravated robbery, firearm-related offenses, and other associated crimes. Multiple law enforcement agencies collaborated to apprehend the suspects and recover the stolen weapons, demonstrating effective regional policing.
Charges: Aggravated robbery with firearm specification Failure to comply Grand theft of a firearm Having weapons under disability Evidence tampering

Title: 4 arrested, including 3 teens, after leading Westlake Police on chase in stolen car
description: In the early morning hours of March 28, 2026, Westlake and Rocky River police in Ohio pursued a stolen yellow Dodge Charger connected to an attempted car theft in Lorain County. Officers attempted traffic stop after spotting the vehicle speeding on I-90 East, but the driver refused to comply, initiating chase. Stop sticks were deployed, deflating a tire, yet the Charger continued before exiting onto West Boulevard, where it struck a center island and came to a stop. Four occupants fled on foot, and one remained briefly inside. A search involving Westlake Police, Rocky River Police, Cleveland, and the Cuyahoga County Sheriff’s Department led to the arrest of suspects. Police recovered multiple firearms, including a stolen Glock 27 with extended magazine, along with numerous key fobs and devices used for vehicle theft. The group was also linked to an attempted break-in at an Elyria car dealership earlier that night.
Charges: 21-year-old driver: felony receiving stolen property, possessing criminal tools, improper handling of firearm, failure to comply Teens: juvenile charges related to stolen vehicle, firearms, and fleeing

Title: Police: Juvenile in critical condition after being hit by car in Middletown; suspect arrested
description: Thomas Harris, 35, of Dayton, Ohio, was arrested after allegedly striking a juvenile on a bicycle with his vehicle at the intersection of Breiel Boulevard and Lefferson Road in Middletown. The incident occurred just before 6 p.m., and the juvenile was airlifted to Cincinnati Children's Hospital, where they remain in critical but stable condition. Following the crash, Harris reportedly fled the scene. Middletown police later spotted his vehicle near a Kroger store on Towne Boulevard and conducted a traffic stop, identifying and arresting Harris at the scene. Officers charged him with aggravated vehicular assault, operating a vehicle while impaired, and fleeing the scene. He is currently held at the Middletown City Jail. The incident is under active investigation, with authorities asking anyone with information to contact the Middletown Police Department. The case highlights the dangers of hit-and-run incidents involving vulnerable road users.
Charges: Aggravated vehicular assault, operating a vehicle while impaired, fleeing the scene

Title: Suspects appear in court after attempted street takeover results in dozens of arrests
description: On March 14, 2026, police responded to a large street takeover event in Cincinnati, which involved high-speed racing, burnouts, donuts, stunt driving, and intentional obstruction of public roadways. Officers arrested 39 individuals and impounded 65 vehicles at the Woodward High School parking lot. Many drivers claimed they were merely spectators rather than participants. Drivers faced towing, storage, impound fees, court costs, fines, and potential damages after running over stop sticks that deflated their tires. Bonds were set around $1,000 at ten percent. Potential legal penalties include up to 180 days in jail, $1,000 fines, probation, and driver’s license suspension ranging from 30 days to three years. The event highlighted both the risks of illegal street racing and the enforcement challenges for local police.
Charges: Street racing, obstruction of public roadway, stunt driving

Title: Armed carjacking in Kennedy Heights leads to police chase across Hamilton County
description: On January 12, 2026, an armed carjacking occurred in Kennedy Heights near Montgomery Road and Tyne Avenue when a man reportedly brandished a handgun and forced a victim out of their vehicle. The suspect then fled in the stolen SUV, prompting a multi-jurisdiction police pursuit across Hamilton County. Officers tracked the vehicle onto southbound I-71 and later into Colerain Township. The chase ended when the stolen SUV crashed and rolled over on I-74. The suspect, identified as 27-year-old Raekwon Douthit, was taken into custody at the scene. Police reported that the firearm used in the carjacking was not recovered. The victim’s injury status was not confirmed at the time of reporting. Douthit was held on bond and faced charges related to the violent theft and police pursuit.
Charges: Aggravated robbery, failure to comply

Suspect Name: Mauricio Arturo Alvarado Ruiz, Oscar Romelio Gonsalez Escobar
Title: Bonds set for men arrested after car slams into front of a popular Mason restaurant
description: On January 20, 2026, a vehicle crashed into the front of Quatman Cafe, a popular restaurant on West Main Street in Mason, Ohio. This was the third such incident at the restaurant in 15 years. Police reported that speed and alcohol may have been contributing factors in the latest crash. Mauricio Arturo Alvarado Ruiz, 27, was identified as the driver and was arrested at the scene. Oscar Romelio Gonsalez Escobar, 31, was also arrested in connection with the incident. Ruiz faces charges of receiving stolen property, operating a vehicle under the influence (OVI), and failure to comply with a police order. Escobar is charged with receiving stolen property and obstructing official business. The crash caused damage to the building's facade. Bond was set at $35,000 for Ruiz and $25,000 for Escobar, with both scheduled to appear in court on January 27, 2026.
Charges: Ruiz: receiving stolen property, OVI, failure to comply with police order Escobar: receiving stolen property, obstructing official business

Title: Cincinnati police make arrest after shots fired Saturday night on the Clay Wade Bailey Bridge
description: On April 26, 2026, Cincinnati police responded to a violent incident that began as an argument at a downtown gas station near Linn and West 8th Streets. The dispute escalated when a firearm was allegedly involved. Shortly after, police say the suspect followed a vehicle onto the Clay Wade Bailey Bridge and fired shots toward it while driving. No injuries were reported. Officers later located and arrested 22-year-old Daniel Jackson-Bey in the Over-the-Rhine neighborhood at 12th and Walnut Streets. During the arrest, police recovered a handgun and two shell casings. The investigation indicated that the victim helped identify the suspect vehicle. Jackson-Bey was taken into custody and faced multiple felony charges connected to the shooting incident, including assault-related offenses and firearm discharge.
Charges: Two felony assault charges, discharging a firearm, disorderly conduct

Title: Driver charged with OVI after escaping before train crashes into his car
description: On April 17, 2026, a driver in Willoughby, Ohio was involved in a crash after leaving his vehicle on CSX train tracks near Erie and Depot Streets. According to police, the driver exited the car before an Amtrak train struck and destroyed it around 3:30 a.m. No injuries were reported. Authorities believe alcohol may have been a contributing factor in the incident. The driver, identified as Sean Boyden, was later charged with operating a vehicle under the influence (OVI). The crash remains under investigation by local police. Officials emphasized the dangers of impaired driving and noted the outcome could have been far more serious given the involvement of a train collision. Boyden is scheduled to appear in Willoughby Municipal Court for arraignment.
Charges: Operating a vehicle impaired (OVI)

Title: Driver arrested after Garfield Heights police chase
description: On January 9, 2026, Garfield Heights police attempted to stop a vehicle that was allegedly speeding on Granger Road. The driver, identified as Isaiah Joseph Coats, refused to pull over and led officers on a short high-speed chase reaching about 90 mph. The pursuit ended when Coats crashed into a light pole on Turney Road near Ella Avenue. He then fled the vehicle on foot, but officers quickly pursued and arrested him without further incident. He was taken to a local hospital for treatment after the crash. Two passengers were reportedly inside the vehicle at the time but remained in the car during the arrest.
Charges: Fleeing and eluding

Title: Westlake Police arrest Cleveland man for OVI, loaded firearm located in vehicle
description: On January 11, 2026, Westlake police responded to a call from a concerned motorist reporting a vehicle stopped in the roadway on Columbia Road between Hilliard and Center Ridge Road. Officers arrived and found the car motionless with brake lights on and the driver reportedly unconscious behind the wheel while the vehicle remained in drive. Police used cruisers to block the vehicle to prevent it from moving before waking the driver. The 28-year-old Cleveland man was found to be impaired and declined field sobriety and breath tests. During the investigation, officers located a loaded 9mm firearm inside the vehicle along with an open container of alcohol. He was arrested for OVI and related offenses.
Charges: OVI (Operating a Vehicle Impaired), Using weapons while intoxicated, Possession of an open container in a motor vehicle

Title: New Philadelphia man speeds away from Dollar General robbery with 2 kids in car, deputies say
description: Dyllan Riter, a 28-year-old man from New Philadelphia, Ohio, was accused of committing two armed robberies at Dollar General stores in Waynesburg and East Sparta, Ohio. According to deputies, he allegedly held store clerks at knifepoint during the robberies and stole hundreds of dollars in cash. Authorities reported that after the robberies, Riter fled the scene in a vehicle while two children, aged 10 months and 5 years, were inside the car. Law enforcement attempted to conduct a traffic stop, but he allegedly refused to comply and drove away at high speeds, endangering public safety. The Stark County Sheriff’s Office stated that he was later taken into custody and is being held on related matters in Tuscarawas County Jail. The case involves both violent robbery allegations and serious child endangerment due to the presence of young passengers during his escape.
Charges: Aggravated robbery, child endangering, failure to comply with police order, theft

Title: Garfield Heights police use Grappler to stop wanted suspect in stolen car: caught on camera
description: Garfield Heights police in Ohio pursued a suspect driving a stolen vehicle that also contained a stolen firearm after officers attempted a traffic stop on Mapleleaf Drive near Turney Road. The driver, who was wanted on a felony warrant, refused to stop and led officers on a brief four-minute pursuit through the area. To end the chase safely, officers deployed a Grappler device, which snagged the rear driver’s side wheel and brought the car to a controlled stop. The suspect then exited the vehicle with his hands raised and was taken into custody without further incident. Police reported that the individual faces multiple charges including possession of a stolen car, possession of a stolen firearm, weapons under disability, fleeing and eluding, and a felony warrant. Authorities stated that the tactic was used to prevent further danger to the public during the pursuit. No injuries were reported during the incident response
Charges: Stolen car, stolen firearm, weapons under disability, felony warrant, fleeing and eluding

Title: Toledo man accused of leading TPD on 100+ mph pursuit with baby in back seat
description: Toledo police investigated a high-speed pursuit involving Christopher Mack, a 21-year-old man accused of failing to stop for officers on South Detroit Avenue and South Avenue in Toledo, Ohio. According to court documents, officers activated lights and sirens, but Mack continued driving, allegedly reaching speeds over 100 mph. A 1-year-old child was in the back seat during the chase, while the child’s mother was in the front passenger seat. The pursuit began shortly after 2 a.m. and ended after officers stopped the vehicle. Mack was arrested at the scene and charged with felony fleeing and eluding, child endangerment, and multiple traffic-related offenses. Authorities later confirmed a grand jury indictment adding failure to comply with a police order and failure to stop after an accident. No injuries were reported, and the child was safely recovered. The case is being handled through the Lucas County court system in Toledo Ohio court system
Charges: Felony fleeing and eluding, child endangerment, failure to comply with police order, failure to stop after an accident, traffic violations

Title: Perry Township police chase ends with two crashes, utility pole damage
description: Police in Perry Township, Ohio investigated a pursuit involving Mark Ertle after officers attempted a traffic stop due to reported speeding near Lincoln Way and Genoa Avenue. Ertle allegedly refused to stop, leading officers on a brief pursuit that was later terminated for safety concerns. Shortly after, he was involved in a crash with another vehicle at the Genoa Avenue and 12th Street intersection, during which a passenger exited the car. Ertle continued driving and later struck a utility pole on 12th Street, causing downed live electrical wires and additional roadway hazards. Following the second crash, he fled on foot but was quickly apprehended by responding officers. Authorities confirmed that Ertle was wanted on an outstanding warrant and now faces additional charges related to fleeing police and both crashes. Emergency services and utility crews responded to secure the scene and restore safety after the collisions and downed power lines and area.
Charges: Outstanding warrant, fleeing and eluding, traffic violations, crash-related charges

Title: Man arrested after robbing store with knife, leading police on pursuit in Wadsworth
description: Wadsworth police responded to a robbery at the Minit Mart convenience store on College Street in Wadsworth, Ohio, where a suspect used a knife to commit the offense early in the morning. The suspect allegedly took an undisclosed amount of cash and forced the store clerk into a cooler before fleeing the scene on foot. Officers quickly identified the suspect and conducted surveillance at his residence. Later that morning, police observed him leaving in a vehicle and attempted a traffic stop, but he refused to comply and led officers on a pursuit. The chase ended when the suspect returned to his residence on West Street, where officers arrested him without further incident. Authorities confirmed that the suspect was taken into custody and charged in connection with aggravated robbery, kidnapping, and failure to comply with police orders. No injuries to the clerk or officers were reported during the incident and response.
Charges: Aggravated robbery, kidnapping, failure to comply with police

Title: Stark County Sheriff tracks down man out on parole for murder with drone
description: Stark County Sheriff’s deputies in Ohio used drone technology to locate and arrest John David Osler after he fled the scene of a traffic-related incident in Nimishillen Township. Authorities stated that Osler was already wanted on an active parole violation warrant and was on parole for a prior 1992 murder conviction in Cuyahoga County. After he fled following a traffic accident, deputies launched a drone equipped with thermal imaging to search nearby wooded areas. The drone operator detected a heat signature consistent with a person hiding in the woods and guided deputies on the ground toward the suspect’s location. Video footage showed Osler moving through dense trees while deputies closed in. He was eventually taken into custody without further incident. Law enforcement confirmed he was booked into jail on the outstanding warrant. The operation highlighted the use of aerial surveillance technology in locating suspects attempting to evade arrest in rural terrain.
Charges: Parole violation (warrant), fleeing after traffic accident

Title: Watch video: Man arrested after van drives onto Atlantic High's athletic fields
description: A 43-year-old man was arrested in Delray Beach, Florida, after driving an unauthorized vehicle onto the athletic fields of Atlantic Community High School during a school track and field event. According to officials, the incident occurred on school grounds while students and spectators were present, forcing the event to be canceled due to safety concerns. Video footage showed the vehicle performing reckless maneuvers on the field, including driving across the grass and damaging fencing near the softball area. Athletes and attendees reportedly fled the scene as the situation unfolded. Police intervened and took the driver, identified as Dimson Cazius, into custody. Authorities charged him with criminal mischief exceeding $1,000, trespassing on school property, reckless driving, and driving with a suspended license. He also faced city citations for DUI-related offenses and refusal to submit to testing. No injuries were reported, but the school emphasized safety concerns following the incident.
Charges: Criminal mischief over $1,000; trespassing on school grounds; reckless driving; driving while license suspended; DUI citation; refusal to submit to test; refusal to sign citation

Title: Pursuit in Holmes County ends in arrest
description: A high-speed pursuit in Holmes County, Florida ended in the arrest of a man identified as Tyler Hutto after deputies attempted to stop a stolen vehicle and trailer. According to the Holmes County Sheriff’s Office, deputies were initially called to a residence on Highway 2 after a report that Hutto had stolen a vehicle and trailer from an individual. About 30 minutes later, a deputy located the suspect vehicle traveling westbound and attempted a traffic stop. During the stop attempt, the suspect allegedly struck a patrol vehicle, prompting a pursuit. The chase reached speeds exceeding 130 mph along Highway 2. Near Highway 177-A, the suspect vehicle suffered a blown tire, allowing deputies to execute a PIT maneuver and force the vehicle off the road. After stopping, Hutto resisted arrest and was subdued using a Taser. Authorities also reported suspected narcotics were thrown from the vehicle during the pursuit. He faces multiple felony charges including aggravated fleeing, assault, and grand theft auto.
Charges: Aggravated fleeing and eluding, reckless driving, aggravated assault with a vehicle, grand theft auto, driving while license suspended, resisting arrest without violence, violation of probation

Title: Bumper Dragging: Tarpon Springs Police Nab Oldsmar Suspect In Brutal US 19 Hit-And-Run
description: A 23-year-old Oldsmar man, Tarrin Gold, was arrested in connection with a violent hit-and-run crash on US 19 in Tarpon Springs, Florida, on April 29, 2026. According to police, a Hyundai Sonata struck a motorcycle near Martin Luther King Jr. Drive and then fled the scene without rendering aid. Witnesses and surveillance footage showed the damaged vehicle with a missing rear bumper and taillight housing as it sped away through Pinellas County. Investigators tracked the car to Oldsmar, where they identified and detained Gold with assistance from the Pinellas County Sheriff's Office. He was taken into custody and charged with leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury, fleeing and eluding law enforcement, and failure to render aid. The investigation remains ongoing as authorities review additional evidence and witness statements related to the incident and the suspect's actions after the collision in Tarpon Springs. Florida case continues ongoing
Charges: Leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury, fleeing and eluding law enforcement, failure to render aid

Title: Hit and run driver arrested, caught huffing nitrous oxide in Gainesville
description: On January 7, 2026, in Gainesville, Florida, police arrested 36-year-old Daisy Mason following a hit-and-run crash on Southwest Archer Road. Authorities said she rear-ended another vehicle and then fled the scene, leaving behind a damaged car and a report of possible injury from the other driver. Investigators were able to identify her using the vehicle tag number provided by the victim. Officers later found Mason at her residence, where she was reportedly inhaling nitrous oxide from a can of “Galaxy Gas,” commonly referred to as laughing gas. Police stated she refused repeated commands to stop using the substance, and officers removed the can and took her into custody. Several similar cans were reportedly found in her vehicle, suggesting repeated use. She was arrested and booked into the Alachua County Jail on multiple charges related to the crash and her conduct during arrest. No life-threatening injuries were reported from the collision scene.
Charges: Leaving the scene of a crash Inhaling a harmful substance (nitrous oxide) Resisting arrest

Title: Columbus man charged after Meigs County police chase ends in crash
description: A police pursuit in Meigs County, Ohio ended in a crash after a driver attempted to flee from law enforcement following a report involving a vehicle complaint in Middleport. According to police, an officer tried to make contact with the suspect, later identified as Jay Hunley, when he drove away, initiating a high-speed chase through local streets. During the pursuit, the suspect allegedly drove at high speed along North Second Avenue and West Main Street in Pomeroy. While attempting to pass other vehicles, his car collided with another vehicle near a local business. The crash injured a woman and a 3-year-old child in the other vehicle, both of whom were taken to the hospital with minor injuries. The suspect was also injured but later released into police custody. Authorities charged Hunley with felony fleeing and driving under suspension. The case remains under investigation by local law enforcement.
Charges: Felony fleeing, driving under suspension

Title: Brookville PD chase ends with four arrested for alleged car theft
description: On March 24, 2026, Brookville Police responded to multiple reports of suspicious activity and vehicle thefts around 2:35 a.m. A stolen GMC Acadia fled from officers and crashed into a Brookville PD cruiser. A high-speed chase ensued, with the vehicle reaching over 100 mph east on Westbrook Road toward Englewood. Englewood PD deployed stop sticks to safely stop the vehicle. Another brief pursuit occurred until the car stopped on a curb in Trotwood. Four suspects—one adult and three juveniles—were apprehended without incident by a coordinated effort including Brookville, Englewood, Trotwood, Huber Heights Police Departments, Montgomery County Sheriff’s Office, and Five Rivers MetroParks Rangers. Authorities recovered multiple stolen firearms, other stolen property, and found one juvenile had removed their ankle monitoring device. The vehicle itself had been stolen from Brookville and was left unlocked with the keys inside, along with a firearm and ammunition.
Charges: Vehicle theft, felony warrants for grand theft of a motor vehicle, failure to comply with court order, tampering with evidence

Title: Miami Beach Police drone captures video of man stealing motorcycle; suspect in custody
description: On March 10, 2026, Miami Beach Police used their drone surveillance system to track and apprehend a suspected motorcycle thief in Miami Beach, Florida. The incident began when the department’s license plate recognition technology detected a motorcycle that had been reported stolen entering the city. A police drone quickly located the motorcycle and relayed its position to officers on the ground. According to authorities, the rider attempted to evade police by driving recklessly through busy areas of South Beach. The suspect allegedly traveled against traffic, rode on a sidewalk, entered residential areas, moved through alleys, and eventually abandoned the motorcycle while trying to escape on foot. Surveillance footage from a nearby business captured part of the incident. Police officers used information from the drone and ground units to locate and arrest the suspect shortly afterward. Officials highlighted the case as an example of how drone technology assists law enforcement in identifying stolen vehicles and apprehending offenders safely and efficiently.
Charges: Grand Theft Auto Fleeing and Eluding Authorities Resisting Arrest

Title: Man accused of leading Escambia County deputies on chase in stolen car
description: On February 16, 2026, deputies with the Escambia County Sheriff’s Office located a vehicle that had been reported stolen in the area of Massachusetts Avenue in Escambia County, Florida. When officers attempted to stop the driver, the suspect allegedly fled, initiating a short vehicle pursuit. During the chase, law enforcement deployed a Precision Immobilization Technique (PIT) maneuver to bring the vehicle to a stop. The driver was then taken into custody without further incident. Authorities identified the suspect as 28-year-old Keontre Forbes. Investigators confirmed the vehicle had been reported stolen prior to the incident. The pursuit ended quickly, and no additional injuries were reported in connection with the arrest. The suspect was transported for booking following the stop. Law enforcement emphasized that the case involved both vehicle theft and an attempt to evade police after being spotted driving the stolen car. The investigation was handled by the Escambia County Sheriff’s Office.
Charges: Possession of a Stolen Vehicle Fleeing and Eluding

Title: Man arrested in connection with string of Winter Park burglaries, police say
description: On Saturday, Winter Park Police Department officers arrested 39-year-old Joel Rosario in connection with a series of residential burglaries in the Winter Park area of Florida. Authorities said the investigation began after multiple burglaries were reported along the Phelps corridor. During a surveillance operation, officers heard loud bangs and observed Rosario allegedly fleeing from an unoccupied residence. Police stated that Rosario attempted to escape in a vehicle and, while doing so, struck an unmarked police car, escalating the incident. A BOLO alert was issued, and the Orange County Sheriff’s Office later located the suspect vehicle. After a brief pursuit, Rosario exited the vehicle and attempted to flee on foot but was quickly apprehended by deputies. Investigators linked him to multiple burglaries occurring over a five-day period, though no confirmed connection to victims was identified at the time. He was taken into custody following the coordinated law enforcement response and surveillance operation.
Charges: Aggravated battery on a law enforcement officer Burglary Criminal mischief Resisting a law enforcement officer with violence Fleeing or eluding a law enforcement officer

Title: 4 arrested in Volusia County after armed carjacking ends in multi-county chase, police say
description: On February 20, 2026, four individuals were arrested in Volusia County, Florida, after an armed carjacking led to a multi-county police chase. According to police, the group stole a vehicle at gunpoint in Seminole County and fled, prompting alerts across neighboring jurisdictions. A Port Orange Police Department officer later spotted the stolen vehicle behind a gas station and attempted a traffic stop. The driver, identified as Joseph Luna, fled from the stop, leading officers on a pursuit. During the chase, the suspect vehicle crashed into a road sign. After the crash, two teenagers stayed inside the vehicle, while Luna and another suspect ran on foot. Law enforcement agencies including Port Orange Police Department, Seminole County Sheriff’s Office, and Volusia County Sheriff’s Office joined the search effort. All four suspects were eventually captured. Officers recovered a handgun, ski masks, and gloves from the vehicle, and all suspects were taken into custody.
Charges: Armed carjacking (all 4 suspects) Fleeing and eluding (Joseph Luna – additional charge)

Title: Olympic runner Sha’Carri Richardson pleads not guilty in super speeder case in Orange County
description: Sha'Carri Richardson, an Olympic sprinter, was stopped in Orange County, Florida, on State Road 429 after deputies alleged she was driving 104 mph in a 65 mph zone. Officers reported she was tailgating, flashing her headlights to move traffic, and making unsafe lane changes in an Aston Martin. During the stop, she apologized to deputies and said she was unaware of her speed, claiming a phone issue and possible tire underinflation. Body camera footage captured her speaking with officers. She was charged under a new Florida law criminalizing driving over 100 mph in a dangerous manner. The incident occurred near Orlando and led to her arrest and release on bond the same day. Her boyfriend arrived later at the scene and faced separate charges. Richardson pleaded not guilty in court, and the case remains pending. Authorities continue reviewing bodycam evidence and witness statements in Orange County case ongoing investigation
Charges: Excessive speeding (driving 104 mph in a 65 mph zone under Florida super speeder law)

Title: Road rage incident leads to aggravated assault arrest
description: An 18-year-old Cape Coral man, Dismas Jeffrey Ballez, was arrested after a road rage incident escalated into an aggravated assault investigation in Lee County, Florida. Police responded late Wednesday night to reports near Santa Barbara Boulevard North and Northeast Pine Island Road, where a driver allegedly pointed a firearm at another motorist before fleeing. The victim reported that suspect, driving a black Cadillac sedan, displayed a black handgun with a green laser attachment and aimed it toward him while making threatening statements. Officers located the vehicle shortly after at a nearby parking lot and identified Ballez as the driver. A passenger confirmed he had brandished the weapon during the encounter. Investigators recovered a handgun from the car and seized it as evidence. Authorities stated Ballez claimed he was scared during the incident. He was taken into custody and charged with aggravated assault with a deadly weapon and held on bond.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon

Title: Findlay man accused of stealing felony amount of items, leading police on chase
description: Christopher Anders, a 37-year-old man from Findlay, Ohio, was arrested following a retail theft incident that escalated into a police pursuit. According to police, officers were dispatched to Dick’s Sporting Goods on Tiffin Avenue after reports that a suspect left the store with a cart full of merchandise without paying and loaded it into an SUV. Police located the vehicle nearby and attempted a traffic stop, but the driver fled, leading officers on a chase through city streets. The pursuit reached speeds of approximately 60 miles per hour, during which the suspect ran a red light at Tiffin Avenue and G Street before eventually stopping at a Wendy’s restaurant. Anders was taken into custody without further incident. Authorities reported that the SUV contained a felony amount of stolen goods from multiple stores. He was charged with theft and fleeing and eluding police. The investigation remains ongoing as officials review evidence.
Charges: Theft, fleeing and eluding

Title: Toledo domestic violence, burglary suspect tries to board moving train while fleeing police, TPD says
description: Deonte Pettaway, a 30-year-old man from Toledo, Ohio, was arrested after a domestic violence and aggravated burglary incident that escalated into a police pursuit. Authorities say Pettaway broke into his ex-partner’s apartment through a bedroom window and assaulted her, with reports also alleging strangulation. After the attack, he fled the scene in a vehicle, prompting Toledo Police Department officers to initiate a pursuit. During the chase, Pettaway abandoned the vehicle and attempted to escape on foot. In a further attempt to avoid capture, he tried to board a moving train but suffered a non-life-threatening leg injury. Officers were able to apprehend him shortly after the incident. He was taken to a medical facility for treatment and then placed into custody. Pettaway faces multiple felony charges, including aggravated burglary, strangulation, and failure to comply with law enforcement. The case remains under investigation by Toledo authorities.

Title: YPD: Teen arrested fleeing party at rental home, faces gun charge

Officers arrived around 2:20 a.m. following reports of a gathering involving multiple individuals, several of whom fled when police arrived. During the incident, a male teen was observed with a firearm in his waistband as he ran from officers. Police say the suspect threw a loaded 9mm handgun into a nearby yard while attempting to escape but was later apprehended on Dover Road. The firearm was recovered and identified as a semiautomatic pistol. Other individuals who fled the scene were also located, including two girls found hiding nearby who reported that attendees at the party were armed. The arrested teen was taken into custody and charged with tampering with evidence, carrying a concealed weapon, and obstructing official business. He was booked into juvenile detention pending further legal proceedings.

Title: WATCH: Ohio man leads police chase, crashes and jumps into Great Miami River
description: Juan Harris, a 31-year-old man from Dayton, Ohio, was arrested after a multi-agency police pursuit that began when officers attempted to stop a stolen vehicle. Franklin police were alerted by Middletown officers who were already in pursuit of the suspect vehicle traveling into their jurisdiction. Authorities say the driver ran a red light, continued at high speed, and later struck a parked vehicle while attempting to evade police. After the crash, Harris fled on foot and jumped into the Great Miami River in an apparent attempt to escape capture. Officers apprehended him after the incident and transported him to a hospital for treatment before booking him into Warren County Jail. No major life-threatening injuries were reported for the suspect, though the driver of the struck vehicle was hospitalized. Harris faces multiple charges, including failure to comply, obstructing official business, and receiving stolen property. The investigation remains ongoing.
Charges: Failure to comply, obstructing official business, receiving stolen property

Title: Two women arrested on more than 30 warrants, thefts dating back to 2019
description: Danielle Custard and Latoya Carter were arrested by U.S. Marshals in Fairfield Township, Ohio, after being wanted on more than 30 active warrants across multiple counties in Ohio and Kentucky. Police say the suspects were linked to a long-running series of retail thefts dating back to 2019, involving stores such as Old Navy, Kohl’s, and other retail outlets. Investigators reported that Custard alone was responsible for thefts totaling thousands of dollars. Authorities also noted both women had warrants related to reckless fleeing from police in addition to theft charges. Custard had 24 active warrants, while Carter had eight. The arrests were the result of a coordinated effort between Fairfield Township Police Department, Butler County Sheriff’s Office, and the Southern Ohio Fugitive Apprehension Strike Team. Custard was booked into the Hamilton County Justice Center, while Carter was already in custody in Butler County Jail since January 2026.
Charges: Theft, multiple active warrants, reckless fleeing police

Title: Fort Myers DUI suspect accused of leading deputies on chase, causing crash on Winkler Rd
description: Corey Dee German, a 44-year-old man, was arrested in Fort Myers, Florida, after deputies say he caused a crash while fleeing a traffic stop. According to the Lee County Sheriff’s Office, deputies initially observed German driving erratically on South Tamiami Trail and attempted to initiate a traffic stop. German allegedly refused to stop and sped away, leading deputies on a brief pursuit. During the chase, law enforcement attempted to deploy a grappler device to stop his vehicle, but it was unsuccessful. Police say German lost control of his vehicle while accelerating and collided with another car at the intersection of Winkler Road and Gladiolus Drive. Both drivers were injured and taken to a hospital. Authorities reported that medical staff indicated German had a blood alcohol level of 0.07. After being medically cleared, he was taken into custody. He faces charges including fleeing and eluding, DUI with property damage, and driving with a suspended license.
Charges: Fleeing and eluding law enforcement DUI with property damage Driving with a suspended license

Title: ECSO chase: Stolen car drives through yard, crashes in wooded area
description: Michael Peavy and Lilian McDaniel were arrested in Escambia County, Florida, after deputies say they were involved in a pursuit involving a stolen vehicle. Law enforcement used a license plate reader to identify a white Nissan Versa reported stolen in Port St. Lucie. Deputies attempted a traffic stop near Olive Road and North Palafox Street, but the driver allegedly fled, initiating a chase. During the pursuit, deputies tried to deploy a pit maneuver, but it was unsuccessful. The vehicle continued into a residential area, where it drove through a backyard, struck a children’s playset, and eventually crashed in a wooded area off a dead-end road. Both occupants were taken into custody following the crash. Authorities also reported finding a firearm and ammunition in the vehicle. McDaniel told deputies she was just a passenger getting a ride. Both suspects were charged after the investigation, which included stolen vehicle and firearm-related offenses.
Charges: Grand theft auto Fleeing and eluding law enforcement Possession of firearm by convicted felon Additional related charges

Title: Coral Springs 19-year-old accused of driving getaway car in chase after shooting
description: A 19-year-old man from Coral Springs, Florida, identified as Kervens Septama, was arrested in connection to a shooting and police chase in Lauderdale Lakes on May 7, 2026. Deputies with the Broward Sheriff's Office say Septama acted as the getaway driver in a Toyota Corolla after a group allegedly fired shots into a minivan carrying seven minors. No injuries were reported in the shooting. The victim told investigators the suspects blocked her vehicle in an apartment complex parking lot, approached with guns, and fired shots before fleeing. Law enforcement located the suspect vehicle and attempted a traffic stop, but Septama fled, leading deputies on a chase through residential areas, including driving through a yard and into oncoming lanes. A PIT maneuver ended the pursuit when the car crashed into a pole. All occupants ran; deputies said Septama dropped a Glock while fleeing and was captured with K-9 units after a search involving canals and backyards. He faces felony charges.
Charges: Aggravated fleeing with damage, resisting an officer without violence, carrying a concealed firearm

Title: Man accused of hitting 3-year-old boy running across beach in alleged DUI
description: Brock Winkler, a 36-year-old man, was arrested in Daytona Beach, Florida, after allegedly driving under the influence and striking a 3-year-old boy on a beach. According to law enforcement reports, Winkler was operating a Jeep on the beach when the child ran across traffic lanes near the shoreline and was hit at a low speed. The child sustained a concussion and a hairline cervical spine fracture but did not require surgery and was later discharged from the hospital. Deputies from the Volusia County Sheriff’s Office reported that Winkler showed clear signs of intoxication, including smelling of alcohol, poor balance, and inability to complete field sobriety tests. Witnesses stated he had consumed multiple beers earlier in the day and even displayed images of empty cans under his vehicle. He was arrested and charged with DUI causing bodily injury and refusal to submit to DUI testing. He was also on pretrial release for a prior burglary case.
Charges: DUI causing bodily injury; refusal to submit to DUI testing

Title: Volusia County deputies use paddleboards to catch fleeing suspect near Daytona Beach
description: Chase Cruz, a 28-year-old man, was arrested in the Daytona Beach area of Florida after fleeing from deputies during an encounter with the Volusia County Sheriff’s Office. According to reports, Cruz was initially being questioned by law enforcement when he suddenly ran from deputies while they were reading him his rights. This triggered a foot pursuit that extended into nearby waterways after Cruz jumped into a river in an attempt to escape. Deputies followed the suspect using paddleboards and continued the chase on water. As Cruz became exhausted and struggled to stay afloat, officers reached him and assisted him onto their paddleboards before returning him to shore. Once back on land, he was taken into custody without further incident. Authorities stated that Cruz was charged with loitering, prowling, and resisting arrest. Officials did not specify the original reason for the questioning that led to the encounter prior to his attempted escape.
Charges: Loitering, prowling, resisting arrest

Title: Chase leads to I-95 crash in Pompano Beach. Man is arrested; road has reopened
description: A 37-year-old man was arrested in Pompano Beach, Florida after a police pursuit that began in Deerfield Beach and ended in a multi-vehicle crash on Interstate 95. According to the Broward Sheriff’s Office, deputies were initially responding to a reported theft when the suspect allegedly committed battery on a law enforcement officer during the investigation. He then fled the scene in a vehicle, prompting deputies to initiate a chase. The pursuit continued onto I-95, where the suspect’s vehicle crashed, involving at least one patrol car and two other civilian vehicles. The crash caused significant traffic disruption, shutting down southbound lanes for several hours. The suspect, identified as Avonta Bailey, was taken into custody and transported to a hospital with non-life-threatening injuries. Authorities stated he has a prior criminal history, including previous convictions for armed robbery, aggravated assault, and burglary. The deputy involved in the crash was not seriously injured.
Charges: Battery on a law enforcement officer, aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, fleeing and eluding police, retail theft

Title: Pensacola child abuse suspect says injuries were self-inflicted, according to arrest report
description: Dynisha Blunt, a 33-year-old Santa Rosa County corrections officer, was arrested in Escambia County, Florida, on child neglect charges after a 3-year-old foster child in her care was found with severe injuries. Doctors at a West Florida Hospital emergency facility noticed bruises, abrasions, possible burns, swelling, malnourishment, and a head hematoma when the child was brought in for treatment. Blunt allegedly became agitated when medical staff raised concerns about abuse and left the hospital with the child before returning during a police search. Deputies later conducted a traffic stop in Pace, where she claimed the injuries were caused by a skateboard fall and time-out discipline. Investigators also found another foster child with additional injuries, prompting removal of all foster children by child welfare authorities. Blunt and another caregiver were both arrested and charged with child neglect resulting in great bodily harm. She was later fired from her correctional officer position investigation.
Charges: Two counts of child neglect resulting in great bodily harm

Title: Cape man charged with DUI, hit and run and DUI with property damage

When officers arrived, they found a car crashed into bushes with front-end damage, a damaged windshield, and skid marks leading toward the canal embankment. Witnesses reported seeing a shirtless man wearing blue shorts flee the area and run toward nearby woods. Officers later located the suspect, identified as Jacob Blasses, who showed visible injuries consistent with moving through brush. Police observed signs of impairment including slurred speech, watery eyes, and balance issues. A witness confirmed he was the driver of the crashed vehicle. Investigation showed the vehicle struck a mailbox, which then damaged another parked car. Blasses agreed to sobriety testing and later provided breath samples showing a high blood alcohol level. Title: Man turns himself after hit and run in Gainesville left motorcyclist seriously injured, denied bond

The collision occurred at the intersection of SW 13th Street and SW 9th Avenue when Lewis allegedly struck the motorcyclist while driving a car. After the crash, he left the scene without stopping or providing aid. Authorities reported that the motorcyclist suffered significant injuries requiring medical attention. Following the incident, Lewis later turned himself in to police. He was arrested and formally charged with leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury, as well as driving with a suspended license knowingly causing serious bodily injury. description: A woman identified as Leandra Williams was arrested nearly two months after a hit-and-run crash during Bike Week in Daytona Beach. According to police, Williams struck two pedestrians who were crossing Harvey Avenue and then fled the scene without stopping to render aid or call emergency services. The victims later described severe injuries, including a concussion, fractured vertebrae, brain bleeds, skull fracture, and long-term complications requiring extensive medical treatment. Investigators said the suspect vehicle, a white Jeep Cherokee with Iowa tag “LUCKI23,” was identified after a witness followed the car immediately after the crash, photographed the license plate, and provided it to law enforcement. The vehicle remained damaged and was later spotted by police in another city before Williams was taken into custody. Title: Man arrested in Hutchinson after allegedly stealing school bus
description: Authorities in Wright County, Minnesota, pursued a stolen school bus driven by a suspect later identified as 41-year-old Joshua Thomas Moist. According to Hutchinson Police Department officers were notified around 9 a.m. by the Wright County Sheriff’s Office that a pursuit involving a stolen school bus had been discontinued. Authorities believed the adult male suspect was traveling to an address in Hutchinson. The bus was later spotted in the area of the suspected destination where officers conducted a high-risk traffic stop. Verbal commands were issued at gunpoint and the suspect complied exiting the vehicle without incident. Police identified the suspect as 41-year-old Joshua Thomas Moist who was taken into custody and transported back to Wright County where he is expected to face charges related to the incident. Charges: Stolen school bus, fleeing law enforcement (expected)

Title: Rochester Teen Arrested in Zumbrota For Driving Wrong Way on Hwy. 52
description: A 17-year-old Rochester teen was arrested in Zumbrota, Minnesota, after police responded to reports of a wrong-way driver on Highway 52. According to authorities, the vehicle was traveling northbound in the southbound lanes of the divided highway near Zumbrota around 6 a.m. Officers located the vehicle still driving in the wrong direction and were able to safely bring it to a stop without using force. No injuries were reported during the incident. Law enforcement stated that the teen was arrested on suspicion of driving under the influence of alcohol, and the case has been referred to the Goodhue County Attorney’s Office for potential charges. Officials did not specify when the wrong-way driving began or provide further details about impairment levels. The incident is being reviewed as a serious traffic safety matter due to the high risk posed to other motorists on the highway.
Charges: Suspicion of driving under the influence of alcohol

Title: 2 arrested for firing at house, vehicles in Apopka
description: Apopka police responded to reports of shots fired at a residence on Martin Place where multiple shell casings were found and property damage occurred to vehicles and fencing. Investigators determined that gunfire damaged a fence and several parked vehicles, though no residents were injured. Witnesses reported seeing two individuals firing from a silver sedan in the area of nearby streets before fleeing. Officers later observed a vehicle leaving the area at high speed and conducted a traffic stop. Inside the vehicle were two occupants who were detained after police found evidence linking them to the shooting. Surveillance footage from nearby homes helped identify Jesus Barragan as the alleged shooter and a 16-year-old male as the driver. Authorities say additional gunfire was heard during the incident, and a live round was found inside the stopped vehicle. Barragan was later arrested and charged after being identified as the primary suspect in the shooting.
Charges: Criminal mischief Causing property damage over $1,000 Shooting a missile into a dwelling/vehicle/aircraft (weapon offense)

Title: Rapper Lil Tjay arrested after Offset shot in Florida
description: A shooting occurred outside Seminole Hard Rock Hollywood casino in Florida in which former Migos rapper Offset was reportedly shot near a valet area. Following the incident, police detained two individuals in connection with the scene, including rapper Tione Merritt, known professionally as Lil Tjay. Authorities stated that Merritt was not accused of being the shooter but was arrested at the scene after being taken into custody during the investigation. He was later charged with disorderly conduct and driving without a valid license. Police confirmed that investigators were still working to identify additional suspects linked to the shooting. Merritt’s attorney publicly denied any involvement in the shooting, stating that he had not been charged with any violent offense. The victim, Offset, was transported to a hospital and was expected to recover. The case remains under investigation, with law enforcement continuing to review evidence and witness accounts from the casino valet area.
Charges: Disorderly conduct Driving without a valid license

Title: Collier County man accused of DUI crashes SUV on his way to file for divorce
description: Collier County, Florida
Charges: DUI with property damage

Title: Port St. Lucie man arrested for driving 90 mph in 40-mph zone
description: A 23-year-old man was arrested in Port St. Lucie, Florida, after police say he was caught driving at 90 mph in a 40-mph zone on NW Prima Vista Boulevard near Sportsman’s Park. Officers reported that the speed was more than double the posted limit in an area frequently used by families and community members. Law enforcement conducted a traffic stop after clocking the vehicle at the excessive speed. Following the stop, the driver was taken into custody and transported to the St. Lucie County Jail. Police issued a citation for a superspeed violation and emphasized public safety concerns, noting that excessive speeding significantly increases the risk of serious crashes and endangers both drivers and pedestrians. Authorities used the incident to remind the public to obey posted speed limits and drive responsibly, especially in high-traffic recreational areas where children and families are often present. No injuries were reported in the incident.
Charges: Superspeed violation (driving 90 mph in a 40-mph zone), citation issued

Title: Elyria man arrested for 7th OVI in Westlake
description: Westlake Police arrested 46-year-old John Leslie Francisco after a traffic stop in a parking lot at the Sonesta Suites on Clemens Road. Officers initially stopped the vehicle for a license violation and discovered the driver had a suspended license due to prior traffic offenses. During the stop, police observed signs of impairment including slurred speech, bloodshot eyes, and the odor of alcohol. Francisco reportedly admitted he had been drinking hours earlier. He was unable to handle his identification properly and handed over his entire wallet to officers. Authorities said he refused both field sobriety testing and a breath test. Due to his history of six prior OVI convictions dating back to 1999, the new offense was treated as a felony. He was arrested on charges of operating a vehicle impaired (OVI) and driving under suspension. He was later held in jail and released on bond after court proceedings.
Charges: OVI (Operating a Vehicle Impaired); driving under suspension

Title: Pursuit, remote-control license plate cover leads to arrest
description: Officers in Warren, Ohio attempted to stop a 22-year-old driver, Alexander Solorzano Benavides, after he allegedly ran a red light at West Market Street and Tod Avenue SW. The driver refused to pull over, initiating a pursuit through several side streets and along East Market Street before entering Central Parkway. Police deployed stop sticks to disable his 2025 Mercedes-Benz, bringing the vehicle to a stop. During a search, officers discovered a loaded rifle placed on the backseat floorboard. Investigators also reported a tinted, remote-controlled license plate cover that concealed the Ohio registration. When officers activated the device, the plate became visible, revealing the custom plate reading “VRROOMM.” The suspect was taken into custody and charged with failure to comply with police officer, improper handling of a firearm in a motor vehicle, and possession of criminal tools related to the plate device. He later pleaded not guilty in Warren Municipal Court.
Charges: Failure to comply with police officer Improper handling of a firearm in a motor vehicle Possession of criminal tools

Title: Officials decide if Daytona Beach police officer will face charges after viral video of arrest
description: A police incident in Daytona Beach, Florida involved a 27-year-old man, David Anderson, during an arrest initiated after he was stopped for allegedly having an open container, which violates city ordinance. Body camera footage shows the situation escalating after Anderson tossed an item toward Officer Joel Llinas during the encounter. Officers proceeded to arrest Anderson, and he was placed in handcuffs. While Anderson was restrained on the ground, the video shows Officer Llinas applying force, including striking Anderson multiple times while holding him down. The officer later stated in the arrest report that Anderson allegedly bit his wrist during the struggle. The video led to public scrutiny and an official review by the State Attorney’s Office in Volusia County to determine whether criminal charges should be filed against the officer. The incident also prompted an internal investigation by the Daytona Beach Police Department. Anderson was charged and later released on bond.
Charges: Battery on an officer (felony) Open container violation (misdemeanor)

Title: PIT maneuver ends chase through Iona neighborhood after suspect rammed modular home with truck
description: Joseph Absalon, a 35-year-old male, was arrested following a dangerous incident in Iona, Florida. According to the Lee County Sheriff's Office, deputies responded to reports of an aggravated assault on Timothy Lane. Witnesses reported that Absalon intentionally backed his truck onto a neighboring property, repeatedly striking a vehicle and a modular home approximately five times. After causing the damage, he drove away and stopped near another residence where deputies attempted to speak with him. Instead of complying, Absalon fled through the neighborhood in his truck. During the pursuit, he drove recklessly, struck a street sign, nearly collided with a marked patrol vehicle, and ignored deputies' emergency lights and sirens. To end the pursuit safely, deputies conducted a PIT maneuver, bringing the vehicle to a stop. Absalon was then taken into custody. Authorities stated that his actions created a significant risk to residents, property, and law enforcement officers throughout the incident.
Charges: Aggravated Assault with Intent to Commit a Felony  Criminal Mischief  Fleeing and Eluding Law Enforcement  Hit and Run  Violation of a Domestic Violence Injunction

Title: PBSO: Man fled deputies, hit patrol car, caused lockdown at St. Mary’s Medical Center
description: A male suspect was arrested by the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office after leading deputies on a vehicle pursuit through West Palm Beach, Florida, on the night of May 29, 2026. Deputies responded shortly after 9 p.m. and attempted to stop the suspect. During the incident, the suspect fled in a vehicle and side-swiped a marked sheriff’s patrol car while trying to escape. Authorities authorized a pursuit, which continued through the city with assistance from the Florida Highway Patrol and the West Palm Beach Police Department. The chase ended at St. Mary’s Medical Center, where the suspect abandoned his vehicle and entered the hospital. According to investigators, his wife was a patient at the facility. As a precaution, the hospital was placed on lockdown while law enforcement officers searched multiple floors for the suspect. Officers located and arrested him without further incident. No injuries were reported, and the investigation into the circumstances surrounding the pursuit remains ongoing.
Charges: Fleeing and Eluding Law Enforcement  Leaving the Scene / Vehicle Pursuit Related Offenses  Damage to a Marked Patrol Vehicle

Title: HCSO arrests carjacking suspect after high-speed pursuit
description: Marion Pina Miranda, 32, was arrested after a carjacking and high-speed pursuit in Sebring, Florida. According to authorities, the incident began when a victim reported that he had given Miranda a ride. During the encounter, Miranda allegedly punched the victim in the face and stole the victim’s silver Chevrolet Equinox. Shortly afterward, a Highlands County Sheriff's Office deputy located the stolen vehicle on East Claradge Avenue near State Road 17 and attempted a traffic stop. Miranda refused to stop and fled, initiating a high-speed pursuit. During the chase, speeds exceeded 100 miles per hour as the suspect drove recklessly through the area. The pursuit continued until Miranda eventually stopped on Arbuckle Creek Road near Scrubpens Road. Deputies and assisting officers then took him into custody without further incident. In addition to the carjacking allegation, Miranda received multiple traffic-related charges and citations stemming from his actions during the pursuit, including fleeing law enforcement and excessive speeding.
Charges: Carjacking  Fleeing and Eluding with Disregard to Safety  Dangerous Excessive Speeding (100 MPH or More)  Driving with a Suspended License  Three Stop Sign Violations  Failure to Drive in a Single Lane

Title: Convicted felon arrested on burglary charges in Gainesville after attempting to flee scene
description: Mikale Fuye, a 20-year-old convicted felon, was arrested in Gainesville, Florida, in connection with a residential burglary and subsequent attempt to evade law enforcement. Deputies with the Alachua County Sheriff’s Office responded to a burglary report at a residence where the garage door had been forced open and windows were broken. The victim reported approximately $6,000 in cash, gold jewelry, and a firearm stolen from the home. Investigators reviewed security footage and identified a suspicious vehicle registered to Fuye in the area around the time of the burglary. On May 20, 2026, deputies located the vehicle and initiated a traffic stop. Fuye attempted to flee, leading deputies on a pursuit. During the escape attempt, he crashed into another vehicle by rear-ending an SUV on Southwest 61st Street and then drove into a ditch near a children's playground. He fled on foot but was quickly apprehended by deputies and taken into custody after being stopped.
Charges: Burglary  Possession of a Firearm  Fleeing and Eluding Law Enforcement
Refrence number: Your request reference number is LERR2026-5806 and your security key is BC5B8181

Title: Driver arrested after fleeing crash that injured pedestrian
description: Samuel Shiete O’Reilly, 19, was arrested after allegedly fleeing the scene of a traffic crash that seriously injured a pedestrian in North Miami, Florida. According to police, the incident occurred on April 28, 2026, near Northeast 125th Street when a pedestrian attempting to cross the roadway was struck by a white Dodge Charger. Investigators said the driver failed to stop and left the scene immediately after the collision. The victim suffered a severe head laceration and was transported to a hospital by Miami-Dade Fire Rescue for medical treatment. During the investigation, a witness provided video footage that reportedly captured the crash and showed the vehicle fleeing eastbound. Later that afternoon, officers located the Dodge Charger nearby and conducted a traffic stop. O’Reilly was identified as the driver. Police stated that he waived his rights and provided statements consistent with the evidence collected during the investigation. He was subsequently arrested and booked into jail pending a bond hearing.
Charges: Leaving the Scene of a Crash Involving Serious Bodily Injury, fleeing crash

Title: Deputy 'Seriously Injured' Attempting to Stop Fleeing Suspect
description: Trevaun Hampton, 31, was arrested after allegedly leading Hernando County deputies on a pursuit through Brooksville, Florida, and seriously injuring a deputy during an attempted traffic stop. According to investigators, the incident began on May 9, 2026, near the intersection of North Main Street and North Broad Street when Deputy Juan Moore attempted to stop Hampton, who was operating a white Kawasaki minibike motorcycle. Authorities said Hampton accelerated as the deputy grabbed his shirt, causing the deputy to be dragged to the ground and suffer serious injuries to his hand, arm, leg, and knee. After the initial encounter, deputies located Hampton again near East Jefferson Street and Bell Avenue, but he allegedly fled a second time. Investigators stated that Hampton drove along a sidewalk during the pursuit, creating a danger to pedestrians. Deputies eventually cornered him on Oakland Avenue, where he reportedly refused commands before being physically restrained and taken into custody without further incident.
Charges: Aggravated Battery Causing Bodily Harm or Disability to a Law Enforcement Officer  Fleeing and Eluding Law Enforcement  Resisting an Officer with Violence  Operating a Vehicle with a Suspended License  Operating a Motorcycle Without Proper Endorsement  Operating an Unregistered Vehicle

Title: 2 arrested following high-speed car chase in Hendry County
description: Natarius Janard Harvey, 24, was arrested after leading Hendry County Sheriff's Office deputies on a high-speed pursuit that began during a traffic stop attempt in the Harlem community of Clewiston, Florida. Deputies attempted to stop a vehicle near 9th Street and Florida Avenue, but the driver refused to pull over and fled. During the pursuit, the vehicle traveled through multiple stop signs and accelerated onto U.S. Highway 27. Authorities reported speeds reached more than 100 miles per hour as deputies continued the chase. The pursuit ended in South Bay, where both occupants exited the vehicle and attempted to flee on foot. Deputies located Harvey in a fenced area and took him into custody. Investigators identified Harvey as the driver of the vehicle. He was charged with offenses related to the pursuit and driving privileges. No injuries were reported during the incident. Harvey was transported to jail following his arrest and booking procedures.Chamorian D. Thicklin, 23, was arrested following a high-speed pursuit involving a vehicle that fled from Hendry County Sheriff's Office deputies in the Harlem community of Clewiston, Florida. Deputies attempted a traffic stop near 9th Street and Florida Avenue, but the vehicle refused to stop and sped away. During the chase, the vehicle traveled through multiple stop signs and reached speeds exceeding 100 miles per hour while traveling on U.S. Highway 27. The pursuit continued until the vehicle stopped in South Bay, Florida. After the vehicle came to a stop, both occupants exited and attempted to flee on foot. Deputies pursued and apprehended Thicklin after a brief chase. Although authorities identified Natarius Janard Harvey as the driver, Thicklin was an active participant in the incident by fleeing from deputies after the vehicle stopped. He was taken into custody without reported injuries and transported to jail. Authorities charged him based on his actions and probation status.
Charges: Natarius Janard Harvey: Fleeing and Eluding Law Enforcement  Resisting Arrest  Driving with a Suspended License, Chamorian D. Thicklin: Resisting Arrest  Felony Probation Violation

Title: Florida man allegedly drove 102 mph with unrestrained 3-year-old, charged with DUI
description: On May 23, 2026, in Lehigh Acres, Florida, deputies with the Lee County Sheriff’s Office arrested Jorge Garcia after a high-speed DUI incident involving a young child. Authorities said Garcia was driving on State Road 82 when he was clocked at 102 mph in a 55 mph zone. During the traffic stop, deputies determined that a 3-year-old child was in the backseat and was not properly restrained. Garcia allegedly told officers he had been returning from a pool party where he consumed alcohol. Law enforcement reported signs consistent with impairment, leading to a DUI arrest. The child’s safety concerns were emphasized due to both the excessive speed and lack of proper seating restraints. Garcia was taken into custody at the scene. He was charged with driving over 100 mph, refusal to submit to DUI testing, and DUI with a minor in the vehicle.
Charges: Operating a vehicle over 100 mph, refusal to submit to DUI testing, DUI with a person under 18 in the vehicle

Title: Sarasota man accused of trying to lure girls into truck
description: A 67-year-old Sarasota man, Edward O’Neil Jr., was arrested after allegedly attempting to lure two girls, ages 12 and 13, into his pickup truck near Bay Road and U.S. 41 in Sarasota, Florida. According to police, the incident occurred on May 16, 2026, while the girls were riding bicycles on a sidewalk. O’Neil, driving a black Dodge Ram pickup truck, reportedly offered the girls a ride and suggested placing their bicycles in the back of his truck. Witnesses observed the interaction and became concerned, approaching the girls and warning the suspect to leave them alone. One witness told police she informed O’Neil that authorities were being contacted. Investigators reviewed traffic camera footage that reportedly showed the truck near the girls and the driver opening his door. Both girls later identified O’Neil in photo lineups. He was arrested during a traffic stop and booked into the Sarasota County Jail, where he was held without bond.
Charges: Attempting to lure or entice a child under 14 (two counts)

Title: Man arrested after high-speed chase in stolen vehicle
description: On May 21, 2026, in Gainesville, Florida, law enforcement arrested Nathaniel Gates, a 27-year-old man following a high-speed police chase involving a vehicle reported stolen from Atlanta, Georgia. Deputies attempted to stop the vehicle after it entered Alachua County on Interstate 75 northbound, but Gates allegedly fled, leading to a pursuit. The chase ended near the Alachua exit where the vehicle was stopped and both occupants were taken into custody. Authorities reported that a pregnant woman was also in the vehicle during the incident and was later evaluated medically before being detained. The case involved a stolen vehicle crossing state lines and evading law enforcement at high speed. Gates was booked into the Alachua County Jail without bond following his arrest. The investigation remained ongoing as officials reviewed the circumstances of the chase and the involvement of the second occupant.
Charges: Fleeing and eluding law enforcement, possession of a stolen vehicle
