Title: Cincinnati man facing sixth OVI charge after traffic stop by OSHP
description: Brandon Robinson, a 40-year-old man from Cincinnati, Ohio, was arrested following a traffic stop conducted by the Ohio State Highway Patrol. According to authorities, the stop occurred around 1:50 a.m. on Seymour Avenue near Paddock Road after troopers observed behavior consistent with impaired driving. During the stop, Robinson allegedly showed signs of intoxication and was taken into custody on suspicion of operating a vehicle under the influence. Further investigation revealed that Robinson had a significant history of prior OVI convictions spanning multiple years, including 2003, 2010, 2015, 2019, and 2021, making the new charge a repeat felony offense. He was also charged with operating a vehicle with a suspended license and refusing chemical testing while having prior OVI offenses on record. Robinson was transported to the Hamilton County Justice Center for booking and is expected to face court proceedings related to his sixth OVI-related arrest. Authorities continue monitoring repeat offender cases closely.
Charges: Operating a vehicle under the influence (OVI); operating with suspended license; OVI test refusal with prior OVI history

Title: West Salem man faces burglary charges in Rocky River apartment break-ins
description: Police in Rocky River, Ohio, arrested a 35-year-old West Salem man, Charles Meek, after a series of connected incidents involving a traffic stop and multiple apartment break-ins. Officers initially encountered Meek walking on Interstate 90 during a traffic stop involving a disabled vehicle. He was first arrested for disorderly conduct while intoxicated. Shortly afterward, police were called to Oxford Court Apartments for reports of a man entering a laundry room through a window and damaging property. Investigators linked the burglary to the earlier traffic stop after noticing a loose dog and identifying matching clothing evidence. Police said Meek was seen wearing distinctive orange clothing that was later found inside the apartment laundry room. Authorities determined that multiple apartments had been unlawfully entered, including one where a tenant was present. Meek attempted to flee when confronted but was later captured after changing clothes. He was charged with several counts of burglary, with additional charges pending.
Charges: Multiple counts of burglary; pending vandalism and theft charges; disorderly conduct while intoxicated

Title: Springfield man faces 10th OVI charge
description: Jonathan Piersoll, a man from Springfield, Ohio, was arrested by the Ohio State Highway Patrol following a traffic stop in which officers suspected impairment. According to officials, he displayed clear signs of intoxication while being evaluated during the stop. Records show this incident is part of a long history of impaired driving offenses, with seven prior OVI convictions recorded between 2001 and 2023. Authorities also noted that Piersoll has two additional pending OVI cases from November 2025 and April 2026, indicating repeated legal involvement for similar behavior. The current arrest adds to what prosecutors describe as his tenth alleged OVI charge. The stop was conducted after troopers observed driving behavior that raised safety concerns. He was taken into custody at the scene without reported incident. Law enforcement stated the case remains under review, and prior convictions are expected to be considered during court proceedings. Further legal action will proceed through the local Ohio court system.
Charges: Operating a Vehicle Under the Influence (10th offense alleged)

Title: Veteran police officer fired after alleged drunken crash while armed and in uniform
description: Kenneth Gallion, a 61-year-old part-time police officer from Chatfield, Minnesota, was arrested after being involved in a late-night car crash while allegedly intoxicated and still armed in full police uniform. According to reports, Gallion had completed a shift at the Minnesota State Fairgrounds and was driving shortly after midnight when witnesses observed his vehicle speeding at nearly 70 mph before crashing in Bloomington. Police said he was found at the scene wearing his uniform and carrying a firearm while displaying clear signs of impairment. Officials later stated he was over three times the legal alcohol limit. The incident led to immediate termination from both the Chatfield Police Department and his role at the state fairgrounds, despite his long career in law enforcement. Authorities indicated he may face charges related to driving while intoxicated and carrying a firearm while intoxicated. The case drew attention due to his decades-long service history and on-duty status.
Charges: Driving While Intoxicated (DWI); carrying a firearm while intoxicated

Title: Alachua man arrested after driving drunk in wrong direction
description: On Tuesday night in Alachua, Florida, police responded to reports of a vehicle traveling in the wrong direction on US Highway 441. Officers say 42-year-old Anh Nguyen was driving slowly against traffic while suspected of being under the influence of alcohol. Body camera footage released by Alachua Police shows officers positioning patrol vehicles to block Nguyen’s path and prevent him from continuing down the roadway. Despite attempts to leave, he was stopped and taken into custody without major incident. Authorities arrested him on suspicion of driving under the influence after determining he was impaired. He was booked into the Alachua County Jail with a bond set at $37,000. The incident raised concerns about roadway safety as wrong-way driving poses a serious risk of head-on collisions. Police continue to remind drivers to avoid impaired driving and report dangerous behavior immediately to law enforcement. Authorities are investigating the case further currently ongoing
Charges: Driving under the influence (DUI), wrong-way driving

Title: Suspected wrong-way drunk driver crashes into 3 cars in Estero
description: On April 30, 2026, in Estero, Florida, a suspected drunk driver traveled the wrong way on South Tamiami Trail and Broadway Avenue West, causing a multi-vehicle crash involving three other cars. Lee County deputies identified the driver as Debra Trautman. According to deputies, she appeared heavily intoxicated at the scene, unable to stand properly and emitting a strong odor of alcohol. She was later transported to a hospital, where her blood alcohol content was reported to be nearly three times the legal limit. The crash resulted in property damage but no reported serious injuries. Witnesses and local residents expressed concern about increasing impaired driving incidents in the area. Authorities charged Trautman with DUI and property damage. The investigation is ongoing as officials review the circumstances leading up to the wrong-way driving incident on a busy roadway along the highway corridor during evening traffic hours in Lee County Florida USA region
Charges: DUI (driving under the influence), property damage

Title: Wrong-way driver arrested for DUI in Walton County
description: On February 8, 2026, in Walton County, Florida, law enforcement responded to 911 reports of a wrong-way driver traveling along State Road 331 South. A vehicle was seen driving south of Rock Hill Road and nearly collided with another driver. Deputies and a DeFuniak Springs Police officer later located the truck continuing northbound in the southbound lanes near Coy Burgess Loop heading toward DeFuniak Springs. The driver was identified as 26-year-old Branden Powell of Coffee Springs, Alabama. Authorities conducted a traffic stop and took him into custody without reported injuries or a crash. He was arrested on charges of driving under the influence with a blood alcohol level of .15 or higher and reckless driving. Officials said the incident posed a serious risk to other motorists due to the wrong-way travel on a busy roadway. Investigation is ongoing by local authorities. No injuries were reported in the incident at scene
Charges: Driving under the influence (.15 or higher), reckless driving

Title: Man found passed out in driver’s seat with 5-year-old son in back, deputies say
description: On May 14, 2026, in Plant City, Florida, deputies from the Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office responded to a call at a Shell gas station about a possible person-down situation. When officers arrived, they found 26-year-old Patrick Voegtly unconscious in the driver’s seat of a parked truck with his 5-year-old son sitting in the back seat. Body camera footage showed deputies removing firearms from Voegtly before waking him. A second gun was reportedly found in his pocket during detention. Authorities said he showed signs of impairment and later refused field sobriety tests but provided a breath sample that was more than twice the legal limit of 0.08. The child was unharmed and reportedly told officers his father was “just sleeping.” Voegtly was arrested on charges related to DUI, child endangerment, and firearm possession while intoxicated. Officials said the case could have resulted in serious harm given the combination of alcohol, weapons, and a minor present in vehicle at scene investigation ongoing by authorities today
Charges: Driving under the influence (DUI), child endangerment, firearm possession while intoxicated

Title: Cross City man arrested for DUI, reckless driving near elementary school
description: Deputies in Gilchrist County arrested a 33-year-old Cross City man after a dangerous driving incident near Trenton Elementary School in Trenton, Florida. According to officials, Caleb Wells was in a line of vehicles outside the school when he allegedly crossed into the wrong lane to pass traffic, forcing other drivers off the roadway. Law enforcement reported that he continued driving recklessly despite the school zone environment, prompting a pursuit by deputies that lasted nearly one mile. The chase ended when Wells crashed his vehicle. Florida Highway Patrol troopers responded and conducted sobriety tests, which he allegedly failed. He was taken into custody at the scene. Authorities charged him with driving under the influence and reckless driving. The incident raised concerns about school zone safety and impaired driving risks during peak school hours in Gilchrist County. Investigation remains ongoing as officials review the pursuit and crash circumstances further in detail today.
Charges: DUI, reckless driving

Title: Deputies arrest 18-year-old after chase and crash in Lehigh Acres
description: Deputies in Lee County, Florida arrested an 18-year-old driver after a high-speed pursuit in Lehigh Acres that ended in a crash and a pit maneuver. According to the Lee County Sheriff’s Office, the suspect was first observed speeding on Gunnery Road and 8th Street Southwest, where he allegedly drove over a median and entered oncoming traffic. When deputies attempted a traffic stop, he refused to pull over, leading to a pursuit through residential roadways. During the chase, authorities say he crossed medians multiple times and struck another vehicle before fleeing the scene. Deputies eventually used a second pit maneuver at 7th Street Southwest and Gretchen Avenue to stop the vehicle and take him into custody. Officials reported he was allegedly impaired and unlawfully carrying a firearm at the time of the incident. The sheriff described the case as involving multiple serious felony and misdemeanor charges connected to reckless fleeing and impaired driving behavior.
Charges: Aggravated fleeing and eluding, DUI, obstruction without violence, unlawful carry of firearm, DUI involving a minor passenger

Title: Wrong-way driver reported on I-90 in Westlake, arrested for OVI
description: A 20-year-old man from Lorain, Ohio, was arrested after allegedly driving the wrong way on Interstate 90 in Westlake during the early morning hours of May 19, 2026. Westlake Police received multiple reports shortly after midnight about a black Hyundai SUV traveling westbound in the eastbound lanes near Columbia Road. Officers searched for the vehicle and eventually found it disabled after it struck a guardrail. The SUV remained facing the wrong direction near Cahoon Road when police arrived. Fortunately, no other vehicles were involved and the driver was not injured. The driver told officers he did not realize he was traveling on the wrong side of the interstate despite other motorists flashing their headlights. Police suspected impairment because the driver appeared intoxicated. He refused field sobriety and breath tests. During the investigation, officers discovered an open bottle of Lunazul tequila inside the vehicle. He was arrested and charged with multiple traffic and alcohol-related offenses.
Charges: OVI (Operating a Vehicle Impaired) Driving the wrong way on an interstate Failure to control Possession of an open container of alcohol in a motor vehicle

Title: Driver hides in water at resort after crashing into deputy vehicle in Port Charlotte, deputies say
description: A hit-and-run and subsequent collision with a deputy patrol vehicle occurred in Port Charlotte, Florida, on May 26, 2026, resulting in the arrest of a 30-year-old man identified as Norvell Johnson III. According to the Charlotte County Sheriff's Office, deputies were initially searching for a black Hyundai SUV involved in a prior hit-and-run incident. When deputies attempted a traffic stop, the driver fled through multiple areas, including Edgewater Drive, a Walgreens parking lot, and nearby residential streets. The pursuit ended when the suspect drove through a stop sign at an intersection and crashed into the passenger side of a marked patrol vehicle. After the crash, Johnson fled on foot and was later located hiding in the water near Sunseeker Resort, where deputies found him partially submerged in an attempt to avoid arrest. Authorities stated that a child was inside the vehicle during the incident. Johnson was arrested and faces multiple charges, including fleeing after a crash and child neglect.

Title: Man arrested in DeSoto County, accused of illegally hunting deer
description: Deputies in DeSoto County, Florida arrested Dominick Carillo of Lakeland after a traffic stop near Northwest Highway 72 and Northwest Pierce Street for running a stop sign. Officers discovered two freshly killed whitetail deer in the bed of his truck, partially covered with plywood. Investigators noted gunshot wounds and found no evidence the animals had been struck by a vehicle. Working with the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission, authorities determined the deer were illegally taken outside the legal hunting season, which had ended on January 4, 2026. Officials said Carillo is a repeat offender with prior hunting violations. He was charged with illegal taking and possession of deer, using a rimfire cartridge to take deer, and taking wildlife outside legal hunting hours and season. The arrest highlights enforcement efforts against illegal hunting and wildlife violations in Florida’s DeSoto County region under state wildlife protection regulations and enforcement actions strictly
Charges: Illegal taking and possession of deer; using rimfire cartridge to hunt deer; taking wildlife outside legal hunting hours and season

Title: Wild video shows sparks flying from a truck with missing wheels on I-4
description: Deputies in Volusia County, Florida responded after multiple 911 calls reported a Chevrolet Silverado pickup truck driving recklessly on Interstate 4 around 4:30 p.m. Witnesses said the truck had been damaged after striking a guardrail and was continuing to travel on three wheels, throwing sparks across the roadway. Some callers alleged the driver was swerving, performing donuts, and endangering other motorists. The vehicle eventually left I-4 and continued onto U.S. Highway 17-92 before stopping at a construction site near South Shell Road. Investigators say Chambers discussed meeting in person, expressed romantic and sexual intent toward the supposed minor, and suggested travel arrangements such as taking an Uber to meet. He also reportedly expressed fear of getting caught and deleted messages at times. Chambers was arrested during a traffic stop and charged with solicitation of a minor, transmission of harmful material to a minor, and unlawful use of a communication device. Officials emphasized the arrest was part of a proactive sting operation aimed at preventing harm to children.
Charges: Solicitation of a minor Transmission of harmful material to minors Unlawful use of a two-way communication device

Title: Woman fled after she was clocked at 103 mph in Range Rover on Palmetto Expressway: Cops
description: A Miami-Dade County woman was arrested after allegedly driving a Range Rover at extreme speeds on the Palmetto Expressway. Law enforcement conducting speed enforcement observed the vehicle traveling approximately 103 mph in a 55 mph zone. When officers attempted a traffic stop, the driver reportedly refused to pull over and accelerated, engaging in a dangerous attempt to evade police. According to the arrest report, the vehicle moved erratically through multiple lanes of traffic, cutting off other drivers and weaving across the highway while attempting to escape. The pursuit ended when the vehicle finally came to a stop in traffic. Officers ordered the driver out of the vehicle and took her into custody at the scene. She was later booked into jail following the incident, which involved high-speed reckless driving and attempted eluding of law enforcement on a major expressway.
Charges: Fleeing or attempting to elude a police officer at high speed; reckless driving

Title: Sheffield Lake woman gets 15 months in prison for fleeing Lorain cops
description: A Sheffield Lake woman was sentenced to prison following a police pursuit in Lorain County that involved high-speed driving and a crash with a school bus. According to prosecutors, officers attempted to stop a vehicle driven by Alyssa Tropkoff, 28, after it nearly caused a crash near West Erie Avenue and Leavitt Road. She allegedly fled from police, driving through residential yards and reaching speeds exceeding 80 mph in 35 mph zones. During the pursuit, she failed to obey stop signs and continued driving until the chase briefly stopped at the Sheffield village limits before resuming. The pursuit ended after her vehicle sideswiped another car and collided with a Lorain school bus carrying students and staff, though no injuries were reported. She later abandoned the vehicle and was found in a nearby home where she was arrested. She was charged with multiple felonies and misdemeanors related to fleeing police, impaired driving, and resisting arrest.
Charges: Failure to comply; obstructing official business; DUI; driving under suspension; resisting arrest; three counts of failure to stop after an accident

Title: Woman allegedly requests burger, fries after being accused of stolen car chase, DUI in Fort Myers
description: Jenny Fales, a 34-year-old woman, was arrested in Fort Myers, Florida, following a police pursuit involving a stolen vehicle and suspected impaired driving. According to the Florida Highway Patrol, troopers attempted to stop a white Honda Accord, but Fales allegedly failed to pull over and continued driving through multiple intersections, reportedly running stoplights and red lights during the chase. Law enforcement later used a PIT maneuver to stop the vehicle. After the car was disabled, officers removed her from the vehicle through a broken window. Authorities reported that Fales showed signs of impairment and refused field sobriety testing as well as a breathalyzer test. During the arrest, she allegedly made unusual statements requesting food and questioning why she could not simply leave. The incident resulted in her detention and transport to the Lee County Jail. Officials noted that she also had a suspended driver’s license from Georgia. The case involves allegations of DUI, fleeing law enforcement, and vehicle theft-related offenses.
Charges: DUI, fleeing law enforcement, running stoplights, and related traffic offenses (stolen vehicle investigation)

Title: Florida woman arrested for allegedly kicking child during youth football game
description: A Florida woman was arrested after police said she ran onto a youth football field during a game at Brooks Park in Fort Myers and repeatedly kicked a 13-year-old player during an on-field fight. Authorities reported that the incident began when players became involved in a brawl, and coaches and others attempted to break it up. During the chaos, the woman, identified as Renee Lambert, who had been watching her child’s team, allegedly rushed onto the field. Witnesses and video evidence reportedly showed her kicking the opposing team’s juvenile player while he was on the ground. Deputies on scene intervened after bystanders identified her. She allegedly became confrontational with law enforcement and resisted arrest. The child victim reportedly had no visible serious injuries but told deputies he was kicked in the leg. The incident led to charges of child abuse and resisting an officer, and child welfare authorities were notified due to the presence of her children.
Charges: Child abuse without great bodily harm Resisting an officer without violence

Title: North Fort Myers woman accused of driving faster than 90 mph in 35 mph zone
description: A 19-year-old North Fort Myers woman was arrested after police said she was caught driving at extreme speeds twice within a short period. According to authorities, Ariana Aldridge was first stopped and issued a warning for speeding by a law enforcement agency. Just two hours later, she was again observed driving at 93 mph in a 35 mph zone in Fort Myers, Florida. Officers with the Fort Myers Police Department conducted a second traffic stop after the repeated violation. Police reported that the driving behavior met the threshold for excessive speeding, defined as more than 50 mph over the posted limit. Following the second stop, Aldridge was arrested. The case involved no reported injuries or crash, but law enforcement emphasized the dangerous nature of repeated high-speed driving in a residential or urban area. She was taken into custody and charged under Florida’s excessive speeding laws.
Charges: Excessive speeding (driving more than 50 mph over the posted limit)

Title: woman arrested in domestic dispute on valentine's weekend
description: On February 15, 2026, around 4 p.m., a Lee County Sheriff’s Office deputy was on marked patrol in Boca Grande when members of the public alerted him to a blue SUV parked in a nearby parking lot at the intersection of East Railroad Avenue and 5th Street. Title: Landscape truck driver flees traffic stop in Southwest Ranches; lockdowns lifted at 2 schools
description: On February 25, 2026, Florida Highway Patrol conducted a traffic stop involving a landscaping truck in the area of South Flamingo Road and Southwest 51st Street in Southwest Ranches. After troopers completed the stop, the driver allegedly fled the scene in the vehicle, prompting a law enforcement response and a broader search of the area. The vehicle was later seen traveling toward the vicinity of Saint Mark Catholic Church and School and Archbishop Edward McCarthy High School, which led to precautionary lockdowns at both schools. Law enforcement and security personnel established a perimeter while searching for the truck and its occupants. The incident caused concern among parents and students but no injuries or confirmed threats were reported. Authorities later confirmed that no individuals were taken into custody in connection with the traffic stop, and the status of the occupants of the vehicle remained unclear at the time of reporting.
Charges: truck driver flees traffic stop, Felony fleeing and eluding police

Title: Woman arrested after Hillsborough Co. deputies chase stolen Red Bull truck across multiple counties
description: On May 9, 2026, deputies from the Hillsborough County Sheriff’s Office responded to a gas station on East Martin Luther King Jr. Boulevard in Tampa after a Red Bull delivery box truck was reported stolen during a delivery. According to authorities, the suspect, identified as Nicole Schuler, allegedly took control of the truck and fled the scene, prompting a multi-county pursuit. Law enforcement units, including aerial support from the sheriff’s aviation unit, tracked the vehicle as it traveled east toward Lakeland. The Polk County Sheriff’s Office and Lakeland Police Department assisted in the coordinated response. The pursuit ended when deputies were able to stop the truck and take Schuler into custody. No injuries were reported during the incident. The investigation indicated the case involved a stolen commercial vehicle and resulted in felony charges related to grand theft auto.

Title: School bus driver arrested after driving bus full of children onto train tracks | Video
description: On April 9, 2026, a Florida school bus driver was arrested in Sumter County after an incident in which she allegedly drove a school bus carrying 29 children onto railroad tracks as a train was approaching. According to investigators and footage reviewed by law enforcement, the bus became stalled or slowed on the tracks while the crossing signals were active, including flashing lights, warning bells, and lowered crossing arms. As the train approached, it struck the bus, which was still on or near the tracks at the intersection. Witnesses, including students on board, reported warning the driver about the approaching train, but the bus did not clear the tracks in time. Authorities later reviewed audio and video evidence from the scene, which contributed to the driver’s arrest. The sheriff stated that the driver’s actions reflected poor judgment that placed multiple children at risk. No fatalities were reported in the incident, and the driver was released on bond following her arrest.

Title: Palm Beach County dismisses ticket for woman accused of texting while driving without a right hand
description: In February 2026, Katie Thomas was pulled over by a Palm Beach County Sheriff’s Office deputy in Lake Worth Beach, Florida, after being accused of holding a cellphone while driving. During the traffic stop, the deputy stated he observed her manipulating a phone in her hand. Thomas denied the allegation and explained that she does not have a right hand, which became central to the dispute. The interaction continued with the deputy repeatedly questioning her about whether she had been using a phone at the time of driving. She maintained that she had not. A citation for distracted driving was initially issued. After further internal review by the Palm Beach County Sheriff’s Office, officials determined there was insufficient evidence to support the ticket. The citation was later dismissed, and no arrest or criminal charges followed the incident. The case drew attention due to the circumstances surrounding the traffic stop and its resolution.

description: Rapper Kodak Black, whose legal name is Bill Kapri, was involved in an alleged traffic stop incident in Broward County, Florida, that led to his arrest on charges of fleeing and eluding law enforcement and obstruction or resisting an officer without violence. The vehicle initially stopped, and Kapri briefly interacted with law enforcement before multiple armed individuals identifying as his security arrived at the scene. After a short exchange, he re-entered the vehicle and allegedly drove away despite being ordered not to leave. The Jeep was later found with another driver, and law enforcement reported discovering oxycodone, cannabis, cash, and jewelry inside the vehicle. During the chase, police reported that the suspect assaulted a female passenger inside the vehicle while continuing to evade officers. He also allegedly attempted to ram or force a patrol vehicle off the road, creating a dangerous situation for both law enforcement and civilians. According to law enforcement, his vehicle was clocked at approximately 101 miles per hour in a 40 mph zone, which placed him more than 60 mph over the posted limit. Officers stopped the vehicle before it reached the Cape Coral Bridge. Police noted that the incident occurred under a new Florida law that makes driving over 100 mph a misdemeanor due to the extreme risk posed to public safety. Residents expressed concern about dangerous driving in the area, while officials emphasized the severity of the speed involved. Authorities also indicated the driver had prior traffic citations for speeding and careless driving. Title: VIDEO: Car flees Parma Heights police, crashes into business
description: Parma Heights police pursued a speeding vehicle early Tuesday around 1 a.m. after officers observed a sedan traveling at nearly twice the posted speed limit on Pearl Road. Police initiated a pursuit with lights and sirens and requested assistance from neighboring agencies. During the chase, the driver lost control while turning and crashed into a business storefront at the intersection of Brookpark Road and Roseside Avenue, causing property damage. Officers arrested two adults at the scene, including one individual who had an outstanding felony warrant in Cuyahoga County. Authorities have not released the identities of those involved. Title: Bond set for man accused of intentionally hitting police cruiser, tossing gun during traffic stop
description: Authorities in Cincinnati, Ohio arrested 19-year-old Kevin Givens after a traffic stop escalated into a dangerous pursuit involving a police cruiser. Court documents state that Givens allegedly attempted to flee from officers during a stop and, in the process, intentionally struck a police cruiser that was occupied by officers. Prosecutors say the impact occurred at a high rate of speed, creating a serious risk of injury. During the incident, Givens is also accused of throwing a tan Glock 9mm handgun from the vehicle while continuing to flee. The discarded firearm reportedly struck another uninvolved vehicle, causing property damage to a window. He was later apprehended and charged with multiple offenses. The case highlights allegations of violent resistance during a traffic stop, along with illegal firearm possession and attempts to destroy or discard evidence during flight. Title: Semi driver arrested after fleeing serious crash Downtown, police say

Police say the collision left a woman in the sedan with broken bones and serious injuries, though she is expected to recover after being treated at the University of Cincinnati Medical Center. Authorities reported that instead of remaining at the scene, the semi driver left the area, triggering a hit-and-run investigation. Officers were able to quickly track the truck to a business in the Price Hill area because identifying information was visible on the vehicle. The driver was taken into custody and arrested for leaving the scene of an accident involving injury. The investigation remains ongoing as police review the circumstances leading up to the crash and the driver’s actions afterward.
Charges: Leaving the scene of an accident (hit-and-run involving injury), fleeing

Title: Man driving stolen vehicle flees from police in Belmont County, chase ends in arrest
description: Authorities in Belmont County, Ohio arrested a Virginia man after a stolen vehicle pursuit that began in a Lowe’s parking lot on May 26, 2026. Police were initially called after reports of a shirtless man with tattoos acting erratically and appearing under the influence while asking people for items. During the pursuit, the vehicle struck a deployed spike strip, disabling one tire, but continued traveling through multiple roads including Mall Road, Banfield Road, U.S. Route 40, and Interstate 70 westbound. Title: Two arrested in Athens County after running from police

A deputy observed the vehicle driving recklessly near SR 144 and Frost Road and attempted a traffic stop, but the driver fled, initiating a chase. Title: Truck driver arrested in Belmont County after mistakenly taking the wrong trailer, OSHP explains misunderstanding

The incident began when the owner of a trucking company in Livingston, California, reported that the trailer portion of a tractor-trailer had been stolen. Acting on that report, the Ohio State Highway Patrol located and stopped the vehicle on Interstate 70. The driver was taken into custody and booked into the Belmont County Jail on a charge of receiving stolen property. Later, investigators learned that the situation was a misunderstanding rather than a theft. Authorities determined that the driver had accidentally picked up the wrong trailer, and the owner mistakenly reported it as stolen when he discovered it missing. Investigators recovered shell casings and a firearm from the scene.

Title: Accomplice arrested in pepper-spray robbery at St. Pete CVS, police say
description: Police in St. Petersburg, Florida, arrested two suspects after a CVS pharmacy robbery involving pepper spray and stolen merchandise. Surveillance video showed Antone Jones and Joseph Lee-Brown entering the store wearing masks and disguises, then confronting employees. Investigators said Jones pushed a clerk while Lee-Brown sprayed pepper spray at staff, causing chaos inside the store. The pair stole over one thousand dollars in goods and fled. Lee-Brown was arrested first in Hillsborough County, and Jones was later taken into custody. Both face armed robbery charges as detectives continue to investigate similar incidents in the region since early January 2026 case

Deputies said the victim was trying to break up the fight when gunfire erupted, striking him in the leg and causing a severe femur injury that required surgery. Title: Suspected drunk driver accused of crashing into multiple cars along Immokalee Road
description: Sylvia Bocwinski, 53, was arrested following a hit-and-run crash investigation in Collier County, Florida. Deputies responded to reports that she struck multiple vehicles along Immokalee Road and continued driving away from the scene. A victim followed her vehicle and contacted law enforcement. Title: Principal of Lake Park Elementary arrested for DUI
description: Carlos Castro, principal of Lake Park Elementary School, was arrested in West Palm Beach, Florida, after deputies investigated a rear-end traffic crash. According to the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office, Castro showed signs of impairment, including bloodshot and glossy eyes, an odor of alcohol on his breath, and difficulty maintaining his balance. Deputies reported that he staggered while walking and later submitted breath samples that measured .214 and .210, both significantly above Florida’s legal limit of .08. He was taken into custody, booked into the county jail, and later released on bond pending further court proceedings.
Charges: Driving Under the Influence (DUI)

Title: Palm Beach County sheriff sergeant charged with DUI after Greenacres crash
description: Christian Jimenez, a Palm Beach County sheriff sergeant, was arrested after a crash in Greenacres, Florida, on January 23, 2026. Deputies conducting a DUI enforcement operation responded to a vehicle crash at the intersection of Lake Worth Road and Haverhill Road. According to investigators, Jimenez left the scene after the collision but was located shortly afterward. Authorities reported that he displayed signs of impairment, including glossy eyes and a strong odor of alcohol. He refused to submit to a breath alcohol test. Following the investigation, deputies determined there was probable cause for arrest and charged him accordingly.
Charges: Driving Under the Influence (DUI)  Leaving the scene of a crash

Title: Boca Raton Woman Allegedly Attacks Daughter’s Boyfriend With Taser
description: Veronica Karlsson, 55, was arrested after an incident at a residence in Boca Raton, Florida. According to investigators, Karlsson discovered her daughter's ex-boyfriend in a bedroom and demanded that he leave. Authorities allege that she later returned with a stun gun and a butter knife, blocked the doorway, and used the stun gun while the man was attempting to get dressed and exit the room. The alleged victim provided video evidence showing Karlsson activating the device multiple times. Deputies investigated the incident, and Karlsson was taken into custody before being booked into the Palm Beach County Jail.
Charges: Open carrying of an electric weapon or device

Title: Woman accused of repeated 911 calls, resisting officers at Fort Myers hotel
description: Madison Heath, 20, was arrested in Fort Myers, Florida, after police responded to repeated 911 calls made from her phone without an emergency. According to the Fort Myers Police Department, officers initially warned Heath that misuse of 911 services was not permitted after responding to earlier calls. Later, officers returned to a hotel where additional hang-up calls were traced back to her phone. Investigators reported signs of impairment and noted inconsistencies in her statements about making the calls. When officers attempted to arrest her, Heath allegedly resisted by pulling away and refusing commands. She was taken into custody and booked into jail.
Charges: Misuse of 911 emergency services Resisting an officer without violence

Title: Homeless man on probation arrested for breaking into Hawthorne home
description: Zackary Terrell Harnage, a 48-year-old homeless man on probation, was arrested in Hawthorne, Florida after deputies responded to a reported residential burglary. A neighbor checking on the home discovered a broken rear window, an unlocked back door, and signs of forced entry, then called authorities. Deputies later found Harnage near the property, appearing nervous and injured. Security footage allegedly showed him inside the home removing items including security cameras and rummaging through belongings. When officers attempted to detain him, he reportedly resisted before being taken into custody. He was already on probation for prior offenses and had violations outstanding.
Charges: Burglary of an unoccupied dwelling; property damage; resisting an officer without violence; violation of probation

Title: Woman accused of throwing Gatorade at Norland Middle School’s assistant principal faces judge
description: Diliana Quintana-Avila, a 40-year-old woman, was arrested after an incident at Norland Middle School in Miami Gardens, Florida. According to police, she entered the school campus during dismissal and argued with the assistant principal after being told she was not allowed to be on campus at that time. Authorities allege that Quintana-Avila then threw Gatorade at the assistant principal, striking them in the face twice. She was later taken into custody and charged with battery and resisting arrest. School officials confirmed they were aware of the incident, and the matter was handled by local law enforcement.
Charges: Battery Resisting arrest

Title: Woman arrested for pointing gun at juvenile playing ding-dong-ditch prank
description: Tiffany Nicole Hall, 40, was arrested in Gainesville, Florida, after an incident involving a group of juveniles playing a “ding-dong-ditch” prank. Hall allegedly confronted the group outside and pointed a firearm at one of the juveniles’ heads, causing the victim to fear for his life. Hall reportedly denied directly brandishing the weapon but admitted she had it during the encounter. The incident escalated after one juvenile allegedly tackled another during the confrontation. Law enforcement responded to the scene and arrested Hall on aggravated assault charges.

Title: Florida State Kicker Is Facing Felony Charges On Spring Break

Title: Woman accused of prostitution, groping undercover detective at Charlotte County massage parlor
description: A woman identified as Hong Zeng was arrested in Charlotte County, Florida after an undercover operation at AAA Rose Massage on Tamiami Trail. description: Isaiah Norton, a 19-year-old passenger, was arrested in Hollywood, Florida after allegedly attacking a 61-year-old Uber driver during a ride that began in Broward County and was headed toward Miami-Dade County. Police say the passenger began punching the driver shortly after entering the vehicle, and the assault continued while the car was in motion. Dash camera footage reportedly showed repeated strikes, attempts by the driver to escape, and the passenger restraining him and continuing the attack after briefly exiting and re-entering the car. The driver sustained injuries and emotional distress. Norton was later arrested and charged after fleeing the scene.

Title: Man accused of pepper spraying family, deputies in southwest Miami-Dade
description: Miguel Jomolca, a 26-year-old man, was arrested in Miami-Dade County, Florida after deputies responded to a family disturbance where he allegedly used pepper spray against multiple people, including family members. According to the Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office, he also sprayed responding deputies despite being ordered to stop and drop the spray. Officers reported that he continued resisting even after a Taser was deployed, leading to a prolonged physical struggle inside the home before he was taken into custody. Several victims and deputies were exposed to pepper spray and treated at the scene, though no hospital transport was required during the incident.
Charges: Aggravated battery on a law enforcement officer; resisting an officer with violence; aggravated battery

Title: Toledo woman accused of attempting to drag her child into oncoming traffic enters no-contest plea
description: Veronica Laraby, a 29-year-old woman, was accused of attempting to drag her child into oncoming traffic in Toledo, Ohio, on March 27, 2026. According to police, she allegedly dragged the child along a sidewalk and then tried to pull the child by the feet and hair into traffic. A bystander intervened and prevented further harm. Multiple witnesses and a responding police officer reported that Laraby appeared highly intoxicated at the scene. She was initially charged with child endangerment. Later, she entered a no-contest plea to a reduced charge of fourth-degree misdemeanor disorderly conduct and was found guilty in court.
Charges: Initial Charge: Child Endangerment Final Charge: Disorderly Conduct (4th Degree Misdemeanor)

description: Shekwon Walker was among 17 individuals arrested during disorderly and chaotic crowds that developed during Cincinnati’s Opening Day celebrations on March 26, 2026. According to authorities, large groups engaged in disruptive behavior that led to police intervention in several downtown areas, including The Banks and Over-the-Rhine. Walker was specifically accused of striking a police officer in the back during the disturbances. He later appeared in court, where a judge emphasized that violence and disorder at public events would not be tolerated. His bond was set at $140,000 secured. The incident prompted widespread concern from city officials and law enforcement.

After initially stopping, Ali drove away and led officers to an apartment complex where he abandoned the vehicle and fled on foot. He was found hiding underneath a vehicle and taken into custody. Police discovered he had an active grand theft warrant, signs of alcohol impairment, and a breath alcohol level exceeding three times Ohio’s legal limit.

description: Robert Rooks, a 44-year-old man from Toledo, Ohio, was arrested after a domestic violence response on February 24, 2026. Title: Man arrested after allegedly vandalizing Vance’s Ohio home
description: William DeFoor, 26, was arrested after allegedly vandalizing Vice President JD Vance’s home in Cincinnati, Ohio, in the early hours of January 5, 2026. According to authorities, a U.S. Secret Service agent observed him entering the property and damaging four residential windows and a vehicle. DeFoor was quickly detained by Secret Service personnel at the scene. Investigators reported that the residence was unoccupied at the time, as Vance and his family were out of town. He was later charged in both federal and local court with multiple offenses, including vandalism, trespassing, obstructing official business, and damaging government property.

description: Lake County deputies in Leesburg responded to reports of a person suspected of checking vehicle door handles in a residential neighborhood during the early morning hours. Witnesses described someone wearing a headlamp moving suspiciously between parked cars. When deputies arrived, they located a vehicle with a warm engine nearby and deployed a drone to search the area. The drone spotted Melesia Dority hiding near a waterline behind a tree. As officers approached, she attempted to flee on foot but was quickly apprehended. A search allegedly uncovered burglary tools including gloves and a socket wrench. She was arrested and taken to jail for questioning and processing.

During the incident, a video reportedly showed Wells throwing a stroller that contained a 10-week-old infant, causing the baby to be thrown onto concrete. He also allegedly acted aggressively toward the child’s grandmother. Deputies said Wells fled into a home before being arrested and charged following the investigation.

Title: ‘Reckless choices’: 3 Florida teens arrested following smoke shop burglary in stolen car, deputies say
description: Three Cape Coral teenagers were arrested after stealing a car, breaking into a smoke shop, and fleeing from law enforcement in Lee County, Florida. Deputies said the group broke into Cloud Factory Smoke & Vape using a bat to smash the storefront glass and stole money and merchandise. They then fled in a stolen black sedan. Law enforcement tracked them to Cape Coral, where a pursuit involving deputies and Florida Highway Patrol took place. The vehicle became stuck in a construction area, and the teens ran on foot before being arrested. All three later admitted planning the burglary to make quick cash.

According to police, the victim was confronted by individuals he knew from a prior dispute. During the incident, Jamar McKay allegedly grabbed a gold chain worth about $22,000 from the victim’s neck. description: Jeremyah Taylor, a 22-year-old man, was arrested in Pompano Beach after Broward Sheriff’s Office deputies responded to a reported shooting near Blanche Ely High School. description: Dexter Rayonne Jackson, 35, was arrested after allegedly robbing a Dollar General store in Summerfield, Florida, while wearing a ski mask and holding a firearm. Deputies said he entered the store, threatened employees, and demanded money, warning he would shoot people if they did not comply. After taking cash, he fled but was quickly located by deputies nearby and arrested following a short pursuit. Authorities recovered stolen money and a firearm close to the scene. Investigators also noted Jackson had recently been released from prison and had prior arrests, including a December incident involving fleeing, assault on officers, and drug possession charges.

Title: Driver accused of crashing at gas station while buying alcohol, faces DUI and hit-and-run charges
description: Walfred Martinez Caravantes, 36, was arrested in Lee County, Florida, after deputies accused him of causing a hit-and-run crash in a Circle K parking lot and later driving under the influence. According to investigators, his truck struck another vehicle while attempting to maneuver in the gas station area. The occupants reportedly entered the store to buy alcohol before leaving the scene. Deputies later located Martinez Caravantes at his residence, where they observed signs of intoxication including slurred speech and an odor of alcohol. He failed field sobriety tests and recorded a BAC of 0.23 on a breathalyzer. He was arrested for DUI and hit-and-run charges.

Title: Manatee County corrections deputy arrested on DUI charge after crash
description: Luciano Centofanti, a 30-year-old off-duty corrections deputy with the Manatee County Sheriff’s Office, was arrested after a single-vehicle crash in Parrish, Florida. Deputies responded after EMS requested assistance for a suspected intoxicated driver. Investigators identified Centofanti as the driver at the scene. No injuries were reported in the crash. Authorities determined he was under the influence at the time of the incident and took him into custody on DUI charges. The sheriff’s office later confirmed he resigned in lieu of termination following the arrest. He had worked for the agency since 2019 prior to the incident.
Charges: Driving under the influence (DUI)

Title: Akron man charged with 5th OVI
description: Richard Hahn, an Akron man, was arrested after Ohio State Highway Patrol troopers stopped him on Interstate 77 for alleged distracted driving. During the stop, troopers observed signs of impairment and took him into custody for operating a vehicle while impaired (OVI). Authorities noted this was his fifth OVI-related offense. The traffic stop occurred in the early morning hours, and he was later charged following the investigation. Hahn is scheduled to appear in Canton Municipal Court for further proceedings. The case highlights repeated impaired driving offenses leading to renewed legal action by law enforcement in Stark County.
Charges: Operating a vehicle while impaired (OVI) – 5th offense

Title: 7-year-old boy left traumatized after being shot in back seat of family car, loved ones say
description: An Ohio family reported that a 7-year-old boy was shot while riding in the back seat of a vehicle on Interstate 75 near Cincinnati as they approached the Harrison Avenue exit. According to police and family statements, an unidentified gunman opened fire on the car, striking the child in the back. The mother said the shooter initially aimed at her before turning the weapon toward the child. The boy survived after being taken to hospital but is traumatized. Cincinnati Police arrested Michael Walker in connection with the shooting. He faces felonious assault and improper discharge of a firearm charges case
Charges: Felonious assault; improper discharge of a firearm

Title: Ohio man indicted in claw hammer attack on officer
description: A man identified as Jacob Culbertson was indicted in Summit County, Ohio, after allegedly attacking a Barberton police officer with a claw hammer during a domestic violence incident. Police responded on February 2, 2026, to a home on Charles Avenue after his mother reported he was out of control and had assaulted his father. Officers said Culbertson, intoxicated and armed with a knife while wearing a bulletproof vest, barricaded himself in a bedroom. When officers forced entry, he allegedly struck one officer in the head with a hammer, injuring him before being subdued with a Taser and arrested by police

description: Police in Westlake, Ohio responded to a report of a suspicious man walking behind a business area while allegedly carrying hatchets and behaving erratically. Officers located the 27-year-old North Olmsted man after a concerned citizen call and reports that he was yelling and possibly planning a robbery. Police stated the suspect initially had at least one hatchet and also a wood-handled mallet. He refused commands and was forcibly detained and handcuffed. During the arrest, he spat on an officer. He was taken into custody after resisting arrest and allegedly making threats toward his girlfriend prior to the incident investigation ongoing.

Title: Woman body slammed by Sweetwater Police at Li'l Abner mobile park found guilty
description: Vivian Hernandez, a 62-year-old woman, was arrested in Sweetwater, Florida at the Li’l Abner mobile home park administrative office during a dispute related to a large eviction order affecting residents. Police said officers responded after reports of disorderly behavior inside the office. Hernandez, a long-term resident, allegedly refused multiple commands to leave the premises and became involved in a confrontation with police. A Sweetwater police sergeant stated he attempted to escort her out before the situation escalated and she was taken to the ground. Hernandez later testified in court claiming she was speaking in a normal tone and felt mistreated during the encounter legal dispute followed.
Charges: Disorderly conduct; trespass after warning; resisting arrest without violence

description: May Ling Ip, 48, and Jamie Allen Mays, 40, were arrested after an intense standoff with Flagler County deputies involving a U-Haul vehicle. Deputies responded to a report of a suspicious vehicle and attempted contact, but the vehicle fled. A traffic stop was conducted, and stop sticks were used to disable the U-Haul. During the struggle, one officer reportedly suffered a dislocated shoulder. Police used a Taser to subdue and arrest her. Authorities stated that Savell was already out on bond in another assault and resisting arrest case. Investigators also cited a history of violent behavior and alcohol-related issues during court proceedings.
Charges: Three counts of assault on a police officer Two counts of felonious assault Obstructing official business Resisting arrest

Title: Dunkirk woman arrested at Dollar General
description: Heather McGinnis was arrested after Logan County Sheriff’s Deputies responded to a report of a woman slumped over the wheel of a running vehicle outside a Dollar General store. Deputies observed signs of impairment and believed she was under the influence of an unknown substance. McGinnis refused field sobriety tests and resisted arrest when officers attempted to place her in handcuffs, pulling away and throwing herself to the ground. During a search, deputies reported finding needles, pills, and suspected drugs including cocaine and marijuana. She was transported to jail where additional contraband was allegedly discovered, including hidden substances and drug-related items.

Title: Woman accused of punching her sister
description: Solimar Barbosa Morales, 30, was arrested after an alleged domestic violence incident involving her sister and another woman. According to police, the dispute began after Morales insulted the home where they lived together. She allegedly threw bottled water in her sister’s face, spit on her twice, then grabbed her by the hair and punched her in the face. When another woman attempted to intervene, Morales allegedly struck her as well. Police observed bruises on both victims. The incident reportedly occurred in the presence of Morales’s 1-year-old son. Morales later denied attacking the second woman and claimed self-defense.

Title: Former Franklin County bailiff pleads not guilty to charges in courthouse assault
description: Kelli Johnson, a former Franklin County Juvenile Court bailiff, was charged following an altercation inside the courthouse in March 2026. Surveillance video reportedly showed Johnson pushing a woman, Victoria Perkins, outside a courtroom and pushing her again in a hallway. The video also appeared to show Johnson swiping Perkins’ cellphone from her hand, causing it to fall to the floor. An incident report stated that Johnson allegedly used profane language during the encounter. Perkins said she had gone to the courtroom to file a complaint when the situation escalated. Johnson later resigned from her position and pleaded not guilty.
Charges: Disorderly Conduct (Misdemeanor) Criminal Mischief (Misdemeanor)

Title: Dayton mom, boyfriend indicted for ‘sadistic’ abuse against children
description: Heather Pippen and her boyfriend, Stephanas Golden, were indicted following a child abuse investigation involving seven children living in a Dayton home. Authorities alleged the children, ages 7 to 15, suffered repeated physical abuse over several years. The investigation began after a teenager recorded Golden beating another child and the video was posted on social media. Police and child welfare officials responded, leading to the removal of seven children from the home. Investigators reported both recent and older injuries on the children. Pippen and Golden were arrested after allegedly refusing police commands, and all children were placed in foster care.
Charges: Heather Pippen:  2 Counts of Endangering Children Strangulation Obstructing Official Business  Stephanas Golden:  7 Counts of Endangering Children 2 Counts of Strangulation Resisting Arrest

Title: VIDEO: Man punches K-9 during arrest after chase through Florida counties, deputies say
description: James Hardy, 48, led deputies on a multi-county chase after fleeing from Seminole County into Volusia County, Florida. According to the Volusia Sheriff’s Office, deputies deployed stop sticks to disable his vehicle, and a precision immobilization technique was used to end the pursuit. Hardy then ran into nearby woods in an attempt to escape. A K-9 unit tracked him down, and during the arrest he resisted violently, striking the police dog multiple times. Deputies eventually subdued and arrested him after the confrontation. Authorities reported that Hardy’s actions endangered motorists during the high-speed pursuit before his capture.
Charges: Fleeing or attempting to elude law enforcement with disregard for safety Resisting an officer Driving with a suspended or revoked license Resisting arrest with violence Possession of drug paraphernalia

Title: Women convicted on reduced charge after police say they left toddler in car during assault
description: Two Toledo women, Dericka Bratton and Tamicka Bratton, were arrested after police said they left a three-year-old child inside a vehicle while they entered a home and committed burglary and an assault. Officers reported that the suspects knew the victim and caused property damage during the incident. Both women were later charged, but in a plea agreement, they were convicted of criminal trespassing while more serious charges including aggravated burglary, vandalism, and child endangerment were dropped. They each received a short jail sentence with credit for time served and were placed on probation for two years following court proceedings reported
Charges: Criminal trespassing

Title: Woman charged in steak knife stabbing that required victim to get emergency surgery
description: Shanika Peterson was arrested in Toledo after police said she stabbed a 27-year-old man during an early morning incident on March 27. Witnesses reported that she used a steak knife to cut the victim’s right arm during an altercation at a residence on Manhattan Blvd. The victim suffered serious injuries and required emergency surgery but was expected to survive. Peterson was later indicted on two counts of felonious assault. She pleaded not guilty in court, and a judge set her bond on her own recognizance while ordering her to avoid contact with the victim and return for future court proceedings.
Charges: Two Counts of Felonious Assault

Title: North Fort Myers woman accused of disorderly intoxication after punching school bus
description: On March 8, 2026, in North Fort Myers, Florida, Roberta Stancel was accused of disorderly intoxication after an incident involving a school bus. Witnesses said she stood at a bus stop near children, shouted at and struck a moving bus, then walked into traffic and confronted drivers. Deputies with the Lee County Sheriff's Office located her at a residence where she entered a vehicle and resisted commands before arrest. She was charged with resisting an officer, disorderly intoxication, and disrupting an educational institution. The case remains under investigation by authorities in Lee County, Florida as of March 2026 report states
Charges: Resisting an officer without violence, disorderly intoxication causing public disturbance, knowingly disrupting or interfering with lawful function of an educational institution

Title: Woman charged with DUI and child neglect after getting pulled over with a child in Lake County
description: Alayshia Martin, a 23-year-old woman, was arrested by the Lake County Sheriff's Office after deputies responded to a report of a suspected drunk driver on State Road 50 in Clermont, Florida. Deputies located a vehicle matching the reported description and conducted a traffic stop. During the investigation, Martin reportedly struggled to provide identification, showed signs of impairment including bloodshot and dilated eyes, and her vehicle smelled of alcohol. Deputies also found two children in the back seat, including one child who was not secured in a car or booster seat. Field sobriety tests were conducted before her arrest.
Charges: Driving Under the Influence (DUI) Child Neglect

Title: Couple arrested after leading authorities on chase with teen in car, Levy County deputies say
description: Angela Birkholz, 42, was arrested after deputies in Levy County attempted to stop her vehicle for running a stop sign in east Bronson, Florida. According to authorities, Birkholz refused to stop and led law enforcement on a vehicle pursuit. The chase ended when Florida Highway Patrol troopers performed a PIT maneuver to disable the vehicle. Investigators reported that a 15-year-old passenger was inside the car during the incident and was later taken into protective custody before being released to a family member. Authorities also discovered that passenger Travis Merrell was wanted on multiple felony warrants and allegedly possessed methamphetamine.
Charges: Fleeing and Eluding Law Enforcement Driving with an Invalid License

Suspect Name: Hularia Brito Cefo, Ismael Gomez, Juan Raymundo, Julio Raymundo Lux
Title: Caught on Camera: Four suspects try to run during traffic stop in Punta Gorda
description: Caught on camera in Punta Gorda, Florida, four men became the subject of a brief manhunt after a traffic stop on January 3, 2026. Deputies with the Charlotte County Sheriff’s Office stopped a vehicle at Burnt Store Road and Zemel Road. All four occupants attempted to flee on foot. Three were quickly captured, while the fourth escaped temporarily. Aviation and K-9 units assisted in the search, and a drone located the remaining suspect hiding beneath a dock. All four were later detained and held at the Charlotte County Jail on ICE detainers. No injuries were reported during the incident noted.
Charges: Fleeing and Eluding Law Enforcement

Title: Man accused of leading Collier County deputies on 100-plus mph chase in stolen car
description: On January 13, 2026, in Collier County, Florida, deputies attempted to locate a stolen vehicle reported from a Racetrac on Tamiami Trail East. A deputy spotted the car at Pine Ridge Road and Whippoorwill Lane and initiated a traffic stop. The driver, later identified as Dylan Reynolds, accelerated onto Interstate 75, reaching speeds over 112 mph while weaving through traffic. A multi-agency pursuit followed, including the Collier County Sheriff’s Office and Florida Highway Patrol. Near a toll area, Reynolds stopped, exited the vehicle, and discarded the keys before being arrested. He was also found to be a habitual traffic offender.
Charges: Grand theft auto, fleeing/eluding officers with disregard for safety, operating a vehicle with a revoked driver’s license

Title: WATCH: Florida motorcyclist clocked at 106 mph in residential zone with child passenger
description: On January 27, 2026, in Marion County, Florida, a motorcyclist was arrested after deputies observed him traveling at more than 105 mph in a 45 mph residential zone while carrying a child passenger. The Marion County Sheriff’s Office initiated a traffic stop as the motorcycle continued through neighborhood roads, making multiple turns before stopping at a residence. Investigators discovered the child was riding on the back of the motorcycle and wearing a helmet during the high-speed ride. The driver, identified as David Johnson, told officers he was testing the motorcycle due to mechanical issues. He was arrested due to the dangerous conduct involving a child.
Charges: Child neglect, operating a vehicle at 100+ mph

Title: Columbus man arrested after high-speed stop on U.S. 33
description: A Columbus man was arrested after a high-speed traffic stop on U.S. 33 in Logan County near Bellefontaine. An officer observed a white Ford Bronco traveling 93 mph in a 70 mph zone. When officers attempted to initiate a stop, the driver did not immediately pull over and continued driving westbound for nearly a mile before slowing. Due to the driving behavior, officers conducted a felony stop. The driver, Arad Cohen, was taken into custody without further incident. A passenger in the vehicle was also detained but later cleared. The vehicle was a rental from the Columbus area.
Charges: Failure to comply with a lawful order

Title: Marion County man arrested after vehicle chase for robbing 3 stores at gunpoint
description: A 55-year-old Marion County man was arrested after allegedly committing a series of armed robberies at three businesses over two days in Ocala, Florida. Deputies say he robbed a Family Dollar, a Shoe Station, and a Murphy Oil gas station at gunpoint. Law enforcement later located the suspect driving on Northwest Eighth Street and attempted a traffic stop. The suspect fled, initiating a police pursuit. During the chase, his vehicle crashed into a power pole at the intersection of Northwest Ninth Avenue and Sixth Street. Following the crash, deputies took him into custody. He was booked into the Marion County Jail without bond.
Charges: Armed robbery (three counts), fleeing and eluding law enforcement

Title: Armed carjacking in Winter Park leads to police chase on I-4
description: A 38-year-old man was arrested in Winter Park, Florida after an armed carjacking and kidnapping incident that led to a police pursuit on Interstate 4. Police responded to reports of an armed robbery on Aloma Avenue, where the suspect allegedly took a victim’s vehicle at gunpoint. Officers later located the stolen vehicle and attempted a traffic stop, but the suspect fled, initiating a chase onto I-4. The Florida Highway Patrol joined the pursuit and used a Precision Immobilization Technique (PIT) maneuver near mile marker 113 to stop the vehicle. The suspect was taken into custody and transported to jail on multiple violent felony charges.
Charges: Armed carjacking, kidnapping with a firearm, armed robbery, aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, tampering with a victim, criminal mischief, fleeing and eluding, battery

Title: North Olmsted officials discuss recent high-speed chase and kidnapping incident
description: Portage County, Ohio
Charges: Failure to comply with police order (felony), outstanding warrant (theft-related), prior criminal history mentioned (domestic violence, drug-related history noted but not charged in this case)

Title: PIT maneuver in Volusia ends cross-county pursuit of stolen car
description: Law enforcement agencies pursued a stolen vehicle across multiple jurisdictions after it was reported taken from Brevard County and entered Volusia County. The driver, John Gordon, led officers from Daytona Beach and Orange City police on a high-speed pursuit while attempting to evade stop sticks and patrol units. Deputies coordinated with air support and ground units as the vehicle continued reckless driving. After repeated intervention attempts, including two deployments of stop sticks, officers executed a PIT maneuver to end the chase safely. The vehicle was disabled and Gordon was taken into custody without further incident. He was transported for booking.
Charges: Fleeing or attempting to elude law enforcement, grand theft of motor vehicle, driving with suspended/cancelled/revoked license, violation of probation

Title: Bronson Brothers Arrested in Auto Thefts
description: On January 22, 2026, a Levy County Sheriff’s Office deputy arrested Justin Ausburn after observing him operating a vehicle despite not having a valid driver’s license. Investigators determined the 2016 black Ford truck he was driving had recently been stolen but had not yet been officially reported missing. On the same day, deputies also investigated the theft of a silver 1989 Ford F450 rollback truck valued at about $10,000 taken from a vacant lot in Bronson. Detectives later linked both thefts through similar methods involving ignition tampering. A tip led to recovery of the F450 and further evidence connecting both Justin and his brother Thomas to multiple felony charges.
Charges: Grand theft auto; multiple felony charges related to vehicle theft and possession of stolen property

Suspect Name: Jason Scott Wolfe; Tanner Riley Wolfe
Title: Jay Father And Son Charged With Stealing 20 Tons Of Asphalt Millings From Santa Rosa County
description: A father and son in Santa Rosa County were arrested after deputies accused them of stealing about 20 tons of asphalt millings from a county surplus yard. Law enforcement reported seeing a truck and dump trailer loaded with the material at the site. A Florida Highway Patrol sergeant initiated a traffic stop after observing the activity. The father claimed county employees had permitted the removal, but officials stated no authorization was given. Investigators also found similar material on the suspects’ property. Both Jason Scott Wolfe and his son Tanner Riley Wolfe were charged with felony grand theft and released on bond following the investigation into the removal of county-owned materials.
Charges: Felony grand theft

Title: Man arrested for stealing person’s car keys at gunpoint in Hawthorne
description: A convicted felon in Alachua County was arrested after allegedly pointing a firearm at a victim and stealing their car keys during an armed confrontation. Deputies said Norman Colon threatened to kill the victim if they contacted law enforcement. Despite the threat, the victim called 911, and law enforcement quickly responded. Investigators located and arrested Colon, who was already wanted in other jurisdictions, including drug charges in Putnam County and prior violent convictions in Pennsylvania. He now faces multiple felony charges related to armed robbery, firearm use during a felony, aggravated assault, battery, drug possession, and grand theft stemming from the incident.
Charges: Robbery with a firearm; aggravated assault; battery; using a firearm during a felony; grand theft

Title: Homestead man faces charges for watercraft theft and resisting arrest
description: A 34-year-old man from Homestead was arrested in Monroe County after allegedly stealing a personal watercraft from a rental business and fleeing law enforcement. Deputies said the suspect arrived at a residence on Grassy Key on a personal watercraft and later gave a suspicious explanation before leaving on foot. Law enforcement located him walking along U.S. 1, where he allegedly fled into nearby mangroves before being captured. Investigators confirmed the watercraft had been stolen, and the suspect was also linked to other recent thefts involving additional vessels and vehicles. He was arrested on charges including grand theft of a vessel, resisting arrest, and providing a false identity.
Charges: Grand theft of a vessel; resisting arrest; providing false name to law enforcement

Title: JCSO: Woman flees at 120 mph, ditches car and runs across freeway
description: Dajanaia Latansie Davillier, a 32-year-old woman from Miramar, Florida, was arrested after allegedly fleeing from a traffic stop on Interstate 10 in Jefferson County, Texas. Deputies said she was stopped for speeding in a construction zone but drove away as the officer approached. The pursuit reached speeds of 120 mph and continued through multiple areas before ending in Orange County. Davillier reportedly abandoned her vehicle, ran across Interstate 10 lanes, and was captured by officers. A search of the vehicle found marijuana residue and a small bag containing marijuana.
Charges: Evading Arrest or Detention with a Vehicle (3rd degree felony)

Title: 3 arrested after high-speed I-75 chase
description: On January 12, 2026, in Cincinnati, Ohio, a stolen vehicle pursuit began after Ohio State Highway Patrol task force attempted a traffic stop on westbound Queen City Avenue. The driver, later identified as Derrick Latham, fled and led officers onto northbound Interstate 75, reaching speeds over 100 mph while Cincinnati police joined the chase. The pursuit ended on Mitchell Avenue near the highway, where authorities arrested three occupants without reported injuries. Latham was taken into custody and charged with multiple offenses including fleeing police, reckless operation, obstruction, receiving stolen property, and driving without a license during ongoing investigation period locally
Charges: Failing to comply with police signal; reckless operation of a motor vehicle; obstructing official business; receiving stolen property; driving without a license

Title: Florida man allegedly caught going 101 mph gives deputies wild excuse when busted
description: On May 6, 2026, in Brevard County, Florida, deputies conducted traffic enforcement operation known as Super Speeder Saturday when they observed Christopher Jones driving at 101 mph in a 70 mph zone. Officers initiated traffic stop and Jones was pulled over after being clocked speeding. He told deputies he was late for wedding. He was dressed in a suit and slide sandals. Authorities arrested him for operating vehicle over 100 mph while threatening persons or property. He was taken to Brevard County Jail and later released on bond. A court date was pending at time of report was pending review
Charges: Operating a vehicle at 100-plus mph while threatening persons or property (misdemeanor)

Title: Rochester Motorist Accused of Fleeing Police With Fugitive from Walmart Parking Lot
description: Rochester police attempted to arrest a suspect with an active warrant at the south Walmart parking lot on March 17, 2026. During the attempt, a wanted individual fled on foot and entered the passenger side of a vehicle driven by Jayden Emmanuel Del Angel Carreon. Carreon then drove away despite officers trying to stop the vehicle. Police later identified him through surveillance footage. Investigators say Carreon admitted he saw officers attempting to intervene but chose to flee. The suspect was later arrested. The report does not confirm whether the original warrant suspect was located after the incident or if additional charges were added later.
Charges: Felony fleeing a peace officer in a motor vehicle

Title: Olmsted County Man Charged After Dakota County Chase
description: Deputies in Dakota County, Minnesota attempted a traffic stop on a 25-year-old Olmsted County man after he was observed driving 85 mph in a 55 mph zone in Vermillion Township on February 3, 2026. The driver allegedly fled, leading deputies on a pursuit across rural roads and into a business parking lot. Officers attempted a PIT maneuver, which initially failed, allowing the suspect to continue fleeing over a snowbank. A second PIT maneuver successfully stopped the vehicle, pinning it between squad cars. The man was taken into custody and later charged in court with felony fleeing police following the incident.
Charges: Felony fleeing police

Title: Cincinnati man accused of ramming police cruisers arrested after running out of gas
description: A 58-year-old Cincinnati man was arrested after leading police on a pursuit in a stolen SUV and allegedly ramming two police cruisers during the incident. Officers attempted to stop the vehicle, but the suspect fled and struck cruisers with officers inside while trying to escape. The chase continued through local roads until the SUV eventually ran out of gas, bringing the pursuit to an end. Officers then took the suspect into custody without further incident. Authorities stated he faces multiple serious felony charges related to the assault on officers, vehicle theft, and failure to comply with police commands during the pursuit.
Charges: Aggravated vehicular assault, felonious assault, failure to comply, additional offenses

Title: APD releases bodycam footage of pursuit that led to Bell man’s arrest
description: A 48-year-old man from Bell, Florida was arrested after a brief vehicle pursuit in Alachua County. Police say officers encountered Micah Ellsworth stopped on the side of the road in his red Dodge pickup truck. When officers from High Springs Police Department attempted to speak with him, he suddenly drove off, leading them on a short chase. The pursuit ended when officers surrounded the vehicle and took him into custody. He was charged with fleeing and eluding law enforcement with lights and sirens active, resisting an officer without violence, and driving while license suspended or revoked for a second offense.
Charges: Fleeing and eluding police with lights and sirens active, resisting officer without violence, driving while license suspended or revoked (second offense)
