Title: Carjacking suspect fled from officers, crashed in Fort Lauderdale, cops say
description: Police in Plantation, Florida reported a carjacking involving a suspect who allegedly battered his ex-girlfriend and stole her vehicle in the early morning hours. About an hour later, Fort Lauderdale officers located a matching vehicle and attempted a traffic stop. The driver fled, leading police on a pursuit through residential streets before crashing into a fence in Fort Lauderdale. The suspect then exited the vehicle and ran through backyards attempting to escape. Officers, with assistance from a police K9, apprehended him shortly afterward. He was taken into custody without serious injuries reported and faces multiple charges related to the carjacking and pursuit.
Charges: Carjacking, simple battery, fleeing and eluding, driving without a valid driver’s license

Title: Man accused of breaking 'super speeder' law, going 100 mph on I-75, CR 484
description: A man from St. Petersburg was arrested after allegedly driving at speeds exceeding 100 mph on Interstate 75 and County Road 484 in Marion County, Florida. Law enforcement officials reported the driver was considered a “super speeder” under state traffic enforcement laws due to the excessive speed. Deputies initiated a traffic stop after observing the dangerous driving behavior. The vehicle was eventually stopped, and the driver was taken into custody without reported injuries or crashes involving other vehicles. Authorities emphasized the risk posed by the high-speed driving on a busy interstate corridor. The suspect was arrested on February 12, 2026.
Charges: Speeding over 100 mph (“super speeder” violation), reckless driving

Title: Hialeah police capture suspect in series of vehicle burglaries
description: Hialeah Police conducted surveillance on a series of vehicle burglaries in the area after multiple reports of stolen items from parked cars. Detectives observed the suspect allegedly removing a wheel from a parked Honda Accord and transferring it into another vehicle before leaving the scene. When officers later attempted to stop him, the suspect fled in a vehicle, driving at high speeds, running red lights, and weaving through traffic. Police eventually discontinued the pursuit due to safety concerns. The suspect was later identified through investigation and arrested. He faces multiple charges connected to burglary, reckless driving, and resisting officers during the incident.
Charges: Burglary of an unoccupied conveyance, fleeing and attempting to elude police, resisting officer without violence, reckless driving

Title: Ft. White man arrested for fleeing on four-wheeler in Archer, crashing into deputy’s patrol vehicle
description: Tyler Malik Bryant, a 20-year-old from Fort White, was arrested in Archer after allegedly fleeing from law enforcement on a four-wheeler during a block party. Deputies reported the ATV was driven recklessly, performing donuts, speeding through neighborhoods, and ignoring stop signs. When a deputy attempted a traffic stop, Bryant initially paused and spoke to the officer but then accelerated away. A second deputy later located him, and during the pursuit, the ATV reportedly spun out and collided with a patrol vehicle. Bryant was taken into custody at the scene. The incident involved active lights and an attempted law enforcement stop.
Charges: Fleeing from law enforcement with lights activated

Title: MPD: Fleeing homeless man injures officer before arrest
description: Michael Andre Peavy Jr., a 29-year-old convicted felon, was arrested in Pensacola, Florida after a high-speed pursuit involving a stolen vehicle. Deputies with the Escambia County Sheriff's Office attempted a traffic stop after a license plate reader flagged a stolen Nissan Versa. The driver refused to stop, leading to a chase through multiple streets. Authorities attempted a PIT maneuver, but the vehicle continued until it crashed through a residential backyard and struck a child’s playhouse before stopping near a wooded area. Both Peavy and a passenger were taken into custody. Officers later found a stolen firearm and methamphetamine in the vehicle.
Charges: Fleeing and eluding, grand theft of a motor vehicle, grand theft of a firearm, possession of a weapon by a convicted felon (two counts), felony criminal mischief

Title: Stolen vehicle chase leads to crash, arrest in Crestview, officials say
description: Isaac Schlabach, a 22-year-old suspect, was arrested in Crestview, Florida after a stolen vehicle chase ended in a crash. Deputies learned the vehicle had been reported stolen out of Jacksonville and tracked it as it moved through multiple counties on Interstate 10. Law enforcement attempted a traffic stop in Walton County, but the driver fled, continuing into Okaloosa County. The pursuit ended when the vehicle crashed off Brookmeade Drive in Crestview. Deputies and local police assisted in the arrest. Schlabach was taken into custody and charged in connection with the stolen vehicle and fleeing from law enforcement during the pursuit.
Charges: Grand theft auto, fleeing and eluding

Title: Armed Clearwater man fled on scooter after burglarizing vehicles, police say
description: A 25-year-old Clearwater man, Christian Lee, was arrested after he burglarized multiple vehicles in a residential area on Grove Street in Clearwater, Florida. Officers responded to reports of a suspect fleeing the scene on a scooter during the early morning hours. Police located Lee nearby, where he attempted to evade officers again by continuing on the scooter before running on foot. After a brief pursuit, he was taken into custody. Authorities reported that he was carrying a handgun at the time of arrest. He was booked into the Pinellas County Jail and faces felony charges for burglary and resisting arrest.
Charges: Armed burglary, resisting arrest without violence

Title: Carjacking suspect allegedly jumps fences, hides in home before arrest in Okaloosa County
description: A 30-year-old Fort Walton Beach man, Matthew Teems, was arrested after a carjacking and burglary incident that led to a multi-agency police response in Okaloosa County. Authorities say he initially attempted to break into a running vehicle with a woman and children inside, but the victim escaped and called 911. He later stole a vehicle and fled from law enforcement. During the pursuit, he abandoned the vehicle and ran through yards, jumping fences before entering a residence to hide. Deputies located him and took him into custody. Officials credited coordination between agencies and residents for the swift arrest.
Charges: Carjacking, burglary, grand theft auto, fleeing and eluding law enforcement

Title: Clearwater driver accused of going 129 mph to make it back from McDonald’s on time
description: A 19-year-old Clearwater man was arrested after police say he drove about 129 mph on U.S. Highway 19 near Sunset Point Road during a work break rush. An officer conducting speed enforcement detected the vehicle traveling roughly 120–130 mph in a 55 mph zone, with radar confirming 129 mph. The driver told police he was rushing back to work because McDonald’s took too long to prepare his food and he had a few minutes left on break. No injuries were reported. He was taken into custody and booked into Pinellas County Jail under Florida’s super speeder law for extreme speeding.
Charges: Speeding 129 mph in a 55 mph zone, reckless driving under Florida super speeder law

Title: Man accused of causing chaos in downtown Fort Myers, crashing car into light pole
description: A man in downtown Fort Myers allegedly fled from police after officers noticed a vehicle creating loud screeching noises while stationary on Dean Street. When officers approached, the driver, Zen Despagni, briefly stopped and then accelerated away, nearly striking an officer during the escape. Police later located the vehicle crashed into a light pole at the intersection of First Street and Monroe Street. Witnesses reported that the suspect struck a blue Tesla and left the scene before the crash. The suspect and another passenger were detained, and Despagni was later arrested after medical clearance and charged for multiple offenses related to the incident.
Charges: Fleeing and eluding police; resisting an officer without violence; hit and run; criminal mischief (two counts)

Title: Motorcyclist arrested after fleeing deputies, running into retention pond
description: A motorcyclist was arrested in Hillsborough County after attempting to flee from deputies during a traffic stop on Gibsonton Drive. Law enforcement tried to initiate a stop, but the rider refused and continued driving away. Deputies launched an aerial aviation unit to track the suspect as he abandoned the motorcycle and ran on foot. The suspect attempted to evade capture by entering a retention pond, but deputies quickly located and detained him without further incident. The arrest followed a brief pursuit involving both ground and air units, ending safely with the suspect taken into custody and facing multiple traffic-related and resisting charges.
Charges: Driving while license revoked as a habitual traffic offender; resisting an officer without violence

Title: Carjacker slips through backdoor of nail salon, steals woman's keys
description: A man entered a nail salon in Port Orange through a back door and stole a woman’s purse and car keys while she was receiving services. When the victim attempted to stop him, the suspect allegedly pointed a firearm at her before fleeing the scene in her vehicle. Law enforcement later identified the suspect as Robert Bryan Tokarz, who traveled from North Chesterfield, Virginia. Officers with the Port Orange Police Department and Volusia Sheriff’s Office pursued the suspect after the theft. He was eventually arrested following his attempt to escape from police custody. The incident involved armed robbery, vehicle theft, and a police pursuit.
Charges: Armed robbery; carjacking; grand theft auto; fleeing and eluding police

Title: Dashcam video shows Hollywood Police using grappler to stop fleeing driver
description: Hollywood Police responded on January 12, 2026, after reports of a man driving erratically. The suspect, identified as 46-year-old Harry Charles, refused to stop for officers and continued driving despite attempts to intervene. During the incident, he reportedly drove directly toward a patrol vehicle, creating a dangerous situation for law enforcement. Due to the escalating risk, officers coordinated with other agencies and used a grappler device deployed by Hollywood Police to safely stop the fleeing vehicle. The pursuit ended without reported injuries. Authorities later charged the driver following the successful stop and investigation into his driving behavior.
Charges: Careless driving

Title: Coral Springs Man Accused of Fleeing Traffic Stop, Resisting Arrest at Home
description: A Coral Springs man was arrested after a police officer observed him speeding on Westview Drive and attempted a traffic stop. The driver, identified as Mateusz Marcin Danczuk, initially failed to pull over and continued driving despite lights and sirens. He briefly stopped but then drove away again after being ordered to shut off his vehicle. Detectives later located his car at a residence on NW 120th Avenue. When officers approached, he ignored commands, walked back toward the house, and was eventually tackled and detained. The arrest followed a pursuit involving evasion from law enforcement and resistance at his home.
Charges: Fleeing police, resisting an officer without violence, speeding, failure to obey law enforcement, not wearing a seat belt

Title: Chitwood: Driver Shot by Deputy Fled Deputies for Over 6 Hours
description: Authorities in Volusia County reported a fatal shooting involving a suspect who fled deputies for over six hours before being stopped in DeLand. Police said the driver, Brandon Joseph Brabin, led law enforcement on multiple evasive incidents involving traffic violations, including running red lights and nearly striking vehicles. The pursuit ended in a Walmart Neighborhood Market parking lot, where deputies confronted the suspect. Officials stated the vehicle moved toward a deputy, prompting the officer to fire a single shot. Brabin was struck and died at the scene. The Florida Department of Law Enforcement is investigating the use of deadly force.
Charges: Fleeing law enforcement; reckless driving (prior warrant/probation-related history mentioned)

Title: Charlotte High School assistant principal Nicholas Brown arrested, accused of DUI
description: Nicholas Brown, 43, an assistant principal at Charlotte High School, was arrested after deputies responded to a report of a reckless driver in Charlotte County, Florida. Authorities said the vehicle drove over a median, damaged a traffic sign, and left the scene. Deputies later stopped the vehicle and observed significant front-end damage. They reported smelling alcohol, noticing Brown had difficulty maintaining his balance, and said he failed field sobriety tests. Breath test results reportedly measured between 0.189 and 0.181 blood alcohol concentration. During a vehicle search, deputies also found a THC vape cartridge, leading to additional drug-related charges.
Charges: DUI  Damage to property  Leaving the scene of a crash  Possession of a controlled substance without a prescription

Title: Teen arrested for reckless driving after crashing into Venice Beach Pavilion, police say
description: A 17-year-old driver was arrested after a high-speed crash into the Venice Beach Pavilion in Venice, Florida. Police say the vehicle struck the pavilion early in the morning while carrying four teenagers, including the driver. The impact caused serious injuries to all occupants, and they were transported to the hospital. Authorities reported significant damage to the pavilion and surrounding landscaping. The teen was later arrested the same night. Investigators charged him in connection with reckless driving that resulted in both serious bodily injury and property damage. The case involves a severe single-vehicle crash during early morning hours at a public beach area.
Charges: Reckless driving with serious bodily injury; reckless driving with property damage

Title: Illinois tourist gets DUI after stealing Key West police cruiser, cops say
description: John Mack, a 38-year-old tourist from La Grange, Illinois, was arrested after authorities said he stole a Key West Police Department patrol vehicle while intoxicated near the Key West Bight Marina. Police said he drove the cruiser around the marina parking lot after taking it from an officer working an off-duty detail. Officers located him nearby, where he admitted drinking several beers. He allegedly failed field sobriety testing, refused a breathalyzer test, resisted arrest, and was found without a valid driver's license. No fatalities or drug involvement were reported. The incident was investigated by the Key West Police Department.
Charges: DUI  Burglary  Grand theft  Grand theft of law enforcement equipment  Reckless driving  Refusal to submit to DUI testing  Resisting arrest without violence

Title: Man arrested for setting fire to Sanford temple, high-speed chase, officials say
description: A 51-year-old Georgia man allegedly set fire to the Wat Navaram Buddhist Temple in Sanford and then fled the scene in a Toyota RAV4, triggering a multi-county high-speed police pursuit. Officers attempted to speak with him after responding to reports of arson, but he immediately drove away. Law enforcement agencies including Sanford Police, Volusia County Sheriff’s Office, and Florida Highway Patrol joined the chase. The pursuit reached speeds around 115 mph on Interstate 4 and continued across several counties. The chase ended in St. Johns County when a trooper used a PIT maneuver, stopping the vehicle and arresting the suspect.
Charges: First-degree arson, burglary of an occupied dwelling, fleeing or attempting to elude law enforcement, resisting arrest without violence

Suspect Name: Elijah Eugene Russell; Treison Lachae Booker; Cortez Daymon Johnson
Title: 3 Georgia men accused of trying to break into home of 'Real Housewives' star in Miami
description: Three Georgia men were arrested after allegedly attempting to burglarize the home of reality television personality Larsa Pippen in Pinecrest, Florida. Police responded to a burglary in progress on March 29, 2026, and observed a vehicle fleeing the area. The vehicle crashed after colliding with another vehicle and a fence, and the suspects fled on foot. Officers from multiple agencies established a perimeter and arrested all three men. Investigators said two suspects were captured on security video damaging glass doors with a blunt object, causing more than $1,000 in damage. The third suspect allegedly acted as the getaway driver after the attempted burglary.

Title: Two Hawaii men arrested, charged for alleged burglary, shooting at Florida home
description: Two men from Hawaii were arrested after a violent attempted burglary in Sarasota County that escalated into a shooting at a residential home. According to investigators, the suspects broke into an occupied dwelling late at night on April 24, 2026. The homeowner confronted them during the intrusion, and multiple gunshots were fired through a sliding glass door, injuring the victim with cuts and wounds. The suspects fled the scene but were tracked by law enforcement, including aerial units, and later stopped in a getaway vehicle. Both individuals were detained and charged with serious felony offenses related to armed burglary and shooting into a dwelling.
Charges: First-degree burglary of an occupied dwelling while armed; second-degree aggravated battery with a deadly weapon; second-degree shooting into a dwelling

Title: Port Charlotte man arrested for DUI on an e-bike
description: Christian Cornell, 45, of Port Charlotte, was arrested after a Holmes Beach police officer observed him operating an electric bicycle erratically on Gulf Drive around 3 a.m. The officer reported Cornell crossed into the opposing travel lane, swerved from side to side, and nearly lost his balance while riding at approximately 20 mph. During the traffic stop, the officer observed signs of alcohol impairment. Cornell refused to perform field sobriety exercises and also declined to provide breath samples following his arrest. He was transported to a hospital for medical clearance before being booked into the Manatee County Jail and later released on bond.
Charges: Driving under the influence (DUI)

Title: Spring break chaos in Daytona Beach: Crowd panic, street fights and officer shot
description: Todd Martin, a 31-year-old suspect, was involved in a violent police pursuit in South Daytona, Florida during a chaotic spring break weekend. Officers attempted to stop him following an incident that escalated into a chase. The pursuit ended on Interstate 95 when the situation concluded with a crash involving a patrol vehicle. During the aftermath, Martin barricaded himself inside a police vehicle, which later caught fire. He suffered severe burns and was reported to be in critical condition. A South Daytona police officer was also shot during the incident and remained in good condition according to officials at the time.
Charges: Not specified

Title: Driver in Destin Charged with Trying to Hit Wife with Car Following Argument
description: Sonia Chaires, 29, of Houston was arrested after deputies responded to a domestic disturbance on Highway 98 in Destin around midnight. According to investigators, following a verbal argument, the other woman exited the Jeep and began walking along the sidewalk. Deputies said Chaires made a U-turn, drove onto the sidewalk, and attempted to strike the woman with the vehicle before leaving the area. Deputies stopped her a short time later and conducted a DUI investigation. They reported observing signs of impairment and finding open alcohol containers inside the Jeep. She was arrested and transported to the Okaloosa County Jail.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon Driving under the influence (DUI)

Title: Police: Georgia man on probation arrested after fleeing cops, crashing in Hollywood
description: On April 3, 2026, Hollywood Police officers conducted a traffic stop near North 19th Avenue and Tyler Street in Hollywood, Florida. During the stop, officers observed a large amount of cash, a firearm, and illicit drugs inside the vehicle. Brandon Cleve Dawkins, who was on federal probation from Georgia, was asked to exit the vehicle but instead fled in the car. He crashed into an electrical control box, continued fleeing on foot, abandoned the vehicle, and was later located at ArtsPark at Young Circle. Members of the Hollywood Police Department's ACE Unit arrested him without further incident.
Charges: Aggravated battery on a law enforcement officer Possession of a weapon or ammunition by a convicted felon  Fleeing and eluding police  Resisting an officer without violence  Driving with a suspended or revoked license

Title: Police ID man accused of leading officers on chase in Pinecrest, crashing in Broward
description: On May 24, 2026, Pinecrest Police officers conducting a crime prevention patrol observed a suspicious gray BMW parked on the wrong side of the road with its lights off. Several individuals dressed in black clothing and ski masks ran from a nearby yard and entered the vehicle. When officers approached, the driver intentionally reversed into a marked police vehicle before fleeing at a high speed. Officers initiated a pursuit but lost sight of the BMW. The vehicle later crashed in Hollywood, Florida, where Hollywood Police arrested Detric McClary. Authorities said the suspects had entered unlocked vehicles at the residence.
Charges: Trespassing of an unoccupied structure  Fleeing and eluding at a high speed  Resisting an officer without violence

Title: Florida DUI suspect tries to escape into ocean after high-speed pursuit, sheriff's office says
description: On January 8, 2026, Monroe County Sheriff’s deputies in the Florida Keys attempted to stop Joshua Derek Guajardo after reports of reckless driving near mile marker 65 on U.S. 1. Guajardo fled from law enforcement, reaching speeds up to 80 mph in a 55 mph zone and driving erratically. Deputies deployed spike strips, disabling his vehicle near mile marker 70. He then abandoned the SUV and ran into mangroves and water on the ocean side. During the pursuit, deputies reported he may have been seen with a possible firearm, prompting a larger response. He was later pulled from the water and arrested.
Charges: DUI  Fleeing and eluding law enforcement  Driving with a suspended license

Title: Florida man arrested for attempting traffic stop on undercover vehicle
description: Authorities in Hillsborough County reported that deputies were conducting undercover operations when a vehicle allegedly activated red and blue emergency lights behind an unmarked police car, attempting to initiate a traffic stop. The driver, identified as Nadi Jabari, was later stopped by detectives. Investigators reported recovering an illegal emergency lighting system, a light bar, and a firearm from the vehicle. Officials stated that Jabari was accused of impersonating law enforcement by using prohibited emergency lights to pull over the undercover unit. The incident was described by the sheriff’s office as dangerous due to the potential confusion and risk to public safety created.
Charges: False impersonation of law enforcement, unlawful use of blue emergency lights, possession of a firearm during commission of a felony

Title: Molino Man Charged With Fleeing Deputies On Motorcycle, Possessing Drugs In Dollar Bill
description: An Escambia County deputy observed a motorcycle traveling at a high rate of speed on East Nine Mile Road and attempted to initiate a traffic stop. The rider, later identified as Spencer Ray Stokes, fled from law enforcement, making evasive maneuvers through intersections and eventually losing contact with the pursuing deputy. Deputies later located the motorcycle parked behind a house under construction, where Stokes was found walking away from the area. A K-9 unit tracked his path and alerted to discarded items, including motorcycle keys and a folded dollar bill containing pills. Stokes admitted to parking the bike and leaving the area
Charges: Fleeing and eluding law enforcement with lights and sirens active, possession of a controlled substance without a prescription

Title: Levy County Traffic Pursuit Results in Arrest of Dangerous Felon
description: Deputies in Levy County, Florida initiated a traffic stop on April 8, 2026 after a vehicle ran a stop sign in the early morning hours. The driver fled, leading law enforcement on a pursuit through Bronson and onto SR 24 and US Highway 19, with Florida Highway Patrol joining the chase. The pursuit ended when troopers used a PIT maneuver to disable the vehicle and bring it to a stop west of Otter Creek. The passenger, identified as Travis W Merrell, was found with methamphetamine, provided false identity, and was arrested on multiple felony charges including warrants. pending investigation.
Charges: Providing False Identity; Resisting Arrest; Tampering with Evidence; Outstanding Violent Felony Warrants

Title: Burglary leads to chase and multi-car crash in West Little River: Deputies
description: A burglary incident in West Little River, Florida, escalated into a police pursuit after Miami-Dade deputies attempted to stop a suspect vehicle near Northwest 98th Street and 22nd Avenue. The driver fled, leading officers on a chase that ended in a multi-vehicle crash near Northwest 95th Street and 27th Avenue. Two vehicles were severely damaged, with one overturned. Four adults were transported to a trauma center in stable condition, and three individuals were taken into custody. Authorities recovered a rifle and a handgun from a vehicle. No deputies were injured, and the investigation is ongoing into the burglary and offenses.
Charges: Burglary investigation, fleeing and eluding police, and related traffic offenses (officially not fully specified)

Title: DUI Arrest: Molino Man Accused Of Battery On Pensacola Officer Following Crash
city and state: Pensacola / Molino area, Escambia County, Florida
description: Police responded to a single-vehicle crash in the Pensacola area after following a fluid trail from a damaged median wall. Officers located a disabled black BMW SUV with heavy front-end damage. The driver, Michael Tabium Watts, was found showing signs of impairment, including slurred speech, strong odor of alcohol, and poor coordination. A passenger reported he had been drinking vodka and smoking marijuana before driving. During field sobriety exercises, Watts became aggressive, resisted arrest, and allegedly grabbed an officer’s radio to prevent backup communication. Officers used physical force to subdue him before taking him into custody. He was charged with DUI and multiple violent offenses.
Charges: DUI (alcohol or drugs); Refusal to submit to DUI testing; Battery on a law enforcement officer; Resisting an officer with violence; Depriving an officer of communication/protection; Leaving the scene of a crash involving property damage; Possession of marijuana

Title: Man arrested after Escambia County standoff Thursday
description: Florida Highway Patrol and Escambia County deputies responded to a traffic stop in Escambia County, Florida that escalated into a standoff. Authorities reported that Wesley Spencer attempted to run over a trooper during the initial stop near Michigan Avenue and Valley Escadido Drive before fleeing the scene. He later barricaded himself inside a residence at Carriage Hills Apartments, where law enforcement initiated negotiations. After more than an hour, deputies deployed tear gas, and Spencer exited the home and was taken into custody. The incident involved a high-risk police encounter with both vehicle and armed standoff elements.
Charges: Fleeing and Attempting to Elude Law Enforcement; Aggravated Assault with a Motor Vehicle (additional charges pending)

Title: ICE detainer placed after DUI arrest of driver found asleep at wheel in Escambia County
description: Florida Highway Patrol and Escambia County deputies responded to a report of a driver found asleep behind the wheel of a locked pickup truck at an intersection in Pensacola, Florida. Officers discovered the vehicle stopped with the driver unresponsive and his foot on the brake. After repeated attempts, troopers were able to wake the driver, place the vehicle in park, and safely remove him. Authorities reported signs of alcohol impairment and confirmed the driver did not have a valid license. He was transported to a hospital for evaluation and later arrested after being medically cleared. ICE placed a detainer following the arrest.
Charges: DUI; Refusal to submit to breath test; Driving without a valid license

Title: Traffic stop turns into police chase in Holmes County
description: A traffic stop in Holmes County, Florida escalated into a brief police chase after deputies attempted to pull over Bobby Ray Bohannon for speeding on Highway 81. Bohannon allegedly fled from law enforcement during the stop, leading officers on a pursuit before he eventually pulled over at a residence on Horse Barn Road. He was taken into custody without further incident. A search of his vehicle reportedly uncovered several grams of methamphetamine. Investigators also determined he had previously trespassed on the same property in February, adding to the charges filed against him following the investigation by authorities thereafter officially charged
Charges: Fleeing and attempting to elude law enforcement, possession of methamphetamine, expired tag, trespassing

Title: Bodycam shows deputy shoot armed man after chase and crash in West Little River
description: Body camera footage released by Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office shows a deputy shooting an armed suspect, William Paulemon, after a chase and crash in West Little River on February 24, 2026. Authorities say a robbery intervention team attempted a traffic stop, but the vehicle fled, crashed into another car, and stopped near Northwest 87th Street. As deputies approached, Paulemon allegedly exited the vehicle armed with a gun in hand and another in his waistband. A deputy fired shots, striking him in the lower body. He was hospitalized and survived. The incident involved fleeing, reckless driving, and an armed confrontation with officers present
Charges: fleeing or eluding police, use or display of a firearm during felony, leaving the scene of a crash with property damage, reckless driving

Title: Alabama man arrested after fleeing traffic stop in Holmes County
description: On April 2, 2026, in Holmes County, Florida, deputies attempted a traffic stop on Highway 2A involving Alabama driver David McCormick of Geneva. The vehicle refused to stop and fled, committing multiple violations including passing in a no-passing zone, crossing double yellow lines, and running a stop sign. A pursuit continued north on Highway 185 until the vehicle reached the state line. McCormick was arrested. He admitted fleeing after throwing methamphetamine from the vehicle during the chase, which deputies recovered. He was taken into custody and charged with fleeing enforcement, reckless driving, tampering with evidence
Charges: Fleeing and attempting to elude law enforcement; reckless driving; tampering with evidence

Title: HCSO deputy arrested for DUI, leaving scene of crash
description: On May 11, 2026, in Sebring, Highlands County, Florida, a Highlands County Sheriff's Office deputy was involved in a minor traffic crash at Sebring Parkway and Kenilworth Boulevard around 7 a.m. After the collision, Deputy Lars Kirkegard left the scene in his vehicle The Florida Highway Patrol was requested to investigate by the sheriff's office Kirkegard was later located and arrested around 10 a.m. He was charged with driving under the influence and leaving the scene of a crash involving property damage No injuries were reported He was placed on administrative leave pending both criminal and internal investigations continuing review
Charges: Driving under the influence; leaving the scene of a crash involving property damage

Title: St. Lucie County deputy on unpaid leave after DUI arrest, officials say
description: Arthur Robert Alfaro, a 47-year-old St. Lucie County deputy, was arrested in Sebastian, Florida, after officers observed him driving 80 mph in a 30 mph zone. When police attempted a stop, he initially fled, leading to a brief pursuit that was later re-engaged and ended with a high-risk traffic stop in a cul-de-sac. Officers reported signs of impairment, including an alcohol odor, red eyes, and erratic driving. A passenger also stated he had been drinking. Alfaro refused field sobriety exercises but later consented to a breath test, which showed a BAC of 0.120 and 0.129. He was charged with DUI.
Charges: Driving under the influence (DUI)

Title: Lee County deputies arrest man accused of DUI, attempting to leave scene of crash on foot
description: Richard Childs, 25, was arrested in Fort Myers, Florida, after deputies responded to a two-vehicle crash involving a rear-end collision at McGregor Boulevard and Summerlin Road. Investigators said Childs, the driver of the Hyundai Elantra, appeared intoxicated, with alcohol on his breath and unstable movements. He allegedly attempted to leave the scene on foot but fell due to impairment. Deputies detained him after he resisted arrest and refused a breath test. He was later released from the hospital and booked on multiple charges, including DUI, hit-and-run, refusal to submit to testing, resisting arrest, and DUI with property damage.
Charges: DUI; DUI with property damage; hit and run; refusal to submit to DUI testing; resisting an officer without violence

Title: Hillsborough deputy faces DUI charges in Manatee County
description: A Hillsborough County Sheriff’s Office deputy, Shannon McBride, was arrested and appeared in court in Manatee County on DUI charges. Investigators said she was found behind the wheel of a vehicle on Manatee River Road after reports of a possibly impaired driver on September 29, 2026. Law enforcement observed clear signs of impairment during the stop. McBride, who worked as a jail detention deputy for seven years, refused to take a breath test. The case is proceeding through pre-trial court hearings in Manatee County. The incident involves alleged impaired driving while on duty as a law enforcement officer.
Charges: Driving Under the Influence (DUI), refusal to submit to breath test

Title: Driver accused of nearly crashing into NW Miami-Dade immigration office identified, charged with DUI
description: Orlando Deus, 42, was arrested after allegedly driving under the influence and nearly crashing into an immigration office in Northwest Miami-Dade. Deputies from the Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office responded after reports of a possible assault in a parking lot near Northwest Seventh Avenue and 88th Street. When officers approached his van, Deus reportedly sped away, then crashed into concrete fixtures outside the facility. Authorities said he failed a sobriety test at the scene. He was taken into custody and charged with DUI, fleeing law enforcement, and property damage while under the influence. The incident involved impaired driving and evading police.
Charges: Driving Under the Influence (DUI), fleeing law enforcement, damaging property or person while under the influence

Title: Woman faces DUI, crash charges after hitting Palm Beach County school bus
city and state: Boca Raton, Palm Beach County, Florida
description: Mary Aimee Elizabeth Tedder, 47, was arrested after police said she crashed her SUV into a Palm Beach County school bus carrying 15 children in Boca Raton. Investigators reported she drove onto a sidewalk, struck signs and bushes, and then collided with the rear passenger side of the bus. After the crash, she allegedly left the scene and was later found with signs of impairment including bloodshot eyes and slurred speech. Police said she refused a lawful blood test and showed inability to recall the incident, mentioning prescription drug use. She was charged with DUI, leaving the scene, and related offenses.
Charges: DUI with property damage or injury, leaving the scene of an accident, refusal to submit to blood test

Title: Two mugshots, same story: Stuart driver accused of another DUI arrest just 52 days later
description: Fernando C. Gutierrez Aguilar, a Stuart resident, was arrested by Stuart Police for driving under the influence for the second time in 52 days. Officers located him in a residential neighborhood where he was found to be impaired while operating a vehicle. This arrest followed a similar prior DUI incident in January, showing a pattern of repeated impaired driving. The Martin County Sheriff’s Office assisted Stuart Police during the investigation that led to his custody. Authorities emphasized ongoing enforcement of DUI laws in residential and public areas. The case highlights repeated offenses involving impaired driving within a short time period.
Charges: Driving Under the Influence (second offense within 52 days)

Title: Bertram Allen Arrested for DUI in Florida
description: On January 13, 2026, Irish Olympian Bertram Allen was arrested in West Palm Beach, Florida, after police responded to a crash on Southern Blvd near the Turnpike entrance. He was allegedly driving from Okeechobee Steakhouse when his vehicle collided with the rear of a stopped car. Officers reported signs of impairment including slurred speech, glassy watery eyes, odor of alcohol, and orbital sway. Breath tests recorded .228 and .242 BAC. No injuries were reported. Allen was arrested for DUI unlawful blood alcohol level causing damage to property or another person. He later entered a not guilty plea through his attorney.
Charges: DUI unlawful blood alcohol level causing damage to property or another person

Title: Man charged with DUI, child neglect after boy hurt in e-bike accident in Port St. Lucie
description: On March 10, 2026, Kevin Joseph Cline was arrested in Port St. Lucie, Florida, after deputies said he operated a motorized bicycle while intoxicated with a child riding on the back. According to investigators, Cline attempted to ride onto a sidewalk near a McDonald’s when the bicycle fell, causing the child to suffer minor knee scrapes. Deputies observed a strong odor of alcohol and multiple signs of impairment during field sobriety exercises. Breath tests later recorded blood alcohol concentrations of .116 and .119. Cline was arrested and booked into the St. Lucie County Jail on multiple charges.
Charges: Driving under the influence (DUI) Child neglect without great bodily harm

Title: VIDEO: Florida mom arrested for DUI at speeds over 120 mph with toddler in car, officers say
description: On May 8, 2026, a woman was arrested in Jacksonville, Florida, after officers stopped her for driving approximately 120 miles per hour on Interstate 10 with her three-year-old child in the back seat. Officers reported smelling alcohol and marijuana during the traffic stop. The driver stated she was hurrying home to bring food to a 10-year-old child she had left alone. A vehicle search allegedly found a lit marijuana joint and multiple empty alcohol bottles. She was arrested for driving under the influence and violating Florida’s Super Speeder Law. Authorities did not publicly release her identity.
Charges: Driving under the influence (DUI) Violation of Florida’s Super Speeder Law

Title: Speeding, allegedly late for haircut appointment lands man in jail; second accused of DUI
description: Port St. Lucie Police arrested Luis Serpas after a traffic stop during patrols on St. Lucie West Boulevard and U.S. Highway 1. Officers reported Serpas was driving under the influence, fleeing and eluding police, driving without a valid license, and resisting an officer without violence. He was observed with a strong odor of alcohol. After being stopped, he was taken into custody and transported to the St. Lucie County Jail. His vehicle was also towed as part of the enforcement action.
Charges: DUI, fleeing and eluding, driving without a valid license, resisting an officer without violence

Title: Ocala man arrested after allegedly traveling to meet an underage girl
description: A 25-year-old man, Horatio Carrie, was arrested after traveling from Ocala to Lake City, Florida, to meet someone he believed was a 14-year-old girl. According to investigators, he had been communicating online with an undercover detective posing as a minor. Authorities say Carrie also sent inappropriate images during the communications. He was taken into custody at the arranged meeting location without incident. Law enforcement confirmed he was already on probation for a prior fleeing and eluding case at the time of the arrest. He is being held without bond pending further legal proceedings in Columbia County.
Charges: Traveling to meet a minor, violation of probation ;fleeing and eluding

Title: Suspect in custody after high-speed chase ends in crash near Shadeville Elementary, FHP says
description: A 15-year-old boy from Crawfordville was arrested after leading Florida Highway Patrol and local deputies on a high-speed chase in a stolen pickup truck. Authorities say the teen, who was also reported missing, stole the vehicle and attempted to flee law enforcement. During the pursuit, he drove off-road and traveled near railroad tracks before reentering a roadway, where the truck collided with an SUV carrying three people. The vehicle then overturned and struck a utility pole before coming to rest. All individuals involved suffered minor injuries. The suspect was taken into custody after the crash.
Charges: Grand theft auto, fleeing or attempting to elude law enforcement, reckless driving, additional juvenile-related charges

Title: LCSO: 2 burglary suspects detained after fleeing from traffic stop
description: Lee County Sheriff’s Office and Florida Highway Patrol responded to an active scene in Cape Coral after two burglary suspects fled from a traffic stop. Authorities say the suspects were initially detained after a pursuit involving multiple law enforcement units. The case remained active as detectives worked to identify all involved parties. Viewer dashcam footage reportedly captured the chase between deputies and the suspects. Both individuals were ultimately taken into custody following the incident. Officials have not released additional identifying details while the investigation continues.
Charges: Burglary (suspected), fleeing or attempting to elude law enforcement (reported), additional charges pending investigation

Title: Midway's Kanzigg to lead Navarre Beach Fire in wake of chief's arrest
description: Navarre Beach Fire Chief Daniel Fureigh was arrested in Santa Rosa County, Florida, after violating probation conditions that required him to abstain from drugs and alcohol. Authorities reported that a court-ordered drug test conducted on April 2, 2026, returned positive for cocaine, later confirmed by a laboratory. He had previously been placed on probation following a DUI arrest that was reduced to reckless driving. Officials also alleged he failed to attend a mandatory DUI impact panel. Fureigh was booked into jail in early May 2026 and later released on bond the same day. The fire district moved to replace him.
Charges: Probation violation, cocaine use (positive test), failure to attend DUI impact panel DUI

Title: Toledo man flees from police after warrant issued for felonious assault
description: Chase Carter, 19, was arrested in Toledo after police attempted to execute a search and arrest warrant related to a felonious assault case. Officers said Carter fled from a residence in north Toledo by jumping out of a second-story window while carrying a loaded handgun. During the pursuit, he allegedly discarded the firearm and an extra magazine over a fence into a nearby yard. Authorities noted the escape occurred in a residential area with people present, creating a public safety risk. He was taken into custody and charged with obstructing official business, tampering with evidence, and felonious assault pending court proceedings.
Charges: Obstructing official business, tampering with evidence, felonious assault fleeing law enforcement

Title: Suspect arrested after police chase
description: Police in Franklin, Ohio pursued a vehicle connected to a burglary investigation and an active warrant, leading to a chase into Middletown. Officers located the suspect vehicle on Fourth Street and attempted a traffic stop, but the driver, identified as Zachary Clary, fled. The pursuit continued across multiple roads with assistance from Warren County Sheriff’s Office, Middletown Police, and Ohio State Highway Patrol. The chase ended in Middletown where Clary was arrested without further incident. Authorities confirmed he was already wanted in Franklin Municipal Court and is now facing additional charges for failure to comply a third-degree felony charge case
Charges: Failure to comply (third-degree felony)

Title: Dash-cam video of fatal deputy-involved shooting on I-85 released
description: Austin Robertson was involved in a traffic stop along Interstate 85 near Exit 11 in Anderson County on April 20, 2026. According to investigators, deputies struggled with Robertson during the stop before placing him in the back of a patrol vehicle. Authorities said Robertson shot an Anderson County deputy during the encounter, and another deputy returned fire. Robertson was fatally shot at the scene. The injured deputy was transported to a hospital and released several days later. Dash-camera video of the incident was later released by the South Carolina Law Enforcement Division, which continues to investigate the deputy-involved shooting.
Charges: Aggravated assault on a law enforcement officer (alleged), exact charges not fully listed due to fatal outcome

Title: Driver strikes multiple Miami-Dade deputies while fleeing traffic stop
description: Two male suspects were taken into custody after a traffic stop in Miami-Dade County escalated into a brief pursuit and collision with deputies on April 8, 2026. Deputies attempted to detain a wanted suspect near Southwest 184th Street and 122nd Avenue when the driver fled, striking multiple deputies with the vehicle. A chase followed and ended near the Florida Turnpike and Southwest 40th Street. The deputies sustained minor injuries and were treated at the scene. Officials reported that a female passenger was released, while charges for the two male suspects were pending following their arrest.
Charges: Charges pending

Title: Palm Beach County chase reaches 90 mph, ends at hospital; suspect identified
description: The incident involved a 22-year-old man, Diego Moran, who allegedly fled from Palm Beach County Sheriff’s Office deputies after being pursued for reckless driving in a Chrysler Pacifica. During the pursuit, Moran reportedly attempted to ram a law enforcement vehicle, forcing deputies to take evasive action. The chase reached speeds over 90 mph in a 40 mph zone and moved through city streets. It ended at St. Mary’s Medical Center in West Palm Beach, where the suspect fled on foot into the hospital. Officers conducted a lockdown search and eventually found him hiding inside a hospital room before arresting him.
Charges: Fleeing a law enforcement officer; aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill; driving without a valid license

Title: Keys deputy misused official databases to pursue woman he met on set of ‘Bad Monkey’: MCSO
description: A Monroe County Sheriff’s Office deputy, Lamar Eliseo Roman, was arrested after investigators said he misused law enforcement databases to track down a woman he met while working security on a television production set. Authorities allege he accessed official systems without authorization and entered the woman’s license plate into a “hotlist” system so he could locate her vehicle. He later conducted a traffic stop on U.S. 1 after allegedly speeding and passing vehicles in a dangerous manner. Investigators say the stop was improper and unreported. The deputy admitted to using the system and acknowledged his actions were inappropriate during questioning.
Charges: Accessing a computer or electronic device without authority

Title: JBPD: Driver faces DUI charges after crashing into patrol car during traffic stop
description: Jacksonville Beach Police Department reported that a suspected impaired driver struck a patrol vehicle during an active DUI traffic stop on 3rd Street South. Officers had already detained one driver when another vehicle approached the scene without headlights and failed to respond to emergency lights or verbal warnings. The approaching vehicle collided with the patrol car, forcing an officer to take evasive action to avoid injury. No officers or civilians were harmed in the incident. Authorities arrested the driver at the scene. Police stated the case highlights the dangers posed by impaired driving and the importance of safe driving behavior.
Charges: DUI DUI with property damage

Title: Eagle One helps track Clermont man to Eustis after fleeing traffic stop
description: Brandon Stuart Brown, a 32-year-old man from Clermont, was arrested in Lake County, Florida, after deputies attempted a traffic stop on a Chevrolet Tahoe with expired tags and equipment violations. According to the Lake County Sheriff’s Office, Brown failed to stop and led deputies on a high-speed pursuit through multiple communities, reaching speeds over 85 mph in a 55 mph zone. The vehicle was later tracked by a sheriff’s helicopter, Eagle One, while deputies deployed stop sticks, disabling the vehicle. Brown fled on foot but was quickly apprehended without incident. He admitted to fleeing and acknowledged multiple vehicle-related violations during questioning.
Charges: Fleeing to elude law enforcement; attaching tag not assigned; driving while license suspended/canceled/revoked ; operating an unregistered motor vehicle

Title: ICE AGENT ARRESTED FOR DUI ASKS JUDGE TO END 1-YEAR PROBATION AFTER 2½ MONTHS
description: On August 13, 2025, Monroe County Sheriff's Office deputies stopped Scott Deiseroth on the Bahia Honda Bridge after a 911 caller reported his pickup truck driving erratically, including traveling in the wrong direction. Deputies observed an overwhelming odor of alcohol, glassy eyes, and unsteady movement. Two young children were inside the vehicle. Deiseroth allegedly failed roadside sobriety tests, resisted arrest, and later provided breath samples measuring 0.170 and 0.174 blood alcohol concentration. He pleaded no contest to driving under the influence and was sentenced to one year of probation, while prosecutors declined to pursue child neglect and resisting arrest charges.
Charges: Driving under the Influence (DUI)

Title: Chase through West Palm Beach ends inside hospital after traffic stop turns violent
description: Investigators with the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office attempted a traffic stop on a driver in West Palm Beach at about 9 p.m. Authorities said the driver allegedly committed an aggravated assault with a deadly weapon against an agent during the stop, prompting a vehicle pursuit. The chase continued through city streets before ending at St. Mary's Medical Center with assistance from the Florida Highway Patrol and the West Palm Beach Police Department. The suspect abandoned the vehicle and entered the hospital, leading to a temporary lockdown. Officers located the suspect after a brief search and arrested the individual without further incident. No additional injuries were reported.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon

Title: Ravenna police: 2 ejected from SUV after wanted suspect flees traffic stop, flips vehicle at I-76 ramp
description: Ravenna Police reported a traffic stop on a Cleveland man with outstanding felony warrants that escalated into a police pursuit. The driver initially stopped for officers but then fled the scene, leading police on a chase through multiple roads in Ravenna, Ohio. During the pursuit, the suspect continued driving at speed before attempting to enter an interstate ramp. The vehicle failed to navigate the curve, overturned multiple times, and crashed. Both the driver and a passenger were ejected from the SUV and injured. Emergency medical services transported them to a nearby hospital. The suspect faces multiple felony charges related to fleeing police.
Charges: Failure to comply with order or signal of police officer (third-degree felony)

Title: Caller tips off police to OVI suspect with an open liquor bottle in his Jeep: North Olmsted Police Blotter
description: North Olmsted Police arrested a male driver for operating a vehicle while intoxicated after a citizen reported a suspected impaired driver. The caller was following a red Jeep Wrangler that was reportedly weaving across lanes and driving erratically while traveling from Fairview Park into North Olmsted. Officers located the vehicle after it made a wide turn and observed continued lane violations. Police activated emergency lights and conducted a traffic stop. The driver was found to be in violation of OVI laws and was taken into custody. The incident highlights the role of citizen reporting in identifying impaired driving and preventing potential crashes.
Charges: Operating a vehicle while intoxicated (OVI)

Title: 16 children rescued from 'deplorable conditions' in Ohio home, officials say: 'Beyond comprehension'
description: Authorities in Vinton County, Ohio, removed 16 children ranging from 18 months to 18 years old from a residence in Hamden after executing a search warrant on June 30, 2026. Officials described the home as being in “deplorable conditions,” including unsanitary living spaces and severe neglect. Seven children required hospitalization, with at least one in critical condition. The investigation indicated the children were largely confined, not enrolled in school, and some could not speak. Authorities stated the situation appeared to be an intra-family case involving grandparents and parents accused of long-term abuse and neglect. Officials called the evidence “beyond comprehension.”
Charges: 16 counts of endangering children (second-degree felony) for each suspect

Title: Cape Coral police chase, arrest driver accused of fleeing traffic stop at more than 100 mph
description: Chase Ciano, a 22-year-old man, was arrested after Cape Coral police said he fled from an attempted traffic stop while driving a dark gray BMW. Officers initially observed him traveling about 60 mph in a 35 mph zone on Del Prado Boulevard South. When police activated emergency lights and sirens, Ciano accelerated and reportedly reached approximately 102 mph in a 30 mph zone. Officers pursued the vehicle until locating it in a parking lot on Cape Coral Street, where Ciano allegedly tried to hide inside a plaza before being arrested. Police emphasized the dangers of his reckless driving through city streets.
Charges: Fleeing/eluding law enforcement Speeding at 100+ mph

Title: Wanted Orlando man leaves young kid behind while fleeing deputies, video shows
description: Jason Kenon, a 24-year-old Orlando man, was arrested after deputies said he fled from law enforcement while driving recklessly with two young children in his vehicle. During the pursuit, Kenon crashed into another vehicle and allowed a passenger to leave with a 1-year-old child but drove away with a 4-year-old still inside. He later stopped, abandoned the vehicle, and fled on foot, leaving the child behind. Deputies quickly apprehended him, and both children were evaluated and found uninjured. Authorities said Kenon was wanted at the time of the incident and now faces multiple felony charges.
Charges: Aggravated fleeing and eluding Leaving the scene of a crash Possession of a firearm in the commission of a felony Two counts of child abuse

Title: Florida man, woman arrested after fleeing deputies with child in back seat
description: A traffic stop in Hillsborough County escalated when deputies attempted to stop a vehicle driven by a habitual traffic offender. The driver and passenger reportedly switched seats before fleeing, leading to a pursuit onto Interstate 75. Florida Highway Patrol assisted as deputies attempted to stop the vehicle again on Big Bend Road, but it continued. A child was found secured in a rear car seat during the incident. The pursuit ended after deputies deployed a tactical stop and K-9 units assisted in arrests. Body camera footage showed the suspects being taken into custody. Both individuals faced multiple felony charges later
Charges: Rogelio Murillo: driving while license revoked (habitual offender), Lourdes Guerrero: fleeing and eluding law enforcement, aggravated fleeing, aggravated child abuse, aggravated assault on a law enforcement officer with a deadly weapon while committing a felony.

Title: ‘A pursuit implies speed:’ Florida motorcyclist very slowly flees from deputy
description: A Flagler County deputy attempted to stop a motorcycle at around 2:23 a.m. after noticing it had no lights and no license plate. The rider allegedly tried to flee, but the pursuit remained slow and unstable due to the condition of the motorcycle. Deputies described the incident as more of a “slow-speed chase” than a typical high-speed pursuit. The rider, later identified as Brian Swartz, eventually lost control of the motorcycle and fell, which led to his arrest. Authorities reported he had an extensive prior criminal history involving multiple arrests, including previous fleeing incidents and various property and vehicle-related offenses.
Charges: Fleeing or attempting to elude law enforcement; operating without a driver’s license

Title: Man Arrested After Attempting to Conduct Fake Traffic Stop on Undercover HCSO Vehicle
description: Hillsborough County deputies arrested a man after he allegedly attempted to conduct a fake traffic stop on an undercover sheriff’s office vehicle. The suspect was reportedly driving a black Chevrolet Suburban that activated red and blue emergency lights while following the undercover unit on U.S. Highway 301 North. Deputies intervened and stopped the vehicle for investigation. During the search, law enforcement recovered illegal emergency lighting equipment, including a light bar, along with a firearm. Authorities stated the suspect was impersonating law enforcement, which is considered a serious public safety offense. No injuries were reported during the incident or arrest.
Charges: False personation; unlawful use of blue lights; possession of firearm during commission of a felony

Title: Deputies, officer fatally shoot armed suspect in Davie, Broward sheriff says
description: Broward Sheriff’s deputies and a Plantation Police officer attempted to take a suspect into custody in Davie on an active warrant related to fleeing and eluding. The suspect was located at a Wawa gas station and then ran across the street to a McDonald’s while armed with a firearm. Deputies pursued him on foot and attempted to detain him in the parking lot. During the encounter, the suspect allegedly raised or attempted to point his weapon at law enforcement officers. Officers then discharged their firearms, striking the suspect. The suspect died at the scene. Authorities noted he had a history of fleeing incidents.
Charges: Active warrant for fleeing and eluding; additional prior criminal charge

Title: Man in US illegally arrested after fleeing during traffic stop, injuring ICE agent
description: Florida Highway Patrol’s Criminal Alien Apprehension Team and ICE agents conducted a traffic stop in Orange County, Florida, during which multiple occupants exited the vehicle and fled on foot. One suspect, identified as Elias Bautista, allegedly ran from an ICE agent who pursued him on foot and attempted to detain him. Authorities say a physical struggle occurred during the arrest attempt, during which Bautista struck the ICE agent, causing a significant head injury. He then fled the scene. Following an investigation involving multiple law enforcement agencies, Bautista was later located and taken into custody during a targeted operation with assistance from the Levy County Sheriff’s Office and ICE.
Charges: Aggravated battery on a law enforcement officer; resisting arrest

Title: Serial armed robbery suspect arrested after fleeing crime scene in Lyft: JSO
description: Jaheim Muhammad, a 21-year-old Jacksonville man, was arrested after allegedly committing a series of armed robberies at multiple convenience stores and fast food restaurants over the span of less than a week. Investigators say he targeted locations including a Whataburger on San Jose Boulevard, a Domino’s on Cassat Avenue, a Dollar General on Old Kings Road South, and a Mobil gas station on Old St. Augustine Road. In one case, he allegedly fled using a Lyft ride, which helped detectives track him to his apartment complex. Surveillance and witness statements linked him to the crimes. He was arrested and charged after being taken into custody by Jacksonville Sheriff’s Office detectives.
Charges: Five counts of armed robbery, resisting officers, and additional related charges

Title: Man wanted on a Lake City BOLO arrested in Columbia County after high-speed chase
description: A Columbia County Sheriff’s Office deputy attempted a traffic stop on a red Ford pickup truck linked to a Lake City BOLO alert. The driver, identified as 48-year-old Samuel Watson, allegedly fled the stop and led deputies on a high-speed chase on State Road 47 and CR-240, reaching speeds over 100 mph. During the pursuit, Watson reportedly lost control of the vehicle, causing it to overturn onto its side. A passenger exited the vehicle before Watson was taken into custody after being medically cleared at a hospital. The passenger was released without charges. Authorities reported the vehicle had equipment violations, and Watson was later arrested on multiple charges, including fleeing and eluding.
Charges: Fleeing and eluding law enforcement, driving with a suspended license

Title: DeSoto County man accused of stealing car arrested after lengthy chase
description: Deputies in DeSoto County responded to a report of a robbery involving a man identified as Jeremy Bernard Daniels, 36. Authorities say Daniels was initially giving a victim a ride when he allegedly threw the victim’s phone out of the vehicle. When the victim exited the car to retrieve the phone, Daniels allegedly stole the victim’s keys and drove off with the vehicle. Law enforcement later located Daniels, but he reportedly fled again, leading officers on a lengthy pursuit involving multiple agencies, including the Arcadia Police Department. The chase ended when officers successfully stopped the vehicle and took Daniels into custody.
Charges: Robbery by sudden snatching, fleeing to elude law enforcement, resisting without violence

Title: Man accused of driving through crowd at Palatka block party booked into Clay County jail
description: Lazayus Bartley, 36, of Palatka, is accused of driving a vehicle through a crowd during a City of Palatka-approved block party at 20th and Eagle Streets. According to police, multiple people were injured during the incident. After driving through the crowd, Bartley allegedly fled the scene, leading officers on a pursuit. Law enforcement later attempted to stop him again when he returned, but he reportedly crashed into a patrol vehicle and other vehicles and people. Officers fired at Bartley during the confrontation. He was taken into custody after being hospitalized for treatment. Authorities charged him following the incident involving the crowd and subsequent pursuit.
Charges: Two counts of aggravated battery with a deadly weapon, aggravated fleeing and eluding with injury

Title: Louisiana Teen Arrested For Fleeing Deputies, Crashing into Innocent Driver
description: A Louisiana teen identified as Peyton Jeremy Jackson fled from Escambia County Sheriff’s Office deputies during a traffic stop attempt in Escambia County. Deputies tried to stop a silver Honda sedan driven by Jackson, but he allegedly fled the scene at high speed. During the pursuit, Jackson crashed into a Hyundai sedan driven by an innocent 20-year-old woman near Mobile Highway and Massachusetts Avenue in Pensacola. Law enforcement later arrested him following the crash. Authorities reported that no injuries occurred in the incident. The Florida Highway Patrol assisted with the investigation.
Charges: Aggravated fleeing and eluding; hit-and-run with property damage; driving without a valid driver’s license

Title: 2 arrested after armed robbery at Bradenton grocery store, Manatee deputies say
description: Juan Falcon and Alexander G. Turner were arrested following an armed robbery at Tienda Latina grocery store in Bradenton, Florida. According to authorities, the suspects entered the store wearing masks and carrying handguns. They allegedly fired shots into the ceiling to intimidate people inside before stealing cash from the register. After fleeing in an older gray sedan, deputies located their vehicle just a few blocks away. Law enforcement executed search warrants and recovered two handguns inside the car. Both suspects were taken into custody without further incident. The investigation was handled by the Manatee County Sheriff’s Office. No injuries were reported.
Charges: Armed robbery; discharge of a firearm during commission of a felony (reported); weapons charges

Title: Holmes County fugitive caught after police chase
description: Christian Crook, a known fugitive in Holmes County, Florida, was arrested after deputies spotted a vehicle matching her description on Highway 160. She had multiple outstanding warrants, including possession of a controlled substance, resisting without violence, escape, and felony battery. When deputies attempted a traffic stop, Crook fled, triggering a pursuit through several roads in the county. The chase ended when additional deputies forced her vehicle off the roadway. She was identified as the driver and taken into custody without further incident. She was also charged with fleeing or attempting to elude, reckless driving, suspended license, and improper tag use.
Charges: resisting without violence, escape, felony battery, fleeing and attempting to elude, driving with suspended license, improper/unauthorized tag, reckless driving,Possession of a controlled substance (3 counts)

Title: Video shows PBSO deputy deploying Taser on fleeing motorcyclist who then slams into SUV on Hypoluxo Road
description: Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office deputies attempted to stop Stanley Jacques after observing him riding a motorbike recklessly near Hypoluxo Road on April 9, 2026. Jacques fled the initial stop and was confronted a second time by deputies. During the encounter, a deputy deployed a Taser, but authorities stated it did not make contact with Jacques. He immediately accelerated onto Hypoluxo Road and collided head-on with an SUV. Jacques was thrown from the motorbike and suffered severe head injuries, leaving him in critical condition. Authorities had not announced whether he would face criminal charges if he recovered.
Charges: fleeing and attempting to elude

Title: Illegal street takeover party busted near Bay Point
description: Bay County Sheriff's Office deputies responded to reports of an illegal street takeover on Magnolia Beach Road on April 8, 2026, after receiving multiple calls about roads being blocked by vehicles and pedestrians. Participants fled when deputies arrived and later moved the gathering to Beach Drive. Investigators identified several participants the following day and arrested multiple individuals connected to the event. Jayden Mathis was arrested for fleeing and obstructing the roadway. Authorities also impounded five vehicles allegedly used during the illegal street takeover. The investigation remained active as deputies continued identifying additional suspects and vehicles involved in the unlawful gathering.
Charges: Fleeing; Obstructing the Roadway

Title: Gainesville man arrested after stealing car, fleeing to roof of a home
description: Alachua County Sheriff's Office deputies arrested Camren Banks after he allegedly stole a vehicle in southwest Gainesville on March 14, 2026. Deputies located the stolen car and surrounded it, prompting Banks to flee by climbing onto the roof of a nearby home in an attempt to avoid arrest. After remaining on the roof for a period of time, Banks surrendered peacefully to deputies without further incident. Authorities took him into custody and charged him in connection with the stolen vehicle. Investigators also stated they were searching for a second suspect believed to have been involved in the incident.
Charges: Burglary; Grand Theft Auto

Title: Multi-county high-speed chase ends in arrest
description: A 23-year-old man, Wilnick Brutus, was arrested after allegedly leading law enforcement officers on a high-speed pursuit across Charlotte, Lee, and Collier counties in Florida on January 31, 2026. Authorities said he fled in a 2025 blue Lexus SUV after deputies attempted to stop him on Interstate 75. Florida Highway Patrol located the vehicle in Lee County, but the suspect continued driving south at high speed. The pursuit ended in Collier County after deputies deployed stop sticks near Exit 107 at Pine Ridge Road, disabling the SUV. Brutus was arrested without further incident and booked into the Collier County Jail.
Charges: Fleeing and eluding Driving while license suspended

Title: Deputies search for Alachua County man accused of kidnapping pregnant woman, fleeing in Dixie County
description: Ayandre Ross, 34, is accused of kidnapping a pregnant woman from her home in Alachua County, Florida, and driving her into Dixie County on January 5, 2026. Authorities attempted to conduct a traffic stop after locating the vehicle, but Ross fled the scene. Law enforcement successfully rescued the victim, while Ross escaped into a wooded area north of Old Town. Deputies from the Dixie County Sheriff's Office, assisted by multiple agencies, searched the area but were unable to locate him. The Alachua County Sheriff's Office later requested the public's assistance in finding Ross, who remained wanted at the time of the report.
Charges: Kidnapping Aggravated battery on a pregnant woman Burglary

Title: Motorcyclist arrested after fleeing deputies, running into retention pond
description: Leaf was arrested after fleeing from Hillsborough County Sheriff's deputies during a traffic stop in Hillsborough County, Florida, early on May 29, 2026. Deputies attempted to stop his motorcycle on Gibsonton Drive, but he refused to pull over and sped away. The Sheriff's Office Aviation Unit tracked him from the air after he abandoned the motorcycle and fled on foot. While trying to escape, he entered a retention pond, where deputies quickly took him into custody without further incident. He was charged with driving while his license was revoked as a habitual traffic offender and resisting an officer without violence.
Charges: Driving While License Revoked as a Habitual Traffic Offender Resisting an Officer Without Violence

Title: Caught on Video: Driver arrested for going 113 mph in Port St. Lucie: Authorities
description: Joseph Moylan, a 26-year-old man, was arrested after police allegedly recorded him driving 113 miles per hour on Port St. Lucie Boulevard late Thursday night. Officers with the Port St. Lucie Police Department conducted a traffic stop after detecting the excessive speed on radar. Body camera footage captured the stop and the arrest. Authorities stated the arrest was made under a new law allowing arrest for drivers exceeding the speed limit by more than 50 miles per hour. Moylan was taken into custody, charged, and later released after posting a $150 bond. No injuries, crashes, or additional criminal activity were reported.
Charges: Moving traffic violation for operating a vehicle 50 mph over the speed limit

Title: Man arrested in Cape Coral after driving 108 mph in 50 mph zone, officers say
description: Anthony Melendez Torres, 20, was arrested after Cape Coral police accused him of driving 108 miles per hour in a 50 mph zone on Veterans Parkway East. According to officers, Torres drove past a police officer in a white Ford Mustang at the excessive speed on May 28, 2026. The officer immediately conducted a traffic stop and questioned Torres, who reportedly offered no explanation for his actions. Police arrested him at the scene under Florida's super speeder law. No crash, injuries, or additional criminal activity were reported in connection with the incident. The case involved only the alleged excessive speeding violation.
Charges: Super speeding

Title: ‘Leg is killing me’: St. Augustine man clocked at 105 mph on I-95 was trying to get to rest stop
description: Rafael Lopez, 62, of St. Augustine was arrested after deputies allegedly clocked him driving 105 mph on Interstate 95 southbound near mile marker 283 in Flagler County. According to the Flagler County Sheriff's Office, Lopez told the deputy his leg was hurting and locked up, and he was trying to reach a nearby rest area instead of stopping on the highway shoulder. Body camera footage captured the traffic stop and conversation. Authorities noted Lopez had a prior speeding conviction from 2022 for driving 127 mph in a 60 mph zone. He was arrested under Florida's super speeder law and later released on bond.
Charges: Dangerously operating a vehicle at 100 mph or more

Title: Florida man doing 101 mph in a 55-mph zone was trying to ‘avoid an animal,’ deputies say
description: Gregory Dolcine, a 32-year-old man in Seminole County, Florida, was arrested after deputies observed him driving at 101 mph in a 55 mph zone on State Road 46 near Geneva. Law enforcement said the vehicle was traveling at an excessively high rate of speed as it crossed a bridge over the St. Johns River around 1 a.m. When stopped, Dolcine told deputies he was speeding to avoid an animal in the roadway. He was charged under Florida’s dangerous excessive speeding law, which criminalizes driving over 100 mph in a way that endangers others. He was booked and later released on bond
Charges: Dangerous excessive speeding (over 100 mph in a 55 mph zone)

Title: 19-year-old accused of driving 108 mph on Burnt Store Rd in Cape Coral
description: Elijah Murray, a 19-year-old driver, was arrested in Cape Coral, Florida, after police reported he was driving an SUV at 108 mph in a 55 mph zone on Burnt Store Road during the early morning hours. Officers initiated a traffic stop and observed the vehicle briefly attempt evasive movement after stopping. The SUV contained six occupants, all of whom were detained and later released except the driver. Authorities said Murray was identified as the operator and taken into custody. He was charged under Florida’s dangerous excessive speeding law for driving over 100 mph, a violation that carries enhanced penalties due to public risk
Charges: Dangerous excessive speeding (100+ mph in a 55 mph zone)

Title: Man arrested, charged after leading police on 'lengthy pursuit' through Toledo, Ottawa Hills
description: Keith Carter, 32, allegedly led police on a high-speed pursuit through Toledo after officers attempted to stop him for running a red light. When officers requested identification, he reportedly fled, reaching speeds over 90 mph while driving through city streets. During the chase, his vehicle collided with multiple cars, struck traffic signs, and hit curbs, eventually losing a tire. The pursuit ended at West Bancroft Street and Boshart Way, where police, including a K-9 unit, arrested him. Authorities reported finding two pistols and suspected fentanyl in the vehicle. Carter was prohibited from possessing firearms due to a prior felony conviction.
Charges: Carrying concealed weapons Improper handling of firearms in a motor vehicle  Having weapons under disability Failure to comply with order of a police officer

Title: Urbana man arrested on OVI charge following reckless driving report
description: Bruce Simon, an Urbana man, was arrested after police responded to a report of a reckless driver on North Main Street. Officers located a yellow Jeep being driven erratically, reportedly unable to stay in its lane and nearly causing a head-on collision. After a traffic stop, Simon showed signs of impairment, including glassy eyes and slow speech. He admitted to drinking earlier. Field sobriety tests indicated impairment, and a breath test recorded a blood alcohol concentration of 0.188, more than twice the legal limit. He was taken into custody and charged with operating a vehicle impaired and marked lane violation.
Charges: Operating a vehicle impaired (OVI) Marked lane violation

Title: Pensacola man charged for DUI after crashing through graveyard, damaging headstones
description: Richard Vallandingham, 40, was arrested after allegedly driving under the influence and crashing his vehicle into a graveyard in Pensacola, Florida, on February 16, 2026. According to police, Vallandingham drove through the fence at the graveyard located near Pace Boulevard and Jackson Street, causing damage to several headstones. Officers responded to the scene and determined that he was allegedly impaired. He also refused to submit to DUI testing when requested by law enforcement. Following the investigation, Vallandingham was arrested, booked into the Escambia County Jail, and later released. The incident resulted in property damage but no reported injuries or fatalities.
Charges: DUI Causing Damage to Property or Person of Another Refusal to Submit DUI Testing
