Title: Suspect in custody following high-speed chase
description: A suspect was taken into custody after a high-speed police chase that began in Lima, Ohio. Lima Police officers attempted to conduct a traffic stop near the intersection of Kibby and Pine streets on May 27, 2026, but the driver allegedly fled. Police later ended the pursuit due to safety concerns after the suspect began operating the vehicle dangerously. The chase continued through areas including Bath Township, where witnesses reported multiple police cruisers pursuing a white car. The suspect was wanted on several active warrants from Hardin County and was later arrested by the Hardin County Sheriff’s Office.
Charges: Active warrants from Hardin County (specific charges not released)

Title: Man in custody following pursuit and field standoff in Hardin County
description: Daniel Murphy was taken into custody after allegedly fleeing from Hardin County deputies during a traffic stop attempt. Deputies said Murphy was traveling at a high rate of speed in the 18000 block of County Road 146 when they attempted to stop him. He allegedly drove into a field before stopping and exiting the vehicle. Authorities said Murphy displayed a handgun toward a deputy and later called 911. Dispatchers convinced him to surrender peacefully. After his arrest, deputies reportedly found drug paraphernalia and a suspected controlled substance. The incident remained under investigation, with possible criminal and traffic charges pending.
Charges: Failure to comply,fleeing

Title: Unlit taillight leads to a car and foot chase in Youngstown
description: A traffic stop in Youngstown, Ohio, turned into a high-speed pursuit after an officer attempted to stop a black SUV for an unlit taillight. The driver accelerated, reaching speeds of about 75 mph while ignoring traffic signals and driving into oncoming traffic. The vehicle eventually stopped, and two occupants fled on foot before being captured by officers. Police identified the suspects as Gabriiyel Wright and Ta’Daryl Sly. Officers reported finding a loaded Glock 23 handgun, another stolen handgun, and suspected cocaine inside and near the vehicle. Both suspects were arrested and booked into jail.
Charges: Resisting arrest Improper handling of a firearm in a motor vehicle Fleeing and eluding (Gabriiyel Wright)

Title: Man arrested after threats to ‘shoot up’ local business
description: Jameson Clark, a 21-year-old man, was arrested after allegedly threatening to “shoot up” a local business in Perry Township, Ohio. Police responded to Octapharma Plasma after the threats caused the business to enter lockdown. When officers arrived, Clark reportedly fled into the West Manor Allotment area, leading to a search involving police officers and a K-9 unit. Authorities later tracked him to a residence on Homewood Avenue in Canton, where he was located and taken into custody. Police said the coordinated response ended the incident safely. Clark faces multiple charges related to threats, resisting police, and fleeing.
Charges: Panic Aggravated menacing Obstructing official business Making terroristic threats Resisting arrest Failure to comply with the order or signal of a police officer

Title: Man accused of reaching 110 mph during pursuit, Findlay police say
description: Da’Shawn Pitts, a 32-year-old man from Lima, was arrested after allegedly leading law enforcement on a high-speed pursuit in Hancock and Allen counties. Officers attempted to stop Pitts for a lane violation in Findlay, but police said he fled onto I-75 South and reached speeds above 110 mph. The pursuit continued for more than 30 miles and lasted approximately 18 minutes before Pitts crashed near North Sugar Street in Lima. Police said he fled on foot and was later located hiding in brush using a drone. After being taken into custody, he was treated at a hospital before jail booking.
Charges: Failure to comply Tampering with evidence

Title: Man leads officers on chase, hitting another car before his capture: Massillon Police
description: Massillon Police detectives attempted to serve a felony arrest warrant on Nelson White at his home on Elmford Avenue. When officers tried to arrest him, White allegedly fled in an SUV, driving through neighborhood yards toward Tuscarawas Street. Officers briefly pursued the vehicle before losing sight of it. Police later discovered a hit-and-run crash at Jackson Avenue and 12th Street NW, with witnesses describing a vehicle matching the SUV. The abandoned SUV was found in Jackson Township, and officers used a K-9 unit and drone team to search the area. White was located and arrested later that afternoon.
Charges: Outstanding felony warrant for menacing by stalking and assault; additional charges pending

Title: 18-year-old learns punishment for role in stolen car chase
description: Javien Jermone Robinson was involved in a stolen vehicle chase in Dayton, Ohio, during which shots were fired at a police officer. The officer was not injured. The pursuit involved multiple police cruisers and ended with authorities locating the stolen vehicle at a residence. Police later found Robinson at another home and arrested him. Investigators reported recovering seven firearms and vehicle key generation devices from the residence. Robinson admitted knowledge of the firearms and devices, which investigators said were connected to stolen vehicle activity. He later pleaded guilty and was sentenced to prison.
Charges: Attempted grand theft, grand theft, having weapons while under disability

Title: Man arrested after assaulting, shooting at teen in west Toledo
description: On April 4, 2026, Thomas Cavanaugh, a 28-year-old Toledo man, was arrested after police said he fled from officers during a vehicle stop in west Toledo and later assaulted a teenage girl. Officers responded to a reported weapon threat and located a vehicle matching the suspect description. Police said Cavanaugh fled when they attempted to stop him, drove onto a curb near his apartment, and ran inside. Authorities allege he punched and kicked a 17-year-old girl and fired a gun at her. The victim was hospitalized and later released. Police recovered the firearm and arrested Cavanaugh.
Charges: Two counts of felonious assault with a weapon, having a weapon while under disability, failure to comply with an order or signal of a police officer to elude or flee

Title: One arrested after early-morning police pursuit ends with crash in Miamisburg
description: On June 30, 2026, a police pursuit involving suspected vehicle theft and break-ins ended in a crash in Miamisburg, Ohio. Officers from Clearcreek Township Police Department and Springboro Police Department pursued two vehicles traveling westbound on State Route 73. Police later focused on a stolen Ford F-150 near Franklin and Interstate 75. The truck crashed into a concrete median on Miamisburg-Centerville Road. Two suspects fled on foot into nearby woods. A Franklin Police K-9 located one suspect, identified as a juvenile passenger, who was arrested. The driver remained missing at the time of the report.
Charges: Receiving stolen property, obstructing official business

Title: Ohio man wanted in several counties arrested after trailer park standoff
description: On April 24, 2026, Bobby L. Mowery, a 51-year-old man, was arrested after a standoff at a trailer park in Celina, Ohio. Authorities said Mowery had been evading police in Mercer and Darke Counties and was wanted on multiple charges. The Mercer County Sheriff’s Office and Grand Lake Task Force located him at Kozy Kampgrounds, and the Auglaize County Sheriff’s Office Special Response Team assisted due to his reported history of violence toward police. Officers ordered him to leave the trailer, but he refused. Police used tear gas and an armored vehicle to enter before locating and arresting him.
Charges: Escape, failure to comply, felonious assault, weapons under disability, resisting arrest

Title: Man arrested after brief chase in Duluth’s Lincoln Park neighborhood
description: A 43-year-old man was arrested after allegedly leading a police officer on a brief vehicle chase in Duluth’s Lincoln Park neighborhood. The incident began when police say the vehicle passed a squad car in a no-passing zone while traveling at a high rate of speed on First Street near Piedmont Avenue. The officer pursued the vehicle for a short distance but ended the chase due to safety concerns. About 15 minutes later, police located the vehicle parked near Mesaba Avenue. Officers arrested the suspect as he exited an apartment building. The man is facing a pending fleeing in a motor vehicle charge.
Charges: Fleeing in a motor vehicle

Title: Man wanted after leading police on chase, going wrong-way on… A man was taken into custody after leading officers on a chase that included going the wrong way on I-675.
city and state: Huber Heights, Ohio / Mad River Township, Ohio
description: Huber Heights, Ohio / Mad River Township, Ohio
Charges: Failure to comply,fleeing

Title: Man arrested after driving through restaurant’s patio while running from police in Celina
description: On March 14, 2026, Trenton Wilson, a 25-year-old man, was arrested after allegedly fleeing from police in Celina, Ohio. A Celina Police sergeant attempted to stop Wilson’s gray Nissan Altima after it failed to stop at a red light. Police said Wilson continued driving through streets and alleys before crashing through the patio area near Brew Nation, damaging patio furniture and a bicycle rack. He later arrived at his home, where officers took him into custody. Authorities reported his blood alcohol concentration was 0.228, nearly three times the legal limit. He was booked into Mercer County Jail.
Charges: Criminal endangering, operating a vehicle under the influence, leaving the scene of an accident on private property, failure to comply with lawful order or signal of a police officer

Title: Juvenile arrested after Englewood car break-ins, police chase
description: A 17-year-old male juvenile was arrested after a series of vehicle break-ins led to a police pursuit in Englewood, Ohio. Police responded to suspicious activity in the Westbrook Meadows subdivision where masked individuals were reportedly checking unlocked vehicles. Several vehicles were entered, and one vehicle with keys inside was stolen. Officers located the stolen vehicle and used tire deflation devices, damaging two tires. The suspect continued driving through Trotwood and Harrison Township before abandoning the vehicle and fleeing on foot. Police took him into custody after a brief pursuit lasting approximately ten minutes.
Charges: Grand theft of a motor vehicle Failure to comply with the order/signal of a police officer

Title: Man facing felony charge after reported police chase through Boardman
description: Malkolm North Jr., 20, was arrested after allegedly leading Boardman police on a vehicle pursuit early Saturday morning. An officer observed North driving a 2019 Land Rover Range Rover and identified him as a driver with a suspended license. When the officer attempted a traffic stop, North allegedly fled, ignored red lights, and reached high speeds during the chase. The officer later located North’s vehicle near his residence and used stop sticks before taking him into custody. North reportedly admitted he was scared of police and did not have a valid license. He was transported to the Mahoning County Jail.
Charges: Failure to comply with an order or signal (4th-degree felony) Driving under suspension

Title: 2 juveniles taken into custody after fleeing from traffic stop in stolen vehicle
description: Two juveniles were taken into custody after fleeing from a traffic stop involving a suspected stolen vehicle. Beavercreek Police officers observed a suspicious and reckless sedan traveling westbound on Dayton-Xenia Road near Grange Hall Road around 3:00 a.m. Officers attempted a traffic stop when the vehicle entered a parking area but the driver fled. The vehicle traveled through the lot, struck a tree, and stopped in the 5000 block of Linden Avenue. Both juvenile occupants ran away on foot but were later apprehended without further incident. Police reported no injuries and the investigation remained ongoing.
Charges: Receiving Stolen Property Failure to Comply Obstructing Official Business

Title: Wanted man arrested after chase through Clark, Champaign counties
description: Jamie Lee Back, 46, was arrested after allegedly fleeing from Clark County Sheriff’s Office deputies who were attempting to serve felony warrants. Deputies reported that Back entered a Jeep Patriot and drove away with a female passenger. A pursuit continued through western Clark County into Champaign County with assistance from the Ohio State Highway Patrol aviation units. Officers deployed tire deflation devices, damaging two tires. Back released the passenger and attempted to continue driving off-road before crashing at low speed. He abandoned the vehicle and hid in a wooded area but was located by aviation support and taken into custody.
Charges: Felony warrants Additional charges related to the police chase Other offenses under investigation

Title: 18-year-old charged, accused of shooting at CPD officers outside police substation
description: An 18-year-old man, Samatar Salad, was arrested after police accused him of firing multiple shots at Columbus police officers outside a police substation. The incident occurred near the 5th Precinct substation on Cleveland Avenue, where three officers were standing near their vehicles. Officers attempted a traffic stop on the suspect vehicle, but the driver fled and later crashed into a snow bank. Police said Salad attempted to run away and ignored commands before being taken into custody. A loaded semi-automatic firearm with an extended magazine was recovered from the vehicle. No officers were reported injured.
Charges: Three counts of felonious assault; failure to comply with order of a police officer

Title: Man accused of driving 83 mph on I-480 arrested after gun recovered: North Olmsted Police Blotter
description: Police recovered a loaded handgun from an SUV after officers observed the vehicle traveling eastbound on I-480 at 83 mph in a posted 60 mph zone. The incident occurred in North Olmsted, Ohio. Officers stopped the vehicle and discovered the firearm during the investigation. The available report does not provide the driver’s identity, details about possible charges, or information about whether the weapon was legally possessed. The case was documented in the North Olmsted Police Blotter. Authorities focused on the speeding violation and the recovery of the loaded handgun from the vehicle during the traffic enforcement encounter.
Charges: gun related charges ,offenses under investigation

Title: Police recover firearm reported stolen during traffic stop
description: An 18-year-old driver was arrested after Boardman police recovered a stolen firearm during a traffic stop near Midlothian Boulevard and Glenwood Avenue. Officers stopped the vehicle after it failed to fully stop at a stop sign. During the investigation, police searched the vehicle after observing an open container of alcohol. A handgun with an extended magazine was found under the driver’s seat and was identified as a firearm reported stolen in July 2025. The driver told police he forgot the gun was in the vehicle and claimed he had purchased it for protection. The firearm was taken as evidence.
Charges: Receiving stolen property Improper handling of a firearm in a motor vehicle Open container Minor misdemeanor traffic charges

Title: Toledo Police officer awaits sentencing after driving under the influence with child in vehicle
description: Toledo Police officer Michael Ellerbrock was involved in a March 23, 2026, vehicle crash in Monroe County, Ohio, where deputies found his truck in a ditch near Lakeside Road. He showed signs of intoxication, including bloodshot eyes, slurred speech, and difficulty providing insurance information. A child was inside the vehicle during the incident. Ellerbrock refused field sobriety tests and later pleaded guilty to misdemeanor operating a vehicle while visibly intoxicated. Breath tests showed alcohol levels of .196 and .20. He remains on restricted duty pending further police review and an internal investigation by the Toledo Police Department following the case.
Charges: Operating a vehicle while visibly intoxicated (misdemeanor) Child endangering charge connected to the incident

Title: YPD deploys spike strips twice to stop fleeing vehicle Saturday
description: David Hardaway, 35, was arrested after allegedly fleeing from Youngstown police during a traffic pursuit. An officer spotted Hardaway driving at a high speed and running a stop sign near Rush Boulevard and East Lucius Avenue. Police attempted a traffic stop, but the vehicle failed to stop. Officers deployed spike strips twice during the pursuit, eventually puncturing two tires. Hardaway continued driving until reaching a dead end on Hillman Street, where he exited the vehicle with his hands raised and surrendered. Police reported he smelled of alcohol and found an open bottle of vodka inside the car.
Charges: Failure to comply with the order or signal of a police officer (third-degree felony) Several traffic offenses

Title: Semi driver flees scene after crash in Putnam County, later arrested
description: Predrag Rasuo, 47, of Greensboro, North Carolina, was involved in a crash in Ottawa Township, Ohio, while driving a semi-truck. Authorities said Rasuo failed to stop at a stop sign at the intersection of Road 7 and State Route 65, causing his Freightliner to strike an SUV driven by Brooke-Lynn Barrientes. Barrientes and two minor passengers were injured and taken for medical treatment. After the crash, Rasuo allegedly fled the scene in the semi-truck. He was later located and stopped by Pandora Police and Putnam County deputies and taken into custody. Impairment is suspected as a contributing factor.
Charges: Fleeing in a vehicle,Failure to comply with the order or signal of a police officer

Title: I-270 wrong-way crash driver had high blood alcohol level, report says
description: Jacob Fischer, 28, was involved in a fatal wrong-way crash on Interstate 270 near Dempsey Road in Columbus, Ohio, on April 23, 2026. Toxicology results showed Fischer had a blood alcohol concentration of 0.183, more than twice Ohio’s legal limit, and THC was detected in his system. The crash involved a head-on collision between Fischer’s Audi A3 and another vehicle driven by Aobyda Nadeem. Both drivers suffered fatal injuries. Investigators continued examining which vehicle was traveling in the wrong direction, using vehicle data and available traffic footage to determine the circumstances surrounding the collision.
Charges: DUI ,Failure to comply

Title: Euclid Police cite teen driving 120+ MPH on I-90
description: A 19-year-old male driver was cited by Euclid Police after being clocked traveling 121 MPH on Interstate 90 in Euclid, Ohio. The traffic enforcement operation was conducted with assistance from the Ohio State Highway Patrol Aviation Section. Officers also observed another driver traveling at 101 MPH and made additional high-speed stops. The teen driver was reportedly not wearing a seatbelt at the time of the stop. Police emphasized the dangers of excessive speed and reminded drivers that high speeds reduce reaction time and increase the risk of serious crashes.
Charges: Traffic citations for speeding and failure to wear a seatbelt

Title: UPDATE: Hardin County man charged after leading officers on multicounty chase
description: Daniel Boutwell, 40, was arrested after allegedly fleeing from a Lima police traffic stop and leading officers on a multi-county chase through Allen and Hardin counties in Ohio. Police said Boutwell failed to stop and drove away, creating safety concerns that caused officers to end the pursuit. His vehicle was later found abandoned in rural Hardin County and secured as evidence by Lima police. Hardin County deputies arrested Boutwell later the same day on a bench warrant related to a previous domestic violence case. Lima police later charged him with failure to comply with an order or signal from an officer.
Charges: Failure to comply with an order or signal of a police officer Failure to appear warrant related to domestic violence charge

Title: Juvenile accused of dragging Youngstown officer during traffic stop
description: A juvenile suspect in Youngstown, Ohio, was accused of dragging a police officer during a traffic stop after officers pulled over a vehicle for traffic violations including failure to signal and no visible registration. Police reported the car smelled of burnt marijuana and contained smoked joints. The teen allegedly drove away while an officer was holding onto him and the vehicle later stopped. Officers detained the suspect and found suspected vape products, pills, and cash inside the vehicle. The juvenile faces assault and obstruction charges and a marijuana possession citation. The case will proceed in juvenile court after further proceedings.
Charges: Felonious assault, obstructing official business, and underage possession of marijuana citation

Title: North Olmsted police report OVI suspect denies swerving, refuses breath test
description: A female driver was stopped by North Olmsted police after an officer observed her Toyota Corolla traveling in a zigzag pattern on Lorain Road while jerking the steering wheel and overcorrecting. Two patrol cars stopped the vehicle as it turned onto Stearns Road. Officers noticed damage to the passenger side and difficulty opening the passenger window. The driver denied swerving or crossing lane markers, but officers reported signs of impairment, including slurred speech, red glossy eyes, and the smell of alcohol. The woman was suspected of operating a vehicle under the influence and refused to provide a breath sample.
Charges: OVI (Operating Vehicle Impaired) Refusal to submit to breath test

Title: Westerville police fight teen gatherings with increased patrols
description: Westerville Police increased patrols along Polaris Parkway in response to large gatherings of teenagers and concerns related to unsafe driving. During the first weekend of the increased enforcement effort in April 2026, officers conducted 75 traffic stops, issued 19 citations, and made two arrests. One arrest involved a driver who fled during a traffic stop and was charged with failure to comply. Police said the initiative aims to prevent disturbances and promote safety before summer months. The department also encouraged parents to help prevent unsafe gatherings and ensure teens have safe places to spend time.
Charges: Failure to comply

Title: OVERNIGHT – Traffic Stop Escalates to High-Stakes Pursuit and Arrest in Pickaway County
description: Tracy Brill, 65, was arrested after a traffic stop escalated into a high-speed pursuit in Pickaway County. Authorities said a deputy conducting a traffic stop on State Route 207 observed Brill’s vehicle allegedly veer dangerously close to the deputy, the patrol cruiser, and another stopped vehicle. The deputy initiated a pursuit after Brill allegedly refused to stop. The chase continued along Locust Grove Road and Dublin Hill Road. After stopping, Brill allegedly became combative and resisted arrest. A search of the vehicle reportedly found a loaded firearm, illegal drugs, and drug paraphernalia.
Charges: Two counts of failure to comply with the order or signal of a police officer

Title: 2 deputies hurt in Cleveland crash involving Cuyahoga County Sheriff's vehicle, pickup truck
description: On March 25, 2026, police attempted to stop a stolen Ford Ranger near Biddulph Road and Ridge Road in Brooklyn, Ohio. The driver, identified as Selena Miller, allegedly failed to comply, leading officers on a pursuit. The chase ended in Cleveland near Fulton Road and Poe Avenue when the suspect vehicle struck a marked Cuyahoga County Sheriff’s Office cruiser. Two deputies were treated for non-life-threatening injuries following the crash. Miller was identified as the suspect, and additional charges were expected to be determined by the prosecutor’s office.
Charges: Vehicular assualt on officers, Failure to comply with an order or signal

Title: Woman climbs fence, escapes Crosswaeh facility in Tiffin
description: Megan Feagins was arrested after allegedly striking a Dayton Police cruiser and leading officers on a vehicle pursuit. On March 8, 2026, around 9:45 p.m., Dayton police attempted to stop a Mercedes with no visible license plate. During the stop, officers instructed the driver to place the vehicle in park, but the Mercedes allegedly remained in reverse and struck the cruiser before fleeing through the grass. Officers pursued the vehicle and used stop sticks before ending the chase after approximately 15 minutes with a PIT maneuver. Police believe the vehicle was also involved in an earlier traffic stop evasion on March 6, 2026.
Charges: Fleeing and eluding Failure to comply with traffic stop Hit/striking police cruiser (reported)

Title: Hughes police officer arrested for DUI crash
description: Corbin Dixon, a Hughes Police Department officer, was arrested after allegedly causing a DUI-related crash on December 26, 2025, at approximately 4:00 a.m. on Highway 49 in Helena-West Helena, Arkansas. The collision involved a Hughes Police Department patrol vehicle and a Ford F-150 that overturned. Helena-West Helena Police Department responded to the scene and found the driver of the pickup truck injured and transported to a hospital. Investigators suspected Dixon was intoxicated, and a portable breath test indicated a blood alcohol concentration of 0.12%. He was arrested for driving while intoxicated. Authorities also reviewed his employment status.
Charges: Driving While Intoxicated (DWI)

Title: Woman arrested after allegedly hitting a police cruiser and fleeing a traffic stop
description: A 36-year-old woman was arrested after allegedly striking a Dayton Police Department cruiser and fleeing during a traffic stop on March 8, 2026, at approximately 9:45 p.m. Officers attempted to stop a white Mercedes that displayed no visible license plate after it pulled into a driveway. Instead of complying, the driver allegedly reversed into the police cruiser and fled. Officers pursued the vehicle and ended the chase in less than 15 minutes using stop sticks and a Precision Immobilization Technique (PIT). The woman was arrested and booked into the Montgomery County Jail. The vehicle was also believed to have been involved in an earlier evaded traffic stop.
Charges: Hit and run (alleged) Fleeing/eluding a traffic stop

Title: Woman accused of fleeing after driving 86 mph in 55-mph zone
description: Genia Jackson, 23, of Jonesboro, Arkansas, was arrested after allegedly fleeing from Paragould police during a traffic enforcement incident. An officer reportedly observed her vehicle traveling 86 miles per hour in a 55-mph zone on the U.S. 412 Bypass Spur. After the officer activated emergency lights and siren, Jackson allegedly continued driving at a high speed, made several turns, and drove behind a residence at the end of a private gravel road. A homeowner directed officers to the location, where they found Jackson attempting to re-enter the driveway. She was arrested and held at the Greene County Detention Center.
Charges: Felony fleeing (Class D felony)

Title: Driver cited after crashing into Fairborn home while fleeing from police
description: A 26-year-old driver was cited after allegedly fleeing from police and crashing into a home in Fairborn, Ohio. The incident occurred early Friday morning, March 20, 2026, when Fairborn Police responded to a crash in the 400 block of West Xenia Drive. According to the crash report, the driver was fleeing from police while traveling on West Xenia Drive. While attempting to negotiate a curve near North Second Street, the vehicle failed to properly turn, left the roadway, struck a fence, and then crashed into a residence. The driver was cited for failure to maintain reasonable control. Further details about the reason for the pursuit were not released.
Charges: Reasonable Control citation

Title: Suspect in Coitsville officer-involved shooting indicted
description: John Doyle, 75, was indicted after an officer-involved shooting during a search warrant operation in Coitsville Township. Authorities said Doyle was wanted by the Poland Township Police Department for allegedly fleeing a traffic stop in December 2025. He was located at a mobile home on Galluppi Drive in February 2026. According to U.S. Marshals, when officers approached him, Doyle allegedly displayed a firearm and pointed it at them, causing officers to fire back. Doyle was injured, taken to a hospital, and later booked into the Mahoning County Jail. No officers were injured during the incident.
Charges: Felonious assault with firearm specification Failure to comply with the signal or order of a police officer

Title: Man gets mom in trouble after talking too much during traffic stop: Highland Heights Police Blotter
description: A 32-year-old University Heights man was stopped for speeding on Wilson Mills Road on January 23, 2026. During the traffic stop, he admitted that his driver’s license was suspended and revealed that his mother knew about the suspension but allowed him to drive her vehicle. His mother arrived at the scene to retrieve the vehicle and was cited for unlawful entrustment. The man was cited for driving under suspension and speeding. He was released after Cleveland Heights police were unable to take custody of him on an active traffic warrant. No injuries or crashes were reported.
Charges: Driving under suspension Speeding

Title: Sleeping snow mover accused of getting plowed in driveway: Pepper Pike Police Blotter
description: A 46-year-old Chardon man was arrested after police responded to a report of a snowplow driver asleep at the wheel in a driveway on Pinetree Road. Officers observed signs of possible impairment and found an open container of alcohol inside his truck. The driver was also found to have a suspended license and refused a breath test. Due to a prior impaired driving conviction, the refusal resulted in an elevated charge. Police took him to the Beachwood Jail, where he later posted bond. A prescribed bottle of amphetamines was found but did not result in charges.
Charges: Impaired driving (OVI) Open container Driving under suspension Refusal to submit to breath test

Title: UPDATE: Suspect allegedly shot; Suspect allegedly fired shots at law enforcement during high-speed chase in Ohio Valley, fled into woods on foot
description: Michael Decker was involved in a high-speed chase in Harrison County, Ohio, after authorities said he allegedly fired shots at law enforcement during the pursuit. The incident began on U.S. Route 250, where a deputy reported being fired upon and later received medical treatment for a shoulder injury unrelated to gunfire. Decker fled in a vehicle before spike strips were deployed, causing him to abandon the vehicle and run into a wooded area near Hopedale. Law enforcement searched the area and later confirmed Decker was shot during the standoff. The Ohio Bureau of Criminal Investigation took over the case.
Charges: Fleeing in a vehicle

Title: “I’m basically the Mayor”: Dapice arrested for OVI
description: Rachelle Dapice, a 34-year-old Bellefontaine woman, was arrested after police said she was driving erratically through downtown Bellefontaine while under the influence of alcohol. Officers observed a white Acura SUV making repeated driving errors around 2 a.m. and initiated a traffic stop on Eastern Avenue. Police reported signs of impairment, including difficulty locating belongings, loss of train of thought, staggering, and admission of alcohol consumption. Officers attempted field sobriety testing, but Dapice was reportedly unable to complete the tests. She was arrested for operating a vehicle while impaired after refusing a breath test and was later released to a sober driver.
Charges: Operating a vehicle while impaired (OVI), breath test refusal resulting in administrative license suspension

Title: Woman charged with drunk driving, assault and harassment after crash: North Ridgeville police blotter
description: A woman was arrested after police responded to a traffic complaint on Bagley Road in North Ridgeville, Ohio, on February 22, 2026. Officers determined she was operating a vehicle while intoxicated. Police charged her with drunk driving, possessing an open container of alcohol, failure to control her vehicle, driving an unsafe vehicle, and failure to stop after an accident. The police blotter did not identify the woman by name or provide additional details about the incident, injuries, or property damage. The case was handled by the North Ridgeville Police Department as part of routine impaired driving enforcement.
Charges: Operating a vehicle while intoxicated (OVI), open container, failure to control, driving an unsafe vehicle, failure to stop after an accident

Title: Driver arrested after taking off from traffic stop, crashing into another car
description: Keyshawn Brown was stopped by Xenia police for driving a black Dodge Charger with expired tags. After initially stopping at a red light, he fled from officers, leading them through city streets. Brown allegedly drove through a four-way stop and crashed into a white Dodge Durango before striking two parked vehicles. The collision also damaged a utility pole and a fire hydrant. The driver and passenger of the Durango were hospitalized with non-life-threatening injuries. Brown was arrested at the crash scene. Police also discovered he had two active warrants from other counties, although they were outside the pickup radius.
Charges: Failure to comply with the order or signal of a police officer Several misdemeanor traffic offenses

Title: Video: Ohio cruiser caught on fleeing suspect’s trailer during pursuit
description: A suspect with outstanding felony warrants fled after Norwood Police Department officers attempted a traffic stop on February 28, 2026. The suspect was driving an SUV while towing a flatbed trailer, leading officers on a 90-minute pursuit that crossed into Indiana before returning to Ohio. During the chase, a Cincinnati police cruiser became lodged on the suspect's trailer. An officer later performed a PIT maneuver, causing the SUV to crash into a tree. The cruiser fell from the trailer and rolled over, while the suspect's vehicle caught fire. Both the suspect and the involved officer were transported to a hospital with injuries.
Charges: Outstanding felony warrants

Title: Hialeah mayor has a vehicle with emergency lights. A Miami cop gave him a ticket
description: Hialeah Mayor Bryan Calvo was stopped by a Miami Police Department motorcycle officer while driving a city-owned SUV equipped with emergency lights. According to the report, the officer initially stopped him for making an illegal left turn. During the traffic stop, the officer observed that the vehicle displayed blue emergency lights, which are generally restricted to authorized emergency vehicles under Florida law. Calvo received two civil traffic citations but was not arrested. He stated that the emergency lighting had been installed before he took office and before the vehicle was assigned to him. He may contest the citations.
Charges: Civil citation for failing to obey an official traffic-control device Civil citation for unlawful use of blue emergency lights on a vehicle

Title: 4 accused in armed robbery of teen arrested after pursuit in Martin County, deputies say
description: Four suspects were arrested after allegedly committing an armed robbery against a 14-year-old in Martin County. Authorities said the teen believed he was meeting the suspects to buy high-end clothing. When he arrived, the suspects allegedly forced him into their vehicle at gunpoint, stole his money and designer watch, and pushed him out of the vehicle. Deputies located the vehicle, but the driver refused to stop, leading to a pursuit. Stop sticks were deployed, stopping the vehicle. The suspects fled on foot into neighborhoods and a wooded area before being captured by deputies. All four were arrested.
Charges: Armed robbery Fleeing and eluding law enforcement (Kaleb Seidel only)

Title: Police chase in Fort Myers follows car theft outside dollar store
description: Police arrested 18-year-old John Gray after a reported vehicle theft outside a Family Dollar store in Fort Myers. Authorities said the victim left the car running and unlocked while entering the store, and Gray allegedly entered the vehicle with another person and drove away. Officers later located the stolen vehicle and attempted a traffic stop near Central Avenue and Crawford Street, leading to a short pursuit. During the chase, an unidentified woman reportedly exited the vehicle. Police said Gray struck a mailbox, sideswiped a tree, and ran toward Central Avenue before being chased into a parking lot and arrested.
Charges: Grand theft Fleeing police Resisting an officer

Title: Martin County teens arrested after 14-year-old boy robbed at gunpoint
description: Four suspects were arrested after a 14-year-old boy was allegedly robbed at gunpoint during a meeting arranged through Snapchat for a clothing exchange in Palm City. Deputies said the victim was taken into a vehicle, threatened with a gun, and had cash and a watch taken before being forced out. A matching white Kia was later spotted, leading to a police pursuit. The vehicle was stopped with spike strips, and all four occupants fled on foot. Martin County Sheriff’s Office deputies, K-9 units, and aviation resources located and arrested all suspects after a coordinated search.
Charges: Armed robbery Fleeing and eluding (driver) Additional charges pending

Title: 3-week nationwide kidnapping case ends in Collier pursuit, arrest of suspect
description: Floyd Stuck, 41, was accused of kidnapping a victim and holding her against her will for three weeks while traveling across multiple states. Authorities said Stuck threatened the victim, took her phone, choked her, tied her up, and used personal information about her family to intimidate her. The victim escaped in San Diego, California, and later returned to Florida. Investigators said Stuck attempted to place an AirTag on the victim’s vehicle before fleeing. After a pursuit in Collier County, he crashed a rented U-Haul, ran on foot, and was captured by deputies with assistance from a K-9.
Charges: Kidnapping, aggravated stalking, unlawful installation of a tracking device, fleeing and eluding, and other related charges

Title: High-speed chase ends with arrest in Jackson County
description: Darrell Edward Terrio, 41, was arrested after a high-speed vehicle pursuit that began in Washington County and continued into Jackson County, Florida. Deputies attempted a traffic stop near Caryville after a reported traffic violation, but Terrio allegedly accelerated and fled, reaching speeds over 120 miles per hour. During the pursuit, authorities said items were thrown from the vehicle’s sunroof and struck a patrol unit. The Florida Highway Patrol joined and took primary pursuit responsibility. Spike strips were later deployed in Jackson County, causing the vehicle to lose control and stop. Terrio was taken into custody and transported to jail.
Charges: Felony fleeing and eluding at high speed; driving while license suspended or revoked

Title: 6 Florida teens caught on camera running out of stolen car after chase in Pinellas County: FHP
description: Six teenagers were taken into custody after a stolen Honda SUV chase in Pinellas County. Florida Highway Patrol troopers located the vehicle through a stolen vehicle alert and attempted a traffic stop. The 17-year-old driver fled, drove into oncoming traffic, and continued until troopers used a PIT maneuver to stop the SUV. The occupants then ran into an apartment complex on foot. Multiple agencies, including Pinellas County Sheriff’s Office and Clearwater Police, assisted in locating them. The driver and passengers were detained. One passenger faced an additional drug charge after marijuana was reportedly found.
Charges: 17-year-old driver: fleeing and eluding, resisting an officer without violence, possession of stolen property Alan K. Garrett: resisting an officer without violence, Four other passengers: resisting an officer without violence

Title: Crash and fight in Sanford lead to arrests after chase in Orlando
description: Two suspects were arrested after a crash, physical altercation, and vehicle pursuit that began in Sanford and ended in downtown Orlando. Sanford Police said a suspect intentionally rear-ended another vehicle and later took items from the victim’s vehicle before fleeing in a red Kia. The vehicle was later found in Orange County, where deputies attempted a traffic stop. During the stop, a passenger moved into the driver’s seat and drove away, striking multiple vehicles before abandoning the car and running on foot. Deputies quickly captured the passenger, and the original driver was also arrested.
Charges: Multiple felony charges related to vehicle theft, fleeing, crash, and other offenses

Title: Driver in custody after fleeing traffic stop, leading pursuit in Miami-Dade, FHP says
description: Bryan Garcia was arrested after allegedly fleeing from a Florida Highway Patrol traffic stop in Miami-Dade County. Troopers said they stopped a silver SUV on the Palmetto Expressway near Northwest 36th Street, but the driver fled, leading authorities on a short pursuit. FHP attempted a PIT maneuver near Southwest 1st Street and 44th Avenue, but the vehicle escaped. After losing sight of the SUV, Miami Police officers located Garcia fleeing on foot and took him into custody. The SUV was later found at a nearby residential complex. Garcia was charged following the incident.
Charges: Fleeing police Driving with suspended license

Title: Driver arrested after 120 mph pursuit ends near Belen Jesuit, FHP says
description: Reshawd James Pond Jr., 24, was arrested after Florida Highway Patrol troopers said he led them on a high-speed pursuit in West Miami-Dade, Florida. Authorities responded after a woman reported that her ex-boyfriend was chasing her, threatening to kill her, and possibly armed. Troopers located a Cadillac Escalade matching the description, but the driver fled. The vehicle reached speeds over 120 mph before crashing after a tire blowout. Pond fled on foot and was later found hiding in a maintenance shed near Belen Jesuit Preparatory School. An AR-15 rifle was recovered from the vehicle.
Charges: Fleeing and eluding law enforcement at high speed; resisting an officer without violence

Title: Florida man arrested after leading authorities on chase, crashing SUV into pond: FHP
description: Nycolye Carrion, 26, was arrested after Florida Highway Patrol troopers said he led authorities on a vehicle chase through St. Petersburg neighborhoods before crashing a Kia SUV into a pond. Troopers reported that Carrion was speeding, failed to stop for a traffic attempt, and reached high speeds through residential streets. The SUV reportedly struck curbs, drove through yards, and nearly hit three people before entering the pond. Carrion exited the vehicle, swam away, and later fled on foot before being found and taken into custody. He was treated for injuries and transported to jail.
Charges: Aggravated fleeing and eluding; reckless driving; reckless driving causing property damage; driving with suspended or revoked license; leaving the scene of a crash; resisting an officer without violence; no insurance; expired vehicle registration

Title: BWC: Fla. officer saves trapped driver as pursuit of carjacking, kidnapping suspect ends in fiery crash
description: A man was arrested in Jacksonville, Florida, after allegedly carjacking a woman’s vehicle while her 1-year-old daughter was still inside. According to the Jacksonville Sheriff’s Office, the suspect forcibly removed the woman from her car and drove away with the child inside. Officers located the stolen vehicle and began a pursuit. During the chase, the suspect crashed into another vehicle. Police arrested the suspect at the scene, and the child was found unharmed in her car seat. The suspect faces multiple charges related to the carjacking and child abduction incident.
Charges: Carjacking; false imprisonment of a child

Title: Suspect arrested five days after rush-hour car chase through Tallahassee
description: Zachary Read, 36, was arrested in Leon County after allegedly leading law enforcement on multiple high-speed pursuits in Tallahassee. Authorities said Read was identified as the driver involved in an earlier chase where he allegedly struck several vehicles while attempting to evade officers. During a later pursuit, Read allegedly drove a gold Toyota van at speeds over 90 mph, traveled into oncoming traffic, and intentionally collided with a U.S. Marshals vehicle. He eventually lost control and crashed into a tree before being taken into custody. in the vehicle.
Charges: Felony fleeing and eluding; driving with suspended license; leaving the scene of a crash; aggravated fleeing and eluding; battery on a law enforcement officer; fleeing and eluding after crash with damage; resisting an officer without violence

Title: Video shows 4-month-old being thrown from SUV during high-speed chase; driver arrested
description: A 28-year-old man, Tyrice Fletcher, allegedly fled from Arkansas State Police during a traffic stop in Camden. The pursuit began after a trooper attempted to stop a Toyota Highlander for a traffic violation. Fletcher reportedly drove over 100 mph, entered oncoming traffic, and lost control of the vehicle, causing it to crash and overturn. Four children, including a 4-month-old baby, were inside the SUV and were not properly restrained. The baby was ejected during the crash but was rescued by a trooper. The children suffered minor injuries and were taken for medical treatment.
Charges: Felony fleeing, possession of a defaced firearm, reckless driving, no driver’s license, four counts of endangering the welfare of a minor

Title: Carvana tow truck involved in police chase, ends with damaged patrol cars in Bay County
description: Jason Michael Slater was arrested after a high-speed police chase involving a Carvana tow truck in Bay County, Florida. Authorities said the pursuit occurred on Highway 231 and resulted in multiple law enforcement vehicles being damaged. Florida Highway Patrol and the Bay County Sheriff’s Office responded to the incident. The suspect was taken into custody after the chase and was charged with several offenses. The vehicle involved was identified as a Carvana tow truck. Officials reported that Slater allegedly committed theft of the vehicle and caused damage during the pursuit, including an incident involving law enforcement officers.
Charges: Grand theft of an automobile Aggravated battery on a law enforcement officer Fleeing in an attempt to elude law enforcement Criminal mischief

Title: FHP: Bradenton man leads troopers on chase across 3 counties, crashes into fence near MacDill AFB
description: Randall Woodson, 31, was arrested after a high-speed pursuit that began in Bradenton and continued across three Florida counties. Authorities said the chase started after Woodson allegedly committed an aggravated assault by intentionally striking another vehicle and sending threatening messages. Deputies attempted to locate him, but he fled and caused another crash. Florida Highway Patrol joined the pursuit as Woodson drove over 100 mph, ran red lights, and eventually crashed into a sign, gate, and fence near MacDill Air Force Base in Tampa. He fled on foot but was captured by a K9 unit. A firearm was found in his vehicle.
Charges: Leaving the scene of a crash with property damage Reckless driving with property damage or personal injury Fleeing to elude Possession of a controlled substance Felon in possession of a firearm

Title: Woman arrested after armed robbery leads to pursuit, two other suspects still at large, court records show
description: Senilah Bolds, 18, was arrested after an armed robbery and carjacking led to a police pursuit in Tallahassee, Florida. Authorities said Bolds and two other suspects allegedly stole a vehicle from a DoorDash driver at gunpoint on Apalachee Parkway. Police later located the stolen Toyota and attempted to stop it, but two male suspects fled on foot. Bolds remained inside the vehicle and surrendered to officers. The victim later identified her as one of the attackers. Bolds was taken to the Leon County Detention Facility and faces multiple felony charges related to the armed robbery and vehicle theft.
Charges: Armed robbery Armed carjacking Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon Possession of a firearm during the commission of a felony Armed trespassing in a conveyance

Title: Armed vehicle burglary suspect caught after running from Sarasota police
description: Sarasota police responded to a report of an armed suspicious person near South Osprey Avenue around 12:30 a.m. Saturday. The resident reported seeing Jaquez Burrows standing near a vehicle with the driver-side door open and a possible holster visible. Police said Burrows left the area on a scooter wearing dark clothing and a ski mask. Officers located a person matching the description and pursued him on foot. With assistance from the Sarasota County Sheriff’s Office helicopter, Burrows was tracked and arrested. Officers later recovered a firearm nearby and collected evidence for further investigation.
Charges: Burglary of an unoccupied vehicle; loitering and prowling; resisting an officer without violence

Title: Driver Charged With OVI After Nissan Flips and Catches Fire on US-23 in Pickaway County
description: Hallie Jo Fargnolli was involved in a single-vehicle crash on June 29, 2026, in Harrison Township, Ohio. Deputies reported that she was driving a 2017 Nissan Rogue southbound on US-23 when she attempted to change lanes and overcorrected, causing the vehicle to leave the roadway, overturn, and catch fire. Emergency crews transported Fargnolli to Grant Medical Center in Columbus for treatment of suspected serious injuries. Investigators suspected alcohol involvement and issued her an OVI citation. The vehicle was destroyed in the fire, and authorities closed the roadway temporarily while crews handled the crash scene.
Charges: Operating a Vehicle Under the Influence of Alcohol (OVI)

Title: Fleming Island woman charged with DUI after inhaling computer duster on St. Pete Beach, PCSO says
description: Lindsay Turner was arrested in St. Pete Beach, Florida, after deputies responded to a vehicle crash involving property damage. Authorities reported finding Turner slumped over the steering wheel of a car that had struck a building wall. Deputies said she was in possession of a computer duster and admitted inhaling tetrafluoroethane, an intoxicating gas from the product. Investigators stated the can showed signs of recent use. Turner reportedly said she had relapsed after three years of sobriety. She was taken into custody and charged with inhalation of a harmful chemical and DUI involving property damage before being released on bond.
Charges: Inhalation of a harmful chemical; DUI involving property damage

Title: Mom charged with DUI after Chick-fil-A employee calls 911, authorities say
description: A Florida mother was arrested for DUI after a Chick-fil-A employee called 911 reporting that she was slurring her words while in the drive-thru. Nassau County deputies stopped her vehicle and found two young children, ages one and six, in the back seat. Authorities also reported finding an open bottle of tequila in the passenger seat. A breath test showed her blood alcohol concentration was more than twice Florida’s legal limit. The woman was taken into custody and charged with DUI. The incident was recorded on body camera footage, according to the Nassau County Sheriff’s Office.
Charges: DUI

Title: Woman arrested for DUI after hitting parked SUV in Belle Isle
description: A woman was arrested for DUI after crashing into a parked SUV in Belle Isle, Florida. Police responded after witnesses reported hearing a loud crash and found the woman inside a heavily damaged vehicle. The impact reportedly pushed the parked SUV about 40 feet down the roadway. Officers conducted field sobriety tests, which the woman failed, and she provided two breath samples measuring 0.133 and 0.125. She was taken into custody and charged with DUI crash. No injuries were reported in the incident, according to the Belle Isle Police Department.
Charges: DUI crash

Title: Florida mom tests nearly twice legal limit for DUI with daughter, 6, in car, police say
description: Joelle Service was arrested after police said she was driving under the influence with her six-year-old daughter inside the vehicle in Apopka, Florida. On June 30, 2026, officers responded to reports of a child standing on a busy highway shoulder waving for help. Police found Service confused, disoriented, and vomiting in the driver’s seat of a damaged vehicle. Her daughter reportedly told officers that Service had consumed wine in Mount Dora and was driving erratically. Service refused field sobriety tests but later provided breath samples of 0.155 and 0.149. She was charged with DUI and child neglect.
Charges: DUI and child neglect

Title: Gun threat at softball game leads to arrest in Panama City Beach
description: April Wilks was arrested after an alleged firearm threat involving another woman following a softball game at Frank Brown Park in Panama City Beach, Florida. According to court documents, Wilks was leaving the park when she stopped her vehicle, reversed, and displayed a revolver toward the other woman. Witnesses reported that she allegedly pointed the firearm and made a threatening statement. Authorities said several juveniles were in the area during the incident. Wilks reportedly left the location and did not return after officers attempted to contact her. She was later arrested and charged with aggravated assault with a deadly weapon and improper exhibition of a firearm.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon; Improper exhibition of a firearm

Title: UPDATE: Woman arrested for DUI after multi-vehicle crash in Pensacola Walmart parking lot
description: A woman was arrested after deputies said she intentionally rammed her vehicle into multiple cars in a Walmart parking lot on Mobile Highway in Pensacola, Florida. The incident occurred on the afternoon of June 27, 2026, causing multiple injuries and damaging several parked vehicles. Authorities said at least one person was struck by the vehicle. Deputies reported that the woman refused to exit her car, requiring officers to remove her. She was described as visibly highly intoxicated and was taken into custody. The Florida Highway Patrol assumed responsibility for investigating the crash, while the suspect's identity had not yet been publicly released.
Charges: DUI

Title: Driver arrested after striking fire truck, leading chase from Daytona Beach to DeLand, deputies say
description: Jamal Anthony Riascos, 27, was arrested after authorities said he struck a Volusia County fire truck at the scene of a rollover crash in Daytona Beach, Florida, and fled from law enforcement. Investigators said Riascos drove toward DeLand, using the shoulder and grass to avoid traffic and nearly causing additional crashes. During the pursuit, he briefly stopped to let two passengers leave before continuing. The chase ended in a DeLand shopping plaza after he crashed into a culvert and utility pole, abandoned his vehicle, and ran through a Publix parking lot. He was later apprehended following a foot chase.
Charges: Fleeing and eluding causing property damage, Leaving the scene of a crash, Reckless driving, Resisting an officer without violence, Violation of probation

Title: NKY woman charged with 8th OVI over the holiday weekend
description: Amber L. Short, 45, of Northern Kentucky, was arrested on July 3, 2026, after deputies conducted a traffic stop in Springfield, Ohio. Authorities alleged that she was following another vehicle too closely and that her vehicle failed to meet rear license plate illumination requirements. During the stop, deputies determined she was operating a vehicle while impaired by alcohol and/or drugs. Officials noted that this was her eighth OVI charge, with seven previous OVI charges between 2007 and 2019, including three felony convictions. Short was released from custody after her arrest and is scheduled to appear in court at a later date.
Charges: Following too close Illumination of rear license plate requirements violation Operating a vehicle while impaired by alcohol and/or drugs (OVI)

Title: 8 illegal guns seized in Cleveland for crime reduction initiative
description: On June 17, 2026, Ohio’s Violent Crime Reduction Initiative conducted a coordinated enforcement operation in Cleveland, Ohio. Multiple law enforcement agencies arrested 11 felony suspects and recovered eight illegal firearms. Among those arrested were Antoine Williams, who fled after a traffic stop before being apprehended with an illegally possessed handgun; Tremaine Harris, who was arrested following a traffic stop after troopers found a loaded handgun in his vehicle; and an unidentified 17-year-old juvenile found carrying a concealed firearm. The operation used intelligence-led policing and coordinated efforts among local, state, and federal agencies to target violent crime and illegal firearm possession.
Charges: Failure to comply Improperly handling a firearm in a motor vehicle Resisting arrest Pending juvenile firearm charge

Title: Toledo girl at center of controversial arrest video arrested Monday in shooting case
description: On May 18, 2026, a 15-year-old girl was arrested in Toledo, Ohio, after allegedly firing a shot inside a residence during a domestic violence incident on Elm Street. Police reported that no one was injured. The juvenile was taken into custody and charged with multiple offenses related to the shooting. During a court appearance on May 19, a judge ordered that she remain detained because the incident involved a firearm. The girl's mother stated in court that she was not the intended victim, claiming her daughter fired the weapon at the ground. A pre-trial hearing was scheduled for June 1.
Charges: Felonious assault Aggravated menacing Domestic violence

Title: BODYCAM: Blown tire ends high-speed stolen car pursuit in Port St. Lucie
description: Savon Damont Montgomery, 32, was arrested after allegedly fleeing from St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office detectives in a stolen Honda Civic in Port St. Lucie. Detectives reported that he sped away from a 7-Eleven parking lot, weaved through traffic, passed vehicles, and drove into oncoming lanes, creating a danger to other motorists. Officers activated emergency lights and sirens, but Montgomery continued fleeing until he lost control on a grassy shoulder, causing a tire to blow out. He then climbed into the back seat before deputies took him into custody. A passenger in the vehicle was released without charges.
Charges: Grand theft auto Fleeing and eluding Driving with a suspended license

Title: High-speed chase through three counties ends in Walton County, suspect named
description: Alexander Razo, 39, of Memphis, Tennessee, was arrested after allegedly leading law enforcement on a high-speed pursuit involving multiple counties in Florida. Authorities said Razo stole a U-Haul and a gray SUV from Panama City before driving recklessly through Panama City Beach and other areas. The stolen U-Haul was reportedly crashed at a hotel parking lot, after which he allegedly took another vehicle and continued fleeing. The pursuit crossed Bay, Walton, and Okaloosa counties before deputies stopped him on Highway 285 with assistance from a helicopter. Deputies reported Razo was experiencing a medical episode suspected to be drug related and administered Narcan.
Charges: Fleeing and eluding Additional charges pending from Bay County

Title: A Gas Station Traffic Stop Turned Into a Chase When the Driver Jumped Into a Stolen Car
description: A 29-year-old man identified as Corrione Lawrence was arrested after allegedly fleeing from officers during a traffic stop at an Ohio gas station. Police said Lawrence entered a vehicle that was reported stolen while the traffic stop was taking place and drove away. Officers pursued the vehicle through Euclid before eventually stopping and arresting him. Lawrence faces charges connected to the stolen vehicle and the pursuit. Authorities stated the case involves allegations of receiving a stolen motor vehicle and failure to comply with a police officer’s order or signal. The final outcome will be determined through the court process.
Charges: Receiving stolen property (motor vehicle) Failure to comply with order or signal of a police officer

Title: Suspect arrested after pursuit in Highland County
description: On July 10, 2026, a Highland County Sheriff’s deputy attempted to stop a vehicle in the Allensburg area on U.S. Route 50 for an alleged traffic violation. The driver allegedly fled, leading to a pursuit with speeds reaching approximately 100 mph. The vehicle entered Hillsboro and reportedly crashed into another vehicle. The suspect then fled on foot but was apprehended by a sheriff’s office K9. Jerry Wayne Harner Jr. was arrested and taken to the Highland County Justice Center. Authorities thanked Lynchburg Police Department and Hillsboro Police Department for their assistance during the incident.
Charges: Obstructing official business, failure to comply, resisting arrest

Title: Driver Reaches 120 MPH in Northwest Ohio Chase Following Retail Parking Lot Fight
description: On June 19, 2026, Dominick Gomez was arrested following a high-speed police pursuit that began after a reported disturbance involving weapons at a retail parking lot in Defiance, Ohio. Police responded to reports of a fight involving firearms and a baseball bat. Officers later located a vehicle matching the suspect description and attempted a traffic stop, but Gomez allegedly fled. The pursuit reached speeds near 120 mph and continued through multiple counties. Law enforcement agencies used a coordinated maneuver near the Fulton-Henry county line to stop the vehicle. Gomez was taken into custody without further incident.
Charges: Formal charges not announced; investigation ongoing

Title: 2 in custody after high-speed police chase out of Englewood
description: Police pursued two suspects after reports of people checking car door handles in Englewood, Ohio. Officers located a stolen Ford Explorer and attempted a traffic stop, but the vehicle fled. Police later found another stolen vehicle crashed and continued searching. The pursuit ended in Dayton near Siebenthaler Avenue and North Main Street after suspects allegedly used a stolen pickup truck to flee and struck another vehicle. Officers used a pit maneuver to stop the truck. Two suspects, an adult and a juvenile, were taken into custody. Police continue investigating multiple alleged vehicle thefts connected to the incident.
Charges: Theft of a motor vehicle Receiving stolen property Failure to comply Obstructing official business

Title: Confrontation ends in gunfire; 1 arrested in Elyria shooting
description: Police arrested Daniel Armstrong, 57, of Oberlin, after a shooting in Elyria that injured another man. Officers responded shortly after 2 a.m. Sunday to the area of Lake Avenue and Foster Avenue after receiving a report of a person shot. They found an adult male victim suffering from a gunshot wound and transported him to a hospital with non-life-threatening injuries. Investigators determined the shooting occurred outside a home on Rush Street following a confrontation between Armstrong and the victim. Detectives identified Armstrong as the suspect, arrested him at his residence, and recovered the firearm believed used.
Charges: Felony assault

Title: Toledo mass shooting suspect arrested in Columbus
description: Ka Nye Taylor, 20, was arrested in Columbus after being wanted in connection with a mass shooting in Toledo. The shooting occurred at the Old West End Festival on June 6, 2026, when gunfire erupted following an altercation. Twelve people were injured, including teenagers and older adults. Police said the incident began after someone was tackled and assaulted, leading to gunfire from multiple individuals. Taylor was arrested at an apartment on East Town Street and was being returned to Toledo to face charges. Authorities credited assistance from multiple law enforcement agencies in locating and apprehending him.
Charges: 11 counts of felonious assault

Title: Caught on camera: Sheriff’s Office drone records suspect shooting at it
description: A man was arrested in Lee County, Florida, after allegedly firing multiple rounds from a BB gun at a Lee County Sheriff’s Office drone. The drone was assisting deputies during a search for a bear when operators observed a group of men in a wooded area. Video footage from the drone showed one man pointing a BB gun toward the drone and firing at least twice. Deputies used the recorded footage as evidence and arrested the suspect. The incident involved an alleged attack on a law enforcement drone, and authorities stated that shooting at an aircraft is a federal offense.
Charges: Firing a weapon at an aircraft

Title: Florida man accused of shooting former workplace vehicles after termination
description: A 36-year-old Florida man, Chase Hemenway, was arrested after deputies said he damaged eight company vehicles at American Air & Heat in Melbourne, Florida. The incident happened days after he was terminated from the company. Surveillance footage allegedly showed a person wearing a dark sweatshirt and knee pads entering the property and firing at the vehicles. Investigators identified Hemenway as a suspect and later found a sports bike, a Valken M17 launcher, and projectiles at his home. Deputies said Hemenway had expressed anger about his termination. He was arrested and held without bond.
Charges: Criminal mischief and armed burglary

Title: Former Chapel Hill police officer arrested in Florida over alleged New Orleans mass shooting threat
description: Christopher Gillum, a former Chapel Hill police officer, was arrested in Destin, Florida, after authorities said he threatened to carry out a mass shooting in New Orleans. Investigators alleged Gillum planned to attend a festival and target Black people before committing suicide by cop. Deputies located him using a license plate reader system and arrested him at a hotel. Authorities recovered a handgun and approximately 200 rounds of ammunition from his hotel room. Gillum was wanted in Louisiana on a terroristic threats charge and was held in Okaloosa County Jail while awaiting extradition.
Charges: Terroristic threats

Suspect Name: Jacorey Lowery, Quincy Desponosse, Semaj Blackshear
Title: 3 arrested amid shooting at Orlando apartment complex, police pursuit
description: Three people were arrested after a shooting at the Pendana at West Lakes Club Apartments on Orange Center Boulevard in Orlando, Florida. Police said surveillance footage showed occupants of a black car and black SUV shooting at two people riding scooters. No one was injured. Officers located the black car and arrested Jacorey Lowery and Quincy Desponosse. Police later attempted to stop the black SUV, but the driver fled. A helicopter tracked the vehicle until it stopped in Altamonte Springs, where officers arrested Semaj Blackshear. The suspects face attempted felony murder and firearm-related charges.
Charges: Attempted felony murder; principal to attempted felony murder with a firearm; fleeing and eluding law enforcement at high speed; resisting an officer without violence; violation of probation as a juvenile

Title: Retired Orlando police officer shot, killed during dispute; man arrested
description: Retired Orlando police officer Dennis Turner was shot and killed during a reported family dispute at a home on Kozart Street in Orlando, Florida. Police found Turner with a gunshot wound around 7 p.m. on New Year’s Day and transported him to a hospital, where he was pronounced dead. Investigators identified Jeffery London as the suspect and said he fled after the shooting. Law enforcement officers from Polk and Highlands counties assisted in locating and arresting London. He faces charges related to the death of Turner, who was a 23-year veteran of the Orlando Police Department.
Charges: First-degree murder; possession of a firearm by a convicted felon

Title: Video appears to show moment man shot by officer in Miami Shores
description: A man was shot by a Miami Shores police officer after officers responded to a disturbance report at Tropical Chevrolet on Biscayne Boulevard. Police said the man was carrying two large-edged weapons and had left the dealership before officers arrived. An officer later located the man near Northeast 86th Street and Biscayne Boulevard. Video footage showed the man appearing to run toward the officer while holding an object. The officer fired their weapon, striking the man. He was treated by officers and transported to Jackson Memorial Hospital. The Florida Department of Law Enforcement is investigating the officer-involved shooting.
Charges: Possession of a firearm, assault on a peace officer

Title: Armed suspect killed after pointing gun at Broward deputies during Davie chase, sheriff says
description: Napolian Marquez Powell, 27, was killed after a confrontation with Broward Sheriff’s Office deputies during an attempted arrest in Davie, Florida. Deputies from the fugitive and gang unit approached Powell at a Wawa gas station while serving an outstanding warrant. Authorities said Powell fled while carrying a firearm and was later tackled in a McDonald’s parking lot. Deputies reported that he refused repeated commands to drop the weapon and attempted to point the firearm at them, leading officers to open fire. Powell died at the scene. The Florida Department of Law Enforcement is investigating the shooting.
Charges: Fleeing and attempting to elude law enforcement; outstanding criminal warrants; DNA warrant related to firearms investigation

Title: Man arrested in Orange City shopping plaza parking lot shooting, police say
description: Joseph Aviles, 21, was arrested in connection with a shooting at Market Place Plaza in Orange City, Florida. Police responded around 10:30 a.m. after a disturbance at Ollie’s Bargain Outlet parking lot escalated into gunfire. Officers found a 46-year-old man suffering from a gunshot wound to the lower back. The victim was transported to a hospital with injuries that were not considered life-threatening. Investigators said the victim and suspects did not know each other and that a verbal altercation occurred before a male passenger fired at the victim. Aviles was taken into custody without incident.
Charges: attempted murder,

Title: Florida man chases down repo man’s tow truck and shoots at him, police say
description: Lawrence Hilbert Morant, 39, allegedly chased a tow truck driver after his Ford F-150 was repossessed from his Miami Gardens home on Monday. Police said Morant followed the driver and confronted him before firing a handgun at the tow truck while the driver was inside. The vehicle was struck several times, but the driver was not injured. Morant later appeared at a nearby Exxon gas station where officers arrested him before any further harm occurred. He admitted intentionally firing at the truck, according to police. The incident involved a repossession dispute that escalated into an armed confrontation involving the suspect.
Charges: Armed criminal mischief; aggravated assault with a firearm; shooting into vehicles

Title: Venice man accused of shooting man outside sports bar: SCSO
description: A 24-year-old Venice man, Colby Moran, was arrested after a shooting outside Outlook Sports Bar in Venice, Florida. According to the Sarasota County Sheriff's Office, Moran was involved in a parking lot argument with another man around 10:40 p.m. on Sunday. Investigators said both men had firearms, and Moran allegedly fired multiple rounds from his vehicle while leaving the area. One bullet grazed the other man's lower leg. A Venice Police Department officer later stopped Moran’s vehicle nearby and detained him until Sarasota County deputies took over the investigation.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon Aggravated battery with a deadly weapon Firing a weapon from a vehicle

Title: Shooting during 'mental health crisis' response sends Osceola County man to hospital
description: A 51-year-old Kissimmee man was shot during a law enforcement response to a reported mental health crisis on July 8, 2026. Deputies from the Osceola County Sheriff's Office responded to a home on Marcos Circle after a family member reported that the man was experiencing a mental health crisis and might be armed. Officials said the man became involved in a physical altercation with a responding deputy, leading to the deputy shooting him. The man was conscious and alert when he was airlifted to a hospital. The deputy was not injured, and additional details were not released.
Charges: not specified

Title: North Carolina man shot, killed by Secret Service and local deputy outside of Mar-a-Lago
description: Austin Tucker Martin, a 21-year-old man from Moore County, North Carolina, was fatally shot by U.S. Secret Service agents and a Palm Beach County Sheriff’s Office deputy outside Mar-a-Lago in Palm Beach, Florida. Authorities said Martin entered the secured perimeter of the property while allegedly carrying a shotgun and a gas canister. Officials stated that officers confronted him and ordered him to drop the items. According to investigators, Martin raised the shotgun into a shooting position, prompting the deputy and Secret Service agents to fire their weapons. Martin was pronounced dead at the scene. The FBI investigated the incident.
Charges: No charges filed (suspect deceased)

Title: 1 dead in deputy-involved shooting following Sanford block party, deputies say
description: Deputies with the Seminole County Sheriff's Office responded to a noise complaint at a large block party in Sanford's Midway neighborhood. On arrival, they encountered two armed individuals exchanging gunfire within the crowd. A deputy engaged one armed suspect who was actively firing and shot him. The suspect, Marcus Barnett, 27, was taken to a hospital where he died. Two bystanders suffered non-life-threatening injuries. No deputies were hurt. The Florida Department of Law Enforcement is investigating the deputy's use of deadly force. Authorities said there is no ongoing threat and the incident is considered isolated while the investigation continues today.
Charges: not specified

Title: VIDEO: Florida deputy survives after body-worn camera struck by bullet
description: Volusia County Deputy José Rivera responded to a battery call when an armed suspect, Luis Diaz Polanco, emerged and fired multiple shots. During the encounter, one bullet struck Rivera’s body-worn camera, while another shot injured him in the leg and shoulder. The injuries were not life-threatening. The suspect was taken into custody and held without bond. Authorities charged him with two counts of attempted murder of a law enforcement officer. The incident involved gunfire between the suspect and deputies while officers were responding to the call. The Volusia County Sheriff’s Office investigated the shooting and released body camera footage.
Charges: Two counts of attempted murder of a law enforcement officer

Title: ‘Hellacious gun battle’: Two dead, two police officers wounded after morning shoot-out in city streets
description: A gun battle occurred during morning rush hour in Gainesville after a suspected shooter allegedly killed a man inside a retail business. Police responded to reports of the shooting, and the suspect fled before stopping his vehicle and opening fire on officers in the street. A two-minute exchange of gunfire followed between the suspect and police. The suspect was killed by a Gainesville police officer, and the original victim was also found dead. Two police officers were wounded, one in the arm and one in the leg, but both were later released from the hospital. The Florida Department of Law Enforcement investigated the officer-involved shooting.
Charges: Unknown (suspect killed during incident)

Title: BWC: Fla. officer shot during confrontation with homicide suspect before OIS
description: On March 9, 2026, Pasco County deputies responded to a property dispute in New Port Richey, Florida, where Aaron Rodriguez allegedly shot two people, killing one and injuring another. Deputies located Rodriguez inside a garage across from the property. When deputies approached, Rodriguez was reportedly holding a firearm and refused commands to drop it. A deputy was shot during the confrontation, and other deputies returned fire, striking Rodriguez. Both the injured deputy and Rodriguez were taken to a hospital. The Florida Department of Law Enforcement investigated the officer-involved shooting, and involved deputies were placed on administrative leave.
Charges: Suspected homicide and shooting two people (specific charges not provided)

Title: Man accused of shooting girlfriend in Auburndale pulls gun on deputies who shot him: PCSO
description: On July 10, 2026, law enforcement officers shot and killed Derrick Brathwaite in Auburndale, Florida, after investigators said he shot his girlfriend outside a Spectrum store. Deputies responded after reports of gunfire and found the woman suffering from gunshot wounds and Brathwaite nearby holding a firearm. Authorities said Brathwaite pointed the gun at responding officers, causing officers from the Auburndale Police Department and Polk County Sheriff’s Office to open fire. Both Brathwaite and the woman died from their injuries. The Florida Department of Law Enforcement investigation continued into the officer-involved shooting.
Charges: Suspected murder (shooting death of girlfriend)

Title: BWC shows Fla. officers pull suspect from burning cruiser after shootout that wounded cop
description: Officers responded to a road rage shooting report in Daytona Beach, Florida, where they located a suspect vehicle and pursued it briefly. The suspect crashed, exited, and fled on foot before firing at South Daytona Police Officer Jake Fessenden. The officer returned fire and was wounded in the leg and shoulder. The suspect entered the officer's cruiser, which later caught fire. Deputies removed the injured suspect from the burning vehicle. Fessenden was hospitalized and expected to recover. The suspect suffered life-threatening injuries and faced attempted murder charges against a police officer. Investigators had not determined how the cruiser caught fire.
Charges: Attempted murder of a police officer

Title: Video shows deputy shoot armed teen during confrontation in SW Miami-Dade
description: Deputies responded to a report of threats involving a firearm at a park in southwest Miami-Dade. Authorities said they found a group of four teens and a confrontation occurred. A 15-year-old armed teen ran from deputies. Body camera footage showed the deputy pursuing the teen and ordering him to surrender.
