Title: Woman dies after shootout with Palm Bay police, chief says
description: Kamla Grimmer, 53, died after an officer-involved shooting during a standoff with Palm Bay Police at a residence on Serenade Street Northwest. Police responded after reports of someone firing a gun. Authorities said Grimmer fired shots from inside the home and later fired toward responding officers and SWAT members. Officers initially did not return fire but later exchanged gunfire after continued threats. Grimmer was found dead inside the residence, and preliminary findings indicated she was killed by police return fire. The Florida Department of Law Enforcement investigated the incident. No other injuries were reported.
Charges: No charges (suspect deceased)

Title: Eviction notice in Ohio leads to shootout with police, woman facing 39 felony charges
description: On March 25, 2026, Rebecca Theresa Ann Besser was scheduled to receive an eviction notice in Muskingum County, Ohio. Authorities said she told officers she had a gun, leading to a standoff with law enforcement. A SWAT team responded, and officials reported that tear gas was used, multiple shots were exchanged, and a drone was shot down during the confrontation. Besser later surrendered without injuries to herself or officers. She was taken into custody and faces numerous felony charges, including attempted murder, felonious assault, obstructing official business, and inducing panic.
Charges: Three counts of attempted aggravated murder, one count of attempted murder, 32 counts of felonious assault, one count of obstructing official business, two counts of inducing panic

Suspect Name: Renan Castro-Gil, Jose Carlos-Martinez, Carlos Figueroa-Castro
Title: Police: Woman dead, 3 men in custody after east Columbus shooting
description: On May 9, 2026, Columbus police responded to reports of gunfire on Malibu Drive and later found 26-year-old Nesya Casaleno suffering from gunshot wounds on Elmsbury Court. She was transported to a hospital where she died from her injuries. Police arrested three men: Renan Castro-Gil, Jose Carlos-Martinez, and Carlos Figueroa-Castro. Investigators said Castro-Gil allegedly planned the shooting and offered payment to the other suspects. Court records indicated a violent relationship between Castro-Gil and the victim. All three suspects were charged and are being held in custody.
Charges: Aggravated murder

Title: 911 call reveals 26-hour captivity before deadly Olmsted Falls SWAT standoff
description: Police responded to a domestic violence shooting near Brentwood Drive and Bagley Road in Olmsted Falls. Officers found Rita Galyas deceased outside a home and Jamie McFarland barricaded inside. McFarland’s ex-girlfriend, the homeowner, escaped after reporting she had been held captive for 26 hours. A SWAT standoff followed with attempts to contact McFarland. Police later found him dead inside the basement from a self-inflicted gunshot wound. Investigators said no officers fired their weapons during the incident. The case involved domestic violence, a shooting, hostage allegations, and two fatalities.
Charges: domestic violence shooting

Title: Florida duo accused of kidnapping Uber driver at gunpoint
description: Isaiah Thurston and Jakeria Riley were arrested after police said they kidnapped an Uber driver at gunpoint in Boynton Beach, Florida. Authorities stated the driver was picked up near Catalina Center on January 16, 2026, before a masked suspect allegedly held a gun against the victim and forced the ride to be canceled. The suspects allegedly made the driver travel through West Palm Beach and Riviera Beach for nearly two hours while attempting to withdraw money using the victim’s credit cards. Police later located both suspects near a hotel. Riley was found with cocaine and credit cards.
Charges: Kidnapping; armed robbery; possession of a controlled substance; violation of probation; resisting arrest

Suspect Name: Rodrico Boyd, Don McAllister, Michael Ashford, Yarli Smith, and 18 other unnamed individuals
Title: Tampa police arrest 22 after ‘Teen Takeover’ at Curtis Hixon Park: TPD
description: The Tampa Police Department arrested 22 people after a reported teen takeover at Curtis Hixon Park in Tampa. Authorities said the group, ranging in age from 12 to 21, caused traffic disruptions, fights, and other disturbances. Police responded with patrol officers, bike units, and Air Service personnel to manage the situation. The arrests included charges related to public fighting, narcotics possession, resisting officers, and unlawful weapon possession. Officers seized two firearms and one vehicle during the operation. Four adults were identified, including individuals charged with drug offenses, weapon violations, fleeing, eluding, resisting, and affray.
Charges: Affray; possession of narcotics; resisting without violence; unlawful possession of a weapon; possession of controlled substance; drug paraphernalia possession; possession of cannabis under 20 grams; possession of cannabis sativa resin; weapon during commission of a felony; fleeing and eluding
Comments: Could be good, just not too sure.

Title: Alachua County woman accused of throwing feces at father during fight
description: Elisa Rivera, 25, was accused of assaulting her parents during a domestic dispute in Alachua County, Florida. According to the arrest report, the conflict began after Rivera’s mother refused to let her join a trip to Gainesville. Rivera allegedly damaged a vehicle, pulled her mother to the ground, and took her purse. Later, after her father refused to give her alcohol, Rivera allegedly threw feces at him. Deputies reported injuries to her mother and a bite mark on her father. Rivera was arrested and booked into the Alachua County Jail on multiple charges related to the incident.
Charges: Robbery without a weapon; criminal mischief; battery on a person 65 years or older

Title: Recent arrests in Bradford, Union and Clay
description: James Brewer was arrested by Bradford County deputies after an alleged domestic violence incident involving his pregnant partner. The victim reported that Brewer restrained her during arguments, threatened her, and later prevented her from leaving. Witnesses allegedly corroborated parts of the incident. Deputies later located Brewer at a convenience store, where he was detained. During a vehicle search, deputies reported finding drug paraphernalia and a substance that tested positive for cocaine. Brewer denied the physical assault allegations but admitted to arguing with the victim. He faces charges related to aggravated battery, cocaine possession, and drug equipment possession.
Charges: Aggravated battery Possession of cocaine Possession of drug equipment
Comments: The Joseph Holmes case is the only one worth pursuing.

Title: Man accused of grabbing woman at Altamonte Springs Ulta store has over 10 prior battery reports, court records show
description: Mario A. Gomez, 39, was arrested after investigators accused him of inappropriately touching two women in separate incidents in Altamonte Springs, Florida. Police said one incident occurred at an Ulta Beauty store where Gomez allegedly followed a woman and grabbed her from behind. Another incident occurred during a Passover service at Chabad of Altamonte Springs, where he was accused of unwanted physical contact with a woman. Authorities said Gomez had a history of similar allegations, including multiple prior reports and convictions. Officers arrested him on Seminole County warrants, and prosecutors upgraded his charges to felony battery due to his criminal history.
Charges: Felony battery

Title: Woman arrested after ramming car with children inside at Dollar General, Marion County deputies say
description: Kayla Agee, 26, was arrested after deputies accused her of intentionally ramming another vehicle with children inside at a Dollar General parking lot in Ocala, Florida. According to the arrest report, Agee became involved in an argument with another woman after being upset that the woman left her children inside her vehicle while entering the store. Deputies said Agee drove her vehicle into the other car before leaving the area. She was later arrested at a Circle K store and booked into the Marion County Jail. The incident involved allegations of child abuse, aggravated battery, and criminal mischief.
Charges: Child abuse, aggravated battery, criminal mischief

Title: Federal Medicare judge, 79, arrested for cutting wife with butter knife, cops say
description: Gerald Foulds, a 79-year-old federal Medicare administrative law judge, was arrested after a domestic violence incident involving his wife in Miami. According to investigators, the couple argued, and the verbal dispute escalated into a physical confrontation. His wife said she went into the kitchen to avoid the argument, but Foulds followed her, grabbed her shoulder, and allegedly cut her left arm with a butter knife. She fled to a neighbor's home for help before seeking medical treatment. Police later interviewed Foulds, who denied the allegations. He was arrested, booked into jail, and later appeared in bond court.
Charges: Aggravated battery with a deadly weapon causing bodily harm

Title: Police: Man accused of pushing girlfriend from moving truck, striking her with pickup
description: On April 15, 2026, Jupiter police investigated an incident in which Austin Arthur Pare allegedly pushed his girlfriend from a moving pickup truck during an argument. Investigators said the victim fell onto the roadway, suffering abrasions, and Pare then intentionally struck her with the truck, causing additional injuries. Witnesses reported seeing the victim on the road and the suspect loading her back into the vehicle before leaving the scene. Police used FLOCK camera technology to identify the truck. The victim later received treatment at Jupiter Medical Center. Following the investigation, Pare was arrested and charged with aggravated battery with a deadly weapon.
Charges: Aggravated battery with a deadly weapon

Title: Woman suspected of being impaired opens fire outside Florida shopping plaza, 2 wounded
description: On April 18, 2026, Homestead Police Department officers responded to reports of shots fired at a shopping plaza parking lot on Northeast 10th Court. Investigators said Samantha Renee Morales, who was allegedly impaired by alcohol, opened fire during the incident. Two people sustained gunshot wounds and were transported to a hospital, where they were reported to be in stable condition. Morales was taken into custody at the scene without further incident. Police alleged that she used a firearm while impaired and injured the victims during the shooting. The investigation remained ongoing following her arrest.
Charges: Aggravated battery Assault with a firearm Use of a firearm while impaired by alcohol
Comments: Again lacking police in action. They arrive after the incident occurs.

Title: Sunrise police: Woman attacks 79-year-old woman at Walmart
description: On January 23, 2026, Keri Estep was involved in an altercation with a 79-year-old woman at a Walmart in Sunrise, Florida. Investigators said Estep cut in front of the elderly woman in the customer service line before pushing, punching, and kicking her. An Allied Universal security officer intervened to stop the attack. Estep initially claimed she was defending herself and her baby, but surveillance video showed she was the aggressor. After reviewing the footage, Estep admitted her version of events was inaccurate and apologized. She was arrested on March 11, 2026, and charged in connection with the assault.
Charges: Aggravated battery on a person 65 years old or older

Title: Taco Bell worker accused of shooting customers over soda in water cup
description: On April 27, 2026, D’Mari Jy’Quan Patterson, a Taco Bell employee in West Palm Beach, Florida, became involved in a verbal dispute with three women after one attempted to fill a water cup with soda. During the argument, Patterson allegedly racked a handgun and fired inside the restaurant. One woman was shot and fell to the ground, another was grazed by a bullet, and the third fled outside. Patterson allegedly followed the third woman and fired another shot that missed. He later called 911, admitted firing the gun, claimed self-defense, and was arrested after police rejected his account.
Charges: Three counts of aggravated assault with a firearm

Title: She was a decoy': Florida woman 'dressed in lingerie' lures victim into ax-wielding ambush at boyfriend's apartment
description: Nicholas Lavallee and Anne Aksell are accused of arranging an ambush robbery at an Orlando apartment complex. Investigators say Aksell lured the victim to the location by inviting him over, while Lavallee and other men allegedly confronted him with weapons. The victim was reportedly threatened with a gun, beaten, struck with an axe, and stabbed before escaping. Authorities said the suspects stole the victim’s phone, wallet, and vehicle keys. Surveillance footage and interviews reportedly supported investigators’ claims that the attack was planned.
Charges: Robbery with a firearm Grand theft of a motor vehicle Battery in the first degree Aggravated battery with a deadly weapon
Comments: Repeat case. Was already requested above.

Title: Woman charged with murder after pursuit leads to deadly crash on Florida Turnpike
description: Anna Giza was accused of driving a stolen vehicle and fleeing from law enforcement during a pursuit in Broward County, Florida. Deputies said the pursuit began after the stolen vehicle investigation and escalated when the vehicle struck law enforcement vehicles. The chase continued onto the Florida Turnpike, where a collision occurred and resulted in the death of an innocent motorist. Giza was injured in the crash and later charged. Authorities said she also allegedly injured law enforcement officers during the incident. The investigation involved the Broward Sheriff's Office and Florida Highway Patrol.
Charges: Murder by another while engaged in a specific felony (felony murder), two counts of aggravated battery on a law enforcement officer, aggravated assault on a law enforcement officer, aggravated fleeing with serious injury or death, grand theft auto, resisting an officer without violence

Title: Cantonment Woman Charged With Aggravated Battery At Downtown Restaurant
description: Martaina Conner was arrested after an alleged aggravated battery incident at Nick’s Boathouse restaurant in Pensacola, Florida. Police said a verbal dispute involving her son and another group escalated in the parking lot. Investigators allege Conner retrieved a Ruger LCP handgun from her vehicle, displayed it during the confrontation, and struck a victim multiple times in the head and face with the firearm. Conner claimed she acted in self-defense, but police said witness statements and social media video showed her initiating the physical attack. The handgun was later recovered from her purse, and she was released on bond.
Charges: Felony aggravated battery with a deadly weapon

Title: Woman arrested for armed robbery and assault outside Miami Gardens Walmart
description: Latoya Denise Jones, 37, was arrested after an alleged armed robbery and violent assault outside a Walmart in Miami Gardens, Florida. Police said Jones met two individuals to discuss relationship issues and became agitated. Investigators allege she retrieved a handgun from her vehicle, pointed it at the victims, and made threats. During the confrontation, one victim dropped an iPhone, which Jones allegedly took. Police said Jones then drove her vehicle into both victims as they attempted to leave, causing one victim to suffer a fractured leg and another to sustain leg injuries before she fled.
Charges: Aggravated battery with a weapon; Armed robbery; Aggravated assault with intent to commit a felony

Title: Florida woman accused of throwing collard greens and threatening victims with skillet
description: Wendy Leigh Messer, 58, was arrested after an alleged altercation at her residence in Satsuma, Putnam County, Florida. Deputies said the incident involved accusations of battery and aggravated assault with a weapon. One victim alleged Messer threw a plate of collard greens and threatened her with a knife. Another victim said Messer approached while holding a cast-iron skillet in a threatening manner. Deputies also alleged Messer swung at one victim during the argument. During the arrest investigation, deputies found suspected cocaine and drug paraphernalia. Messer was taken to Putnam County Jail after the incident.
Charges: Battery; Aggravated assault; Possession of cocaine

Title: Roommate altercation in Orlando leads to arrest on multiple charges
description: Lashawanda Denise Boyce, 45, was arrested after an alleged roommate dispute in Orlando, Florida. Deputies said Boyce and her roommate Richard Damarick Mitchell had an argument while Mitchell was moving out of their shared apartment. Boyce allegedly threw bleach on Mitchell during the first confrontation. Later, she allegedly followed him to another residence, damaged windows with a cooking pot, and struck him in the head with the pot, causing a large knot and minor laceration. Deputies located Boyce nearby and arrested her. The incident resulted in criminal charges related to the alleged assault and property damage.
Charges: Aggravated battery; Criminal mischief

Title: 12-year-old charged with attempted murder after middle school stabbing attack
description: A 12-year-old male student was accused of stabbing two students and an adult paraprofessional at Walton Middle School in DeFuniak Springs, Florida. Authorities said the suspect entered a school bathroom, later emerged wearing a mask and carrying a sharp object, and attacked victims in a hallway. Two seventh-grade students were hospitalized in critical condition, while the paraprofessional was later released. The attack lasted about 45 seconds, according to officials. The suspect was taken into secure juvenile detention and faces multiple charges, including attempted murder. Authorities said the motive for the random attacks remains unclear.
Charges: Attempted murder; Two counts of aggravated battery with a deadly weapon; Wearing a mask during the commission of a felony; Tampering with evidence; Disrupting a school function

Title: Miami woman arrested in violent kidnapping and robbery, separate burglary, cops say
description: Kihmanii McKenziee, 27, was arrested after investigators alleged she kidnapped and robbed a man at gunpoint following a meeting at Haulover Beach. Police said she threatened to shoot the victim unless he gave her money, repeatedly punched him, forced him to drive while holding him at gunpoint, and struck him in the head with a pistol, causing a laceration. The victim stopped the vehicle on Interstate 95, allowing McKenziee to flee. She was later stopped by police, and officers found a pistol in her purse. She also faces separate burglary and assault-related charges from a 2024 incident involving her ex-boyfriend.
Charges: Armed robbery Kidnapping with aggravated battery Burglary with assault or battery Burglary of an occupied structure

Title: Florida man allegedly shot woman in neck, dragged her back inside before hiding in backyard pool
description: Robert Anthony Morgan, 40, was arrested after allegedly shooting a woman in the neck during a domestic violence incident in Wildwood, Florida. Police responded to reports of an argument followed by a gunshot and found the victim in a driveway with life-threatening injuries. Investigators said Morgan dragged the wounded woman back toward the property and threatened her mother when she attempted to get help. Officers later found Morgan hiding in a backyard swimming pool and took him into custody. A rifle was recovered at the scene, and authorities also found blood leading from the street to the residence. Four children were inside the home.
Charges: Attempted Felony Murder Aggravated Battery with a Deadly Weapon Possession of a Firearm by a Convicted Felon Discharging a Firearm in Public or on Residential Property

Title: Cooking up trouble: PBSO says woman used kitchen pot in alleged assault
description: Nathalie Alcenat, 23, was arrested after deputies said a domestic dispute escalated into an alleged assault involving a kitchen pot as a weapon. Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office deputies responded to an apartment on Alora Isles Drive after receiving a domestic disturbance call. When officers arrived, they found the involved individuals separated. The man involved showed deputies cellphone video that allegedly captured Alcenat attacking him with the cooking pot. After reviewing the footage, deputies arrested Alcenat on a felony charge of aggravated battery with a deadly weapon. She was taken into custody and transported to jail without incident.
Charges: Aggravated Battery with a Deadly Weapon

Title: Woman arrested after throwing beer bottles at toddler in Florida: deputies
description: Carolyn Miller was arrested after deputies alleged she threw beer bottles toward a 3-year-old child in the Fort Walton Beach area. Authorities said the incident occurred after Miller fell from her bicycle and the toddler approached her to check on her condition. Investigators stated that Miller picked up two beer bottles and threw them in the child’s direction with enough force that the child could have been struck. The child’s parents and witnesses provided statements to deputies. Miller reportedly could not provide a clear explanation and said she believed she was being attacked. No injuries were reported, and she was charged with aggravated assault.
Charges: Aggravated Assault with a Deadly Weapon
Comments: Lacks story as well as police in action.

Title: Bodycam shows foot chase of dancer accused of attacking strip club manager with pole
description: Princess Aaliyah Bell, 23, was arrested after police alleged she attacked a strip club manager with a metal pole following a workplace dispute in North Miami Beach. According to investigators, Bell had been fired from the club and returned to collect her belongings but allegedly caused a disturbance by throwing items and arguing with staff. Police said she later returned with a 7-foot metal pole and struck the manager in the leg before fleeing. Officers located Bell nearby and a body camera captured the foot chase and arrest. She was taken into custody and booked on multiple charges related to the incident.
Charges: Aggravated Battery Aggravated Assault with a Deadly Weapon Resisting an Officer Without Violence Giving a False Name or Identification

Title: Woman indicted on 2 felony charges after allegedly assaulting Akron paramedic
description: Kevelyn Evans was indicted after allegedly assaulting an Akron paramedic during a medical response incident. Paramedics arrived at a senior high-rise apartment building for a medical call involving a man. After determining the patient did not need hospital transport, family members became upset and followed the paramedics outside. Investigators said Evans approached an ambulance and punched a paramedic in the face while he was seated inside. The paramedic suffered bruising and a swollen eye. Police described the situation as hostile, and Evans was later charged following the investigation into the assault.
Charges: Assault; Aggravated possession of drugs

Title: Going to kill them all': Mother accused of setting fire to apartment with 4 kids inside
description: Hawa Hassan was arrested after allegedly setting fire to an occupied apartment building in Columbus, Ohio, while four of her children were inside. Police responded to the apartment at 3740 Eakin Rd. and determined that a bedroom had been intentionally set on fire. Investigators said Hassan admitted she started the fire. Witnesses reported that the children said their mother used a lighter to start the fire and threatened to kill them. The children were removed and placed with Franklin County Children’s Services. No injuries were reported. Hassan faces felony and misdemeanor charges related to the incident.
Charges: Aggravated arson, domestic violence, assault

Title: Ohio firefighter allegedly shot woman and lit house fire, then showed up to extinguish it
description: Peyton Beam, 22, a volunteer firefighter in Ohio, is accused of killing Ericka Kramer and setting her home on fire. Authorities said firefighters responded to the blaze and discovered Kramer's body inside the residence. Investigators determined her death was a homicide. Prosecutors allege Beam shot Kramer multiple times, poured gasoline on her body, and ignited the fire before arriving with other firefighters to extinguish it. Beam had reportedly worked for Kramer and considered her a second mother. He was arrested and charged in connection with the death and house fire. The investigation remains ongoing.
Charges: Aggravated murder, aggravated arson

Title: Mother tells 911 her child wasn't breathing before admitting to suffocating her to death
description: Sharon Sakoulos, a 41-year-old Columbus mother, is accused of killing her 3-year-old daughter Cassidy on New Year’s Eve 2025. Police said Sakoulos called 911 reporting that her child was unresponsive and later allegedly admitted to suffocating the child with a plastic bag. Officers found the girl unresponsive at the family home on Orson Drive, and she was pronounced dead after being taken to Nationwide Children’s Hospital. Sakoulos was arrested and remains jailed on a $2 million bond. The case involves allegations of child abuse, murder, and suffocation, with court proceedings ongoing.
Charges: Aggravated murder Murder Strangulation or suffocation Endangering children

Title: Woman shot, man arrested in Westwood
description: Donte Graves, 43, was arrested after a woman was shot in the foot at a residence on McHenry Avenue in Cincinnati. Police said officers responded shortly after 10:30 p.m. and found the victim suffering from a non-life-threatening gunshot wound. Investigators recovered a firearm and detained Graves at the scene. The victim told police that Graves chased her with a gun and fired one round, striking her foot. Authorities identified the incident as a domestic violence situation and requested a temporary restraining order. Graves was booked into the Hamilton County Justice Center following the shooting.
Charges: Felonious assault; Having weapons while under disability

Title: Cleveland man found guilty in violent carjacking that left mother shot in face
description: Ronald Loftis, 47, was convicted for a violent carjacking that occurred in Cleveland’s Detroit-Shoreway neighborhood. Authorities said Loftis attacked Tiffanie Muscatello in her driveway while she was placing her 1-year-old son into her vehicle. Investigators alleged he demanded money, attempted to steal the car with the child inside, and shot Muscatello in the face during the struggle. The vehicle was recovered shortly after the incident. Cleveland detectives later located and arrested Loftis at a residence without incident. A Cuyahoga County jury found him guilty on multiple robbery, assault, and weapons charges.
Charges: Three counts of aggravated robbery; Four counts of robbery; Three counts of felonious assault; Unlawful use of a weapon by a career criminal; Having weapons under disability; Grand theft of a motor vehicle

Title: Former Ohio House Candidate faces serious charges in Florida
description: Daniel J. Kalmbach, 31, a former Ohio House candidate, faces upgraded charges related to an alleged domestic violence incident in a Miami apartment. Prosecutors accuse Kalmbach of confining his girlfriend for multiple days, preventing her from leaving, and assaulting her with scissors and a knife. Authorities said the victim suffered bruises, cuts, and injuries that caused scarring. Police responded after a domestic violence call and found the victim in the building lobby seeking help. Kalmbach allegedly admitted to striking his girlfriend during an argument. He pleaded not guilty and requested a jury trial.
Charges: Kidnapping with a weapon; Aggravated battery causing great bodily harm and using a deadly weapon
Comments: Good story and alleged action, but lacking police intervention.

Title: Miami man, 98, arrested for allegedly stabbing caregiver: Police
description: Juan Perez, a 98-year-old Miami man, was arrested after police said he allegedly stabbed his caregiver during a confrontation at an apartment building in the 200 block of Southwest 18th Court. According to the arrest report, the caregiver was helping his mother-in-law when Perez allegedly approached her with a knife and struck her arm. The victim suffered heavy bleeding and was taken to Mercy Hospital. Perez told investigators that an argument occurred and claimed the victim grabbed him before he stabbed her. Police recovered three kitchen knives from bushes near the apartment.
Charges: Aggravated battery with a deadly weapon

Title: LCSO: Man arrested after firing multiple rounds at delivery driver’s vehicle
description: Aaron Harwell, 21, was arrested after deputies said he fired multiple rounds at a delivery driver’s vehicle in Leon County. The incident occurred when the driver entered Harwell’s driveway while attempting to locate an address during a routine delivery. Authorities said Harwell retrieved his father’s firearm, confronted the driver, and fired at the vehicle as it left the area. The vehicle was struck several times, but the driver was not injured. Harwell told investigators he did not intend to hurt the driver but wanted to prevent the person from returning to his residence. He later bonded out of jail.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon
Comments: More of an accidental shooting. Need more action and police in action.

Title: Fernandina Beach man arrested after allegedly shooting, killing friend accidentally
description: Ty Richardson, 25, was arrested after a shooting that killed his friend inside a home on South 13th Terrace in Fernandina Beach. Police said Richardson called authorities early Tuesday morning and reported that he had accidentally shot his best friend. Officers arrived and found Richardson attempting to help the victim, who had suffered a gunshot wound to the head. The victim was taken for medical treatment but later died at a local hospital. Investigators determined there was probable cause that Richardson placed the firearm against the victim’s head and pulled the trigger. Richardson was charged with manslaughter.
Charges: Manslaughter
Comments: Again mostly accidental and lacking police intervention.

Title: Jacksonville man charged with attempted murder after shootout with covert officers in Brentwood
description: Samuel Cook, 35, was involved in an officer-involved shooting in the Brentwood area of Jacksonville, Florida. Jacksonville Sheriff's Office task force officers were conducting surveillance related to reported drug activity when Cook allegedly approached their unmarked vehicle and pointed a firearm at officers. Police said officers fired their weapons, and Cook exchanged gunfire with them while fleeing on foot. He was shot multiple times but surrendered and was taken to a hospital with non-life-threatening injuries. The two officers involved were not injured. Cook was later charged with aggravated assault and attempted murder of a law enforcement officer.
Charges: Aggravated assault; attempted murder of a law enforcement officer

Title: Drive-by style' shooting leads to arrest of Lake City man, police say
description: Jamal Waters, 23, was arrested after Lake City Police investigated a reported drive-by style shooting. Officers responded to the area of NW Bascom Norris Drive and NW Oakland Avenue after a FLOCK gunshot detection alert. Police found shell casings and vehicle debris suggesting a crash occurred. A victim later arrived at HCA North Florida Hospital with gunshot wounds. Investigators determined a Ford Mustang had pursued a Toyota Tundra before an occupant of the Mustang fired multiple rounds. Police identified Waters as the shooter and arrested him. He faces attempted murder and firearm-related charges.
Charges: Attempted second-degree murder while armed with a firearm; possession of a firearm by a person under 24 with a prior qualifying delinquency

Title: Arrest made in deadly Jacksonville apartment shooting
description: Isaiah Micaleb Robinson, 19, was arrested in connection with a fatal apartment shooting in Jacksonville, Florida. Jacksonville Sheriff's Office responded to an apartment on Collins Road after receiving reports of a person being shot. Officers found a woman suffering from at least one gunshot wound. She was transported to a local hospital, where she later died from her injuries. Robinson was detained at the scene and identified as the suspect during the investigation. After interviews and review of evidence, police arrested him and charged him with manslaughter in connection with the shooting that caused the woman’s death.
Charges: Manslaughter

Title: Man charged with murder after one killed, two injured in shooting near Silverleaf construction site
description: Yovany Lopez Cobo, 20, was arrested in connection with a deadly shooting near a Silverleaf construction site in St. Johns County, Florida. According to the St. Johns County Sheriff's Office, an argument between construction workers near Crimson Leaf Drive and Johns Island Parkway escalated when Cobo allegedly pulled out a firearm and shot three men. One victim was shot multiple times and died at the scene, while two others were injured and expected to recover. After fleeing, Cobo and his brother were located traveling on State Road 206 and stopped at a Love's Travel Stop.
Charges: Second-degree murder; two counts of attempted second-degree murder

Title: JSO: Man dead after argument inside Southside Circle K escalates into shooting; suspect arrested
description: Mai-Kel Bryant, 22, was arrested after a deadly shooting outside a Circle K gas station on Southside Boulevard in Jacksonville, Florida. According to the Jacksonville Sheriff's Office, Bryant, who was an employee of the gas station, became involved in an argument with another man inside the store. The argument continued into the parking lot, where shots were fired. The victim, identified as 36-year-old Omar Padilla, was taken to Memorial Hospital and later died from his injuries. Police said Bryant left the scene in a red Dodge Charger before being taken into custody at a nearby home.
Charges: Second-degree murder; tampering with evidence
Comments: Lack of police intervention. We are looking for cases where the police are involved in the incident as opposed to arriving after it occured.

Title: Jacksonville men charged after string of armed restaurant robberies escalates to shooting
description: Bronquell Hutchinson and Isaac Rodriguez were arrested in Jacksonville after investigators linked them to a series of armed robberies involving food trucks and a restaurant between May 19 and May 21, 2026. Police said the suspects committed multiple robberies before a shooting incident involving a food truck owner who followed their vehicle. The owner reported that shots were fired at his vehicle, causing bullet damage and minor injuries to him and a passenger. Investigators said Hutchinson and Rodriguez were identified and taken into custody. Both suspects face several felony charges, including armed robbery and attempted murder related to the shooting.
Charges: Armed robbery, attempted murder, multiple felony charges

Title: Man shot by Clay County deputy identified by sheriff's office, deputy placed on leave
description: Morris Anthony Davis, 48, was shot and killed by a Clay County Sheriff's Office deputy in Oakleaf Plantation, Florida. Deputies responded while assisting the Department of Children and Families and discovered Davis was wanted in Mississippi on a homicide warrant. Investigators said Davis was armed with two knives and resisted attempts to take him into custody. Deputies said multiple taser attempts were unsuccessful before Deputy D. Brown shot Davis in a neighbor’s yard. Davis died at the scene despite life-saving efforts. The incident is under investigation by the Florida Department of Law Enforcement and State Attorney’s Office.
Charges: No charges (suspect deceased)

Title: Jacksonville officers kill man accused of threatening officers and employees with gun
description: Michael Krause Jr., 49, was shot and killed by Jacksonville Sheriff's Office officers during an armed standoff at a Gate gas station on Bowden Road. Police responded to a reported armed robbery involving threats toward store employees. Krause allegedly displayed a handgun, forced employees to leave, and made statements about shooting officers. After officers arrived, police said Krause exited the building with a gun and moved toward them. An officer fired a rifle, striking him. Krause was pronounced dead at the scene. No officers, employees, or civilians were injured during the incident.
Charges: No charges (suspect deceased)

Suspect Name: Walter Johnson; Malice Wheeler; Cornelius Scott
Title: Three men arrested after string of vehicle burglaries in Jacksonville Beach
description: Three men were arrested after a series of vehicle burglaries in Jacksonville Beach. Police responded around 3 a.m. to reports of suspects entering vehicles on 1st Street South. Officers established a perimeter and detained one suspect who fled the area. A K-9 unit located stolen items, and video evidence helped identify additional suspects. Police said at least four vehicles were burglarized. Walter Johnson was arrested on multiple theft-related charges, Malice Wheeler faced burglary and theft charges, and Cornelius Scott was arrested on an outstanding theft warrant. Stolen property was recovered during the investigation.
Charges: Walter Johnson: Burglary of a conveyance, grand theft, resisting without violence, fraudulent use of a credit card, petit theft Malice Wheeler: Burglary of a conveyance, grand theft, resisting without violence Cornelius Scott: Outstanding warrant for petit theft

Title: Police release body-worn camera video from shooting of Westside murder suspect
description: Robert Phillips, 53, was identified as a person of interest in a Westside Jacksonville shooting that killed a woman and critically injured another person. Jacksonville Sheriff's Office investigators located Phillips’ vehicle in the Mandarin area and attempted to take him into custody through a planned tactical vehicle block. Police said Phillips armed himself with a handgun while inside his vehicle and fired two shots at deputies. Officers returned fire, killing Phillips at the scene. Authorities stated that if Phillips had survived, he would have faced charges including murder, attempted murder of a law enforcement officer, and theft.
Charges: Theft; murder; attempted murder; attempted murder of a law enforcement officer (would have been charged if he survived)

Title: Tampa Police Arrest Suspect in Attempted Murder After Monday Shooting
description: Emanuel Watson, 33, was arrested by Tampa Police after a shooting near N. 27th Street and E. 97th Avenue on February 16, 2026. Police said Watson and the victim, who were known to each other, became involved in a verbal argument that turned physical. Investigators said Watson produced a firearm and shot the victim multiple times, causing critical injuries. Officers provided emergency medical care before the victim was taken to a hospital. Police located Watson in the backyard of a nearby residence and detained him without further incident. The victim remained in critical but stable condition.
Charges: Attempted Murder, Aggravated Battery with a Weapon, Possession of a Controlled Substance

Title: Man charged with attempted murder after violent attack at Hollywood intersection
description: Enrique Santana, 35, was arrested after police said he attacked a man at an intersection in Hollywood, Florida. Investigators said Santana and the victim were involved in a verbal argument at the crosswalk near Johnson Street and North State Road 7 before the situation became violent. Police alleged Santana exited his vehicle, struck the victim with a metal object, then ran him over with his car before leaving the scene. The victim was hospitalized in critical condition. Santana was arrested several hours later near Van Buren Street and faces attempted murder and aggravated battery charges.
Charges: First-Degree Attempted Murder, Aggravated Battery with a Deadly Weapon

Title: Pair arrested in violent Miami Gardens carjacking that left elderly man hospitalized, police say
description: Two men, Ktwon Bailey and Christian Sarmiento, were arrested after an alleged violent carjacking at a Marathon gas station in Miami Gardens. Police said the suspects approached an elderly man, demanded money, assaulted him, and stole his GMC pickup truck. The victim suffered severe injuries, including head and neck trauma, and was hospitalized. Authorities later located the stolen vehicle and detained the suspects. Surveillance footage and the victim’s identification helped investigators connect both men to the crime. The suspects face multiple serious charges, including attempted felony murder causing injury, robbery carjacking, false imprisonment, and aggravated battery.
Charges: Attempted felony murder causing injury, false imprisonment, robbery carjacking, aggravated battery on a person 65 or older

Title: Man accused of attempted murder after shooting into ex-girlfriend's car in Osceola County
description: Josue Emmanuel Figueroa Jr., 27, was arrested after deputies said he shot into his ex-girlfriend’s vehicle, assaulted her, and fled from law enforcement in Osceola County. Authorities said the incident began after an argument and physical attack, followed by continued harassment. The suspect allegedly fired multiple rounds into the victim’s car while her 4-year-old daughter was inside, stole her cellphone, and fled. Deputies later located Figueroa at his residence, where he escaped on a motorcycle before abandoning it and hiding in a wooded area. His mother helped convince him to surrender, and he was taken into custody.
Charges: Attempted murder, aggravated battery, aggravated stalking, discharging a firearm in public, armed burglary, child neglect, grand theft, criminal mischief, robbery with a weapon
Comments: Don't really know about the case but the chase might be good.

Title: Attempted murder suspect arrested in Lady Lake stabbing
description: William Tyler Warren, 42, was arrested and charged after an alleged stabbing near Veterans Memorial Park in The Villages, Florida. Police said an altercation occurred in a parking lot on Paige Place involving a 37-year-old female acquaintance and resulted in a 39-year-old man suffering life-threatening injuries. The victim was treated at a local hospital before being airlifted for surgery and survived. Investigators said Warren had recently relocated from Georgia to the area. Police located and arrested him following the incident. The investigation remains ongoing, and authorities are continuing to review the circumstances surrounding the stabbing.
Charges: Attempted murder, aggravated battery

Title: Body camera video shows police officer allegedly kidnapped by armed robbery suspect in roadside showdown
description: On February 20, 2026, Antioch Police officers responded to an armed robbery at a FoodMaxx grocery store. During the attempted arrest, suspect Dominick Desouza allegedly rammed a police vehicle and fled in a car while Officer Travis Donaldson became trapped inside. As the vehicle sped through the area, the officer repeatedly ordered the suspect to stop and warned he would shoot if necessary. After the suspect allegedly threatened to crash, the officer fired one shot into Desouza's leg to stop the danger. The suspect later crashed, fled on foot, was arrested, and faced multiple felony charges.
Charges: Kidnapping, robbery, burglary, and assault on a police officer

Title: Man armed with hatchet shot, killed after crashing into house in Fruitland Park, police say
description: On March 25, 2026, Fruitland Park Police responded to a report of a pickup truck that had crashed into a home on East Mirror Lake Drive. Officers found 53-year-old Duane Terrell Holston walking away from the truck while holding a hatchet. Despite repeated commands from two officers to stop and drop the weapon, Holston refused. Police said he then reached for a gun, prompting officers to fire their weapons. Holston was struck and transported to a hospital, where he later died. No officers were injured. The Florida Department of Law Enforcement is investigating the officer-involved shooting.
Charges: No charges filed (suspect died before arrest)

Title: Barricaded man armed with a knife dead after hours-long standoff with Broward deputies, SWAT officers
description: On May 30, 2026, Broward Sheriff's Office deputies responded to an apartment complex in Oakland Park after reports of a man armed with knives threatening residents. The suspect, Kevin Dominick Almonte, barricaded himself inside an apartment and allegedly claimed to possess firearms, propane tanks, and bombs, prompting the evacuation of nearby residents. Deputies, SWAT officers, K-9, and the Violent Crimes Unit attempted for several hours to negotiate a peaceful surrender. According to BSO, Almonte later advanced toward deputies while armed with knives. A deputy then fired, striking him. Almonte was transported to a hospital, where he was pronounced dead.
Charges: No charges filed (suspect died before arrest)

Title: Tice man facing battery, drug charges wanted for violating release terms
description: Adriel Martinez was wanted in Lee County, Florida, for allegedly violating release conditions related to battery, obstruction, drug charges, and witness or victim tampering. According to authorities, Martinez went to a home in Lehigh Acres and became involved in a verbal argument with a woman. The argument allegedly escalated when he threw an object at her face while children were nearby. He allegedly took her phone when she attempted to call 911 and damaged property while leaving. Deputies later located him, where he allegedly resisted arrest and was found with marijuana and amphetamines.
Charges: Two counts of battery, obstruction, drug charges, tampering with a witness or victim, violation of release terms
Comments: Lacking police intervention during the incident.

Title: Teacher assistant arrested on campus for child abuse and battery in Lake County
description: A teacher assistant at Lake Hills Elementary School in Lake County, Florida, was arrested after school surveillance footage and employee reports indicated he abused a non-verbal student. According to the Lake County Sheriff’s Office, the 60-year-old suspect, Mark McArthy, was observed on video bending the student's arm in an unreasonable manner and pushing the child against a wall five separate times. Additionally, witnesses reported that McArthy placed his hand over the child’s mouth. The incident occurred at a school serving students with special needs. McArthy is facing charges including child abuse and battery, with an arraignment scheduled for June 1.
Charges: Battery, child abuse, and resisting an officer without violence

Title: Repeat offender assaulted woman jogging in Volusia County, deputies say
description: A repeat offender was arrested after allegedly assaulting a woman in broad daylight. According to law enforcement officials, the thirty-two-year-old suspect, Cameron David Lyons, ran up to a woman while she was out jogging. Lyons forcefully touched her chest before fleeing the area on foot. The victim stated to responding deputies that she immediately recognized Lyons from a previous assault that occurred last May. Authorities located the suspect shortly after the incident took place. Lyons was taken into custody and booked into the Volusia County Jail, where he is being held on multiple criminal offenses.
Charges: Stalking and battery

Title: 11 arrested after police raid ‘nuisance property’ in St. Cloud
description: On May 7, 2026, police executed a search warrant at a suspected nuisance property on W. New Nolte Road in St. Cloud, Florida. St. Cloud and Kissimmee police reported that 11 people were arrested after the raid. Authorities said the property had received more than 40 police calls in 2025. Officers seized more than 60 pieces of evidence, including approximately 28 grams of methamphetamine and drug paraphernalia. Items tested positive for methamphetamine and fentanyl. Those arrested faced charges including possession, dealing in stolen property, resisting arrest without violence, and providing false identification.
Charges: Possession, dealing in stolen property, resisting arrest without violence, providing false identification to law enforcement

Title: Man with pitch fork, hatchet arrested after attempted nighttime break-ins: Deputies
description: On January 28, 2026, Charles Reed Knight III was arrested after deputies responded to reports of attempted nighttime break-ins and property damage in Merritt Island, Florida. Authorities said Knight was seen walking through a neighborhood, attempting to enter homes, damaging security cameras with a pitchfork and hatchet, and damaging property. A deputy found Knight and attempted to detain him after he refused commands and allegedly pulled away and threw punches. The deputy used a Taser, and Knight was taken into custody after continuing to resist. No injuries were reported during the incident.
Charges: Assault on a law enforcement officer, resisting arrest with violence, trespassing, battery, burglary

Title: Affidavit: Man charged with assaulting officers at Bay Pines VA hospital
description: William George was arrested at the Bay Pines VA Hospital in Pinellas County after officers responded to reports of him yelling at medical staff and police. Authorities said George became aggressive and stated he would leave “one way or another.” According to the arrest affidavit, he wrapped his hands in medical gauze while holding a pen and toothbrush in a threatening manner. An officer used a bear hug maneuver to bring him to the ground. George was taken into custody and charged after the confrontation with multiple law enforcement officers at the hospital.
Charges: Battery on a law enforcement officer, aggravated assault on a law enforcement officer, resisting an officer
police department: Bay Pines Veterans Affairs Police Department

Title: FCSO Arrests Palm Coast Man Who Sexually Assaulted Teen and Tried to Flee the State
description: Micah McGuire, 21, was arrested by the Flagler County Sheriff’s Office after an investigation into allegations that he sexually assaulted a teenager. Detectives identified McGuire as the suspect after a juvenile victim reported the offense. Authorities said McGuire recorded part of the encounter on the victim’s cellphone. During the investigation, detectives learned McGuire planned to leave Florida for Colorado. When detectives contacted him with a search warrant, McGuire allegedly became uncooperative, attempted to close the door, and resisted officers. He was taken into custody and transported to the Flagler County detention facility.
Charges: Lewd or lascivious battery; promoting sexual performance by a child; resisting an officer without violence

Title: Man charged after fleeing police and attacking K-9 in Boynton Beach
description: Jaquez McMillian was arrested after police said he fled from officers and attacked a police K-9 in Boynton Beach. According to the Boynton Beach Police Department, officers responded after McMillian allegedly fled from Gulfstream police and entered a restricted utility property with posted no-trespassing signs. A police drone located him hiding under a trailer. When officers and a K-9 approached, McMillian reportedly ran, leading to a chase. Police said he pushed the K-9 down and pinned it by the neck before continuing to flee. Officers later surrounded him in a wooded area and arrested him.
Charges: Touching or striking a police K-9; resisting an officer without violence; burglary of an occupied structure without a weapon

Title: WPB officer placed on leave after alleged DUI crash, ER altercation with deputies
description: Timothy Joseph Walsh, a West Palm Beach police officer, was arrested after a suspected DUI crash and an alleged altercation with Palm Beach County Sheriff’s deputies inside a hospital emergency room. Deputies said Walsh was involved in a multi-vehicle crash and showed signs of impairment, including slurred speech and a strong odor of alcohol. While hospitalized, Walsh allegedly became confrontational, shoved a deputy, resisted being handcuffed, and made threats. Multiple deputies and hospital staff were needed to restrain him. Walsh was placed on administrative leave by the West Palm Beach Police Department pending further investigation.
Charges: Felony battery on a law enforcement officer; felony resisting an officer with violence; misdemeanor driving under the influence causing property damage; misdemeanor assault on specified personnel

Title: Man Arrested for Armed Sexual Battery, Kidnapping and Attempted Murder; Other Victims Possible
description: Brett Pincomb, 31, was arrested by the Jacksonville Sheriff's Office Special Assault Unit after an investigation into multiple violent attacks against women. According to JSO, the investigation began after a woman was attacked inside an elevator at a Point Meadows apartment complex on May 15, 2026. While officers were investigating, Pincomb allegedly attacked another woman with a knife. Detectives later determined that Pincomb armed himself and sexually battered multiple women over several months, with the violence escalating over time. He was arrested on charges involving armed sexual battery, kidnapping, and attempted murder.
Charges: Armed sexual battery; kidnapping; attempted murder
Comments: Lacking police intervention during the incident.

Title: North Miami Beach woman charged in hit-and-run that left pedestrian seriously injured
description: Shannon Mackey, 32, was arrested after police said she struck a pedestrian with her vehicle and fled the scene in North Miami Beach. The crash occurred near Northeast 167th Street and Northeast Eighth Avenue. The pedestrian suffered serious injuries, including a head laceration, and was taken to Aventura Hospital for treatment. A witness provided information about the vehicle and license plate, helping investigators locate a damaged white Kia at a residence. Police identified Mackey as the driver, and she was taken into custody after speaking with officers following Miranda warnings.
Charges: Leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury; knowingly driving with a suspended license; misrepresenting proof of insurance

Title: Woman arrested in West Park hit-and-run that killed pedestrian, BSO says
description: Karen Essick, 66, was arrested in connection with a fatal hit-and-run crash in West Park, Florida. Authorities said a pedestrian, Mishell Laurine Warner, was struck near Barry Road and West Hallandale Beach Boulevard and later died at a hospital. Investigators said surveillance video showed Warner being hit by Essick’s maroon Toyota Corolla. Officials allege Essick briefly stopped, got out of the vehicle, made a U-turn, returned to the area, and then fled. Detectives later located the damaged vehicle at a repair shop. Essick admitted involvement in a crash with a pedestrian and was arrested.
Charges: Tampering with physical evidence; failure to remain on scene in an accident involving death
Comments: Again lacking police intervention during the incident.

Title: North Port woman charged with hitting pedestrian, leaving the scene
description: Kathy Dove, 59, of North Port, Florida, was arrested after police said she struck a pedestrian and left the scene of the crash. The incident happened on Price Boulevard near Purdue Street when a man was hit while crossing the road. The victim suffered life-threatening injuries and was transported to Sarasota Memorial Hospital. Investigators found vehicle debris and traced surveillance footage to Dove’s yellow Hummer. Police found the SUV with damage and a missing side-view mirror. Dove reportedly admitted she was driving and said she thought she hit a traffic cone, but she did not stop or contact police.
Charges: Leaving the scene of a crash with great bodily injury or death
Comments: Good story but police aren't in action at all.

Title: Clearwater woman arrested in deadly hit-and-run on Gulf-to-Bay Boulevard: Police
description: On February 4, 2026, 51-year-old Dawn Dunkle was driving a red 2024 Ford Mustang westbound on Gulf-to-Bay Boulevard. Around 9:30 p.m., her vehicle struck 60-year-old pedestrian Elbert Gilbert while he was walking inside a designated crosswalk. Dunkle did not stop, administer aid, or contact emergency services, leaving car parts at the scene. Gilbert was transported to Largo Medical Center as a trauma alert but succumbed to his injuries. Police located the damaged Mustang days later. Dunkle allegedly told others she believed she hit a speed bump or a box before she was subsequently arrested.
Charges: Leaving the scene of a crash involving death and possession of a controlled substance
Comments: Again lacking police intervention during the incident.

Title: Woman accused of murdering husband in Orange Park
description: Jasmine Brown, 33, was arrested after authorities accused her of killing her husband, Kerbisson Sion, at his Orange Park residence. Investigators said Brown went to Sion’s home on Gano Court in the early morning hours and the two became involved in an altercation. Sion was found shot and killed near his home at approximately 5:15 a.m. Brown was later located at an apartment complex in Jacksonville with assistance from the Jacksonville Sheriff's Office. She agreed to return to Clay County and was arrested on a second-degree murder charge. The investigation was handled by local law enforcement agencies.
Charges: Second-degree murder

Title: Woman, 47, uses pickleball paddle as ‘deadly weapon’ to attack another player during argument, deputies say
description: A 47-year-old St. Augustine woman was arrested after deputies accused her of attacking another pickleball player with a paddle during an argument at Treaty Park. Authorities said the dispute began during a pickleball game and continued after the match when the woman became involved in a disagreement between her son and the victim. Deputies alleged she struck the man in the head several times with the paddle, causing facial cuts and heavy bleeding. The woman claimed she was defending her son, but investigators said witnesses did not observe an immediate threat. She also allegedly provided false identification to deputies.
Charges: Aggravated battery with a deadly weapon; giving a false ID to law enforcement
Comments: Could be good depending on the interview with the woman.

Title: Man accused of running away from Keystone Heights traffic stop caught after heavy police response
description: A man in his late 30s was arrested after allegedly fleeing from a traffic stop in Keystone Heights, Florida. The Clay County Sheriff’s Office launched a search near Paradise Drive and Southwest Pecan Street, leading to a heavy police presence and a temporary secure status at Keystone Heights Junior/Senior High School. Deputies described the suspect as having a beard and tattoos and possibly wearing a gray shirt. The circumstances of the traffic stop and specific criminal allegations were not released. Authorities later confirmed the man was located and taken into custody.
Charges: Fleeing and eluding law enforcement

Title: Hampton City Council member arrested for allegedly threatening to kill neighbor
description: Douglas Williamson, a 67-year-old Hampton City Council vice chair, was arrested after allegedly threatening to kill his neighbor in Bradford County, Florida. According to the arrest report, Williamson confronted neighbor Marcus Bradley and allegedly pointed a revolver-style pistol at him during a dispute. Authorities said Williamson accused Bradley of breaking into his trailer and made multiple statements threatening to kill him. Deputies later interviewed Williamson, who allegedly repeated a threat involving using a firearm. Williamson was taken into custody and charged with aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill

Title: Somebody's worst nightmare': Man charged for Springfield house fire that killed one
description: Julius Lindo, 49, was arrested after investigators accused him of intentionally setting a house fire in Jacksonville’s Springfield neighborhood that killed one person. The Jacksonville Sheriff’s Office said the fire occurred at a home on Ionia Street and resulted in the death of 62-year-old Willie Haywood Jr. Authorities charged Lindo with murder, arson, and eight counts of attempted murder. Neighbors reported hearing a loud explosion and seeing the home engulfed in flames. Most residents escaped, but Haywood, who used a wheelchair, died in the fire. Lindo remains in Duval County Jail.
Charges: Murder, arson, eight counts of attempted murder
Comments: Lackin police intervention/in action during the incident.

Title: Tampa Police investigating use-of-force after Ybor City arrest goes viral
description: Jeffrey Brownfield, 22, was arrested in Tampa after a confrontation with police officers in Ybor City. A viral video showed Brownfield, who was shirtless, involved in a verbal altercation with several Tampa Police Department officers. Police said Brownfield caused a disturbance at a nightclub, refused to leave after being removed, took a fighting stance, and verbally threatened officers. During the arrest, an officer used force to take him to the ground. The incident is under review by Tampa Police, including body camera footage. Brownfield was charged with disorderly conduct after the encounter.
Charges: Disorderly conduct

Title: ‘He’s biting my leg off’: Lake Placid man arrested after K-9 mauls his leg, deputies say
description: Nathan Mark Theo Johnson, 23, was arrested after deputies responded to a domestic violence call in Lake Placid, Florida. According to authorities, Johnson climbed out of a bathroom window after seeing law enforcement and attempted to flee on foot. Highlands County Sheriff’s Office K-9 units located him, and K-9 Gentry chased and restrained him by biting his leg until deputies arrived. Johnson was handcuffed and transported to a hospital for treatment. Authorities stated he will face multiple charges after his release, including aggravated assault, false imprisonment, battery, and resisting arrest.
Charges: Aggravated assault, false imprisonment, battery, resisting arrest

Title: K-9 TITAN TAKES FIRST BITE OUT OF CRIME, APPREHENDING DOMESTIC BATTERY SUSPECT
description: Deputies responded to a Palm Coast home after a domestic disturbance call involving Ilia Javoronkov. The victim reported that Javoronkov assaulted them, threw them, caused injuries, strangled them, and threatened to kill them while attempting to access a gun safe. Javoronkov barricaded himself inside the residence and refused to surrender. Deputies attempted negotiations for about 2.5 hours before Flagler County Sheriff’s Office K-9 Titan apprehended him. Javoronkov was taken into custody, medically cleared, and transported to jail. He faces multiple charges related to domestic violence, obstruction, and false imprisonment following the incident.
Charges: Domestic violence battery by strangulation, obstruction without violence, false imprisonment
Comments: The first case of domestic violence looks good. Avoid the DUI one.

Title: Florida man accused of stabbing, killing his wife's boyfriend, deputies say
description: Austin Noel, 32, was arrested after deputies said he fatally stabbed Jacob Barrho, 34, during a domestic dispute at a home on Gary Road in Daytona Beach. Investigators said Noel confronted Barrho after relationship tensions involving Noel’s wife and Barrho. According to deputies, Noel allegedly took a kitchen knife and stabbed Barrho in the chest. Barrho was transported to a hospital but later died from his injuries. Noel was taken into custody and charged with first-degree premeditated murder. A judge ordered Noel held without bond following his first court appearance.
Charges: First-degree premeditated murder
Comments: Good story just lacking police intervention.

Title: Costco employee shot, killed after confronting shopper with gun, authorities say
description: On April 25, 2026, police responded to a Costco store in Strongsville, Ohio, after a shooting involving a shopper and an employee. Authorities said 22-year-old Christian M. Bryant entered the store area carrying a firearm with a drum magazine. Employee Randy Corrigan confronted Bryant and told him he could not enter with the weapon. Police said Bryant allegedly pulled out a handgun and shot Corrigan multiple times. The 61-year-old employee was transported to a hospital but later died. Bryant was arrested and charged with murder. He is being held on a $5 million bond.
Charges: Murder

Title: Suspect claims he was cleaning gun in shooting death of 15-year-old girl, police say
description: An 18-year-old man, Jakob Heintzelman, was arrested after 15-year-old Symini Moore was fatally shot inside an apartment in Northwood, Ohio. Police said Moore was found with a gunshot wound on January 23, 2026, and later confirmed deceased at the scene. Heintzelman allegedly told investigators that he was cleaning his firearm when it discharged accidentally, striking Moore. Four people were inside the apartment during the incident. The Lake Township Police Department investigated the case and charged Heintzelman with reckless homicide. The shooting was not an officer-involved incident, and the suspect was taken into custody after the death.
Charges: Reckless homicide

Title: Suspect arrested in Chicago weeks after high-speed crash that injured Florida officer
description: Artiom Echiusciu was accused of crashing a BMW into a Hollywood Police patrol car at a speed exceeding 100 mph near Hollywood Boulevard and North Ocean Drive. The crash seriously injured a police officer, who was hospitalized and later recovered. After the collision, Echiusciu allegedly fled on foot and left the damaged vehicle behind. Investigators identified him and tracked him to Chicago with assistance from federal authorities. He was arrested by the U.S. Marshals Service Great Lakes Regional Fugitive Task Force and is expected to face charges in Broward County after extradition proceedings.
Charges: Leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury; reckless driving causing serious bodily injury; reckless driving causing property damage; driving with a suspended license; leaving the scene of a crash involving property damage; failure to register a motor vehicle

He was evaluated at a hospital and later booked into the Santa Rosa County Jail.

Detectives alleged that he sent sexually explicit images to the minor and provided money, drugs, or alcohol in exchange for sexual activity. When deputies attempted to arrest him at his Silver Springs home, he fought with them and resisted. Deputies deployed a Taser, but it was ineffective. description: Andrew Mark Williams barricaded himself inside a residence after locking his elderly relatives out of the home. Flagler County Sheriff's deputies entered the residence with the homeowner's permission. Williams armed himself with a knife, became aggressive, and physically resisted deputies attempting to detain him. During the struggle, he cut a deputy's hand with the knife. Deputies deployed a Taser multiple times before Williams complied and was handcuffed. He refused medical treatment but was transported to AdventHealth Palm Coast before being booked into the Flagler County jail. The injured deputy received treatment for a hand injury and was not seriously hurt.

description: A man in Miramar, Florida, allegedly resisted a civil vehicle seizure when deputies arrived to take possession of a 2019 Chevrolet Corvette due to an unpaid court judgment. During the incident, the suspect entered the Corvette and attempted to drive away while a deputy was standing beside the vehicle. The deputy was dragged as the Corvette moved down the street and suffered minor injuries. Deputies later detained the man with assistance from his son. The suspect was transported for medical evaluation and later charged after refusing to provide a statement.
Charges: Aggravated battery on a law enforcement officer Resisting arrest with violence

Title: Leesburg police arrest suspect in Eustis park stabbing, second violent attack
description: James Edward Thompson, 32, was arrested after police said he attacked two victims in separate violent incidents in Lake County, Florida. The first incident occurred at Ferran Park in Eustis, where Thompson allegedly stabbed Brandon Slaton nine times, causing severe injuries and blood loss. Hours later, police said Thompson attacked Randy Banks in Leesburg, striking him in the head with a table leg containing a protruding screw. Officers later located Thompson, arrested him, and used a taser when he resisted inside the police department. He was transported to jail after medical clearance.

description: A Stuart, Florida resident and roofer was arrested after FDLE agents and ICE-related authorities conducted a traffic stop during an early-morning enforcement operation. Agents alleged the man made a rolling stop and attempted to detain him after the stop. The man, who had a Florida driver’s license and said he had lived in the United States for 18 years with a work permit and pending asylum case, refused to exit his van. Officers broke the van window, pulled him through broken glass, and restrained him. He was later charged with resisting arrest with violence and sentenced to jail.

Title: Queens woman accused of kicking deputy after being kicked off flight at MIA
description: Jamie Romanski, a 49-year-old woman from Astoria, Queens, New York, was arrested after an incident aboard an American Airlines flight at Miami International Airport. Authorities said she had a verbal argument with flight crew and appeared intoxicated. Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office deputies escorted her off the aircraft after attempting to calm the situation. During the escort on the jet bridge, officials said Romanski kicked a deputy’s thigh multiple times, causing pain. She was taken to the airport sheriff’s station and later booked into custody. She faces felony charges related to assaultive behavior toward law enforcement.

Deputies investigated reports of shots fired near County Road 55 and County Road 10 and later found a group of people at a residence where another gunshot was heard. Deputies stated Pride argued with officers about firearm use on private property and refused to provide identification. When deputies attempted to arrest him for disorderly conduct, he allegedly refused commands and resisted. Officers took him to the ground during a struggle and later transported him to the Logan County Jail.
Charges: Obstructing official business; resisting arrest

Officers questioned 19-year-old Traveon Grace, who was speaking on his cellphone. Larson was taken into custody and booked into jail. He faces kidnapping and resisting arrest charges following the investigation by Hocking County authorities.

Police responded to a report of aggravated robbery with a deadly weapon, kidnapping, resisting arrest, and obstructing official business. Officers investigated the incident and located the suspect. An officer pursued him on foot and used a stun gun twice before taking him into custody with assistance from a sheriff’s deputy. The suspect was evaluated at a hospital before jail transfer.

Police said officers responded to the area of East Marks Street and Kenilworth Terrace following reports of a stabbing. After the stabbing, Matthie fled the scene but was located shortly afterward at a nearby restaurant, where officers took him into custody. He faces serious criminal charges related to the stabbing and resisting arrest.

Title: Former Indian River County administrator faces hit-and-run, resisting arrest charges
description: Joseph A. Baird, former Indian River County budget director and county administrator, was accused of leaving the scene after crashing his SUV into a parked pickup truck in Vero Beach. Police said the March 31 crash caused significant damage, and witnesses reported Baird left the area on foot after saying he could not go to jail. Surveillance footage allegedly showed him appearing unsteady before driving and later returning to the area. He was arrested at his residence on April 17 after deputies served a warrant. description: On July 23, 2026, Jacksonville Sheriff's Office officers responded to a reported stabbing outside the Leyu Food Store on Kings Road in Jacksonville. Officers found 41-year-old Yolanda Haynes suffering from severe stab wounds. She was transported to a local hospital, where she later died. Investigators quickly identified Brittany McLean as the suspect and initially arrested her on charges of aggravated battery and tampering with evidence. After reviewing witness statements, McLean’s statement, and physical evidence, homicide detectives established probable cause and upgraded the case to murder.
