Miami Gardens Police responded to a report of a stabbing and found the victim with a severe puncture wound to his abdomen. The victim said Willard assaulted him earlier, punched him, and later stabbed him with a kitchen knife. Willard allegedly claimed the victim stabbed himself, but investigators arrested her based on evidence and statements. The victim was taken to Aventura Hospital for surgery. Willard was already on bond for a previous Broward stabbing case.
Charges: Attempted Second-Degree Murder Aggravated Battery with a Weapon Causing Great Bodily Harm

Title: Marcellus Wiley Arrested in Florida on Domestic Battery Charge
description: Former NFL defensive end and sports media personality Marcellus Wiley, 51, was arrested in Florida over the Fourth of July weekend on a domestic battery charge. According to court records, Wiley was booked into the Orange County Jail on July 4 after being arrested by the Orange County Sheriff’s Office. A misdemeanor battery case was filed in Orange County, Florida, with a complaint submitted on July 5. Authorities have not released details about the alleged victim or circumstances of the incident. The case remains open, and Wiley has not publicly commented on the arrest.
Charges: Misdemeanor Battery (Domestic Battery)
Comments: No celebrities. Could result in a lawsuit.

Title: Deputies arrest Lehigh Acres woman after gun incident over missing cellphone
description: Rosa Salvador was arrested in Lehigh Acres, Florida, after deputies alleged she pointed a shotgun at a man during a dispute over a missing cellphone. According to the Lee County Sheriff’s Office arrest report, Salvador and the victim had been drinking together when she became aggressive after failing to locate her phone. Police said the victim was forced to leave his home and search for the device. After reviewing video evidence, deputies surrounded Salvador’s residence and ordered her to surrender. She was found inside a bedroom and taken for medical treatment. A shotgun matching the reported weapon was recovered.
Charges: Aggravated assault on a person 65 or older, false imprisonment

Title: Tampa woman arrested after chasing man with knife during domestic disturbance
description: Andrea Patino, 25, was arrested in Tampa, Florida, after Hillsborough County deputies alleged she chased a man with a knife during a domestic disturbance. Deputies responded to a residence on Abonado Road early June 29, 2026. According to authorities, the man had taken Patino’s car keys to stop her from driving while under the influence. Investigators said Patino retrieved a knife and followed the man outside the home. No injuries were reported in the sheriff’s office statement. Patino was taken into custody and charged with aggravated assault with a deadly weapon following the reported incident.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon

Title: Woman arrested after throwing firecracker at deputy's patrol vehicle
description: Latoya Bowles, 38, was arrested in Royal Palm Beach, Florida, after deputies said she threw a lit firecracker at a marked patrol vehicle and threatened to use fireworks against a neighbor. According to the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office, a deputy arrived at Rhythm Circle and saw Bowles standing in the road. She allegedly lit a red firecracker, threw it at the patrol vehicle, and attempted to light another. The deputy reported fearing the firework could be used to cause harm. Bowles was taken into custody without further incident and faces multiple charges, including aggravated assault.
Charges: Aggravated assault, weapon offense charges

Title: Gainesville woman charged with child abuse for threatening girl with axe, officers say
description: Christina Madison, 45, was arrested in Gainesville, Florida, after Alachua County Sheriff’s deputies accused her of threatening a girl with an axe and physically assaulting her. According to the arrest report, Madison allegedly forced her way into the victim’s bedroom by breaking the door handle. The victim told deputies that Madison threatened to kill her with the axe, grabbed her by the throat, and struck her multiple times. Madison denied making the threats and said she was upset about being disrespected. She was booked into jail on felony charges involving aggravated assault with a deadly weapon and child abuse.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon; child abuse

Title: Tampa Police Arrest Violent Assault Suspect
description: Moises Estee Buitrago, 25, was arrested by Tampa Police after an investigation into allegations of prolonged domestic violence against a woman with whom he was in a relationship. Police said the abuse began in October 2025 and involved physical and sexual violence, restraint, threats, and controlling behavior. Investigators alleged Buitrago destroyed the victim’s phone and identification, restricted her movements, withheld medical care, and distributed private images without consent. The situation escalated on March 24, 2026, when he allegedly threatened the victim and forced entry into a room where she was hiding. He was later arrested without incident in Seffner.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon; battery; false imprisonment; two counts of digital voyeurism

Title: Woman arrested for aggravated assault with deadly weapon in Lake City, police say
description: Princess Brown, 28, was arrested in Lake City, Florida, after police said she threatened several people with a knife during a disturbance. According to the Lake City Police Department, officers responded to the 700 block of NE Center Avenue after receiving reports of an armed person. Investigators said a verbal altercation occurred, and Brown allegedly armed herself with a large knife and threatened multiple individuals outside the residence. Police reported that no injuries occurred. Brown was taken into custody without incident and transported to the Columbia County Detention Facility, where she was charged with aggravated assault with a deadly weapon.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon
Comments: Lack of action and police intervention.

Title: Pregnant woman feared for safety as man pulled gun in road rage incident: PSLPD
description: Robert Kniceley was arrested after police said he pointed a loaded handgun at a pregnant woman during a road rage incident in Port St. Lucie, Florida. The incident occurred after the victim reported aggressive driving by a pickup truck. Police said Kniceley pulled alongside her vehicle and allegedly pointed a firearm at her. The victim provided video evidence and license plate information, allowing officers to identify him. Investigators recovered a loaded Smith & Wesson handgun from his home. Kniceley admitted being involved and was taken into custody. No injuries were reported during the incident.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon
Comments: Good story, but lacking police intervention.

Title: Former LSU star Demetrius Byrd made threats while armed with tool in Miami Beach, report says
description: Demetrius Byrd was arrested in Miami Beach after police said he threatened a passenger while armed with a multi-tool during a bus incident. Officers responded after reports of a man yelling threats and carrying what appeared to be a knife. According to the arrest report, Byrd became involved in an argument with another passenger, pulled out the tool, opened it to resemble a blade, approached the victim, and asked if he wanted to die. Police located Byrd near the bus stop, detained him, and found the multi-tool during a search. The incident was captured on transit surveillance.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon

Title: Man accused of sexually assaulting woman at knifepoint in Merritt Island had 30 priors before latest attack
description: Kelvin Johnson was arrested after authorities accused him of forcing his way into a Merritt Island apartment and sexually assaulting a woman at knifepoint. According to investigators, the victim was moving out when Johnson allegedly confronted her near her apartment, threatened her with a knife, and assaulted her inside. The victim escaped and received help from a neighbor before contacting police. Witness descriptions helped deputies identify Johnson. Officials stated he had a lengthy criminal history, including prior arrests and convictions. A judge denied bond, citing his alleged violent history and threat to the community.
Charges: Sexual battery, home invasion robbery, aggravated assault, violation of probation
Comments: Lacking story and police in action.

Title: Former pro Uruguayan tennis player arrested in Doral after damaging rackets at store, police say
description: Nicolas Xiviller Pardodeir, a former professional Uruguayan tennis player, was arrested in Doral after police said he caused a disturbance at a tennis store. Authorities reported that he damaged two tennis rackets valued at $568 and threatened store employees with the rackets. Surveillance footage allegedly showed him arguing inside the store, damaging property, and later hitting the front glass door. Police located him at a nearby gas station and arrested him. Pardodeir was charged with aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, criminal mischief, and disorderly conduct following the incident.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, criminal mischief, disorderly conduct

Title: Report: 84-year-old Milton woman fired gunshot as warning to neighbor cutting grass
description: Charlene Davis, an 84-year-old Milton woman, was arrested after allegedly firing a warning shot during a dispute with her neighbor. According to deputies, the neighbor was mowing grass when he heard a gunshot and saw Davis holding a revolver. Davis reportedly admitted to firing her Smith and Wesson .38 Special revolver into the ground because of ongoing noise complaints and wanting to scare the neighbors. The incident was recorded by a Ring doorbell camera, showing Davis leaving her home and firing one shot. She was charged and later released from Santa Rosa County Jail after posting bond.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, discharging a firearm on residential property

Title: Woman arrested after firing gun near family in road rage incident in Palm Springs
description: Jessica Piltz, 38, was arrested after police said she fired a gun during a road rage incident involving a family in Palm Springs, Florida. According to investigators, the confrontation began after a family leaving a restaurant stopped vehicles in a parking lot. Police said Piltz argued with the group, later stopped her vehicle on a roadway, retrieved a firearm, and fired a shot toward the family, which included a child. Witnesses identified Piltz and reported seeing her fire the weapon before leaving the area. She was later arrested and held on bond at the Palm Beach County Main Detention Center.
Charges: Four counts of aggravated assault, discharging a firearm from a vehicle
Comments: Lacks story and police in action.

Title: Florida woman allegedly swerves toward children, calls it ‘target practice’
description: Pamela Dresser was arrested after allegedly swerving her vehicle toward a group of children playing in the street in Cocoa, Florida. Police said witnesses reported that Dresser drove toward four children, causing them to run away for safety. Authorities said Dresser allegedly made a comment referring to the act as “target practice” and later claimed it was a joke. A witness reported that Dresser used a racial slur and allegedly admitted attempting to run the children over. She faces multiple charges related to aggravated assault, child abuse, and threats against a public servant.
Charges: Aggravated assault while evidencing prejudice, child abuse without great bodily harm, corruption by threat against a public servant

Title: Homestead mother accused of assaulting daughter during argument
description: Martha Juliana Mendoza, 43, was arrested after police accused her of assaulting her daughter during a domestic argument in Homestead, Florida. Officers responded to a domestic battery report and learned the victim claimed her mother grabbed her hair, pulled her inside the home, hit her head against a wall, and restricted her breathing. Mendoza admitted pulling her daughter’s hair and holding her on the floor but denied some allegations. Police observed redness on the victim’s face and found evidence of a struggle. Child welfare authorities were notified following the incident.
Charges: Domestic battery, battery by strangulation, aggravated assault with intent to commit a felony, child abuse without great bodily harm

Title: Man armed with baseball bat, gun arrested in Gainesville for threatening woman, deputies say
description: James Nickell, 35, was arrested after deputies said he threatened a woman and her dog while armed with a baseball bat and a handgun in Gainesville, Florida. According to authorities, Nickell went to a home on Northeast Waldo Road and demanded money while holding the bat. He allegedly indicated he had a pistol in his waistband and threatened to shoot the homeowner and the dog if his demands were not met. A witness intervened and forced Nickell to leave the property. Deputies later located him on Northeast 78th Lane and arrested him after questioning.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon

Title: Volusia County woman says same man attacked her twice on morning jog, one year apart
description: Cameron  Lyons was arrested after deputies accused him of assaulting the same woman during a morning jog in DeBary, Florida, one year after a previous attack involving the same victim. The woman reported that Lyons approached her and grabbed her breast while she was jogging. Investigators identified Lyons as the suspect, and records showed he had previously been convicted in connection with an earlier assault on the woman. Lyons was taken into custody and faces charges including battery, stalking, and possession or display of a forged ID. Authorities noted his prior criminal history involving assault-related offenses.
Charges: Battery, stalking, possession or display of a forged ID

Title: South Florida mom forced child to eat from trash, beat her with frying pan, arrest report says
description: Naseline Timouche, a 27-year-old Miami-Dade woman, was arrested after authorities accused her of repeatedly abusing her 8-year-old daughter. Deputies conducting a welfare check reported finding the child with numerous scars and marks consistent with alleged long-term abuse. The child told investigators she was frequently left alone, denied regular meals, and forced to eat expired food or food from the trash. She also alleged being struck with a cord, frying pan, spatula, and charging cable. A neighbor reportedly provided the child with food and clothing after noticing signs of neglect. Timouche was taken into custody following the investigation.
Charges: Aggravated child abuse causing great bodily harm; child neglect without causing great bodily harm

Title: Hialeah Walmart road rage attack left victim with skull fracture and brain bleed, police say
description: Christian Salgado was arrested after an alleged road rage confrontation in a Walmart parking lot in Hialeah, Florida. According to police, the dispute began between two drivers. Investigators said Salgado left but returned and blocked the victim's vehicle while the victim's pregnant girlfriend and child were inside. Police allege Salgado punched the victim and slammed him onto the pavement, causing a skull fracture and brain bleed that required emergency surgery. The victim may also need corrective spine surgery and could permanently lose the ability to walk. Salgado claimed he acted in self-defense but was later arrested and charged by investigators.
Charges: Aggravated battery causing great bodily harm

Title: Florida man arrested after crashing Kia Soul into officer's patrol vehicle, police say
description: Garrett Burr, a 28-year-old Fort Myers man, was arrested after allegedly intentionally crashing his 2025 Kia Soul into a marked Clearwater Police Department Ford F-150 at an intersection in Clearwater, Florida. Police said the officer was stopped at a red light when Burr accelerated and struck the patrol vehicle. The officer suffered minor injuries, was transported to Morton Plant Hospital, treated, and released. Investigators stated Burr admitted he intentionally hit the police vehicle but did not provide a motive. He was booked into the Pinellas County Jail, and authorities said the incident remains under investigation.
Charges: Aggravated battery with a deadly weapon

Title: Man wanted on sexual battery, extortion warrant accused of attacking officers
description: Jacoby Shaddix Harper-Silva, an 18-year-old Boca Raton man, was arrested after allegedly escaping police custody at a hospital in Boynton Beach and fighting with officers. Police said Harper-Silva was initially taken into custody on a warrant related to allegations of sexual battery on a minor with a firearm and extortion. While receiving medical treatment at Bethesda Hospital, police said he ran through an emergency exit after freeing one hand from his handcuffs. Officers alleged he struck one officer, resisted attempts to restrain him, and attempted to escape again before being recaptured. He was charged with escape and battery on officers.
Charges: Escape; Two counts of battery on a law enforcement officer; Three counts of resisting arrest without violence; Remaining in custody on warrant for sexual battery and extortion

Title: Florida man arrested after threatening officers, victim with kitchen knife: police
description: Nicholas Efrain Rosario, 24, was arrested after police said he threatened a person and officers with a kitchen knife in Kissimmee, Florida. Officers responded to a residence after receiving a 911 call that was disconnected. Police said they found Rosario sitting outside the home with a large kitchen knife after he allegedly threatened another person inside the residence. Authorities stated Rosario refused commands to drop the knife and threatened to charge at officers. Body camera footage reportedly showed him advancing toward officers, leading one officer to deploy a TASER. Rosario was taken into custody, and no serious injuries were reported.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon; Resisting arrest without violence

Title: Florida deputies find dog in agony; owner accused of aggravated animal cruelty
description: Michael Crandall, 40, was arrested after deputies said he failed to provide medical care for his dog following a vehicle accident in Alva, Florida. According to the Lee County Sheriff's Office, deputies responding to a domestic violence call found Crandall hiding in a drainage ditch with his dog Loki. The dog was reportedly suffering from severe injuries, including spinal trauma, after being struck by a car days earlier. Investigators said Crandall refused to take the dog to a veterinarian despite its worsening condition. Animal cruelty officials rescued the dog, which received treatment. Crandall was later arrested on multiple charges.
Charges: Aggravated animal cruelty; Battery; Resisting arrest

Title: Ring camera captures Florida man with his hands down his pants, peering into home
description: Christian Haekeker, 37, was arrested after a Ring surveillance camera allegedly captured him looking into a home in Martin County, Florida. According to the Martin County Sheriff’s Office, Haekeker walked back and forth outside the residence for several minutes before approaching a window. Video reportedly showed him peering inside while a woman and child were present and placing his hand down his pants. The homeowner contacted authorities after being alerted to the person outside. Deputies identified Haekeker, who lived in the same community, and later arrested him. He was taken to jail and charged with voyeurism, disorderly conduct, and resisting arrest.
Charges: Voyeurism; Disorderly conduct; Resisting arrest

Title: Miami police find meth in man’s Louis Vuitton bag after 2 car crashes, chase, cops say
description: Matthew Grant, 25, was arrested after Miami police said he committed multiple traffic violations, crashed into two vehicles, and fled from officers in Little Havana. Police said Grant ran a stop sign and red light while driving a Hyundai, struck another vehicle, continued driving the wrong way, and later crashed into a pickup truck. He allegedly ran from the vehicle but surrendered after being chased by officers. Police found a Louis Vuitton bag containing suspected methamphetamine, drug paraphernalia, and bottles with suspected codeine and promethazine. Grant was charged with drug offenses, fleeing, hit-and-run, resisting arrest, and possession of drug paraphernalia.
Charges: Two felony drug charges; felony fleeing and eluding; felony hit-and-run without serious injury; misdemeanor resisting arrest; possession of drug paraphernalia with intent to use

Title: Woman arrested after bringing sword hidden inside cane to Cincinnati City Hall
description: On May 6, 2026, a woman was arrested at Cincinnati City Hall after attempting to bring a sword into a city council meeting. Police said Alexandra Dalton concealed the sword inside a cane and passed through security by claiming the cane was for a disability. During the public comment session, she questioned officers taking her cane. Police attempted to remove her from the chamber and arrested her after a confrontation. Authorities said everyone inside the building was safe, and the meeting was briefly recessed before continuing.
Charges: Resisting arrest, inducing panic, carrying concealed weapons, interrupting a lawful meeting
Comments: Pretty sure this is a repeat case.

Title: Suspicious woman cited for resisting arrest and littering: Medina Police Blotter
description: On February 20, 2026, Medina police responded to a suspicious person call on State Road at 2:01 a.m. Officers encountered an intoxicated woman and cited her for multiple offenses. The woman was accused of resisting arrest, obstruction, littering, and disorderly conduct. The incident involved police contact with the suspect, but no details were provided about injuries, weapons, or further escalation. The case was handled by the Medina Police Department.
Charges: Resisting arrest, obstruction, littering, disorderly conduct

Title: Man charged with murder after attack at St. Pete park: police
description: On July 6, 2026, a man was attacked at a park in St. Petersburg, Florida. Police said D’eauary Thurman, 49, approached the victim, who was lying on a picnic table bench, and allegedly punched, kicked, and stomped him, causing severe head injuries. Authorities said Thurman also went through the victim’s backpack and robbed him before leaving the area. The victim was taken to a hospital in critical condition and later died. Thurman was initially charged with robbery and attempted murder, but the charge was upgraded to first-degree murder.
Charges: First-degree murder, robbery

Title: Suspect charged with murder after fatal Deerfield Beach shooting, BSO says
description: On July 19, 2026, Broward Sheriff’s Office deputies responded to a reported shooting near the 5100 block of East Lakes Drive in Deerfield Beach. Deputies found Ryan McGowan, 25, suffering from gunshot wounds. He was transported to a hospital, where he later died. Investigators said Mauro Lopez, 27, remained at the scene and was detained. Authorities said Lopez and McGowan had an argument earlier in the day and that Lopez later encountered McGowan outside the home and shot him several times. Lopez was arrested and charged.
Charges: Second-degree murder with a firearm, aggravated assault with a firearm

Title: OCSO Charges Baker Man with Agg Assault after Shots Fired at Juvenile
description: On March 23, 2026, Okaloosa County Sheriff’s Office deputies responded to reports of shots fired near Skeeter Lane in Baker, Florida. Investigators said James Knight believed a juvenile near his family’s property was an adult and ordered him to leave. Knight allegedly fired multiple rounds from a 20-gauge shotgun in the juvenile’s direction to scare him away. The juvenile was not injured but reported fear during the incident. Deputies determined Knight’s actions created a reasonable fear of imminent harm and arrested him for aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill

Title: Road-rage shooter arrested in Osteen shooting
description: On April 14, 2026, Taylor Taft was arrested following a road-rage shooting incident on SR 415 in the Osteen area of Volusia County, Florida. Deputies said a driver reported that a white Honda Civic cut him off, swerved in front of him, and the driver pointed a handgun before a shot damaged the victim’s rear tire. Investigators identified Taft through vehicle records and recovered a Glock 48 handgun from his residence. No one was injured during the incident. Taft was charged with multiple firearm-related offenses, including aggravated assault with a deadly weapon and shooting into an occupied vehicle.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill; discharging a firearm from a vehicle; shooting into an occupied vehicle

Title: Barricaded Florida man accused of pointing gun at deputies during hours-long standoff
description: On July 10, 2026, Raymond Michael Rhodes was arrested after a domestic disturbance and hours-long standoff in Gateway, Florida. Deputies responded to a home on Country Day Circle after a child reported a physical disturbance. Authorities said Rhodes battered a woman, armed himself with a firearm, threatened to kill her, and threatened to take his own life. During the response, Rhodes allegedly exited the garage holding a camouflage-patterned shotgun and pointed it at deputies. Officers rescued a trapped 1-year-old child and later took Rhodes into custody. No shots were reported fired between deputies and Rhodes.
Charges: Aggravated assault on a law enforcement officer; aggravated assault; false imprisonment; battery

Title: WATCH: Florida teens arrested after deputies say they pointed BB guns at their helicopter
description: Three Florida teens were arrested after Hillsborough County Sheriff’s Office deputies said they pointed BB guns at a sheriff’s helicopter during a late-night neighborhood incident in Lutz, Florida. Deputies responded after reports of three people carrying what appeared to be firearms. The Aviation Unit located the teens, who allegedly aimed the weapons at the helicopter before entering a home. Deputies issued commands, and all three suspects surrendered without incident. Investigators later determined the weapons were BB guns. The teens were charged with aggravated assault on a law enforcement officer with a deadly weapon.
Charges: Two counts of aggravated assault on a law enforcement officer with a deadly weapon (each suspect)
Comments: Lacking story and police in action.

Title: Man threatens woman with machete in Lehigh Acres over scooter dispute, deputies say
description: Yasmani Diaz De Celis, 43, was arrested in Lehigh Acres after deputies accused him of threatening a woman with a machete during a dispute over a scooter. According to the Lee County Sheriff's Office, De Celis approached the victim, demanded the scooter, and later pulled a machete from his waistband while making threatening gestures. The victim went inside and a 911 call was made. Deputies arrived and saw De Celis return and drop the machete. During a search, deputies found a glass pipe that tested positive for cocaine. He was taken into custody.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill; possession of drug equipment

Title: $2 million bond set for mother accused of killing 2 young daughters, burying bodies in suitcases
description: Aliyah Henderson, a 28-year-old woman, was arrested after authorities discovered the bodies of her two young daughters buried inside suitcases in a field in Cleveland's South Collinwood neighborhood. The victims were identified as 10-year-old Amor Wilson and 8-year-old Mila Chatman. Police began investigating after a man walking his dog found the remains and called 911. Detectives identified Henderson as the suspect and arrested her at her home. Another child found inside the residence was unharmed and placed in protective custody. Henderson was arraigned, and the court set her bond at two million dollars pending further legal proceedings.
Charges: Two counts of aggravated murder

Title: Sylvania man accused of killing ex mother-in-law indicted on slew of charges
description: Jonathan Dunbar Schmidt, 35, was arrested after authorities alleged he killed his former mother-in-law, 68-year-old Marcia VanDruten, at her home in Sylvania, Ohio. Police responded after receiving a report of an intoxicated driver and followed information that led them to VanDruten’s residence, where they found her deceased. The Lucas County Coroner ruled the death a homicide caused by multiple blunt force trauma. Investigators later arrested Schmidt in LaSalle, Michigan. Authorities described the incident as isolated and targeted. Schmidt pleaded not guilty and remained in custody while facing multiple felony charges related to the victim’s death.
Charges: Two counts of aggravated murder Two counts of murder Two counts of felonious assault One count of aggravated burglary

Title: Woman arrested after confessing to stabbing roommate to death in Punta Gorda
description: Shannon Rose Giblin was arrested after investigators said she confessed to stabbing her roommate, Paul De Wayne Bradley, to death following an argument at their Punta Gorda home. Deputies found Bradley deceased and discovered his pickup truck was missing. The vehicle was later located in Sarasota County, where deputies detained Giblin. Investigators said she admitted to the stabbing and leaving the scene in the victim’s truck after covering his body with a tarp.
Charges: Murder  Grand theft of a motor vehicle

Title: Mother accused of stabbing 6-year-old daughter more than 20 times, killing her
description: April Oliva was arrested after deputies found her 6-year-old daughter, Valerie Oliva, stabbed to death inside their home in Milton, Florida. Authorities said Valerie suffered more than 20 stab wounds. Oliva was found lying next to her daughter with self-inflicted cut wounds and was taken for medical treatment. Investigators said a kitchen knife was found inside the home. A relative discovered the scene after Oliva made concerning statements during a phone call.
Charges: Second-degree murder
Comments: Good story, just lacking police in action during the incident.

Title: Woman accused of stabbing 83-year-old stepfather with knife she wished was sharper
description: Jennifer Gill was arrested after authorities said she stabbed her 83-year-old stepfather multiple times at their Ocala-area home. Deputies responded after a 911 call reporting the attack. Investigators said Gill admitted she stabbed him in an attempt to kill him and used a spray bottle with dish soap to blind him before attacking with knives and striking him with a walking cane. The victim suffered traumatic injuries and was taken to a hospital.
Charges: Attempted murder

Title: Authorities: St. Pete mother arrested, charged in death of 4-year-old son
description: Diana Collum was arrested after her 4-year-old son was found dead inside their home in St. Petersburg. Police responded after a 16-year-old daughter reported finding her younger brother and an injured adult. Investigators said the child died after being suffocated with a plastic bag. Collum was found with self-inflicted, non-life-threatening stab wounds and was taken to a hospital before being arrested. Authorities said a note was found at the scene and identified Collum as the suspect.
Charges: First-degree murder

Title: Gainesville woman charged with killing 7-month-old daughter
description: Tierra Scott-Franklin was arrested after Gainesville police said she admitted to drowning her 7-month-old daughter in a bathtub. According to investigators, Scott-Franklin called 911 and reported that she placed the infant in the tub and left the bathroom while expecting the child to die. The baby was later found unresponsive and pronounced dead at a hospital. Authorities said Scott-Franklin was involved in a custody dispute and made statements indicating her motive. She was taken into custody and charged following the investigation.
Charges: First-degree premeditated murder

Title: UPDATE: Suspect Arrested, Victim Identified in Seffner Homicide
description: Natasha Nelson was arrested after authorities accused her of stabbing Aroshan De Silva to death in Seffner, Florida. Deputies responded to a reported altercation on Black Dairy Road and found De Silva suffering from upper body trauma. He was transported to a hospital, where he later died from his injuries. Investigators identified Nelson as the suspect during the homicide investigation. Authorities charged her after detectives determined she was responsible for the fatal stabbing and alleged attempts to tamper with evidence.
Charges: First-degree murder with a weapon (premeditated) Tampering with physical evidence

Title: Vice mayor’s death investigated as domestic violence, husband faces murder charge
description: Coral Springs Vice Mayor Nancy Metayer Bowen was found dead at her home after failing to attend a meeting and respond to calls. Police investigated the death as a domestic violence incident and arrested her husband, Stephen Bowen. Authorities allege he shot her multiple times before attempting to conceal evidence inside the residence. The case led to charges of premeditated murder and tampering with or fabricating physical evidence. Officers stated that family members provided information about statements made by the suspect after the shooting. The investigation remains focused on the circumstances surrounding the killing and collection of additional forensic evidence.
Charges: Premeditated murder; tampering with or fabricating physical evidence

Title: Second body found in the search for 2 missing USF students, officials say
description: Hisham Salah Abugharbieh, a 26-year-old former University of South Florida student, was arrested after the deaths of two USF doctoral students, Zamil Limon and Nahida Bristy. Authorities found human remains during a search near where Limon’s body was discovered. Abugharbieh, who was Limon’s roommate, was taken into custody after a standoff at his family’s home. Investigators said evidence led to additional charges, including two counts of first-degree murder with a weapon. The case remains under investigation as authorities continue examining the circumstances surrounding the deaths and the suspect’s alleged involvement.
Charges: Two counts of first-degree murder with a weapon (premeditated); battery; false imprisonment; tampering with evidence; failure to report a death; unlawfully holding or moving a dead human body

Title: Woman rescues struggling swimmer then learns he’s a double murder suspect
description: Jesse Ellis is accused of fatally shooting his estranged wife, Stacie Mason, and her romantic partner, Danny Ooley, both employees of Indian River County. Authorities said Ellis became the subject of a double homicide investigation after the killings. During the search for him, a woman rescued a struggling swimmer from the ocean near Riomar Beach in Vero Beach, later believed by police to be Ellis. The rescuer said she did not know his identity at the time. Police continued searching for Ellis after identifying him as the suspect in the double murder investigation.
Charges: Two counts of murder (charged in connection with the deaths of Stacie Mason and Danny Ooley)

Title: 73-year-old randomly stabbed at least 50 times while walking her dog, police say
description: Kersten Francilus, 25, was arrested and charged in connection with the death of 73-year-old Joyce Thompson Adams, who was attacked while walking her dog. Investigators said Adams was stabbed more than 50 times during the incident. Neighbors reported seeing a suspicious man approaching homes before the attack. Authorities said the knife used in the stabbing came from Francilus’ home. Officials also noted previous law enforcement encounters involving mental health concerns but said there was no indication the attack was motivated by antisemitism. Francilus was taken into custody and charged with first-degree premeditated murder in the case.
Charges: First-degree premeditated murder

Title: Man accused of forcing ex-girlfriend into car at knife-point, stabbing her after breakup
description: Jose Alberto Vazquez Carrasco, 32, was arrested after authorities accused him of kidnapping and stabbing his ex-girlfriend following a breakup. Investigators said the victim had ended the relationship earlier that day and later encountered Vazquez Carrasco while going to work. Police allege he grabbed her by the hair, held a knife to her throat, forced her into a vehicle, and drove around before releasing her on a roadway in Spring Hill. The victim suffered an abdominal stab wound and was taken to a trauma center for treatment. The suspect was located and arrested without further incident.
Charges: Kidnapping; aggravated battery with a deadly weapon

Title: Teen Arrested Following Violent Dating Violence Investigation
description: Jai’Keen Barlow, 17, was arrested following a violent dating violence investigation in Brandon, Florida. According to the Hillsborough County Sheriff’s Office, Barlow allegedly held his girlfriend against her will during a verbal altercation, threatened her with a firearm, and physically assaulted her. Authorities said he choked, slapped, and struck the victim with the firearm while making threats against her and her family. He also allegedly took her phone to stop her from seeking help. The victim suffered non-life-threatening injuries and was treated at a local hospital. Detectives recovered the firearm used during the incident.
Charges: Armed kidnapping; armed false imprisonment; aggravated battery with a deadly weapon; battery; battery by strangulation; felon in possession of a firearm; felon in possession of ammunition (7 counts); tampering with a witness

Title: Man arrested in Coconut Creek home invasion where victim was stripped naked, cops say
description: Police said Tevin Dean was arrested in connection with an armed home invasion that occurred in June at a Coconut Creek apartment. Investigators said Dean and another suspect entered the residence armed, threatened the victim with a firearm, forced the victim to strip naked, restrained him with duct tape, and covered his eyes. The suspects allegedly threatened the victim with a kitchen knife to obtain passwords for his Coinbase account, then stole cryptocurrency and personal property worth more than $27,000. They also deleted Ring video recordings, reset the victim's phones, and pawned them before fleeing, leaving the victim bound until he escaped.
Charges: Armed home invasion Armed kidnapping Aggravated battery with a deadly weapon Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon False imprisonment Using or displaying a firearm during a felony Grand theft Fraud
Comments: Good story simply lacking police in action.

Title: Boynton Beach man accused of racial slur, gun threat at Wellington Burger King
description: Jacob Nathan Witt was arrested after investigators said he threatened two Burger King employees during a drive-through dispute in Wellington. According to deputies, Witt became involved in an argument over service, used a racial slur directed at a Black employee, and pointed a black semiautomatic handgun toward the drive-through window, causing the employees to fear they would be shot. He allegedly lowered the firearm and drove away before deputies arrived. Investigators later identified him through Crime Stoppers tips and a photo lineup. One aggravated assault charge was enhanced as a hate crime because authorities determined it was motivated by racial prejudice.
Charges: Two counts of aggravated assault with a firearm without intent to kill One aggravated assault charge enhanced as a hate crime (second-degree felony)

Title: Man arrested, accused of slapping victim, displaying gun in road rage incident in Lee County
description: Bobby Jones III was arrested after deputies investigated a road rage incident in Lee County. According to investigators, the victim, a delivery driver, was aggressively tailgated near Daniels Parkway and pulled over to allow the other vehicle to pass. Instead, Jones also stopped, approached the victim, and confronted him. Deputies said Jones slapped the victim, displayed a firearm, and threatened to shoot during the altercation. The victim called 911, and responding deputies arrested Jones. Authorities charged him with aggravated assault with a deadly weapon and battery in connection with the incident. No injuries from gunfire were reported.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon Battery

Title: Cantonment Man Charged With Aggravated Assault With Deadly Weapon, Child Abuse
description: Colton David Gideons was arrested after deputies said he threatened a woman and forced her vehicle off the road while a child was inside. According to the Escambia County Sheriff’s Office, Gideons allegedly confronted the woman at a residence in Cantonment, lunged toward her with a closed fist, and made verbal threats. Investigators said he later followed her vehicle in his Dodge Ram truck, drove aggressively, swerved into her path, and slammed on his brakes, causing her vehicle to spin out of control. The incident was recorded by the victim and reported to authorities. A child abuse investigation was also initiated.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon Child abuse without great bodily harm Misdemeanor assault

Title: Pompano Beach man arrested for waving gun during road-rage encounter, deputies say
description: Michael Beasley was arrested after deputies said he displayed a firearm during an alleged road-rage encounter in Pompano Beach. According to the arrest report, the incident occurred when Beasley allegedly drove a silver Ford Taurus that swerved in front of a woman’s vehicle, nearly causing a collision. The woman said the driver brake-checked her, then displayed a silver handgun and waved it toward her while she was driving with four children. She reported that the man later stopped and pointed the gun again while asking if she wanted to die. Authorities identified Beasley through the vehicle’s personalized license plate.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon Improper exhibition of a firearm

Title: Punta Gorda man accused of pointing gun at workers and threatening to kill them
description: Shelton H. Roy Jr. was arrested after deputies said he pointed a firearm at two workers installing a fence near his Punta Gorda property. Investigators said Roy confronted the workers, used racial slurs, threatened to kill them, and later displayed a silver revolver. The workers took cover, and one called 911 while the other retrieved a firearm for self-defense. Roy also called 911 and reportedly admitted he had a gun while making additional offensive statements. Deputies arrived, detained Roy after he ignored commands, and recovered a loaded revolver during a search. A hate crime enhancement was added due to alleged racial statements.
Charges: Two counts of aggravated assault with a deadly weapon Resisting an officer without violence Hate crime enhancement

Title: Orbeez toy gun prank leads to arrest of Florida man and teen, cops say
description: A 49-year-old man identified as Davis was arrested in Port St. Lucie, Florida, after an incident involving a juvenile using an Orbeez toy gun. Police said the toy gun prank caused a man and his fiancée to believe their vehicle was being shot at. Davis allegedly followed the juveniles’ vehicle, confronted them with a loaded 9mm handgun, and ordered three juveniles out of the car at gunpoint. Officers arrived and found the juveniles on the ground while Davis was nearby. No injuries were reported. The juvenile involved in the prank was also arrested.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill; false imprisonment of a child to commit aggravated abuse
