Title: Florida man accused of swinging machete at victim on boat, chasing him during violent attack, Monroe deputies say
description: Luis Ancieto Herrada, 66, was arrested in Marathon, Florida, after authorities said he attacked another man aboard a vessel in the Florida Keys. According to the Monroe County Sheriff’s Office, Herrada became involved in an argument with a man staying on his boat and allegedly swung a machete at him. Deputies stated that Herrada chased the victim and struck him with an unknown object before the victim escaped the vessel. No serious injuries were reported. Herrada was taken into custody and booked into jail on felony charges related to aggravated assault and battery.
Charges: Aggravated assault; battery

Title: Florida man jailed in alleged 'road rage,' aggravated battery incident
description: Jeffrey Henry, 45, was arrested in Port St. Lucie, Florida, after an alleged road rage incident involving vehicle attacks. According to police records, Henry allegedly used his vehicle to strike another vehicle during a confrontation near Crosstown Parkway and Southeast Sandia Drive. The victim reported that Henry swerved into his lane, attempted to hit his vehicle multiple times, ran a red light, and later collided with the victim’s vehicle while the victim was calling 911. A passenger recorded parts of the incident, including the suspect vehicle and license plate. Henry was identified, arrested, and later released on bond.
Charges: Two felony counts of aggravated battery with a deadly weapon; three misdemeanor charges

Suspect Name: Daniel Noe Valencia and Daniel Carlos Valencia
Title: Two arrested for aggravated battery in Holmes County
description: Daniel Noe Valencia and Daniel Carlos Valencia were arrested in Holmes County, Florida, after deputies responded to a reported disturbance at a residence on Highway 177. When deputies arrived, the victim was already receiving medical treatment. Investigators collected the victim’s statement, reviewed the 911 recording, and searched for evidence related to the incident. Based on the evidence gathered, deputies arrested both men and charged them with aggravated battery. Authorities did not release details about the victim due to Marsy’s Law protections. The case remains under investigation by the Holmes County Sheriff’s Office.
Charges: Aggravated battery

Title: Ex-NFL player Tre Mason accused of battery on pregnant girlfriend in Palm Beach County
description: Trence Q. Mason, 32, a former NFL and Auburn University football player, was arrested in Palm Beach County, Florida, on allegations involving a domestic incident with his pregnant girlfriend. According to the Palm Beach County Sheriff’s Office, Mason allegedly pushed his girlfriend during a confrontation outside a Boynton Beach restaurant and threatened to punch her. The woman told deputies she was pregnant with Mason’s child. Deputies located and detained Mason shortly after the incident. Mason denied pushing or threatening her, but authorities determined there was probable cause for the arrest. He was released on bond.
Charges: Aggravated battery on a pregnant victim; domestic intent threat to do violence

Title: Woman charged with aggravated battery in Panama City hotel stabbing
description: Bridgett Morgan, 33, of Panama City, Florida, was arrested after an alleged stabbing incident at a hotel in the St. Andrews area. Police responded to the Rodeway Inn around 8:30 p.m. and found the victim, Taylor Morgan, inside a room with a non-life-threatening stab wound to the neck. Investigators reviewed surveillance footage that allegedly showed Bridgett Morgan leaving the room while holding a knife and getting into a vehicle. Officers later located her at a residence in Springfield and arrested her. A knife was reportedly found in the vehicle. The case involves a domestic violence allegation.
Charges: Domestic aggravated battery with a deadly weapon

Title: Machete-Wielding Florida Man Jailed After Parking Lot Chase Outside Bar
description: Pablo Arturo Rivero, 50, of Marathon, Florida, was arrested after an alleged machete-related assault outside a bar. According to the Monroe County Sheriff’s Office, deputies responded to the Brass Monkey bar parking lot around 4:06 a.m. on July 12, 2026, following reports of a battery. An adult male victim told authorities that after an argument with Rivero, the suspect allegedly chased him while carrying a machete. No life-threatening injuries were reported. Investigators identified Rivero as the suspect, obtained an arrest warrant, and later booked him into the Monroe County Jail on an aggravated battery charge.
Charges: Aggravated battery
Comments: Only the second case is worth pursuing.

Title: Lehigh Acres woman accused of threatening pest control salesman with gun
description: Cecilia Ross, 62, of Lehigh Acres, Florida, was accused of threatening a pest control salesman with a firearm. According to deputies, the incident occurred near Monroe Avenue and East Ninth Street while the salesman was going door-to-door for work. Authorities said Ross arrived in a Nissan SUV, pointed a gun at the salesman, and threatened to shoot and kill him if he returned to her home. The salesman reportedly hid behind a nearby house and contacted authorities. Ross was charged with aggravated assault with a deadly weapon. No shooting or injuries were reported during the incident.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon

Title: Steak knife used by Cape Coral man accused of aggravated assault during argument, officers say
description: Jaxson Williams, 31, of Cape Coral, Florida, was arrested after an alleged aggravated assault involving a steak knife during an argument at a residence. According to the Cape Coral Police Department, officers responded to an assault report around 3:05 p.m. Williams told officers he had been attacked by the victim, but the victim stated Williams had been drinking, causing disturbances, and became aggressive after entering the victim’s room. The victim alleged Williams threatened to get a knife and later lunged toward him with a black steak knife. The victim used a pocketknife in self-defense. Both knives were collected as evidence.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon

Title: Road Rage: Hammer-wielding Florida trucker allegedly leaves driver bloodied at red light
description: Jose Antonio Rosa Negron, 39, of Lakeland, Florida, was arrested after an alleged road rage assault involving a hammer. According to the Lee County Sheriff’s Office, deputies responded to an altercation near Helena Road and Cypress Gardens Boulevard on May 6, 2026. Authorities said a driver involved in a dispute with two trucks was blocked at a red light, where an argument escalated. Rosa Negron allegedly opened the victim’s car door, struck him, returned with a hammer, and attacked him multiple times, causing bleeding and bruising. He was arrested the following morning and faces multiple felony charges.
Charges: Burglary with battery; aggravated battery with a deadly weapon; four counts of false imprisonment

Title: Man arrested after swinging machete, making threats behind Palm Springs gas station
description: Miguel Robaina Dominguez, 56, was arrested in Palm Springs, Florida, after an alleged machete-related threat behind a RaceTrac gas station. According to the Palm Springs Police Department, Dominguez allegedly approached a man and woman near the gas station, pulled out a large machete, and swung it close to the man’s face while making threats. The victim was not cut but had a red mark on his neck. Police reviewed security footage that reportedly showed the incident. Officers later found Dominguez at a nearby Marathon Gas station, detained him after a brief foot chase, and recovered the machete.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill; trespassing

Title: Man arrested after knife reported at Duren’s Piggly Wiggly
description: A man was arrested after police responded to reports that he displayed a knife in a threatening manner at Duren’s Piggly Wiggly in Port St. Joe. Witnesses described the suspect as a thin white male with numerous tattoos carrying a red and black knife. Officers searched the grocery store and surrounding area before locating a man matching the description inside a nearby business. Police recovered a knife matching the witnesses’ description and arrested the suspect. He was transported to the Gulf County Jail. Authorities stated the investigation remained active and requested anyone with additional information to contact the department.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon Improper exhibition of a weapon Disorderly conduct

Title: Longtime felon pepper-sprays employee in Aventura Nordstrom Rack robbery, cops say
description: Pappy Tina Miller, 57, was accused of stealing nearly $1,800 worth of merchandise from a Nordstrom Rack in Aventura, Florida. According to police, after leaving the store with the concealed items, a loss prevention employee attempted to stop her and recover the merchandise. Investigators said Miller resisted, struggled to keep control of the shopping cart, forcefully pushed the employee, pepper-sprayed him, and fled the scene. Officers later located her near a Best Buy store, where she allegedly gave a false name and denied the accusations. Police identified her, arrested her, and booked her into jail.
Charges: Armed robbery; Armed grand theft; Evidence tampering; Felon in possession of a weapon

Suspect Name: Rosa Lamourt Tiru and Lance Mulonas
Title: Deltona Couple Charged After Attacking Teen They Mistook for an Adult
description: Rosa Lamourt Tiru, 45, and Lance Mulonas, 61, were arrested in Deltona, Florida, after allegedly attacking a 15-year-old boy they mistakenly believed was an adult. According to authorities, the teenager had dropped their daughter home after an overnight party when the couple allegedly blocked his vehicle. Mulonas reportedly struck the car with a metal pipe, held a knife near the teen’s neck, and restricted his movement, while Tiru allegedly displayed a firearm during the confrontation. The teenager escaped and contacted his mother, who called 911. Both suspects were arrested and held without bond.
Charges: Rosa Lamourt Tiru: aggravated battery, aggravated child abuse, aggravated assault Lance Mulonas: aggravated battery, aggravated child abuse, aggravated assault, false imprisonment, criminal mischief

Title: Man chases down driver who flipped him off in Florida City, pulls gun on him, police say
description: Billy Graham Tindal, 63, was arrested after a road rage incident in Florida City, Florida. According to police, the confrontation began when Tindal honked at another driver in an intersection. After the other driver made an obscene gesture, Tindal allegedly followed him, attempted to force his vehicle off the road, and pointed a handgun at him multiple times. The victim called police while following Tindal from a safe distance. Investigators reviewed Tindal’s dashboard camera footage, which they said showed aggressive driving. Officers later seized a firearm and arrested Tindal. No injuries or shots fired were reported.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon; Reckless driving

Title: Dramatic Video Shows Carwash Employee Tackling Ax-Wielding Man Who Was Threatening Them
description: Bryce Thayer, 36, was arrested after allegedly threatening two carwash employees with an ax at a property in Marion County, Florida. According to authorities, Thayer was told to leave the property but became angry and approached the employees while holding the weapon in a threatening manner. Video released by the Marion County Sheriff's Office showed an employee tackling Thayer and restraining him until deputies arrived. Another employee helped remove the ax during the struggle. Deputies responded, took Thayer into custody, and charged him with aggravated assault with a deadly weapon and possession of drug paraphernalia.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon; possession of drug paraphernalia

Title: Leesburg man accused of trying to ram roadside workers with tractor
description: Johnny Aaron Paulk, 52, was arrested after allegedly driving a tractor toward roadside workers during a confrontation over flashing work lights on County Road 452 near Felkins Drive in Leesburg, Florida. According to the Lake County Sheriff’s Office, workers reported hearing gunfire nearby before Paulk confronted them about their warning lights. Deputies said Paulk threatened to flip one of their trucks and later drove a red-orange tractor with front forks toward the workers at high speed. The tractor became stuck about 15 feet from a truck, allowing the workers to escape. Paulk was arrested without incident.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon

Title: Nokomis man charged after allegedly chasing teens with machete on Blind Pass Beach
description: John Anthony Slodyczka, a Nokomis man, allegedly chased a group of ten youths between the ages of 12 and 18 with a large machete on Blind Pass Beach around 11 p.m. while they were fishing. The frightened teens ran from the suspect and called 911 for help. Sarasota County Sheriff's deputies responded and noticed Slodyczka attempting to leave the beach parking lot in a Jeep matching the description provided by the victims. Deputies reported that he gave inconsistent statements, appeared intoxicated, and had a half-empty alcohol bottle inside the vehicle. He was arrested and booked into the Sarasota County Jail.
Charges: 10 counts of aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill Disorderly intoxication Resisting arrest Failing to register a motor vehicle Violating a county ordinance for being in a county park after 10 p.m.

Title: Teen charged as adult in fatal Hollywood shooting
description: Gentle Edwards, 15, was charged as an adult in connection with the fatal shooting of 17-year-old Robin Bouza Jr. in Hollywood, Florida. According to police, the shooting occurred shortly before 9:30 p.m. on April 22, 2026, in the 7300 block of Farragut Street. Bouza was pronounced dead at the scene. Investigators later identified Edwards as the suspect. He surrendered to authorities at the Hollywood Police Department on May 28, 2026. Authorities transferred him from juvenile detention to the Paul Rein Detention Facility. Police have not released a motive for the shooting, and the investigation remains ongoing.
Charges: First-degree murder; Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon
Comments: Lack of police intervention during the incident.

Title: Surfside police video shows arrest of ‘increasingly unwell’ armed man wanted in Miami Beach
description: Steven Goldman, 53, was arrested after police said he threatened valet workers with a firearm following a dispute over a parking violation sticker at his Miami Beach apartment complex. According to authorities, Goldman left his vehicle in the valet area for about 40 minutes, became angry after receiving the sticker, pushed an employee, and pointed a gun while making threats. Police later located Goldman driving and reported signs of possible intoxication, including bloodshot eyes, slurred speech, and alcohol odor. Officers found two firearms in his possession. His wife also reported concerns about his behavior and requested removal of additional firearms from their home.
Charges: Burglary with assault or battery; Aggravated assault with a firearm; DUI warrant case

Title: Homestead woman accused of drunkenly shooting 2 outside ceviche bar
description: Samantha Morales, 34, was accused of shooting two women outside Dr. Limon Ceviche Bar in Homestead, Florida. Police said Morales confronted the victims after they left the restaurant, displayed a firearm, and opened fire during an argument. The victims were shot, and one reportedly attempted to disarm Morales before police separated them. Morales told investigators she did not remember the incident but claimed she was defending herself. She was arrested and faces multiple felony and misdemeanor firearm-related charges.
Charges: Three counts of aggravated assault with a firearm, two counts of aggravated battery with a deadly weapon, one count of using a firearm, improper exhibition of a firearm, and using a firearm while under the influence of alcohol

Title: Keys man accused of attacking relative with broom, threatening her with knife
description: Jacob Edward Stogner, 22, was arrested after deputies responded to a family disturbance at a home on Flamingo Hammock Road in Islamorada. According to the Monroe County Sheriff’s Office, Stogner allegedly struck a family member multiple times with a broom, causing bruises consistent with the reported attack. The victim also told deputies that Stogner grabbed a kitchen knife and threatened her during the incident. Stogner was taken into custody and faces felony charges related to the alleged assault and battery.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon and aggravated battery

Title: Deputies: Man kicks 2 deputies during arrest after hitting 2 roommates in Miami-Dade
description: Brandon Ramos, 28, was arrested after deputies said he injured two roommates and two law enforcement officers in Miami-Dade County. According to court records, Ramos allegedly threw a beer can at a roommate’s face during an argument and later struck another roommate during a separate dispute. When deputies arrived to arrest him, authorities said Ramos resisted and intentionally kicked two deputies while he was handcuffed. He was booked into the Turner Guilford Knight Correctional Center and faced multiple battery and assault-related charges.
Charges: Battery, resisting arrest, two counts of aggravated assault on a law enforcement officer

Title: Fort Lauderdale woman accused of impersonating officer during armed road rage incident
description: Shaley Joanne Alvarez, 35, was arrested after police said she pointed a handgun at another driver during a road rage incident in Fort Lauderdale. According to authorities, Alvarez allegedly cut off the driver near State Road A1A and Sunrise Boulevard, then displayed a firearm while claiming to be a police officer. The driver pulled over near the Galleria mall and contacted 911 because he believed he was being stopped and feared for his safety. Alvarez was later arrested and charged with firearm and impersonation offenses.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, impersonating a law enforcement officer in the commission of a felony, and improper exhibition of a firearm

Title: Gunfire Incident Leads to Aggravated Assault Arrest
description: Ricky Eugene Foster, 56, was arrested after a disturbance involving gunfire at a residence in Walnut Hill, Florida. Deputies responded to reports of shots fired and found Foster, who admitted firing a handgun and appeared to have been drinking. According to investigators, Foster blocked a victim's vehicle, pointed a handgun at the victim, and made death threats during the confrontation. A witness reported hearing multiple gunshots. Foster told deputies he fired the gun into the air. He was charged with aggravated assault with a deadly weapon and later released from jail after posting a $5,000 bond.
Charges: Felony aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill

Title: West Palm Beach man accused of armed sexual battery, false imprisonment and grand theft auto
description: West Palm Beach, Florida
Charges: Two counts of false imprisonment, sexual battery with a deadly weapon or physical force, domestic battery by strangulation, aggravated assault with a firearm, grand theft auto, possession of cocaine, possession of a firearm during the commission of a felony, and violation of probation. [1]

Title: Suspect accused of crashing into Port St. John yard and stabbing residents, says deputies
description: A man involved in an Interstate 95 hit-and-run crashed his vehicle into the front yard of a Port St. John home. The suspect, Jadarius West, ran onto the back porch and entered the house through a sliding glass door. Once inside, West demanded vehicle keys from the residents. He then grabbed a knife, cut one victim on the hand, and stabbed a second victim in the neck while a third resident escaped unharmed. West remained inside the residence as law enforcement established a perimeter. He was arrested after jumping out of a window.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon and multiple other unlisted charges.

Title: Florida man accused of wielding weapon after truck repossessed
description: A confrontation erupted in an Ocala neighborhood when two workers attempted to repossess a truck. The vehicle owner, 54-year-old Clifford Duvall, ordered them to stop before getting inside the vehicle. When Duvall exited the truck, he brandished a dangerous metal weapon described as a tomahawk or machete. He removed the sheath, approached the workers, and pointed the weapon at them. Duvall then swung the weapon and struck the metal towing cable. Despite his claims to deputies that he only targeted the equipment, video evidence showed him wielding the weapon within a few feet of the victims before his arrest.
Charges: Two felony counts of aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill.

Title: Man accused of 3 attacks within minutes near Publix, Chili's near Delray Beach
description: A man targeted three individuals within fifteen minutes in a Delray Beach shopping area. Alens Charles first approached a woman in a Publix parking lot, pointing a hidden knife wrapped to simulate a handgun at her boyfriend. Minutes later, Charles confronted a grocery shopper, demanding his bags before striking him in the face. Finally, Charles ambushed a 65-year-old food delivery driver outside a nearby Chili's, striking him from behind and kicking him. The delivery driver suffered a broken rib and multiple cuts. Police tracked Charles's vehicle to a Boca Raton hotel and initiated a felony traffic stop.
Charges: Strong-arm robbery, simple battery, aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, aggravated battery, and aggravated battery on a person 65 years of age or older.

Title: Pinellas Park police arrest man after his gun discharged during altercation on PSTA bus
description: A verbal altercation aboard a Pinellas Suncoast Transit Authority bus escalated when a passenger displayed a firearm. The suspect, 28-year-old Victor Lambert, pulled out the weapon, prompting the victim to engage in a physical struggle over it. During the scuffle, the gun discharged inside the bus, but the round did not strike anyone. Lambert fled the transit vehicle on foot immediately after the discharge. Police tracked him down several hours later near Freedom Lake Park and arrested him. The victim suffered minor injuries from the physical fight and received treatment at a local hospital.
Charges: Aggravated assault and improper exhibition of a firearm

Title: Knife-wielding Florida man arrested after setting restaurant on fire with flaming propane tank: authorities
description: Rubiel Maceo Castillo, 53, was arrested after allegedly wielding knives and carrying a flaming propane tank through a Tampa restaurant on July 7, 2026, causing a fire. Deputies arriving at the scene found the building filled with smoke, with Castillo still inside. He had reportedly cut a woman's wrist when she tried to stop him from charging at people inside. Working with fire rescue crews, deputies extinguished the blaze and took the suspect into custody.
Charges: First-degree arson of an occupied structure, aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, and criminal mischief.

Title: Man Arrested For Holding Teens At Gunpoint After Orbeez Shot At Car
description: Gregory Allen Davis, 49, was arrested after allegedly confronting three teenagers in Port St. Lucie, Florida, believing they had fired BB guns at his vehicle. Police said Davis exited his fiancée's car at a traffic light, drew a handgun, and ordered the teens out of their vehicle and onto the ground. Officers responded to the scene and arrested Davis without resistance. Investigators later determined the teenagers had been using an Orbeez toy gun that shoots water beads, not a real firearm. One 15-year-old was also charged with firing into an occupied vehicle after claiming it was intended as a prank.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill  False imprisonment of a child to commit aggravated abuse

Title: Archer man arrested after fight with hospital worker, deputies say
description: Ashley Kirksey, 20, of Archer, was arrested after a disturbance at UF Shands Kanapaha ER in Gainesville, Florida. Deputies said Kirksey accompanied his girlfriend to the hospital, where both became involved in a disturbance. After being asked to leave by hospital staff, Kirksey allegedly threatened employees, challenged them to come outside, and returned toward his vehicle. When a hospital employee went outside to prevent him from reentering, Kirksey allegedly threw the first punch and attempted to continue the fight multiple times. Deputies also said he spat on the victim three times, and a handgun was later found in his vehicle.
Charges: Armed trespassing  Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon on a specified person  Three counts of battery on a specified person

Title: Florida man accused of using rifle in threatening another man at Wawa
description: According to the affidavit, Jeremy Vigil was accused of threatening another man with an AR-style rifle during a dispute over payment for a previous job. The incident occurred at a Wawa parking lot in Port St. Lucie. The victim said Vigil pointed the rifle at him and made threats before a physical altercation occurred. Police reviewed surveillance footage and later searched Vigil’s home, where they reported finding an AR-style rifle inside a safe. Vigil initially denied the allegations. He was arrested and taken to the St. Lucie County Jail following the investigation.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon; Battery

Title: Dunnellon Man Accused of Threatening Father with Knife During Domestic Dispute
description: According to the Marion County Sheriff’s Office, Anthony Haig was arrested after deputies responded to a domestic disturbance at a residence in the Dunnellon area. Investigators said Haig argued with his father over loud music and allegedly threatened to kill him while holding a knife. The victim left the home and contacted authorities, stating he feared for his life. Witnesses reportedly heard the threats, and Haig’s mother said she saw him holding a kitchen knife. Deputies said Haig admitted making the threat and stated he had been drinking alcohol. He was taken into custody without incident.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill

Title: Man arrested, accused of using BB gun on children as punishment in Marion County, deputies say
description: According to the Marion County Sheriff’s Office, Jacob McClain was arrested after deputies said he used a BB gun to threaten children during a punishment exercise. Deputies said McClain made children run and perform pushups before aiming and firing the BB gun toward one child, striking a metal trash can nearby. Investigators said McClain admitted he used the BB gun as a scare tactic during discipline and had previously fired it toward the children. The child reportedly feared being shot. McClain was arrested and transported to jail following the investigation.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon; Child abuse; Probation violation

Title: Driver arrested after off‑duty officer says gun was pointed, blue laser shone into car: JSO
description: Andre Bigelow, 27, was arrested after an alleged road-rage incident involving an off-duty Jacksonville Sheriff’s Office officer. According to the arrest report, the officer said Bigelow followed his vehicle, repeatedly honked, shined a blue laser into the vehicle, and pointed what appeared to be a firearm during the encounter. Investigators identified the suspect vehicle using license plate readers and located Bigelow in a Jacksonville parking garage. Officers conducted a felony takedown and arrested him without incident. Police reported finding a Glock 19 handgun, an AR-style BB rifle, and a blue laser device in the vehicle.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill; Misuse of a laser lighting device on a motor vehicle

Title: Man released from jail days earlier accused of choking, attacking child with knife at DeLand bus stop
description: Christopher Steven Schwable, 36, of Pierson, was arrested after police said he attacked a 13-year-old boy at a school bus stop in DeLand. Authorities alleged Schwable choked the child, struck him, and threatened others with a knife. A passerby saw the incident, intervened, and restrained Schwable until officers arrived. Police recovered a green-and-black folding knife from Schwable. The victim reported injuries from the attack, and witnesses supported the allegations. Schwable was taken into custody and charged with aggravated child abuse and aggravated assault with a deadly weapon. The investigation was handled by DeLand Police Department.
Charges: Aggravated child abuse Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon

Title: Okeechobee man arrested in Florida Keys for threatening woman with revolver
description: Charles Durand Wilkinson, 77, of Okeechobee was arrested in the Florida Keys after deputies responded to a domestic situation involving a firearm. The Monroe County Sheriff’s Office said Wilkinson allegedly retrieved a revolver during an argument with a woman and threatened to shoot her. The woman reportedly took control of the situation by disarming Wilkinson and throwing the firearm into nearby bushes. Deputies located the revolver and arrested Wilkinson. He was transported to jail and charged with aggravated assault with a deadly weapon. No shooting occurred, and no injuries were reported during the incident.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon

Title: Man accused of stabbing grandmother 11 times during Mother’s Day dispute
description: Keo Lavar Nottage Jr., 29, of West Palm Beach, was arrested after authorities said he stabbed his 74-year-old grandmother during a domestic dispute on Mother’s Day. Police reported that an argument began after family members returned from shopping and escalated when Nottage became increasingly agitated. Investigators said Nottage made threats, retrieved a knife from the kitchen, and stabbed his grandmother multiple times. The victim was taken to a hospital, where officials documented 11 stab wounds. Surveillance footage and witness statements were used in the investigation. Nottage was detained and charged with attempted murder and aggravated assault.
Charges: Attempted first-degree murder with a deadly weapon Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill

Title: Hollywood man accused of threatening family, officer while holding machete
description: Rene Matute Godoy, 43, was arrested in Hollywood after police said he threatened family members and a responding officer while armed with a machete. Authorities reported that Matute Godoy arrived home intoxicated, argued with his wife, and threatened to hit her. Police said he grabbed a machete, damaged items inside the home, struck his wife’s vehicle, and made threats to kill his family. Children were reportedly moved to safety during the incident. Matute Godoy also allegedly threatened an officer before being taken into custody. He was charged with multiple offenses, including aggravated assault and child neglect.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill Assault on an officer Criminal mischief/damaging property Child neglect Resisting an officer without violence

Title: VIDEO: Stark County man takes gun from officer, fires off shot as officers attempted to arrest him
description: A twenty-five-year-old Stark County man wanted on outstanding felony warrants was arrested following a violent altercation with law enforcement. Officers initially responded to a welfare check after receiving reports of a man lying against a tree in a wooded area. The suspect provided false identification to officers before his true identity and active violent offender warrants were revealed. When officers attempted to place him under arrest, the suspect fled on foot into the woods. Officers pursued and tackled him to the ground, where the suspect disarmed an officer, discharged a single round, and threatened to continue shooting before being subdued.
Charges: Two active felony warrants with a violent offender designation

Title: Police: Intoxicated man found with loaded gun at Ohio park after hours
description: An intoxicated man was arrested after law enforcement officers discovered him with a loaded firearm inside a closed public park after hours. Flushing Police Department officers observed a vehicle parked inside Schuler Park at approximately nine-nineteen in the evening, well past the designated closing time. Upon approaching the vehicle, officers found the suspect inside and detected a strong odor of alcohol. The suspect failed standardized field sobriety tests and recorded a blood alcohol concentration of point one three seven. A subsequent vehicle search revealed a loaded nine-millimeter handgun, holsters, and extra ammunition, leading to immediate jail transport.
Charges: Operating a Vehicle While Under the Influence (OVI) and Using Weapons While Intoxicated

Title: Miami Gardens cop arrested on domestic assault charge in Opa-locka, attorney says
description: A forty-one-year-old Miami Gardens police officer was arrested following a violent domestic dispute with his girlfriend. The couple pulled their vehicles over after the suspect allegedly drove erratically. The suspect entered the victim's passenger seat, brandished a black handgun, pointed it at the windshield, and threw it onto the dashboard. When asked to exit, the suspect grabbed the victim by the neck with both hands and choked her. Following the confrontation, the suspect repeatedly contacted the victim, urging her to recant her statement and stop cooperating with law enforcement. He later surrendered voluntarily to the police department.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a firearm, illegal use or display of a firearm while committing a felony, and misdemeanor witness or victim tampering

Title: Mentor man pleads guilty to assaulting bicyclists before police standoff
description: A forty-two-year-old Mentor man pleaded guilty following a violent series of events involving an SUV attack on bicyclists and a subsequent barricade situation. On June 3, the suspect crossed the center line of Headlands Road in his vehicle and struck a seventy-two-year-old bicyclist. He drove further down the road, stopped his vehicle, and physically assaulted a sixty-eight-year-old bicyclist before tossing the second victim's bicycle into a nearby pond. Both victims suffered serious injuries. Law enforcement tracked the suspect's vehicle to an Orchard Road home, where he engaged in an hourslong standoff with police before being arrested.
Charges: Two counts of felonious assault and one count of robbery

Title: Grafton police officer arrested on felonious assault charge after woman injured: I-Team
description: An off-duty police officer was arrested after an altercation at a local bar patio left a woman injured. Security footage shows the woman taking a fighting stance to play-wrestle before being thrown heavily to the floor. Witnesses reported that the suspect told the victim he was taking souls prior to the physical encounter. The victim awoke on the ground with the suspect's foot resting on her hair, and hospital staff later diagnosed her with muscle strains and a concussion. The suspect fled the establishment before deputies arrived but was subsequently taken into custody and placed on administrative leave.
Charges: One count of felonious assault
Comments: Good action, just lacking police intervention during the incident.

Title: Police: Man arrested after firing gun at truck during road rage dispute in Springfield Township
description: A forty-three-year-old Norwood man was arrested following a violent road rage shooting. The incident began after a near-crash occurred between a blue SUV and a gold truck on Springfield Pike. Both vehicles continued driving until they stopped at a red light at Vine Street and Shadybrook Drive, where a confrontation escalated. The suspect, who was a back-seat passenger in the SUV, produced a handgun and fired two rounds at the truck. One bullet shattered a rear window, causing minor arm injuries to the truck driver from flying glass. Police later tracked both vehicles to a Green Township hardware store and arrested the suspect.
Charges: Felonious assault and improperly handling firearms inside a motor vehicle

Title: Man in custody after northeast Columbus shooting, hourslong SWAT barricade
description: A thirty-three-year-old man was arrested following a random morning shooting and an hourslong SWAT barricade situation in northeast Columbus. Law enforcement officials state the suspect shot a victim who was driving to work along Joyce Avenue, an individual with whom the suspect had no known prior relationship. Following the shooting, police tracked the suspect to his home on Brentnell Avenue, prompting a SWAT response. The suspect escaped before the perimeter formed and hid inside a neighbor's car trunk without their knowledge. Upon discovery, the suspect exited the trunk and assaulted two detectives before being taken into custody.
Charges: Felonious assault, improperly handling firearms in a motor vehicle, discharge of a firearm over a roadway, burglary, having weapons while under disability, and assault on a peace officer

Title: Couple indicted in death of 6-day-old baby
description: A thirty-two-year-old man and a twenty-nine-year-old woman were indicted following the death of a six-day-old infant. Police responded to an early morning emergency call regarding an unconscious, non-breathing infant at a residential home. The parents reported placing the newborn to sleep on a pillow in their shared bed after feeding. Responding emergency personnel discovered drug abuse instruments and drug paraphernalia, alongside baby pacifiers and suspected cocaine residue, in the couple's bedroom. Following the comprehensive death investigation, a grand jury indicted the pair on felony charges including involuntary manslaughter.
Charges: Two counts of involuntary manslaughter, one count of endangering children, and one count of possession of cocaine

Title: Toledo man convicted in officer assault gets suspended sentence
description: A thirty-three-year-old Toledo man was arrested and subsequently convicted following a physical altercation with law enforcement. The incident occurred near the intersection of Monroe Street and Huron Street at approximately two-forty-five in the morning. A police sergeant attempted to place the suspect under arrest, which immediately triggered a physical fight between the two individuals. During the violent struggle, the arresting sergeant suffered a broken hand, while the suspect sustained minor injuries that were treated directly at the scene. The suspect later entered a plea of no contest and was convicted of misdemeanor assault, receiving a suspended jail sentence.
Charges: Misdemeanor assault  felony assault on a peace officer

Title: TPD: Driver hits officer with car door, tries to hit two others patrolling on bicycles
description: A thirty-six-year-old Toledo man was arrested following a violent incident at a traffic intersection that endangered law enforcement and children. The suspect was driving a vehicle near East Broadway and Front when an officer working traffic detail noticed a passenger screaming for assistance. As the officer approached the open passenger door, the suspect shifted into reverse and accelerated away, hitting the officer with the car door and striking another vehicle. The suspect then intentionally drove through barricades, attempting to run down two additional officers patrolling on bicycles. Law enforcement eventually stopped the vehicle near Main and Riverside.
Charges: Three counts of felonious assault and six counts of endangering children

Title: Eustis man faces attempted murder charge after dragging officer 330 feet
description: A twenty-eight-year-old man was arrested after turning himself in following a violent traffic stop encounter. Law enforcement officers initiated a traffic stop on the suspect's vehicle at approximately three in the morning for a traffic violation. An officer noted the smell of marijuana and instructed the suspect to exit the vehicle. The suspect refused to comply with the directive. As officers tried to remove him, the suspect shifted into drive and accelerated. An officer became physically pinned against the suspect and was dragged roughly three hundred thirty feet at speeds reaching thirty-five miles per hour before breaking free.
Charges: Attempted murder of a law enforcement officer, aggravated battery on a law enforcement officer, fleeing to elude, resisting an officer with violence, and resisting an officer without violence

Title: Man accused of erratic driving, threatening deputies in the Keys arrested
description: A thirty-nine-year-old man was arrested in the Florida Keys following reports of erratic driving, property damage, and aggressive behaviour. Monroe County Sheriff's Office deputies responded to a gas station near a mile marker in Islamorada at approximately twelve-forty-eight in the morning. Investigators learned that the suspect had struck an off-duty deputy's motorcycle before fleeing the immediate scene. Witnesses at the location reported that the suspect's reckless driving caused several near-collisions on the roadway. Witnesses also noted that the suspect exhibited highly aggressive behavior and made multiple threats toward individuals. He was apprehended and booked into custody.
Charges: DUI, assault on a law enforcement officer, and threatening to kill a law enforcement officer

Title: Miami Beach man assaulted parking officer, slashed truck tires over citation, cops say
description: A forty-year-old Miami Beach man was arrested after allegedly stalking and assaulting a municipal parking enforcement officer. The incident began when the officer issued a parking citation to an illegally parked motorcycle on Espanola Way. The suspect exited a nearby bar, discovered the ticket, and angrily confronted the official. For approximately twenty minutes, the suspect followed the parking officer on his motorcycle while issuing verbal threats of physical harm. Surveillance footage later captured the suspect using a sharp metal object to slash two tires on the officer's city-issued truck. The suspect was subsequently identified and taken into custody. [1]
Charges: Aggravated assault on an official employee and criminal mischief

Title: Martin County deputies: Road rage suspect rams family's car into barbed-wire fence
description: Michael Jeffrey Spiers allegedly carried out a violent road rage attack in Stuart, Florida, after chasing a woman and later targeting her brother's SUV carrying his wife and young son. Investigators said he threw objects, brake-checked the vehicle, and intentionally performed a PIT maneuver, causing the SUV to spin off the road and crash into a barbed-wire fence. The family escaped the vehicle and hid until deputies arrived. No one was injured. Deputies located Spiers at a nearby gas station and arrested him. Authorities said the victims were strangers to him, and he allegedly believed they were stealing his money.
Charges: Aggravated battery with a deadly weapon Child abuse Reckless driving

Title: Florida man arrested after pointing gun at victim’s face, demanding drugs in bar bathroom: deputies
description: Ryan Glenn McDonough was arrested after deputies said he threatened another man with a handgun inside a bar bathroom in Islamorada, Florida. According to investigators, McDonough repeatedly asked the victim for a "baggie," which the victim believed referred to illegal drugs. After the victim said several times that he did not use drugs or have any, McDonough allegedly pulled a black handgun from his waistband and pointed it directly at the victim's face. The victim reported the incident to deputies. McDonough was arrested, and deputies recovered a .45-caliber Glock handgun from his possession during the arrest.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon

Title: Man linked to possible road rage shooting in Lake County arrested, deputies say
description: A possible road rage shooting occurred near State Road 40 and County Road 445A in Astor, Florida. Authorities said Levon Coakley allegedly fired a shot at another vehicle, injuring the occupant with a non-life-threatening injury. After the incident, Coakley fled and was pursued by law enforcement into Flagler County. He later abandoned his vehicle near I-95 and fled on foot. Deputies used helicopters, K-9s, and other resources to locate him. He was eventually found and taken into custody after a chase involving vehicle crashes and stop sticks.
Charges: Fleeing and eluding Resisting arrest without violence Leaving the scene of an accident with injuries

Title: Man accused of assaulting police officer, stabbing another man at a camper home
description: Jason Collins-Wild was accused of stabbing a man above the knee during an argument at a camper home in Loxahatchee, Florida. According to investigators, the victim recorded video showing Collins-Wild advancing with a pointed object before the stabbing. After the incident, Collins-Wild left the area but was later located and detained by deputies. While being transported for medical treatment, he allegedly resisted officers, attempted to pull away from custody inside the emergency room, and kicked a deputy in the torso after being restrained. He was returned to the patrol vehicle and taken into custody to face multiple criminal charges.
Charges: Aggravated battery with a deadly weapon Resisting an officer without violence Battery on specified personnel

Title: College Park jogger attacker Tyler Feight accused of attacking corrections officer in jail
description: Tyler Feight, who was already in jail on previous charges, was accused of attacking a corrections officer after requesting recreation time. According to the arrest affidavit, Feight struck the officer in the back of the neck on July 1, 2026. The officer was able to restrain him until additional staff arrived. The officer told responding deputies that Feight appeared to be experiencing a mental breakdown and had not previously displayed aggressive behavior. Following the incident, authorities charged Feight with battery on a corrections officer. He remained in custody while facing the new criminal charge in addition to his previous cases.
Charges: Battery on a corrections officer

Title: Hours-long standoff ends after man points shotgun at Volusia County deputy, officials say
description: Austin Mowery, a 28-year-old Seville man, was accused of engaging in a standoff with deputies after law enforcement responded to his home for a well-being check related to concerns about his mental stability. According to the Volusia County Sheriff’s Office, Mowery allegedly pointed a shotgun at a deputy through a window of the residence on Lake Juanita Road. The standoff lasted several hours before Mowery surrendered around 2:30 a.m. Monday. No injuries were reported to Mowery or deputies. He was taken into custody and booked into the Volusia County jail on an aggravated assault charge involving a law enforcement officer.
Charges: Aggravated assault on a law enforcement officer

Title: Broward Sheriff Fire Rescue lieutenant arrested in battery of patient, BSO says
description: Carlos Antonio Lewin, a Broward Sheriff Fire Rescue lieutenant, was arrested after authorities accused him of assaulting a 65-year-old patient inside a rescue vehicle. According to investigators, the incident occurred after firefighters responded to a medical call in unincorporated central Broward. Authorities said Lewin argued with the wheelchair-bound patient, then allegedly struck the patient’s head against a stretcher, pressed his fingers into the patient’s eyes, and choked him. The patient suffered head, neck, and eye pain and was taken to a hospital for evaluation. Lewin was arrested after an investigation and was suspended without pay by the department.
Charges: Two counts of battery on a person 65 or older

Title: Man who barricaded self at Fort Lauderdale Airbnb after alleged battery arrested, police say
description: Andrew Green, 42, was arrested after police accused him of battering his girlfriend and barricading himself inside an Airbnb in Fort Lauderdale. According to police, officers responded after receiving a report of a woman needing help and determined a domestic violence incident had occurred. The woman was found injured and seeking assistance from neighbors. Police said Green refused to leave the Airbnb while one of his children was inside. A SWAT team responded, and after a lengthy standoff, officers used an aerosol irritant to force Green out of the home. He was then arrested and charged in connection with the incident.
Charges: Domestic battery by strangulation False imprisonment of person Battery/domestic violence

Suspect Name: Michael Espinoza, Isaiah Seeraj, Charlie Lopez
Title: 3 arrested after gunfire erupts during fight at Orlando parking garage, police say
description: Three men were arrested after a fight between two groups escalated into gunfire at the Liberty Parking Garage on E. Pine Street in Orlando, Florida. Police responded around 2:30 a.m. Sunday after receiving reports of a shooting. Investigators said an altercation turned into a physical fight, and one person retrieved a firearm that was discharged during the confrontation. No one was hit by the gunfire. Officers stopped two vehicles attempting to leave the garage and seized two firearms. Michael Espinoza, Isaiah Seeraj, and Charlie Lopez were arrested on separate charges related to the incident. The investigation remains ongoing.
Charges: Michael Espinoza: Aggravated assault with a firearm; reckless display of a firearm Isaiah Seeraj: Hit-and-run with property damage Charlie Lopez: Possession of a firearm by a convicted delinquent

Title: Road-rage shooting suspect in Cutler Bay arrested: Sheriff
description: Christopher Portillo, 37, was arrested after a road rage shooting in Cutler Bay, Florida. Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office deputies responded to Southwest 184th Street and 117th Avenue after reports of a shooting following a traffic dispute. Investigators said Portillo fired one round into another vehicle, with the bullet passing through the rear windshield and striking the driver’s side headrest. A shell casing was recovered from the roadway. Portillo told deputies he fired because he believed the other vehicle’s passenger displayed a gun. He was arrested and charged after the investigation. No injuries were reported in the incident.
Charges: Shooting/throwing a deadly missile

Title: Man charged with attempted murder after family dispute leads to shooting in Orange City, police say
description: Malik I. Brown, 27, of Longwood, was arrested after a shooting during a family-related dispute at the Reserve at Orange City apartment complex. Police said the confrontation involved the victim and the father of his girlfriend’s children. Investigators allege Brown fired multiple rounds from inside his vehicle, striking the victim several times. Brown’s two young children were inside the vehicle during the shooting. Officers provided medical aid, secured the scene, and arrested Brown without incident. The victim was hospitalized with multiple gunshot wounds and underwent surgery. He was listed in stable condition while recovering in intensive care.
Charges: Attempted second-degree murder; child neglect; additional charges not specified

Title: Woman and daughter caught in crossfire outside Orange County Jail, shooting suspect arrested
description: Anthony Myles, 23, was arrested after a domestic-related shooting near the Orange County Jail in Orlando, Florida. Police said Myles was targeting his ex-girlfriend and another man while chasing them through the area. Investigators said Myles pointed a firearm at the pair and fired three shots through the windshield when the man attempted to escape. A passing vehicle carrying a woman and her mother was struck by gunfire, with one bullet hitting the mother’s shoulder and causing minor injuries. The incident ended in the Orange County Jail parking lot, where Orlando Police officers apprehended Myles.
Charges: Two counts of aggravated assault with a firearm; aggravated battery with a firearm; discharging a firearm from a vehicle

Title: Man arrested after video shows fight with officer on Southwest Airlines flight at MIA
description: Marcial Martinez, a 32-year-old resident of New Mexico, was arrested after an alleged violent altercation aboard a Southwest Airlines flight at Miami International Airport. Authorities said Martinez became disruptive during boarding and allegedly pushed a U.S. Department of Energy officer who attempted to intervene. Video showed Martinez arguing, resisting removal from the aircraft, and later grappling with the officer. Deputies reported signs of intoxication, including bloodshot eyes and the smell of alcohol. Martinez was taken into custody and booked at Turner Guilford Knight Correctional Center following the incident.
Charges: Battery and disorderly intoxication

Title: MDSO: Multiple people injured in Miami-Dade armed carjackings; suspect arrested
description: Alejandro Martinez, 33, was arrested after investigators linked him to a series of violent armed carjackings and robberies in southwest Miami-Dade County. Deputies said the incidents began when a victim was beaten, stabbed, and robbed of his vehicle. Martinez allegedly fled in the stolen vehicle and was connected to additional carjackings and armed robberies. Several victims were injured and transported to hospitals. Deputies located a stolen vehicle and later arrested Martinez after a foot chase. Investigators said he was also involved in other attacks where victims suffered serious injuries requiring medical treatment.
Charges: Attempted felony murder, armed robbery with carjacking, armed robbery with a weapon, aggravated assault with a deadly weapon

Title: ‘Dress for arrest': Florida man in jail outfit arrested for trespassing, sheriff says
description: On March 20, 2026, deputies with the Brevard County Sheriff's Office responded to a hotel after receiving a report that a guest refused to leave after his reservation had expired. Deputies identified the guest as 53-year-old Farron Fullerton, who was wearing a stolen Mitchell County Jail uniform. Authorities instructed him to leave the property, but he refused. When deputies attempted to arrest him, he resisted being placed in handcuffs before being taken into custody. Investigators later confirmed the jail clothing had been stolen when Fullerton was released from the Mitchell County Jail.
Charges: Trespassing, resisting an officer without violence

Title: Family seeks answers after man falls into coma following Orlando police arrest
description: On March 27, 2026, Orlando Police officers conducted a traffic stop after observing traffic violations. Officers reported smelling burnt cannabis and seeing cannabis inside the vehicle. Terry Mitchell allegedly refused repeated commands to exit the vehicle and resisted officers during the arrest. Police said they recovered cocaine, methamphetamine, cannabis, and pepper spray. Mitchell was accused of attempting to destroy suspected narcotics by chewing them and later experienced a medical emergency after being transported for booking and then to a hospital. He fell into a coma and remained hospitalized while an internal investigation into the arrest continued.
Charges: Possession of cocaine, possession of methamphetamine, possession of cannabis (less than 20 grams), tampering with evidence, possession of a concealed weapon by a convicted felon, resisting an officer without violence (two counts), battery on a law enforcement officer

Title: Hallandale Beach police arrest man accused of lewd acts, targeting child and adult
description: On March 14, 2026, Hallandale Beach police investigated two incidents involving Roberto Lazaro Sosa. Police said he first acted suspiciously while watching a woman and her child from his vehicle before driving away. Later that day, officers responded to a report that Sosa exited his vehicle outside an Airbnb, exposed himself, and committed a lewd act in public. Police later located his vehicle using the city's license plate reader system and arrested him. Investigators also found cocaine in his possession at the time of his arrest. Authorities believe there may be additional victims.
Charges: Possession of a controlled substance without a prescription, resisting an officer without violence, exposure of sexual organs

Title: Fort Myers felon wanted for skipping court after arrest on drug charges
description: Andrew Ballard, 45, was wanted on an unrelated warrant when Lee County deputies spotted him in North Fort Myers. On January 2026 (exact date not provided), Ballard fled on foot, leading deputies on a chase before being apprehended. During the arrest, deputies found cocaine and methamphetamine in his pockets. He was arrested and remained in jail for approximately four months before being released pending court proceedings. Ballard later failed to appear for his scheduled court hearing, resulting in a warrant for his arrest. Authorities reported he had an extensive criminal history with numerous prior arrests.
Charges: Possession of cocaine, possession of methamphetamine, resisting arrest

Title: Man arrested on multiple drug trafficking charges after foot chase in Fort Walton Beach
description: On March 8, 2026, Fort Walton Beach Police Department officers attempted to stop a black pickup truck driven by Lekendrick Ingram for a traffic violation on Holmes Boulevard Northwest. Ingram allegedly refused to stop, drove through yards, damaged a cement mailbox, and later abandoned the vehicle. Officers found him hiding in a backyard after a foot chase. Near the location, police discovered a modified aerosol can containing suspected narcotics. Authorities seized cocaine, methamphetamine, fentanyl, oxycodone pills, and cash. Ingram was arrested and charged with multiple drug trafficking offenses, fleeing law enforcement, and resisting arrest without violence.
Charges: Trafficking in fentanyl; trafficking in cocaine; trafficking in methamphetamine; possession of a controlled substance without a prescription; fleeing or attempting to elude law enforcement; resisting arrest without violence

Title: VIDEO: Son seen leaving parents' condo moments before police discover their murders
description: Philip Repaci Jr., 56, was charged with killing his parents, Philip Repaci Sr. and Joan Repaci, inside their Harbour Isle condominium in Fort Pierce. Police said the victims were found dead from multiple gunshot wounds during a welfare check. Investigators reported that Repaci Jr. was seen leaving the residence before officers arrived and later fled in his vehicle. Deputies stopped him in Indian River County after a vehicle pursuit. Evidence recovered from the home and vehicle, including a firearm and shell casings, was linked to the shootings. Repaci Jr. remained in custody facing homicide charges.
Charges: Two counts of first-degree premeditated murder with a firearm

Title: Man accused of attempted carjackings at Whitehall car wash
description: On April 28, 2026, Whitehall police responded to reports of attempted carjackings at the Moo Moo Express Car Wash on East Main Street. Authorities said Doren Thomas attempted to take multiple vehicles while people were still inside or near them. Police reported that he entered three different vehicles, including one where he allegedly placed the car in reverse while a person was outside. After fleeing the scene, Thomas was pursued by officers on foot. Police said he claimed he was armed during the chase, causing an officer to draw a weapon. Thomas was arrested and booked into Franklin County Jail.
Charges: Robbery; resisting arrest; obstruction of official business

Title: 1 hospitalized, 1 arrested in Loveland beating attack: Court docs
description: Tristen Greatorex, a 21-year-old man from Maineville, Ohio, was arrested after an alleged beating attack in Loveland. Police said the incident occurred at a convenience store on Loveland-Madeira Road and was captured on video. Court records allege Greatorex fought with another man and repeatedly assaulted the victim with his fists. He is accused of causing serious injuries by striking the victim’s head against the pavement, requiring hospitalization. Authorities also stated that Greatorex allegedly threatened to kill the victim during the attack. He was arrested by Loveland police and booked into the Hamilton County Jail.
Charges: Felonious assault and aggravated menacing

Title: Wanted man arrested after hours-long SWAT standoff in Bethel
description: Aaron Abbott, a 41-year-old wanted Clermont County man, was arrested after an hours-long SWAT standoff at an apartment complex on South Street in Bethel, Ohio. Police attempted to arrest Abbott on felony drug possession warrants related to his parole, but he allegedly fled inside the residence and refused to surrender. Officers surrounded the location and Clermont County SWAT responded. Abbott’s girlfriend, Rebecca Sampson, was also inside and later arrested. Police negotiated her exit from the apartment. No injuries were reported, and no firearms were found in Abbott’s possession. Abbott was taken into custody after the standoff ended.
Charges: Felony obstructing, resisting arrest, inducing panic, possession of drugs related to parole violation

Title: Two arrested for allegedly firing flare gun at house multiple times after street fight in Springfield
description: Two men, Kristian Graves and Jason Davis, were arrested after allegedly firing a flare gun multiple times at a house following a street fight at a party in Springfield. Police said a vehicle involved in the incident struck parked cars while fleeing, and witnesses reported seeing flares fired from the vehicle. Officers later stopped the vehicle and found an orange flare gun with fired and live cartridges inside. Both suspects were taken into custody and charged with multiple offenses related to the alleged attack and weapon possession.
Charges: Kristian Graves: Attempted aggravated arson, possession of a dangerous ordinance, carrying concealed weapons, throwing or shooting missiles, leaving the scene of a crash, improper backing. Jason Davis: Attempted aggravated arson, possession of a dangerous ordinance, carrying concealed weapons, throwing or shooting missiles, failure to disclose personal information, falsification.

Title: 2 charged with inciting riot, resisting arrest after party in Lockland, police say
description: On April 23, 2026, Lockland police responded to a large gathering on the 600 block of W. Wyoming Avenue where loud music and blocked sidewalks were reported. Officers asked the group to end the party and clear the area, but police said some individuals refused. Authorities stated that Tremell Jones and Quinton Thomas became aggressive and attempted to encourage others to ignore police orders. When officers attempted to arrest them, both men resisted. Police used less-lethal Pepperball rounds to gain control. The two suspects were arrested and transported to the Hamilton County Justice Center.
Charges: Inciting a riot; disorderly conduct; resisting arrest

Title: After being tased in fight with police, suspect allegedly turned taser on the officer
description: On May 2, 2026, Christopher Kempke was involved in an incident with police in the 4100 block of Shady Grove in Toledo, Ohio. According to police records, when officers informed Kempke that he was under arrest, he attempted to flee on foot. A physical struggle followed between Kempke and an officer. Police stated that Kempke was tased during the confrontation but allegedly grabbed the taser and used it against the officer. Kempke was arrested and later faced multiple charges, including felony assault on a peace officer, resisting arrest, and disorderly conduct. His bail was set at $25,000.
Charges: Felony assault on a peace officer; resisting arrest; disorderly conduct

Title: Domestic incident leads to assault arrest in Urbana
description: A 37-year-old Urbana man, Joshua Boardman, was arrested after a reported domestic assault incident on Washington Ave. in Urbana, Ohio. Police responded around 2:20 a.m. on February 10, 2026, following a domestic disturbance report. According to police, Boardman admitted arguing with the victim and drinking alcohol. He allegedly blocked the doorway, preventing the victim from leaving, and officers observed facial discoloration consistent with being struck. Boardman was also accused of making repeated threats. He was taken into custody and transported to the Tri-County Jail after officers investigated the reported assault and related threats.
Charges: Assault and menacing
Comments: Lacking police intervention during the incident.

Title: Toledo Police arrest 4 people in brutal attack on homeless man caught on camera
description: Cantrelle Henderson, a 20-year-old Toledo man, was arrested in connection with a brutal assault on a 63-year-old homeless man. Police said surveillance video showed four people cornering the victim against a wall and repeatedly punching, kicking, and stomping him. Henderson was identified partly through Crime Stopper tips and an ankle monitor he was wearing during the attack. Investigators used the video, location, and ankle monitor data to place him at the scene. Henderson was arrested for a parole violation and faces an additional assault charge. Three juveniles were also taken into custody in connection with the attack.
Charges: Assault and parole violation
