Title: Arrest made in Montgomery County for aggravated murder suspect
description: D’Angelo Blackburn was arrested in Montgomery County by the Montgomery County Sheriff’s Office and the U.S. Marshals Service Southern Ohio Fugitive Apprehension Strike Team (SOFAST). He was wanted by the Scioto County Common Pleas Court in Portsmouth for alleged involvement in serious crimes. Authorities said Blackburn was facing possible charges including one count of aggravated murder and two counts of murder. The arrest was made on March 18, 2026. No details were provided about the alleged incident that led to the charges.
Charges: Aggravated murder and two counts of murder

Title: Man Arrested for Attempted Murder
description: Leo Palacios, 60, was arrested after deputies responded to a reported shooting on State Road 674 in Wimauma. Authorities said four victims were fishing on a boat in Lake Wimauma when Palacios allegedly shouted at them, went to his residence, retrieved a firearm, and fired multiple shots toward the victims. The shots missed, and no injuries were reported. One victim recognized Palacios, allowing deputies to locate him at his residence. He was arrested and charged with multiple firearm and attempted murder offenses.
Charges: multiple firearm and attempted murder offenses.

Title: 19-year-old accused of DUI and fleeing after crash into mailbox in Lee County
description: A 19-year-old man, Nicholas Bloomston, was accused of driving under the influence after crashing into a mailbox on Twin Palm Drive in Lee County, Florida. According to the Lee County Sheriff's Office, he attempted to flee the scene following the crash but was stopped by a K-9 unit and taken into custody. Neighbors reported being awakened by the presence of multiple sheriff's vehicles, a fire truck, and an ambulance. Residents described the neighborhood as generally safe and said such incidents are uncommon. No injuries, fatalities, or shootings were reported during the incident, and the suspect was arrested without further escalation.
Charges: Driving under the influence (DUI) Fleeing the scene after the crash

Title: Florida sex offender steals car, flees on foot, deputies say
description: Deputies with the Marion County Sheriff's Office located a stolen Nissan Altima being driven by Chad Cordrey on August 1, 2026. When deputies attempted a traffic stop, he fled, leading officers on a pursuit. A sheriff's helicopter monitored the chase while deputies deployed stop sticks, but the suspect continued driving until the vehicle's tires fell off. He abandoned the car and ran into a nearby yard, where deputies found him hiding underneath a vehicle. He was taken into custody without any reported injuries or use of gunfire. Authorities also identified him as a registered sex offender during the incident.
Charges: Grand theft Fleeing/eluding Resisting arrest

Title: Opa-locka man arrested after allegedly fleeing deputies at more than 100 mph on U.S. 1 in Florida Keys
description: Harold Junius Walker, a 41-year-old man from Opa-locka, allegedly fled from Monroe County Sheriff's Office deputies after they attempted to stop his Dodge truck for speeding on U.S. 1 near Mile Marker 29 at approximately 3:00 a.m. Deputies pursued the vehicle as it traveled southbound at speeds exceeding 100 mph. Tire-deflation devices were deployed, but Walker continued driving on flattened tires until stopping near Mile Marker 19. He reportedly refused commands to exit the truck, and deputies forcibly removed him. Authorities said he continued resisting before being arrested. No injuries or shootings were reported during the incident.
Charges: Fleeing officers Resisting lawful arrest Driving without a valid driver's license Excessive speeding Multiple traffic citations

Title: Driver accused of running over 2 at Miami-Dade street takeover arrested, deputies say
description: on June 5, 2026, after deputies went to a residence to serve a felony arrest warrant. Myers had failed to appear in court on charges related to a previous incident involving a stolen truck and a police pursuit. During the search, deputies found him hiding inside the home's air conditioning system air handler behind ductwork in an attempt to avoid arrest. Deputies removed him from the confined space and arrested him without incident. No injuries or use of force involving firearms were reported during the arrest.
Charges: Grand theft Fleeing and eluding Driving with a suspended license Excessive speeding Resisting an officer

Title: Fort Myers man accused of probation violation following 49th arrest
description: Dessie Crawford, 63, was accused of violating probation after authorities said he was involved in another fleeing and eluding incident. Deputies reportedly observed Crawford roll through a stop sign at a busy intersection and attempted to conduct a traffic stop. According to officials, Crawford continued driving for about two miles before stopping at a local business. Authorities said he was operating a vehicle with an expired tag and an indefinitely suspended driver’s license. Crawford was arrested and taken to jail. Officials stated this was his 49th arrest, with previous charges including grand theft, robbery, aggravated assault, and drug-related offenses.
Charges: Probation violation Fleeing and eluding Driving with an expired tag Driving with an indefinitely suspended license

Title: Cape Coral officers arrest man after chase, neighborhood search and drone response
description: Norman Ewart was arrested after Cape Coral police said he fled during a traffic stop and led officers on a chase. Police reported stopping Ewart for reckless driving, but he allegedly drove away. Officers tracked the vehicle’s license plate and later found him leaving a Mercedes-Benz and entering a home on Southeast 26th Terrace. When approached by police, Ewart allegedly refused to cooperate, ran away, and jumped a fence. Officers used drones and searched the neighborhood before locating him hiding in bushes near a home on Southeast 27th Street. Ewart reportedly told police he fled because of an outstanding warrant.
Charges: Fleeing and eluding Reckless driving Driving with a suspended license Other charges pending

Title: Plan hits dead end after Florida man tries to use Uber to escape deputies
description: Emmanuel Ayala, 39, was accused of causing a crash near Glory Days Grill in Hernando County and leaving the scene. Deputies later located his vehicle and attempted a traffic stop, but authorities said Ayala fled. He abandoned the vehicle, removed the license plate, and hid in nearby woods. Deputies used a drone and K-9 unit during the search. Ayala allegedly attempted to escape by requesting an Uber, but the driver alerted deputies. He was found hiding and taken into custody. His children were with him during the incident and were safely released to their mother.
Charges: Fleeing and eluding law enforcement; leaving the scene of a crash involving injuries; child endangerment-related charges; federal probation violation

Title: Stabbing in domestic dispute leads to two Bay County arrests
description: Tyhesha A. Blackwell, 33, was arrested after a domestic dispute in Bay County, Florida, that resulted in a stabbing. Police responded to a parking lot near East 6th Street and MacArthur Avenue close to Ascension Sacred Heart Bay Hospital after a reported altercation. Officers found Blackwell and Jonathan A. Nieves involved in a physical domestic argument. Authorities said Blackwell stabbed Nieves in the hand during the fight. Both individuals were treated for injuries before being taken into custody. Blackwell was charged with domestic aggravated battery, while Nieves was charged with domestic battery.
Charges: Domestic aggravated battery

Title: Port St. Lucie woman accused of throwing acid at deputies, sparking SWAT, HAZMAT response
description: Jadyn Dominique Gary, 22, was arrested after allegedly throwing hydrochloric acid at deputies during a law enforcement response at an apartment complex in Port St. Lucie, Florida. Deputies arrived to serve legal paperwork and found Gary inside a bedroom. According to investigators, she opened the door and threw a liquid substance at two deputies, causing burning sensations and breathing difficulties. Authorities said Gary admitted throwing the acid because she believed the deputies deserved it. The incident led to a SWAT response, hazardous materials team involvement, and evacuation of nearby residents. Gary was taken into custody and hospitalized before booking.
Charges: Two counts of aggravated battery on a law enforcement officer Resisting an officer with violence

Title: Alachua County mother charged after hitting truck carrying 2-year-old daughter, deputies say
description: Anna Lewis, 23, was arrested after Alachua County deputies said she intentionally used her vehicle to strike a pickup truck carrying her 2-year-old daughter. According to the arrest report, Lewis arrived at her parents’ home while intoxicated, where her ex-husband was visiting their child. The father left with the child in his truck because he feared a confrontation. Deputies said Lewis followed the truck and struck the driver’s side with her vehicle. Authorities charged her with aggravated assault for using her vehicle as a deadly weapon and child abuse. No shooting was reported in the incident.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon Child abuse

Title: Updated: Stabbing in Holmes County, law enforcement at the scene
description: Jennifer Darley is accused of stabbing her boyfriend during an altercation at a home on Highway 179 in Holmes County, Florida. According to the Holmes County Sheriff’s Office, the male victim suffered multiple stab wounds to his arm and shoulder. Deputies said Darley initially locked herself inside the residence but later came out and was taken into custody without incident. The victim was transported by Holmes County EMS to a local hospital with non-life-threatening injuries. Darley was arrested and charged with aggravated battery with a deadly weapon following the investigation into the stabbing.
Charges: Aggravated battery with a deadly weapon

Title: Woman facing charges after shooting man at Fort Lauderdale bus bench: Police
description: Shallante Christina Gardner, 34, is accused of shooting a man during a verbal argument at a bus stop in Fort Lauderdale, Florida. According to Fort Lauderdale Police, the incident happened around 9:50 a.m. at a bus bench in the 900 block of Northwest 7th Avenue. Police said Gardner and the victim were involved in an argument before she allegedly shot him. Gardner reportedly fled on foot but was taken into custody nearby while carrying a firearm. The victim was transported to Broward General Medical Center and was expected to survive. Gardner was booked into jail following the incident.
Charges: Aggravated battery; possession of a weapon by a convicted felon; grand theft of a firearm

Title: Woman accused of antisemitic attack on Jewish man at Starbucks inside Miami-Dade Target: "I hate them"
description: Chyvonne Juanita Palmer, 43, of North Miami, Florida, is accused of attacking a Jewish man at a Starbucks inside a Target store in North Miami Beach. According to police, Palmer approached the victim, who was wearing a yarmulke, and allegedly struck him twice with a cellphone. Investigators said she later grabbed a metal chair and raised it as if attempting to strike him while shouting an antisemitic statement. Bystanders intervened before the victim was hit with the chair. Palmer was arrested at the scene and later released after posting bond. She was ordered to undergo a mental health evaluation.
Charges: Aggravated battery; aggravated assault with a deadly weapon with prejudice; disorderly conduct

Title: Broward woman tried to hit boyfriend and 3-year-old daughter with car outside Burlington, Hollywood police say
description: Alexis T. Baber, 22, is accused of attempting to hit her boyfriend and his 3-year-old daughter with a vehicle outside a Burlington store in Hollywood, Florida. According to the Hollywood Police Department, officers responded after receiving reports of a woman trying to strike a man carrying a child. Police said Baber drove over a curb toward the man and toddler during an argument. Officers later conducted a traffic stop on the suspect vehicle after observing it driving erratically. Baber was detained and arrested. She was charged after investigators determined the child was placed in danger during the incident.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill; child neglect

Title: ECSO: Woman Pepper Sprayed Victim, Took Swing With Pink Baseball Bat In Century Assault
description: Alexis Marie Cooper, 27, of Atmore, Alabama, was arrested following an alleged assault at Century Woods Apartments in Century, Florida. According to the Escambia County Sheriff’s Office, Cooper allegedly arrived at a victim’s apartment during a verbal dispute and escalated the confrontation by using pepper spray and swinging a pink baseball bat toward the victim’s head. The victim was sprayed in the face and attempted to defend herself. A witness and a teenage witness reportedly identified Cooper, and the baseball bat was collected as evidence. Cooper was charged and later released on bond.
Charges: Aggravated battery with a deadly weapon Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill

Title: Mother charged with 5-year-old son's homicide after body found in Perdido Bay
description: Jalynda Smith, 36, was arrested in connection with the death of her 5-year-old son in Escambia County, Florida. Authorities reported that the child’s body was recovered from Perdido Bay near Lillian Highway after deputies received concerns from Smith’s sister. The child’s remains were found inside a trash bag, and investigators searched Smith’s apartment as part of the homicide investigation. The exact cause of death was pending medical examiner results. Smith was booked into the Escambia County Jail and charged with aggravated negligent manslaughter of a child. She was held without bond while the investigation continued.
Charges: Aggravated negligent manslaughter of a child

Title: Teen arrested for battery after spitting on deputy during transport
description: Autumn Bellows, 18, of Palm Coast, Florida, was arrested after authorities said she spit on a deputy while being transported to a mental health facility. Deputies initially responded to a report of an intoxicated woman in distress. During transportation, Bellows allegedly became aggressive, escaped her handcuffs, and resisted deputies attempting to restrain her. Authorities said she spit on a deputy, making contact with his face and hair. Deputies then used additional restraints and a spit mask before taking her for medical clearance and transport. Bellows was charged with battery on a law enforcement officer and later released on bond.
Charges: Battery on a law enforcement officer

Title: Police: Woman accused of firing Taser at driver in Allapattah
description: Raeyana Hamilton, 25, was arrested after police alleged she used a Taser to shock a driver while riding as a passenger in his vehicle in Miami, Florida. According to investigators, the victim reported that Hamilton fired the Taser into his neck, causing temporary electrical shock, but he maintained control of the vehicle. The victim stopped the car, confronted Hamilton, and recovered the Taser, which officers later collected as evidence. Hamilton denied using the Taser. Police located and arrested her at a nearby gas station. She was booked into jail and remained in custody on bond.
Charges: Aggravated battery with a deadly weapon

Title: Putnam County sheriff says woman who held boys at gunpoint should have handled accused trespassing differently
description: Baby Hamilton, 68, was arrested after authorities alleged she confronted two boys she believed were trespassing on private property near a pond in Palatka, Florida. Investigators said Hamilton pointed a handgun at the boys, forced them into her vehicle, and drove them to their apartment complex against their will. The children later told their parents what happened, prompting a sheriff’s investigation. Deputies executed a search warrant at Hamilton’s home and recovered a handgun matching the children’s description. Hamilton was arrested and booked into the Putnam County Jail, where she was held without bond.
Charges: Two counts of aggravated assault with a weapon Two counts of kidnapping of a minor

Title: Hendry County deputy accused of domestic violence, attempting to stab victim with screwdriver
description: Susan Kelly, 50, a Hendry County correctional officer, was arrested after deputies responded to a reported domestic violence incident at her home. According to investigators, a verbal argument escalated into a physical confrontation. Authorities said Kelly was armed with a handgun and a screwdriver during the incident and allegedly attempted to stab the victim with the screwdriver, causing injuries to the victim’s hand. Deputies arrested Kelly and charged her with multiple domestic violence-related offenses, including possessing or using a firearm during the commission of a felony. She was later released on bond pending further court proceedings.
Charges: Battery (domestic violence) Aggravated battery (domestic violence) Possession or use of a firearm during the commission of a felony

Title: 21-year-old arrested after accidental shooting
description: Tyron Amon Fred Weatherspoon, 21, was arrested after authorities said he accidentally shot a 17-year-old girl in the leg inside a residence in Lake Placid, Florida. Deputies responded to the home and found the victim, who was later airlifted to a hospital with non-life-threatening injuries. Investigators determined Weatherspoon was handling a pistol when it discharged. After the shooting, he allegedly fled the residence and attempted to hide the firearm before deputies arrived. Officers later located and arrested him nearby and recovered the gun. He was charged with multiple offenses related to the shooting and investigation.
Charges: Aggravated battery Culpable negligence Tampering with evidence

Title: Woman suffers facial fractures, brain bleed in domestic attack: PCSO
description: A 39-year-old Treasure Island man was arrested after allegedly attacking his wife during a domestic violence incident. Authorities stated that the victim suffered serious injuries, including facial fractures, orbital fractures, significant bruising, and a small brain bleed. The injuries required surgery to repair a facial fracture. The suspect was accused of punching, kicking, and dragging the victim’s body during the attack. He was arrested by the Pinellas County Sheriff's Office and was also charged with violating a pre-trial release related to a previous domestic violence case.
Charges: Aggravated battery, false imprisonment, violation of pre-trial release for domestic violence

Title: Man breaks into Indian River Estates home, assaults woman, sheriff’s office says
description: Kalani Gordon, 19, was accused of breaking into a woman’s home in the Indian River Estates Community in Fort Pierce, Florida. Deputies from the St. Lucie County Sheriff’s Office responded around 5:45 a.m. after receiving a burglary report. Investigators said Gordon allegedly entered the residence, assaulted the woman, and fled on foot. Deputies established a perimeter and used a K-9 unit during the search. A shotgun was found in a vacant lot near the home. Gordon was later located at a nearby business and taken into custody. He faces multiple burglary, stalking, weapons, and resisting charges.
Charges: Aggravated stalking; burglary with assault or battery; burglary of a dwelling while armed; fraud and abuse; armed trespassing in a structure or conveyance; resisting an officer without violence

Title: Florida store employee accused of filming under shopper's dress using spider as excuse
description: Johnnie Evans, 18, was arrested after deputies said he secretly recorded underneath a shopper’s dress and touched her at a Winn-Dixie store in Belle Glade, Florida. According to investigators, Evans allegedly approached the woman while pretending to help remove a spider and touched her buttocks while recording the encounter. Surveillance footage reportedly showed him using his phone to record under her dress. Deputies said Evans was later found in a restroom stall attempting to delete images from his phone. His phone was seized as evidence. He faces charges related to digital voyeurism, battery, and evidence tampering.
Charges: Digital voyeurism; battery; tampering with evidence

Title: Armed Trespassing Suspects Identified in Copper Theft
description: William McCrae was arrested after Levy County Sheriff’s Office deputies investigated an armed trespassing and copper theft case in Bronson, Florida. Authorities said property owners found multiple individuals trespassing with trucks on their land. When confronted, McCrae allegedly threatened a person with a shotgun. Investigators later located the vehicles and discovered a concealed copper wire stripping operation containing copper wire, insulation, and equipment. Detectives said McCrae admitted involvement in stealing copper wire from electrical substations in Levy County and nearby areas. He was arrested and charged following the investigation into the theft operation.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon; two counts of grand theft

Title: Woman stabbed, forced into car before hospital trip; Cape Coral man arrested
description: Alexander Ballester was arrested after deputies accused him of stabbing a woman and forcing her into his vehicle in Lee County, Florida. Authorities said the victim arrived at Lee Memorial Hospital on June 8 with a life-threatening stab wound to her abdomen. Investigators initially received a report of an unknown attacker, but later determined Ballester was allegedly involved after inconsistencies appeared in the statements. Deputies said surveillance footage and witness accounts supported the investigation. Ballester was accused of stabbing the woman, threatening her to prevent reporting, and driving her around before taking her to the hospital.
Charges: Aggravated battery; kidnapping

Title: Manatee candidate arrested again after violating release terms, deputies say
description: Tony Barrett, 59, was arrested after deputies accused him of violating pretrial release conditions following a domestic battery arrest in Bradenton, Florida. Authorities said Barrett returned to a home where he was prohibited from being due to a no-contact order involving the victim. Barrett was previously arrested on June 18 after deputies alleged he attacked his ex-girlfriend during an argument, pulling her hair and repeatedly striking her head against the bedroom floor. After the reported violation, he faced additional charges. Barrett was booked again while his original domestic battery case remained pending in court.
Charges: Violating pretrial release conditions; domestic battery
Comments: Lacking action, and avoid famous people.

Title: Woman charged in power tool, knife attacks that occurred hours apart in Miami-Dade: Deputies
description: Latifah Marie Thompson, 32, was arrested after deputies accused her of attacking two people in separate incidents in southwest Miami-Dade within a few hours. Authorities said she allegedly struck a man multiple times in the head with a Sawzall power tool, causing head injuries and a fractured spine. Later the same day, deputies said Thompson stabbed a woman in the back during an altercation using a knife. Investigators located and arrested Thompson the following day. She was booked into the Turner Guilford Knight Correctional Center and faces serious felony charges related to both attacks.
Charges: Attempted felony murder causing injury; Aggravated battery causing great bodily harm with a deadly weapon

Title: 2 arrested after gunfire erupts during road rage incident, crash in Martin County
description: Dashon Henderson, 27, was arrested after a road rage incident in Martin County escalated into gunfire and a vehicle crash. Deputies reported that Henderson and another driver, William Dinardo Jr., became involved in aggressive driving, attempting to pass and block each other. Investigators said Henderson fired a handgun during the confrontation, striking the rear passenger window of Dinardo’s pickup truck. Both vehicles were involved in reckless driving behavior before the crash. Henderson was charged with aggravated assault with a deadly weapon. The case remained under investigation by the Martin County Sheriff’s Office.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon

Suspect Name: Jonna Leigh Kimla; Dillon Jason Hill
Title: Deputies find drug suspects hiding under floor and in closet during raid
description: Deputies with the Okeechobee Narcotics Task Force, DEA, ATF, and Okeechobee County Sheriff’s Office served a probable cause search warrant at a residence in Okeechobee County. The suspects, Jonna Leigh Kimla and Dillon Jason Hill, allegedly refused to leave the home. Deputies entered the residence and found Kimla hiding beneath the floor in an air-conditioning access area and Hill hiding inside a bathroom closet. Both suspects were arrested. Authorities reported finding methamphetamine, controlled substances, firearm ammunition, and drug paraphernalia during the search. The investigation focused on alleged illegal narcotics sales at the residence.
Charges: Possession of Methamphetamine with Intent to Sell; Possession of a Controlled Substance (Clonazepam 1 mg); Possession of a Controlled Substance (Adderall 30 mg); Possession of Drug Paraphernalia; Resisting an Officer Without Violence

Title: What happened before the viral video? Fort Pierce police release additional footage
description: On July 21, 2026, at about 11:47 a.m., Fort Pierce Police officers witnessed 42-year-old Justin Ikeler allegedly shove an adult woman to the ground, threaten her, and raise a water jug in a threatening manner near Seaway Bridge. When officers attempted to detain him, Ikeler allegedly refused commands, pulled away, ran, and assumed a fighting stance. Officers used physical force to subdue him after he continued resisting arrest. The woman declined to press charges, stating Ikeler falsely accused her of stealing his wallet. Ikeler sustained minor abrasions during the arrest and was transported to the St. Lucie County Jail.
Charges: Resisting arrest without violence

Title: Martin County deputy arrested after altercation with 15-year-old daughter
description: On March 12, 2026, Martin County Sheriff's Office Deputy Emmanuel Perez was arrested in Port St. Lucie following a domestic incident involving his 15-year-old daughter. Police said Perez initially reported that his daughter was attempting to run away from home, and officers returned her to the residence. Shortly afterward, another confrontation allegedly became physical. The teenager accused Perez of battering her, leading Port St. Lucie police to investigate and arrest him. Following the arrest, the Martin County Sheriff's Office placed Perez on paid administrative leave pending the outcome of the case. He was charged with domestic battery and child abuse without physical harm.
Charges: Domestic battery Child abuse without physical harm

Suspect Name: Ryan Chase , Michael Chase , Douglas Nipper
Title: At least three arrested at Morgan Wallen concert
description: Three individuals were arrested during a Morgan Wallen concert at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium in Gainesville, Florida. Deputies were approached by two children who alleged that Ryan Chase and Michael Chase touched them inappropriately. However, authorities stated there was insufficient evidence to make arrests based on those allegations. The brothers were arrested after causing a disturbance when deputies approached them and were charged with resisting arrest. Michael Chase also faced a disorderly conduct charge. A third person, Douglas Nipper, was arrested after allegedly causing a disturbance in the stadium, refusing to leave, pushing barriers, and confronting officers.
Charges: Resisting arrest, disorderly conduct

Title: North Carolina man accused of attacking officer and deputy on Marco Island
description: Michael Bonfiglio, 42, of North Carolina, was arrested after police said he crashed his vehicle near Cape Marco Drive and South Collier Boulevard on Marco Island, Florida. Officers responding to the crash reported that Bonfiglio became aggressive and combative. Police said he shoved an officer during the encounter, and later, while being processed at the jail, he allegedly grabbed and shoved a corrections deputy. Bonfiglio was taken into custody and faces charges related to battery and resisting an officer.
Charges: Two charges of battery, resisting an officer

Title: 18-year-old arrested following shooting incident in Gulf County
description: Adam Cooper, an 18-year-old from Wewahitchka, was arrested following a shooting incident in Gulf County, Florida. Authorities said deputies received a report of shots fired in the 100 block of Sycamore Avenue. The victim identified Cooper as the suspect and stated that multiple shots were fired at them, but they were not struck. Deputies located and detained Cooper approximately 10 minutes after receiving the call. Due to the location near local schools, school resource deputies were notified and schools were placed under a precautionary lockdown. Officials said the individuals involved knew each other and there was no public threat.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon
Comments: Lacking police intervention during the incident.

Title: Deputy shot, father and son dead after Baker County domestic violence response, officials say
description: Deputies from the Baker County Sheriff's Office responded to a domestic violence incident at a residence off Harry Rewis Road. Authorities said the suspect had shot a family member before deputies arrived. When officers approached the home, the suspect fired at them, striking Deputy Fisher in the arm and hitting his protective vest. Deputies returned fire, critically injuring the suspect. Marcus Shane Hodges, 36, was pronounced dead at the hospital. Officials said Hodges had also killed his father, Marcus Gene Hodges, 60. The investigation into the circumstances surrounding the shooting remains ongoing.
Charges: No charges filed due to suspect death

Title: Crestview man arrested after high-speed chase from Alabama into Okaloosa County
description: Akeeme Calloway of Crestview, Florida, was arrested after a high-speed vehicle chase that began in Covington County, Alabama, and ended in Okaloosa County, Florida. Deputies reported that Calloway reached speeds of approximately 120 miles per hour during the pursuit. The chase ended when law enforcement performed a PIT maneuver to stop the vehicle. After the crash, Calloway was medically evaluated before being taken to the Okaloosa County Jail. Authorities said he faces multiple charges in Florida and Alabama related to the pursuit, crash, and failure to comply with officers during the incident.
Charges: Aggravated fleeing and eluding; leaving the scene of a crash with injury; resisting an officer without violence; additional charges in Alabama

Title: Broward burglary suspect arrested after confrontation with a homeowner while using his shower, victim says
description: Abraham Recinos was arrested after a series of alleged burglaries in Broward County, Florida. According to authorities, Recinos entered multiple homes, took property, and was involved in a confrontation with a homeowner after entering the victim’s residence and using his shower. The homeowner discovered him inside while Recinos was reportedly holding a gun, leading to a physical struggle in which the homeowner took the weapon. Recinos was later captured by the Broward Sheriff's Office and charged with multiple offenses, including burglary, aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, hitting a service animal, and trespassing.
Charges: Burglary, aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, hitting a service animal, trespass

Title: Man accused of shooting teenager in Collier County arrested after months on the run
description: Pablo Llanes, 19, was arrested in Lee County after being wanted for months in connection with a shooting in Collier County, Florida. Authorities said Llanes was accused of shooting a 17-year-old victim at the Poinciana Apartments on Airport-Pulling Road in April 2026. The victim was injured in the incident, and Llanes allegedly fled before deputies could arrest him. Lee County deputies located and arrested Llanes on July 4, 2026. He was later extradited to Collier County and booked into jail on charges related to the shooting.
Charges: Aggravated battery with a deadly weapon, discharging a firearm in public

Title: Man arrested Wednesday after armed standoff with law enforcement in Suwannee County
description: On January 28, 2026, a domestic dispute in Suwannee County, Florida, escalated into an armed standoff with law enforcement. A victim called 911 after allegedly being beaten and strangled by Jeremy Brogdon and escaping the residence. Deputies responded to the home on the 16200 block of 221st Road, just north of Mayo, where Brogdon remained inside. Officers reported hearing a gun being loaded, and because of prior threats toward law enforcement, the Suwannee County Sheriff's Office deployed its SWAT team. After a brief standoff, deputies took Brogdon into custody without gunfire. He was arrested and booked on felony charges.
Charges: False imprisonment Felony battery by strangulation

Title: 15-year-old charged with attempted murder following shooting in Walton County
description: Cameron Harris, a 15-year-old male, was arrested following a shooting incident in Walton County, Florida. Authorities said the shooting occurred on Stella Drive during what investigators described as an isolated domestic dispute involving people known to each other. One victim suffered non-life-threatening injuries. Following the incident, nearby schools were placed on lockdown as a precaution. Deputies used K-9 teams and a drone unit during the search. Harris was located and taken into custody after running from a wooded area. He was transported to Walton County Jail and faces multiple felony charges related to the shooting.
Charges: Attempted murder, aggravated battery, tampering with a victim, tampering with physical evidence, resisting without violence, possession of a firearm by a minor, criminal mischief

Title: Baker County man charged with attempted murder after shooting shotgun twice at deputy: sheriff’s office
description: Deputies responded to a domestic disturbance on County Road 120 in northeast Sanderson. Authorities said Kenneth Goethe Sr. was seen inside a residence and, after noticing law enforcement outside, allegedly released a dog toward deputies before retrieving a shotgun. Deputies said Goethe pointed the firearm toward them and fired two shots in their direction. With assistance from a family member, deputies were able to subdue, disarm, and arrest Goethe without injuries. He was taken into custody and faces multiple charges related to the shooting and domestic violence incident.
Charges: Attempted second-degree murder of a law enforcement officer, aggravated assault on a law enforcement officer, domestic battery by strangulation, battery (domestic) on a person 65 years of age or older

Title: Lake City shooting suspect who injured 3 remains in jail despite incomplete court records
description: Davario Watkins, 34, was arrested in connection with a shooting in Lake City, Florida, that injured three people. Police said Watkins allegedly shot two men and one woman in a parking lot across from the Encore Lounge and Event Hall early Sunday morning. Two victims were released from the hospital, while the third victim was reported to be improving. Authorities charged Watkins with aggravated battery and hit-and-run for allegedly damaging a vehicle while leaving the scene. Watkins remained in jail with a $1.3 million bond after initial court records incorrectly showed he had been released.
Charges: Aggravated battery Hit-and-run

Title: Man arrested for firing shots at vehicles after bar fight in Dixie County, deputies say
description: Kelton Lazo was arrested after allegedly firing multiple shots at two people following a fight at Charlie’s Bar in Old Town, Florida. Deputies responded to reports of gunfire and investigators said Lazo became involved in a physical altercation with two unidentified men. As the men attempted to leave in their vehicles, Lazo allegedly shot at both vehicles and followed them in his own vehicle. He later crashed into a fence and returned to the bar, where deputies took him into custody. No injuries were reported during the incident. The investigation involved assistance from Cross City Police Department.
Charges: Aggravated assault; shooting a missile into a vehicle; leaving the scene of a crash

Title: Man accused of hitting people with crowbar, drug possession after fight at North Naples bar
description: Mark Ferreira, 43, was arrested after deputies said he attacked people with a crowbar during a fight at Jacks Bait Shack in North Naples, Florida. Witnesses reported that Ferreira approached the bar carrying a crowbar and struck one victim, then hit another person who tried to intervene. Surveillance footage reportedly showed Ferreira holding and swinging the crowbar during the confrontation. Deputies later located Ferreira inside his vehicle near US-41 and Audubon Boulevard. A search reportedly found cocaine, drug paraphernalia, and brass knuckles. Ferreira was taken into custody and faces multiple charges.
Charges: Aggravated battery with a deadly weapon, possession of drug paraphernalia, possession of a weapon by a convicted felon

Title: Homicide suspect arrested in Charlotte County; attempted to shoot deputy
description: Brian Hewson, 51, was arrested in Charlotte County after deputies investigating a burglary-related vehicle incident discovered he had outstanding warrants, including a homicide warrant from Pennsylvania. During the arrest attempt, deputies said Hewson resisted and pulled a concealed firearm, pointing it at a deputy and pulling the trigger. The firearm was loaded but did not fire because there was no round in the chamber. Deputies used tasers to subdue Hewson and secured the weapon. He was arrested and charged with multiple offenses, including aggravated assault on a law enforcement officer and possession of a firearm by a convicted felon.
Charges: Aggravated assault on a law enforcement officer, possession of a firearm by a convicted felon, possession of a controlled substance, resisting with violence, possession of drug paraphernalia

Title: Former NYPD Officer, Ex-Pasco Deputy Arrested on Child Sex Battery, Marijuana Distribution Charges
description: David Agosto, a former New York Police Department officer and former Pasco County Sheriff’s Office deputy, was arrested in Hernando County after investigators alleged he committed multiple child sexual battery offenses. Authorities said the investigation began after a victim reported years of alleged abuse. Detectives also searched Agosto’s residence and reportedly found more than 160 grams of marijuana packaged for distribution. He faces several felony charges related to sexual battery, child molestation, and drug offenses. A judge found probable cause on the charges and set a total bond of $1.6 million for the child-related charges.
Charges: Two counts of Sexual Battery by a Person 18 Years of Age or Older Upon a Child Under 12 Three counts of Sexual Battery by a Person in Familial or Custodial Authority Upon a Child Between 12 and 18 Lewd or Lascivious Molestation Upon a Child Under 12 by an Adult Possession of Marijuana with Intent to Sell Possession of Drug Paraphernalia

Title: DeLand police ID suspect in double shooting of 2 Florida teens
description: Keyan Jayden Rundell, 17, was arrested in Ellenton, Florida, in connection with the fatal shooting of two teenagers in DeLand, Florida. Police said Rundell was wanted for the deaths of Dustin Rose, 19, and Samson Campbell, 18, who were found shot multiple times at an industrial property on July 29, 2026. Authorities stated that Rundell and the victims knew each other and that an altercation occurred before the shooting. A search warrant was executed with assistance from SWAT teams, and investigators recovered evidence believed to connect Rundell to the crime. He was taken into custody by U.S. Marshals.
Charges: Two counts of second-degree murder

Title: Dixie County man arrested after traffic stop, wanted for aggravated battery
description: James Williamson Jr., 46, of Old Town, Florida, was arrested during a traffic stop by Cross City Police officers. Authorities said Williamson was stopped on U.S. Highway 19 because he was driving with an expired vehicle registration. During the stop, officers discovered that he had an active warrant related to an aggravated battery case. Williamson was taken into custody and transported to jail. Police noted that he has prior convictions for assault and criminal mischief. The arrest was based on the outstanding warrant, with the traffic violation leading officers to locate him.
Charges: Aggravated battery

Title: Man wanted on felony charges arrested after multi-day search in Hendry County
description: Yasiel Azcuy Alfonso, 34, was arrested after a multi-day search in Hendry County, Florida. Authorities said he was wanted following allegations of physical violence against a victim. The victim reported that Alfonso repeatedly struck them in the face, threatened to kill them with a knife while displaying a firearm, and threatened children living at the residence. Deputies said he also held the victim against their will before the victim managed to leave and contact law enforcement. After several days of searching, deputies located and arrested Alfonso. He was booked into the Hendry County Jail without bond.
Charges: Robbery - sudden snatching with firearm/weapon; kidnapping - false imprisonment; aggravated battery with a deadly weapon; aggravated battery with intent to commit a felony

Title: Cincinnati police officer punched in head, suspect arrested: court docs
description: Courtney Edwards, 35, of Westwood, Cincinnati, was arrested after allegedly attacking a Cincinnati police officer and another civilian. According to court documents, Edwards struck a police officer in the head with a closed fist while the officer was performing official duties. He was also accused of attacking another man with his hands and feet, causing serious physical injuries. Edwards was taken into custody and is being held without bond at the Hamilton County Jail. He faces felony charges related to assaults on the officer and civilian. Further details about the incident and the officer’s condition were not immediately released.
Charges: Felony assault for striking a police officer; felonious assault

Title: Grand Junction man accused of shooting U.S. marshal faces delayed extradition, DA says
description: Thomas Steffens, a 72-year-old Grand Junction man, was arrested in Florida while wanted on Colorado charges related to alleged sexual assault, drugging, and strangulation. During an arrest attempt near Vero Beach, authorities said Steffens opened fire on law enforcement officers and shot a U.S. marshal. Officers returned fire, and Steffens was shot multiple times before being taken to a hospital alive. He faces attempted murder charges in Florida related to the shooting, along with existing Colorado charges. Officials said extradition to Colorado will likely occur after Florida proceedings are completed.
Charges: Attempted murder Sexual assault charges Felony strangulation Additional assault-related charges

Title: Man arrested after attempted robbery at Indian River County drive-thru convenience store
description: Paul Markay was arrested after an alleged attempted robbery at a drive-thru convenience store in Indian River County. Deputies said the incident began on June 25 when Markay became involved in a dispute with victims and allegedly took a cell phone. Authorities said one victim attempted to recover the phone, leading Markay to exit his truck and physically attack the victims. Surveillance video reportedly showed the altercation. A deputy later conducted a traffic stop on Markay’s pickup truck, and he exited with his hands raised. He was taken into custody and booked on multiple charges.
Charges: Robbery by sudden snatching Felony battery Driving under the influence

Title: Video shows driver pointing gun during I-75 road rage incident, deputies say
description: Jordan Patascher, 29, was arrested after deputies accused him of pointing a handgun at another driver during a road rage incident on Interstate 75 in Hillsborough County, Florida. The incident allegedly occurred in heavy traffic near the U.S. 301 exit, where video showed a driver of a white SUV holding and pointing a firearm toward another vehicle. Investigators said Patascher was identified as the driver and later changed the vehicle’s license plate in an attempt to avoid identification. He was arrested by the Pasco County Sheriff’s Office in connection with the Hillsborough County investigation.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon; possession of a firearm by a convicted felon; driving with a revoked license as a habitual offender
Comments: Lacking police intervention during the incident.

Suspect Name: Sharif Dawud Hale and Larry Martin
Title: 2 Escambia County Corrections officers arrested in connection with inmate assault
description: Sharif Dawud Hale and Larry Martin, two Escambia County Corrections officers, were arrested in connection with an alleged inmate assault at the county jail. Investigators said the incident occurred in March 2026 when the officers entered an inmate’s cell. Hale was accused of physically assaulting the inmate, causing serious injuries that required surgery. Martin was accused of attempting to conceal information about the incident during an investigation. Both officers were arrested on March 25, 2026, and later released. The case involves allegations of excessive force and obstruction related to the handling of an inmate assault investigation.
Charges: Sharif Dawud Hale: Battery, obstructing justice Larry Martin: Obstructing a criminal investigation
Comments: Corrections officers in this county do not wear bodycams, making the case lack action.

Title: UPDATE: Man taken into custody after standoff at Escambia County home
description: Phillip Resmondo, 37, was arrested after a standoff with Escambia County deputies at a home in Ferry Pass, Florida. Deputies initially responded to a criminal mischief complaint involving a man allegedly hitting a stop sign with a baseball bat. When law enforcement arrived, Resmondo reportedly went inside a residence and refused to come out. Authorities said he fired fireworks at deputies during the standoff. SWAT assisted deputies before Resmondo was taken into custody. He was booked into the Escambia County Jail and faces charges related to assaulting emergency personnel and property damage.
Charges: Aggravated assault on an officer/firefighter/EMT, criminal mischief under $200, criminal mischief over $200 and under $1,000

Title: Lee County deputies use grappler device to stop suspect after four-day domestic investigation
description: Ryan Hillaker was arrested by Lee County deputies after a four-day domestic investigation in Lee County, Florida. Deputies said Hillaker threatened to kill a person during an argument in Estero and allegedly took the victim’s phone when they attempted to call 911, throwing it away before leaving the scene. Authorities later located Hillaker’s vehicle and used a grappler device to safely stop the car near the Westbrook Homes community on Three Oaks Parkway. The device helped deputies end the pursuit without a dangerous collision. Hillaker was taken into custody and faces criminal charges related to the incident.
Charges: Obstructing justice; simple assault

Title: Man accused of punching firefighters after pickup crash, then stealing another truck
description: Cesar James, 35, was arrested after allegedly crashing multiple pickup trucks, including one that was reported stolen, and assaulting emergency personnel. Deputies responded to a crash on South Dixie Highway in Lake Worth Beach, where James allegedly became aggressive toward Palm Beach County Fire Rescue personnel and attempted to strike firefighters. He was later accused of threatening deputies at a hospital. The following day, authorities said James was found driving another stolen pickup truck that crashed into a streetlight. Investigators identified him as the driver in both incidents and took him into custody.
Charges: Grand theft of a motor vehicle; battery on a firefighter; corruptly threatening a public servant; intent to threaten violence; driving while license suspended or revoked causing serious bodily injury/fleeing; operating a motor vehicle with revoked license

Title: Cary police officer arrested in Florida after allegedly slamming woman to ground, repeatedly stomping on her face
description: On March 1, 2026, Jeremy T. Dutton, a Cary Police Department detective, was arrested in Sarasota, Florida, after an alleged assault outside Gateway Live bar. Deputies responded to a battery call and found a woman who reported that Dutton grabbed her, slammed her to the ground, and stomped on her face twice, causing her to briefly lose consciousness. Witnesses also reported seeing the attack. Deputies said Dutton appeared intoxicated and resisted being detained. Bystanders assisted deputies in restraining him. The victim was taken to a hospital with facial injuries. Dutton later resigned from the Cary Police Department.
Charges: Felony battery Resisting arrest

Suspect Name: Walfre Barrios Ozorio; Walter Barrios Ozorio
Title: 2 brothers arrested after standoff in Lake County, deputies say
description: Two brothers, Walfre Barrios Ozorio and Walter Barrios Ozorio, were arrested after a standoff at a residence in Fruitland Park. Lake County deputies responded to Sunnyside Drive after reports of two barricaded suspects, with one allegedly threatening a neighbor with a firearm. Deputies evacuated nearby residents and a negotiator contacted the suspects. Walfre surrendered and was taken into custody by Lake County deputies. Walter was also arrested after remaining inside the residence. The incident involved an armed threat and a law enforcement response, but no shooting between deputies and suspects was reported.
Charges: Walfre Barrios Ozorio: aggravated assault with a firearm, resisting arrest without violence, improper exhibition of a firearm Walter Barrios Ozorio: resisting arrest without violence

Title: Okaloosa County deputies arrest man after alleged lewd act, assault
description: On July 8, 2026, deputies with the Okaloosa County Sheriff's Office responded to a report of indecent exposure near Third Avenue and Johnson Street in Holt, Florida. According to authorities, they found 31-year-old Xavier Stachowiak allegedly committing a lewd act while lying on the ground. When a deputy attempted to arrest him, Stachowiak allegedly resisted, tried to strike the deputy with his elbow, and attempted to spit on the deputy. He was taken into custody and booked into the Okaloosa County Jail on charges including battery on a law enforcement officer, resisting an officer with violence, exposure of sexual organs, and disorderly intoxication.
Charges: Three counts of battery on a law enforcement officer One count of resisting an officer with violence Two counts of exposure of sexual organs One count of disorderly intoxication

Title: Crestview man held on murder charge in connection to body found on Taylor Rd.
description: Authorities in Okaloosa County arrested 20-year-old Kavari McQueen in connection with a fatal shooting that occurred on Wednesday. Investigators said McQueen and the victim were inside a vehicle when they became involved in an altercation. During the confrontation, gunshots were fired, resulting in the victim's death. According to deputies, McQueen left the scene in the vehicle after the shooting. Investigators identified him as the suspect and took him into custody at approximately 5:30 p.m. the same day. He was booked into the Leon County Jail and is being held on an open count of murder while the investigation continues.
Charges: Open count of murder

Title: Coral Springs Crime Blotter: Scam Victim Loses $44,000; Assaults, Thefts Also Reported
description: Jose Manuel Sanchez was arrested by the Coral Springs Police Department on August 1, 2026, for aggravated assault with a deadly weapon. The incident was included in a weekly crime report covering multiple offenses in Coral Springs. The report did not provide additional details about the circumstances of the aggravated assault, the identity of the victim, the weapon involved, or the location of the incident. The arrest was one of several arrests made by police during the reported period. Sanchez remained accused of the offense following his arrest.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon

Title: Drug deal turned robbery leads to shooting; 6 arrested
description: Police arrested six suspects following a shooting that investigators said resulted from a drug deal that turned into an armed robbery at Gilmore Park in Chipley, Florida. Authorities received reports of gunshots on June 2 and later used surveillance audio and video to identify the location and suspects involved. Investigators said buyers attempted to rob sellers during a marijuana transaction, leading to gunfire as vehicles left the area. Seven people were believed to be involved, with six arrested and one additional suspect still being sought. Charges included armed robbery, conspiracy, marijuana sale, and firing a weapon in public.
Charges: Samuel Baxley — robbery with a firearm Quicky Brundidge — criminal attempt to solicit/conspire third-degree felony and marijuana sale Landon Hall — robbery with a firearm Khmari Massaline — robbery with a firearm Marley Medley — criminal attempt to solicit/conspire third-degree felony and marijuana sale Omzavious Peacock — firing a weapon in public
Comments: Lacking police intervention during the incident.

Title: ‘Feared for their lives:’ Water gun sparks shooting scare near Denny’s restaurant in Cocoa Beach
description: Police responded to an armed disturbance at a Denny’s restaurant parking lot in Cocoa Beach. According to the arrest affidavit, Talan Hall became involved in an argument with a group of juveniles riding e-bikes. After an escalation, Hall allegedly picked up and slammed a shopping cart, then later displayed what appeared to be a black pistol toward the group. The weapon was later identified as a water gun. The juveniles stated they believed the weapon was real and feared for their lives. Hall was arrested and charged after the incident.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill; Improper exhibition of a dangerous weapon
Comments: Lacking police intervention during the incident.

Title: Cocoa police apprehend teen after brief pursuit ends in multiple crashes
description: Police identified 18-year-old Kamari Duncan as the suspect in a brief vehicle pursuit that ended in multiple crashes on Merritt Island. Officers first observed Duncan driving recklessly near Peachtree Street and South Wilson Avenue. When police attempted a traffic stop near U.S. 1 and King Street, Duncan allegedly fled. The pursuit was discontinued due to dangerous driving, but police said Duncan continued and crashed into multiple vehicles. After the crashes, Duncan and two passengers fled on foot. Duncan later surrendered to a Cocoa Police K-9 officer and was taken into custody.
Charges: Aggravated fleeing; Driving with a suspended license; Additional traffic-related charges

Title: Bodycam shows arrest of accused minivan thief in Lake County
description: James Siegfried, 30, was arrested after allegedly stealing a family’s minivan from a gas station in the Clermont area. Deputies responded after a caller reported a suspect entering a vehicle and taking the van. A family member attempted to stop the theft and was allegedly struck multiple times by the suspect. Authorities tracked the vehicle using a cellphone left inside and used a Clermont police drone to monitor its location. The van became stuck in a wooded area near Lake Louisa Road. A Lake County Sheriff’s Office K-9 located Siegfried, and deputies arrested him.
Charges: Possession of a firearm during the commission of an offense; Grand theft of property ($5,000 to $10,000); Aggravated battery with a deadly weapon; Possession of less than 20 grams of marijuana; Possession of a firearm by a convicted felon; Criminal mischief with property damage; Resisting an officer without violence (2 counts); Fleeing and eluding law enforcement; Driving while license suspended (habitual offender) (2 counts); Possession of a controlled substance (methamphetamine); Grand theft of a motor vehicle

Title: Police: Pinellas County deputies kill armed man who broke into woman's home, attacked her
description: Adam Charles Siauciunas, 39, was fatally shot by Pinellas County deputies after allegedly breaking into a woman’s Clearwater home and attacking her with a knife. The woman escaped and called 911 after fighting him off. Deputies responded to the home and attempted to get Siauciunas to surrender. After entering the residence and clearing rooms, deputies encountered him in the garage. Police said Siauciunas pointed a firearm at deputies while holding a flashlight, causing officers to open fire. He was pronounced dead shortly afterward. No deputies were injured during the incident.
Charges: No charges filed due to suspect death

Suspect Name: Noel Marsh III , Nigel Charleak Carleston
Title: Shooting victim arrested in connection with Clearwater ‘teen takeover’ as police issue 6 warrants for rioting
description: A large “teen takeover” gathering at Clearwater Beach on May 31, 2026, resulted in a shooting, riot-related investigation, and multiple arrest warrants. Clearwater Police reviewed digital evidence and identified five juveniles and one adult accused of participating in riotous behavior. A 17-year-old shooting victim was later arrested after investigators said he was also involved in the disturbance. Police arrested Noel Marsh III, 16, on charges including attempted second-degree murder and firearm offenses. Another 17-year-old suspect from Brandon was arrested after allegedly fleeing with a concealed firearm. Authorities continued searching for additional suspects connected to the event.
Charges: Attempted second-degree murder, firearm possession offenses, rioting-related charges

Title: Man who said he wasn’t afraid of battery charge now faces one after allegedly punching deputy
description: Marcus Antonio Austin, 30, was arrested after deputies responded to a mental health call at a Pensacola residence. According to the Escambia County Sheriff’s Office, deputies were attempting to detain Austin under a Baker Act complaint when he allegedly became uncooperative and punched a deputy in the face with a closed fist. The strike reportedly damaged the deputy’s prescription glasses and caused injury. Austin was taken into custody at the scene and transported to the Escambia County Jail. He was charged with battery on a law enforcement officer, a felony offense under Florida law.
Charges: Battery on a law enforcement officer

Title: Aggravated Battery Arrest - Mobil Gas Station
description: DeAndre Randolph, 29, was arrested after an altercation at a Mobil Gas Station parking lot in St. Petersburg, Florida. Police said Randolph and Anthony Oliver, 41, were involved in a verbal dispute shortly after 1 a.m. Randolph allegedly struck Oliver over the head with a cinder block during the confrontation. Oliver then fired a gun at Randolph. Both men suffered non-life-threatening injuries and were transported to Orlando Health Bayfront Hospital. Randolph was arrested and charged with aggravated battery with a deadly weapon. Oliver was separately arrested on firearm and controlled substance charges related to the incident.
Charges: Aggravated Battery with a Deadly Weapon
Comments: Lacking police intervention during the incident.

Title: Man arrested in Hillsborough County accused of forcing ambulance to crash into utility pole
description: Johnny Arman, 35, was arrested after authorities said he followed an ambulance transporting a patient, blocked its path, and caused it to crash into a utility box and utility pole in Hillsborough County, Florida. According to the sheriff’s office, Arman became hostile toward first responders at a residence and later pursued the ambulance after it left. Deputies said he drove toward the ambulance near Upper Creek Drive and Galen Court, forcing the driver off the road. The crash caused significant infrastructure damage, while paramedics, the patient, and others were placed at risk during the incident.
Charges: Aggravated battery on a firefighter (2 counts) Aggravated battery with a deadly weapon Unlawfully impede, threaten, or harass a first responder (2 counts)
Comments: Good story, but lacking police intervention.

Title: TikTok argument led to Miami shooting that left woman hurt, another arrested, cops say
description: Celia Penichet Lopez, 41, was arrested after police said a TikTok-related dispute led to a shooting in Miami. Authorities responded to a ShotSpotter alert and found a woman suffering from a gunshot wound to her leg. Investigators said an argument between groups began after conflicts on TikTok Live. Surveillance footage reportedly showed Penichet Lopez firing a weapon before another person returned fire, injuring the victim. Police said Penichet Lopez admitted she fired first after initially claiming the other person shot first. The victim was hospitalized in stable condition following the incident.
Charges: Aggravated battery with a weapon causing bodily harm

Suspect Name: Everette Krichbabum and James Tristian Gay
Title: Two men arrested after machete fight in Publix parking lot, police say
description: Two men, Everette Krichbabum and James Tristian Gay, were arrested after a machete fight in a Publix parking lot in Panama City, Florida. Police said a verbal argument between the men escalated into a physical confrontation involving fixed-blade weapons. Investigators said Gay confronted Krichbabum over alleged prior harassment and later grabbed a machete after seeing Krichbabum with a hatchet. Both men suffered injuries during the struggle and were taken to a hospital. Authorities charged both men with aggravated battery with a deadly weapon.
Charges: Aggravated Battery with a Deadly Weapon
Comments: Lacking police intervention during the incident.

Title: Nebraska running back arrested in Florida on aggravated battery charge
description: Mekhi Nelson, a 20-year-old Nebraska football running back, was arrested in Key West, Florida, on an aggravated battery charge involving a pregnant woman. Authorities provided limited details about the alleged assault. Nelson was taken into custody by police and was scheduled for arraignment in court. The incident occurred in June 2026, and the Key West Police Department was asked for additional information regarding the allegations. Nelson remained listed on the Nebraska football roster at the time of the report.
Charges: Aggravated Battery Involving a Pregnant Woman

Title: Officer on leave after video shows punch of handcuffed suspect
description: A Daytona Beach Police officer was placed on administrative leave after body camera footage showed the officer punching David Anderson while he was handcuffed during an arrest related to an open-container warning. The incident began when Anderson was told to dispose of a tequila bottle or face arrest. Video shows Anderson throwing a bottle cork at the officer before being detained. During the struggle, Anderson was taken to the ground and later restrained with handcuffs. Police Chief Jakari Young said the officer’s actions were concerning and emphasized the importance of de-escalation. The incident is under review by the department.
Charges: Open container violation (reported); other charges unknown

Title: Manhunt widens as US Marshals boost reward to $16K for Florida murder suspect on the run
description: Isabelle Johnson, 38, is wanted in connection with the death of Jason Christopher Coulthart, 43, in Walton County, Florida. Authorities say Coulthart was reported missing from Niceville on May 24, and investigators later discovered human remains buried in a shallow grave on a Freeport property. DNA testing confirmed the remains belonged to Coulthart. Johnson was identified as a murder suspect and remains at large. Multiple law enforcement agencies in Florida, Georgia, and Alabama are searching for her. Several other individuals have been arrested for allegedly assisting Johnson after the killing, including providing shelter and transportation.
Charges: Open count of murder

Title: Driver faces life sentence in deadly Casselberry crash that killed two brothers
description: Marquavious Tayvon Wheaton allegedly fled from Seminole County deputies during an attempted traffic stop connected to a suspected drug trafficking investigation. He drove at speeds exceeding 100 mph, weaving through traffic and running red lights before crashing into another vehicle on U.S. Highway 17-92 in Casselberry. The crash killed brothers Christopher Marier and Tyler Marier. Wheaton survived with minor injuries and was taken into custody. Prosecutors charged him with two counts of second-degree murder, alleging he acted with a depraved mind and disregard for human life during the dangerous pursuit.
Charges: Two counts of second-degree murder, fleeing and eluding, excessive speed, violation of probation, unlawful window tint related stop

Title: A Cape Coral police officer is arrested, accused of battering spouse
description: On March 27, 2026, Cape Coral Police Department officers responded to a disturbance involving off-duty police officer Timothy Allen. During the investigation, authorities determined that Allen allegedly battered his spouse. Allen was arrested and later placed on administrative leave by the Cape Coral Police Department pending an internal investigation. Police Chief Anthony Sizemore stated that officers are held to high professional standards and that no one is above the law. Additional details about the incident, including the circumstances of the alleged battery and court proceedings, were not released at the time of the report.
Charges: Battery (domestic violence)

Title: Florida teens caught riding on top of SUV going 40 mph, cited; police say
description: A 19-year-old man, Gary Mathurin, was arrested in Belle Isle, Florida, after police said he drove an SUV while multiple people were riding on the roof and hanging from the vehicle. Officers reported the SUV was traveling approximately 40–45 mph during the late-night incident. Police said the vehicle was stopped after an officer observed the unsafe behavior. A search reportedly found a bottle of whiskey, a handgun, and a bag containing a pipe inside the vehicle. The driver was arrested and cited, while the individuals riding on the vehicle were also issued citations and released.
Charges: Reckless driving; citations for allowing passengers to ride on top of the vehicle

Title: Marion County man beats up 2 teens during argument over riding ATVs in neighborhood, deputies say
description: Sheriff’s deputies arrested Ivan Sobal, 42, after he allegedly confronted two teenagers riding ATVs in a Marion County neighborhood. Authorities said Sobal walked from his property and argued with the teens before grabbing one victim by the hair and neck, punching him in the face, and kicking him. He then allegedly punched the second teenager. Deputies observed injuries including bruising and a bloody nose. The victims were 14 and 15 years old. Sobal was booked into the Marion County Jail on child abuse and battery by strangulation charges.
Charges: Child abuse Battery by strangulation

Title: Suspect arrested after armed standoff in Suwannee County
description: Daniel Martinez was arrested after an armed standoff in Suwannee County, Florida. Deputies said Martinez barricaded himself inside a home after an argument where he allegedly threatened people. Authorities believed he was armed with a handgun and several knives. Deputies used a drone to enter the residence through a window and determine Martinez’s location before safely making the arrest. The drone assistance helped deputies resolve the situation without reported injuries. Martinez was taken into custody and booked into jail following the standoff.
Charges: aggravated assault

Title: Bodycam video shows arrest of softball player accused of hitting opponent with bat in Aventura
description: On June 21, 2026, during a softball league game at Waterways Park in Aventura, Florida, police said a verbal dispute between teams escalated into a physical confrontation. Authorities alleged that Roberto Araujo, 41, grabbed a metal bat and struck another player, William Rodriguez, in the back of the head. Aventura police responded to the scene, investigated the incident, and later arrested Araujo. Body camera footage showed officers taking him into custody. The suspect was charged with aggravated battery with a deadly weapon. No shooting occurred, and the incident involved an alleged assault during a sports-related altercation.
Charges: Aggravated battery with a deadly weapon
Comments: Lacking police intervention during the incident.

Title: Massachusetts man assaults woman, 62, at Aventura bus stop for refusing sex, cops say
description: According to police, Wetsmy Louicius, 25, was arrested after allegedly attacking a 62-year-old woman at the Aventura Mall Transit Bus Depot in Aventura, Florida. Authorities said the suspect approached the victim while she waited for a bus and asked for sex. After she refused, he allegedly punched her in the face, causing serious injuries including multiple facial fractures. Surveillance footage helped investigators identify and track him. Police said he was also linked to previous alleged attacks in Boston. Louicius was taken into custody and charged with aggravated battery. The victim received medical treatment following the violent unprovoked bus stop attack.
Charges: Aggravated battery
Comments: Lacking police intervention during the incident.

Title: Man dubbed 'Tequila Bandit' accused of liquor theft, later arrested for DUI
description: Michael Ruiz, 31, was identified by the Martin County Sheriff's Office as the suspect known as the "Tequila Bandit." Investigators allege Ruiz stole multiple bottles and cases of alcohol from a retail store after surveillance video showed him placing tequila bottles into a backpack and removing additional cases from a back room. After the theft investigation began, Ruiz was later stopped in St. Lucie County on suspicion of driving under the influence. Deputies identified him as the theft suspect and arrested him. Authorities believe Ruiz may be connected to other liquor thefts in the area.
Charges: Liquor theft charges and DUI

Title: 17-year-old charged as adult after shooting at 14-year-old girl’s home twice, Seminole County deputies say
description: Zebron Trenton Biggs, 17, was arrested and charged as an adult after authorities accused him of shooting at a 14-year-old girl’s home on two separate occasions. Investigators said Biggs admitted to firing shots at the residence because he believed the girl had lied about her age and said he did not want to have a baby with her. Surveillance footage reportedly showed a vehicle connected to Biggs near the home before gunshots were heard. The shootings occurred on May 22 and May 24, 2026. No one was injured, and Biggs was taken into custody.
Charges: Two counts of attempted first-degree premeditated murder

Title: Teen arrested in deadly shooting of 4-year-old boy at Orlando apartment complex, police say
description: Brandon Sir Nevaeh McCloud, 18, was arrested in connection with the fatal shooting of a 4-year-old boy at the Stella West Apartments in Orlando. Police said officers responded on July 17, 2026, after reports of a shooting and found the child suffering from a gunshot wound. The child was transported to Arnold Palmer Hospital but later died from his injuries. Investigators determined McCloud was handling a firearm in a careless manner when the shooting occurred. McCloud was taken into custody by the Orlando Police Fugitive Task Force and faces a manslaughter charge.
Charges: Manslaughter

Title: Oviedo man faces aggravated assault charge after HOA dispute turns violent
description: John Etzler was arrested after a dispute with a homeowners association turned violent in Oviedo, Florida. According to the Seminole County Sheriff’s Office, Etzler entered the Palm Valley subdivision community office to discuss HOA violations related to his property. During the interaction, he allegedly pulled out a handgun and pointed it at the community manager. The manager reportedly pushed the gun away and fled for safety. Deputies later arrested Etzler at his home. He was charged with aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill and was ordered not to possess firearms.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill

Title: ‘Profound loss’: Florida communications officer killed in murder-suicide, officials say
description: Ralph Varela Sr. was identified as the suspect in a murder-suicide that resulted in the death of Palm Beach County Sheriff’s Office Communications Officer Elizabeth “Liz” Ortega. The incident occurred at Ortega’s home in Port St. Lucie, Florida. Investigators said Varela allegedly shot Ortega multiple times while she attempted to flee into the front yard. Ortega was transported to a hospital where she was pronounced dead. Responding officers later found Varela deceased inside the home from an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound. The case was investigated as a domestic-related shooting and murder-suicide.
Charges: No charges filed (suspect died)
Comments: Lacking police intervention during the incident.

Title: Santa Rosa County teenager charged with allegedly killing his girlfriend
description: Dominic Wasshenova was arrested and charged in connection with the alleged murder of his girlfriend, Azalia Dotson-Salinas, in Santa Rosa County, Florida. Deputies responded to a residence on Floridale Drive after the victim’s mother became concerned about not hearing from her daughter. Authorities found Dotson-Salinas deceased from a gunshot wound caused by a pistol. Investigators said Wasshenova was arrested in Athens, Alabama, and was being extradited back to Santa Rosa County. Officials stated the couple had recently moved to the area and had no prior reported incidents. He faces a homicide-related charge.
Charges: Murder dangerous depraved without premeditation

Title: Man accused of pointing gun at people at Port Charlotte Beach Park
description: Deputies responded to Port Charlotte Beach Park after reports of a man with a gun. Investigators allege Daniel Arnot pointed a Springfield Echelon 9mm handgun at several people, including a fisherman and others at the park. In one encounter, a witness said Arnot pulled the trigger, but the gun only clicked and did not fire. Investigators also allege he threatened another person and later resisted deputies during his arrest. Arnot requested an attorney and declined to provide a statement. No injuries were reported in the incident.
Charges: Four counts of aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill; one count of resisting an officer without violence

Title: Two men charged after machete, hatchet fight outside Florida Publix
description: On August 4, 2026, James Tristan Gay allegedly confronted Everette Eric Krichbaum in a Publix parking lot in Panama City. Police said Gay approached Krichbaum aggressively, returned to his vehicle, retrieved a machete, and re-engaged him. Krichbaum displayed a hatchet, and the two men struggled over the weapons. According to investigators, Gay struck Krichbaum in the face with the sheathed machete and later struck him in the head, causing him to lose consciousness. Surveillance video reportedly supported the investigation. Both men suffered non-life-threatening injuries and were charged in connection with the fight.
Charges: Aggravated battery with a deadly weapon

Title: Repeat road rage driver accused of pulling gun on motorists: 'They gamble with lives,' chief says
description: On July 31, 2026, police responded to reports of a reckless driver near Education Way and North State Street in Bunnell. Two motorists told police that a Hyundai Tucson driver, identified as Joshua Alexander Walker, was swerving between lanes and allegedly pointed a handgun at them when they passed him. Flagler County deputies later located Walker's vehicle traveling south on U.S. 1 near Old Dixie Highway and pulled him over. Deputies reportedly found several firearm magazines inside the vehicle. A subsequent search warrant resulted in the recovery of a 9mm handgun and three loaded magazines.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill

Title: Gainesville man arrested for allegedly fleeing from deputies and ramming patrol vehicle
description: Fredrick Tyrone Perryman Jr., 24, was arrested on June 5, 2026, after deputies attempted to stop him because of active warrants from Volusia and Polk counties. Deputies said Perryman fled in a Mercedes SUV after seeing marked patrol vehicles with lights and sirens activated. An unmarked deputy vehicle was positioned behind him, and Perryman allegedly intentionally rammed it before being boxed in by additional patrol vehicles. He was arrested after exiting the SUV. Deputies reportedly found about 67 grams of marijuana, sandwich bags, and an electronic scale inside. He was also booked on two outstanding warrants.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon; fleeing with lights and sirens active; possession of marijuana with intent to sell; driving without a valid license; possession of drug paraphernalia; plus active warrants

Title: Alachua County felon arrested after attacking pregnant woman, deputies say
description: James Ivey III, 42, was arrested after deputies said he attacked a pregnant woman during a verbal argument on Sunday night. According to the Alachua County Sheriff’s Office, the argument became physical when Ivey allegedly threw the woman onto a vehicle, causing the windshield to shatter. Ivey reportedly left the scene after the alleged attack. Deputies canvassed the surrounding area and subsequently located and arrested him. He was booked into the Alachua County Jail on a $75,000 bond. Authorities said Ivey is a convicted felon with prior convictions including assault and grand theft auto. The report does not mention firearms or any exchange of gunfire.
Charges: Aggravated battery on a pregnant woman

Title: 1 arrested for manslaughter in connection to deadly Milton shooting
description: On January 10, 2026, at approximately 2:50 a.m., Santa Rosa County Sheriff’s Office deputies responded to Galahad Trail in Milton after a reported shooting.
