Deputies found 21-year-old Tyler James Caraway-Appleby suffering from a gunshot wound. He was pronounced dead at the scene. Investigators determined that 21-year-old Cameron Rayshaun Keys was in possession of the firearm when it discharged and struck Caraway-Appleby. Keys was subsequently arrested and charged with manslaughter in connection with the fatal shooting. The report does not state that police exchanged gunfire with Keys, that Keys was shot, or that a vehicle pursuit or traffic stop occurred during the incident.
Charges: Manslaughter

Title: Gainesville man arrested for attacking roommates with large knife on New Year’s Day, deputies say
description: Thomas Sanford, 44, was arrested after deputies responded to a reported stabbing at a home on Southeast 45th Terrace during the early morning hours of New Year’s Day. Deputies said Sanford argued with a female roommate and threatened to kill everyone in the home. He allegedly grabbed a large kitchen knife, and when a male resident attempted to defend the woman, Sanford cut the man’s leg with the knife and threw him onto a table. When deputies arrived, Sanford reportedly refused orders to leave his room. An agency K9 was deployed and restrained him. Sanford was taken to a hospital before being booked into the Alachua County Jail.
Charges: Aggravated battery with a deadly weapon; felony battery with prior convictions; resisting without violence

Title: Man arrested on attempted murder charges after car found in Merritt Island canal
description: On April 6, 2026, customers at a KFC in Merritt Island reported a possible battery incident involving a man and a woman inside a white vehicle. Deputies from the Brevard County Sheriff's Office said 43-year-old John Lucas was seen beating the woman in the passenger seat. When deputies arrived, Lucas allegedly rammed his vehicle into a patrol car and fled, leading officers on a chase. The pursuit ended when his vehicle flipped over in a canal. Lucas was arrested and faces charges including attempted murder, kidnapping, and fleeing law enforcement. The woman's condition was not immediately known, and authorities had not explained how the vehicle entered the canal.
Charges: Attempted murder, kidnapping, fleeing law enforcement

Title: Cocoa man, 25, charged with beating woman, shooting man in break-in
description: On March 10, 2026, 25-year-old Brytton Dane Hurd targeted a home in the 2000 block of Amallfi Drive in Cocoa, Florida. Hurd kicked open a bedroom door inside the residence and confronted a 32-year-old woman with whom he shared a past relationship, along with her 33-year-old male acquaintance. During the violent home invasion, Hurd struck the woman in the head, knocking her down, before turning a pistol on the man and shooting him in the lower abdomen. Hurd then pistol-whipped the wounded victim and threatened his life before fleeing the scene.
Charges: Attempted first-degree murderAggravated battery with a firearmBurglary with assault or battery

Title: Florida man accused of chasing person with knife in Cocoa Beach 7-Eleven
description: On January 6, 2026, around 10:00 p.m., 48-year-old Joshua Hunt entered a 7-Eleven convenience store in Cocoa Beach, Florida. Hunt confronted a male store employee whom he was court-ordered to avoid following a previous motorcycle theft conviction. During a physical dispute, Hunt pulled out a knife that was hanging around his neck and pointed it at the worker. Hunt chased the employee throughout the store and followed him behind the front counter while a second employee called emergency services. Law enforcement tracked Hunt down two days later and took him into custody without incident.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weaponFelony violation of probation

Title: Miramar man arrested after five‑hour SWAT standoff
description: On January 2, 2026, Miramar police responded to a home on Juniper Street regarding a mental health call involving 27-year-old Styvens Jean. Upon the arrival of law enforcement officers, Jean barricaded himself inside the residence while armed with a knife. After initial police attempts to establish contact with him failed, a specialized SWAT tactical unit was deployed to surround the property. Following an extensive five-hour negotiation process with the barricaded individual, Jean surrendered to the tactical team without further escalation and was placed onto a medical stretcher to be taken into custody.
Charges: Aggravated assaultSimple battery
Comments: Don't know if we want standoff cases.

Title: Sunrise police: Man in search of a job ends up enraged and in handcuffs after hurting woman
description: On April 6, 2026, 28-year-old Ralph Estinord visited a Burger King restaurant located inside the Sawgrass Mall food court in Sunrise, Florida, while looking for employment. Estinord became highly enraged when he was informed that he could not speak directly with the restaurant's manager. During the subsequent verbal altercation with a female employee, Estinord picked up a heavy metal container intended for holding straws and threw it directly at her face. The impact inflicted a laceration on her lip and knocked out one of her teeth. Sunrise police officers responded and apprehended him.
Charges: Aggravated assault

Title: BSO: Man arrested in Dania Beach attack that left mother, 8-year-old girl wounded
description: On January 14, 2026, Broward Sheriff's Office deputies responded to a stabbing report at a residential home located in the 4500 block of Southwest 23rd Terrace in Dania Beach, Florida. Investigators determined that 31-year-old Daquan Delancy became embroiled in a severe domestic argument with a woman. During the confrontation, Delancy assaulted her and threatened to stab her. An eight-year-old girl present at the scene sustained a significant cut to her hand during the attack. The victims traveled to Memorial Regional Hospital in Hollywood for treatment, where responding deputies located and took Delancy into custody.
Charges: Attempted murderAggravated battery with a deadly weaponAggravated assault with a deadly weaponAggravated child abuseChild neglect with great bodily harmChild neglect without great bodily harm

Title: Man facing murder charge after crashing into canal while fleeing, killing passenger, BSO says
description: On March 22, 2026, Michael Malik Harvey was spotted driving a stolen GMC van recklessly in West Park, Florida. When a Broward Sheriff's Office deputy attempted a traffic stop, Harvey rammed the patrol vehicle and fled. During the subsequent multi-agency pursuit, Harvey intentionally steered the van toward a Pembroke Pines police officer, forcing them to take evasive action. Harvey then drove the wrong way into a Fort Lauderdale RV park, crashed through a metal gate, and plunged into a canal. Law enforcement pulled Harvey and a female passenger from the submerging van. The female passenger was later pronounced dead at the hospital.
Charges: Felony murder Aggravated fleeing and eluding causing death Aggravated assault on a law enforcement officer Grand theft of a motor vehicle Leaving the scene of a crash involving an occupied vehicle

Title: Broward Sheriff's deputy fired after arrest for alleged sexual battery, BSO says
description: On March 16, 2026, 25-year-old Edwin Horace, a probationary detention deputy with the Broward Sheriff's Office, attended a house party in Deerfield Beach, Florida. During the gathering, a female guest reported that Horace forced her into a non-consensual sexual encounter. Horace initially claimed the contact was completely mutual, but investigators established probable cause to arrest him the following day. As detectives continued their inquiry into the party's events, they identified a second female victim. This discovery led to additional allegations involving an off-duty pattern of physical restriction, choking, and multiple separate instances of physical battery.
Charges: Sexual battery (two counts)False imprisonment (two counts)Strangulation dating violenceTouch or strike battery (two counts)

Title: Shots fired in Calhoun County; suspect charged with assault
description: On April 5, 2026, Calhoun County Sheriff's Office deputies responded to a report of shots fired near Goodman Road and Grace Peacock Road. Their investigation revealed that William Ronnie Johnson had engaged in a verbal altercation with the complainant. Following the argument, Johnson pursued the victim in a vehicle and fired two rounds from a handgun in their direction near State Road 71 South. The victim was not harmed and successfully escaped into a nearby wooded area. Responding deputies located Johnson, who admitted to discharging his firearm during the incident, and placed him under arrest.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill

Title: BREAKING NEWS: Man faces multiple charges after 2-county chase
description: On March 28, 2026, Anthony Eugene Gay fled a traffic stop in Port Charlotte, Florida, initiating a multi-agency pursuit across two counties. During the high-speed chase, Gay slammed his brakes on, causing a pursuing sheriff's patrol vehicle to collide with the rear of his pickup truck and disabling it. Gay continued fleeing onto Interstate 75 at speeds exceeding 100 mph amid heavy rain. Upon entering Lee County, he exited into a densely populated Fort Myers neighborhood, lost control of his vehicle in a front yard, and flipped into a ditch. State troopers apprehended Gay, discovering illegal narcotics and a defaced pistol inside his truck.
Charges: Trafficking in fentanylFleeing to elude with wanton disregardAggravated fleeing to eludePossession of a firearm or ammunition by a convicted felonRemoving a serial number from a firearmPossession of a controlled substance without a prescriptionPossession of marijuana over 20 gramsLeaving the scene of a crash involving property damageReckless drivingResisting an officer without violence

Title: Florida dad arrested after allegedly flashing gun at substitute bus driver
description: On May 21, 2026, Otoniel Carlos O’Valle drove his older model blue Chevy Blazer to a school bus stop situated at North Velvet Terrace and West Bromin Court in Citrus County, Florida. O’Valle, whose elementary school children routinely use the stop, approached a substitute school bus driver and pulled a black handgun from his waistband. Upon learning she was a substitute, he pocketed the firearm and made threatening remarks regarding the route's regular driver. Following a multi-agency investigation that utilized internal bus surveillance recordings, the Ocala Police Department located and apprehended O’Valle on an active warrant.
Charges: Possession of a firearm on school propertyAggravated assault on a public transit employee

Title: Deputies: Wrong-way turn led to chase, crash, arrest
description: On March 2, 2026, 32-year-old John Joseph Rush initiated a high-speed vehicle pursuit after executing an illegal wrong-way turn along a major thoroughfare in Citrus County, Florida. Deputies observed the infraction and attempted a traffic stop, but Rush accelerated away to elude capture. During the erratic chase, he drove against oncoming traffic before losing control of his vehicle and crashing directly into a residential property fence. Following the collision, Rush exited the damaged automobile and attempted to flee the scene on foot. Responding deputies successfully tracked and apprehended him, discovering evidence of drug paraphernalia and impairment.
Charges: Felony fleeing or attempting to elude law enforcementDriving under the influence (DUI)DUI with property damagePossession of drug paraphernaliaResisting an officer without violenceLeaving the scene of a crash with property damage

Title: Floral City man arrested following fire-turned-homicide investigation in Citrus County
description: On April 7, 2026, William Michael Larsen allegedly ignited a fire at his own residential property in Floral City, Florida. Hours later, Larsen returned to the area and set fire to a nearby shed. When a resident tried to extinguish the flames, Larsen stabbed him to death on the scene before fleeing in a pickup truck. Law enforcement launched a massive manhunt and subsequently discovered Larsen's abandoned truck inside the Withlacoochee State Forest. Deputies tracked Larsen through the woods, locating and taking him into custody without further incident to face multiple severe felony charges.
Charges: First-degree premeditated murderArson
Comments: Good story, but lacking police in action during the incident.

Title: JSO officer arrested for battery at a Clay County bar
description: On February 14, 2026, Clay County Sheriff's Office deputies responded to a report of an assault at a local bar during the early morning hours. Investigators established that a victim, who was 65 years of age or older, attempted to intervene and de-escalate a verbal altercation taking place at the business. During the dispute, 49-year-old John H. Tiedeman, a veteran patrol officer with the Jacksonville Sheriff's Office, allegedly physically battered the victim. Deputies located and detained Tiedeman during a subsequent traffic stop. Following an interview with investigators, he was arrested and booked into the Clay County Jail.
Charges: Felony battery on a person 65 years or older

Title: Convicted felon accused of brandishing CO2-powered rifle during road rage incident in Collier County
description: On February 27, 2026, 27-year-old Bryan Gomez was driving a black Ford Ranger pickup truck near the intersection of Airport-Pulling Road and Pine Ridge Road in Collier County, Florida. Gomez became involved in a morning road rage incident with the driver of a blue Tesla. During the dispute, Gomez brandished a CO2-powered rifle and verbally threatened the other motorist. Fearing for their life, the Tesla driver discharged a firearm at Gomez. No injuries were reported from the gunfire. Collier County Sheriff's Office deputies responded to the scene, investigated the altercation, and subsequently placed Gomez under arrest.
Charges: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon

Suspect Name: Trey Jacobs, Bridget Butcher, unnamed 16-year-old male
Title: Three arrested after man reports marijuana, iPhone stolen during drug deal in Lake City
description: The Columbia County Sheriff's Office arrested three individuals following an armed robbery during a drug deal. A victim attempting to sell marijuana to Trey Jacobs on SW Elizabeth Court was targeted. Jacobs held the victim and his girlfriend at gunpoint, while two masked individuals searched them, stealing an iPhone and marijuana. One assailant punched the girlfriend in the face. Jacobs and his girlfriend, Bridget Butcher, who helped him evade law enforcement, were arrested. Investigators later identified and arrested a 16-year-old boy. Deputies recovered the stolen phone and seized multiple firearms and ammunition.
Charges: Armed robbery, accessory after the fact to armed robbery, robbery with a firearm, aggravated battery with a deadly weapon

Title: Trenton teen arrested after pointing gun at, punching woman
description: The Gainesville Police Department arrested Tristin Miller early Saturday morning after a violent confrontation at an apartment complex on Southwest 20th Avenue. Police reported that Miller, a resident of Trenton known by the alias "Crack," went to the location intending to assault the victim’s boyfriend. During the incident, Miller allegedly shouted at the female victim, aimed a desert sand-colored pistol equipped with a transparent extended magazine at her without a lawful reason, and later punched her in the face in the parking lot. Miller denied threatening or touching anyone, and police are seeking a search warrant for his car.
Charges: Aggravated Assault, Simple Battery
Comments: Lacking story and police intervention during the incident.

Suspect Name: Yeri Flores Salgado, Rafael Hurtado Martinez
Title: Two men arrested after machete attack in Arcadia leaves 1 injured
description: The Arcadia Police Department arrested two DeSoto County men following a violent machete attack. Officers responded to a disturbance near the SuperMatt Laundry in Arcadia, where a man was assaulted and injured with a machete. The two suspects, identified as Yeri Flores Salgado, 32, and Rafael Hurtado Martinez, 28, fled the scene after the attack. In coordination with the DeSoto County Sheriff's Office, police located the suspects' vehicle and conducted a successful traffic stop. Both men were taken into custody and booked into the DeSoto County Jail, where they are currently held without bond.
Charges: Aggravated battery with a deadly weapon

Title: WATCH: Wanted Florida man leads deputy on chase around car in Arcadia, deputies say
description: A DeSoto County Sheriff’s deputy initiated a traffic stop on a vehicle displaying a registration tag that had been expired since March 2025. During the investigation, the passenger falsely identified himself as Nick Villegas, a name for which dispatchers found no matching records. When the deputy approached the passenger side of the car, the suspect jumped out and initiated a foot chase around the vehicle before running into a nearby brush area. The deputy successfully tackled and handcuffed the man, identifying him as Michael Villegas, an eight-time convicted felon with multiple outstanding warrants across three separate Florida counties.
Charges: Resisting an officer giving a false name while lawfully detained, possession of marijuana, possession of drug paraphernalia, and multiple active warrants from DeSoto, Charlotte, and Sarasota counties

Title: Woman accused of running into pond after leading Collier County deputies on car chase
description: Collier County Sheriff's deputies arrested Amber Evans following a vehicle pursuit along Rattlesnake Hammock Road. Deputies attempted to pull Evans over, but she refused to comply and led them on a car chase. After coming to a stop, video footage shows Evans jumping out of the driver's seat and running straight into a nearby pond in an aquatic attempt to evade law enforcement. Despite jumping into the water, deputies successfully tracked her down and took her into custody. She was booked into jail on charges of fleeing or eluding law enforcement and resisting arrest.
Charges: Fleeing/eluding law enforcement officers, resisting arrest

Title: Woman flees Hollywood police with child in car, crashes head-on into cruiser, cops say
description: The Hollywood Police Department arrested Julia Pilkington, 35, after she fled from officers attempting a welfare check. Cops found Pilkington conscious but uncooperative inside a Jeep Grand Cherokee with a young child in the back seat following reports she had fainted in a drive-thru. When an officer reached inside to unlock the vehicle, Pilkington sped away, driving westbound in eastbound lanes and through a construction zone. Failing to maintain control, she crashed head-on into a responding marked police cruiser. She was taken into custody and booked on multiple child endangerment and traffic offenses.
Charges: Child neglect without great bodily harm, resisting an officer without violence, and reckless driving

Title: Fugitive on the Run Located and Arrested for Felony Battery
description: The Flagler County Sheriff’s Office Fugitive Unit apprehended Diana Reid following a monthlong investigation into a domestic disturbance. Law enforcement initially responded to a residence after Reid struck a victim with a broom and threw items, including kitchen plates, mustard, and a watermelon. Reid, who was on probation, fled the area before deputies arrived and went into hiding across various parts of the state. Deputies eventually tracked her to a home on Quarter Horse Lane. Units from the Fugitive, Crime Enforcement, and K-9 teams responded to the location and took her into custody without further incident.
Charges: Felony domestic battery with prior conviction, violation of probation

Title: Fleeing driver arrested after leaving man with life-threatening injuries: police
description: The Bradenton Police Department arrested 34-year-old Lindsey Gore following a severe hit-and-run incident. Law enforcement reported that a male victim was walking his bicycle across 14th Street West when Gore's Toyota 4Runner struck him. Following the crash, Gore parked her vehicle nearby, exited to survey the scene, and subsequently fled without rendering aid. The victim was transported to a local hospital with life-threatening injuries. After releasing suspect and vehicle images to the public, officers successfully located and arrested Gore less than twelve hours later, placing her into custody.
Charges: Hit-and-run causing serious bodily injury

Title: VIDEO: Florida man accused of fighting, threatening to kill deputy after 7-Eleven robbery
description: On August 9, 2026, deputies responded to a 7-Eleven on Lee Boulevard in Lehigh Acres, Florida, after a masked man reportedly stole approximately $5 worth of rolling papers. Deputies located Steven Rosario Jr., 21, at another gas station across the street. According to the Lee County Sheriff’s Office, Rosario fought with a deputy during the arrest and knocked the deputy into a trash can. The deputy deployed a taser to help take him into custody. While being handcuffed, Rosario repeatedly threatened to kill the deputy. Authorities arrested him on charges related to theft, resisting an officer, threats, and marijuana possession.
Charges: Theft; resisting an officer; making threats to a law enforcement officer; possession of marijuana

Title: Man accused of exposing himself, stealing wine cooler at Target in Davie, report says
description: On August 10, 2026, Davie police responded to a Target store after reports of a lewd incident. According to the arrest report, Justin Blenman, 29, was seen on surveillance video entering the store and exposing himself in the beauty product aisle while facing an unsuspecting shopper. He then allegedly engaged in sexual activity behind the shopper. Blenman later took a wine cooler, placed it in his shopping basket, and moved to the laundry aisle, where he allegedly concealed the cooler in his pocket. When officers approached him, he ran but was caught. Blenman later admitted exposing himself and taking the wine cooler.
Charges: Exposure of a sex organ; petit theft; resisting an officer

Title: Florida man arrested after following Publix shoppers while armed with knife: police
description: On June 17, 2026, deputies responded to a Publix store in Marathon, Florida, after customers and an employee reported that John Paul Roberts was following them inside the store and toward their vehicles. Authorities said Roberts had a sheathed knife on him. One customer ran from the store, but Roberts allegedly continued following him. Another customer reported that Roberts was kicking and swatting chickens outside the store. Deputies said surveillance video captured him following customers. Roberts was arrested and charged with stalking, disturbing the peace, and obstruction after allegedly failing to identify himself to law enforcement.
Charges: Stalking; disturbing the peace; obstruction for failure to identify himself to law enforcement

Title: Suspect climbs tree to avoid arrest after Freeport property dispute, WCSO says
description: Raymond McGlamry, 46, allegedly arrived at a Freeport property dispute while holding a gun and began yelling at power company employees. Walton County Sheriff’s Office deputies working an off-duty detail reportedly ordered him multiple times to drop the weapon. McGlamry eventually threw the gun in front of his vehicle and climbed a tree in an apparent attempt to avoid arrest. Deputies arrested him shortly afterward. According to the report, the incident involved threats with a firearm toward power company employees and a law enforcement officer. McGlamry faces multiple aggravated assault charges involving a deadly weapon, including one involving a law enforcement officer, as well as resisting arrest without violence.
Charges: Two counts of aggravated assault with a deadly weapon; one count of aggravated assault on a law enforcement officer with a deadly weapon; one count of resisting arrest without violence

Title: Florida woman fights off attacker after being dragged into woods while on jog
description: Jayson Thomas, 22, allegedly attacked a woman who was jogging along Tynes Boulevard in the Two Creeks area of Middleburg. According to the Clay County Sheriff’s Office, Thomas grabbed the woman from behind, dragged her into nearby woods, threw her down, and began forcibly removing her clothes. The victim fought him off and escaped to a nearby home, where residents called 911. Deputies searched the area and learned Thomas had fled into a nearby neighborhood. He allegedly changed clothes and entered a residence belonging to people he did not know. He fled again but was located by deputies and taken into custody within approximately 30 minutes.
Charges: Kidnapping; attempted sexual battery; burglary to an occupied residence; resisting without violence

Title: Martin Found Guilty of Spitting on Officer, Violation of Injunction
description: On January 25, 2026, around 2 a.m., officers responded to a Jacksonville residence after a victim reported that Rasheed Martin was allegedly trying to set a mattress on fire inside the home. Martin was subject to an active injunction for protection against domestic violence that required him to remain at least 500 feet from the victim’s home. Officers found Martin inside the residence and attempted to arrest him. Martin reportedly pulled away and tensed his body, prompting officers to take him to the ground and handcuff him. While handcuffed, Martin spat on an officer, striking the officer on the left side of the face. He was later convicted of multiple charges.
Charges: Battery on a law enforcement officer; violation of an injunction for protection against domestic violence; resisting officer without violence

Title: Deputies: Century man arrested at food mart after attacking elderly man at home
description: On May 29, 2026, deputies responded to a mobile home in Century after reports that Cortez Davison attacked an elderly disabled man. Witnesses said Davison punched the victim, lifted him, and threw him onto the floor. Deputies attempted to arrest Davison, but he resisted and fled through a glass window. Deputies used a Taser and later fired bean-bag rounds as he continued fleeing. Davison eventually entered a Century Foodmart and locked himself in a bathroom. Deputies obtained a key, removed him from the bathroom, and arrested him without using additional force. The elderly victim was reportedly assaulted during the incident.
Charges: Abuse of an elderly or disabled adult; criminal mischief; resisting an officer without violence

Title: Seminole man, 57, arrested after slashing youth football posters at complex
description: On August 9, 2026, Anthony Dell’Aquila, 57, was reportedly captured on surveillance video entering the Seminole Youth Athletic Association Complex and cutting six football posters belonging to youth football players and cheerleaders in half with a sharp object. The following evening, he returned to the complex, where staff members identified him and contacted 911. A person followed Dell’Aquila to his home and provided deputies with his location. When deputies confronted him at his residence, he attempted to retreat inside. Deputies said he resisted when they attempted to arrest him. He was subsequently charged with criminal mischief and resisting an officer without violence.
Charges: Criminal mischief Resisting an officer without violence

Title: Man arrested after Ilhan Omar attacked during town hall in Minneapolis
description: On January 27, 2026, Anthony James Kazmierczak, 55, allegedly confronted Rep. Ilhan Omar during a town hall in Minneapolis. Police said he walked toward Omar and used a syringe to spray an unknown liquid onto her while appearing to demand her resignation. A security guard tackled him, and police arrested him and booked him into the Hennepin County Jail. Omar was not injured and continued speaking at the event. Minneapolis forensic scientists responded to examine the substance. Police said Kazmierczak was arrested on suspicion of third-degree assault, although the report stated he had not yet been formally charged.
Charges: Third-degree assault (suspicion; not formally charged at the time of the report)
Comments: No celebrities/famous people, and this lacks police intervention.

Title: It was very unnerving for me': Man arrested, accused of attacking Florida House candidate at St. Johns County voting site
description: On August 11, 2026, Charles Hunt allegedly confronted Florida House candidate Diana Jordan-Baldwin at an early voting site at 21 World Golf Place in St. Johns County. Jordan-Baldwin said Hunt arrived in a black pickup truck and began yelling obscenities after she attempted to move her car. The confrontation escalated when Hunt allegedly made insulting comments about her late husband. Jordan-Baldwin said her current husband stepped between them, but Hunt went around him and punched her in the face. She said Hunt then struck her husband in the head and attempted to kick her. Witnesses intervened, and Hunt left before deputies located and arrested him.
Charges: Two counts of simple battery
Comments: Lacks police intervention during the incident.

Title: Man arrested for threatening to shoot and kill everyone at Dunnellon bar
description: Christopher Rabenort, 53, was arrested after deputies responded to a disturbance at Swampy’s Bar and Grille in Dunnellon, Florida. According to the Marion County Sheriff’s deputies, Rabenort was intoxicated and began yelling that he was going to shoot and kill everyone inside the bar. Deputies located him in his vehicle in the parking lot and observed signs of impairment. When deputies detained him, he reportedly resisted arrest. Rabenort was taken to the Marion County Jail and booked on charges including disorderly conduct and resisting an officer. He later posted bond on Saturday morning following his arrest.
Charges: Disorderly conduct; resisting an officer

Title: GPD: Man attempts to light Gainesville officers on fire, arrested for attempted murder
description: Henry Chambers, 66, was arrested after Gainesville Police Department officers responded to a report of a person experiencing a mental breakdown near Gainesville Lodge on West University Avenue. Officers said Chambers appeared hostile and that they observed a crack pipe. When officers attempted to detain him, Chambers allegedly threw alcohol on them and resisted. During the struggle, he reportedly threatened to kill law enforcement officers and grabbed a torch lighter. Police said he ignited the lighter near an officer’s groin area, causing the officer to feel heat. Officers eventually gained control of Chambers and took him into custody. One officer suffered burns, while two others sustained minor cuts and scrapes.
Charges: Attempted murder; battery on a law enforcement officer; resisting an officer

Title: Man who bailed out of of car after traffic stop in Doral arrested, police say
description: Kaio Da-Cruz-Oliveira, 23, was arrested after attempting to flee from law enforcement twice in Doral. The incident began Thursday night shortly after 9:30 p.m. near the intersection of Northwest 107th Avenue and 41st Street. Doral police stopped a vehicle because its owner had a suspended driver’s license. After the vehicle was stopped, Da-Cruz-Oliveira and a woman exited and ran from officers. The woman was arrested, but Da-Cruz-Oliveira initially escaped. Police later located him Friday morning hiding inside a storage shed. He was arrested and charged with burglary, trespassing, and resisting law enforcement.
Charges: Burglary; trespassing; resisting law enforcement

Title: Woman Caught with Cocaine in Her 'Lower Region' Blamed 'Intimate Encounter' for How It Got There, Cops Allege
description: On June 27, 2026, Reagan Cox, 30, was arrested in Brevard County, Florida, after allegedly resisting arrest during a traffic stop. After being booked into the Brevard County Jail, authorities said a body scanner detected an abnormality in her lower region. During a subsequent private search, officers alleged Cox attempted to cover her buttocks with her hand. When officers moved her hand, a baggie containing approximately 3.8 grams of cocaine reportedly fell to the floor. Cox allegedly claimed she did not know the cocaine was there and suggested someone placed it inside her during an intimate encounter. She was released that same day.
Charges: Resisting arrest; bringing a controlled substance into a county detention facility

Suspect Name: Benjamin Andrew Frey; Kristi Lynn Ruiz
Title: Florida man and woman busted after allegedly having sex at park in front of family: MCSO
description: On March 28, 2026, Monroe County Sheriff’s Office deputies responded to the City of Marathon Children’s Rotary Park and Dog Park after a family, including a juvenile, reported seeing a man and woman allegedly engaging in sexual activity in plain view. Deputies identified the suspects as 35-year-old Benjamin Andrew Frey and 42-year-old Kristi Lynn Ruiz, both from Marathon. Authorities said the alleged acts were visible to people in the park. Both suspects were arrested and transported to the Monroe County Detention Center. No injuries were reported in connection with the incident.
Charges: Lewd and lascivious exhibition; indecent exposure; resisting arrest

Title: Suspect accused of stabbing Wayne County Sheriff Thomas Ballinger, Sgt. Dan Broome indicted by grand jury
description: Chad Palmer, 33, was accused of stabbing Wayne County Sheriff Thomas Ballinger and Sgt. Dan Broome during a law enforcement response in West Salem, Ohio. Authorities said deputies initially responded to reports of Palmer acting suspiciously and threatening to kill a caller’s family. During a later response, Palmer allegedly stabbed two deputies with a pocket knife before fleeing. A large manhunt followed, and Palmer was found hiding in a shed near a wooded area. Hostage negotiators persuaded him to surrender, and authorities took him into custody without further incident. Both injured deputies were hospitalized and later treated and released. Palmer was subsequently indicted.
Charges: 3 counts of attempted aggravated murder; 3 counts of felonious assault; attempted murder; trespass in a habitation; grand theft of a motor vehicle; obstructing official business; aggravated menacing; 2 counts of criminal damaging or endangering; 4 counts of criminal trespass

Title: Fort Pierce truck stop call leads to homicide arrest, murder charges
description: On January 15, 2026, St. Lucie County Sheriff’s deputies responded to a suspicious-person call behind a Pilot Truck Stop on South Rock Road in Fort Pierce. Deputies found Olson Jean, 41, near a semi-truck that had left the roadway and entered a ditch. Blood was reportedly discovered inside the truck cab near the passenger-side door and on the truck’s exterior. Jean was initially arrested for resisting an officer without violence. Investigators later developed the incident into a homicide investigation concerning Wendy Moncion, 32. On January 17, Jean was additionally arrested and charged with first-degree murder with a firearm and tampering with evidence.
Charges: First-degree murder with a firearm; tampering with evidence; resisting an officer without violence

Title: Melbourne man carrying samurai sword arrested for suspected arson at Savannas Preserve State Park
description: On April 22, 2026, Morgan Grante Lentz, 22, was arrested after investigators said he set grass on fire at Savannas Preserve State Park in Jensen Beach. A witness reportedly saw Lentz pour gasoline onto a motorcycle near Goose Pub and later observed a man matching his description carrying a lit torch and setting grass on fire. Deputies located Lentz at the preserve, where he was reportedly carrying a samurai sword. He surrendered at gunpoint but allegedly resisted after being taken into custody. Investigators found approximately one-and-a-half gallons of gasoline in milk jugs. The fire spread about 40 yards before firefighters extinguished it.
Charges: Intentional or reckless land burning; criminal mischief over $1,000; resisting arrest without violence

Suspect Name: Ja'Quan Jeudi; Jamarrion Moore; Javonte Sheppard
Title: 3 men arrested in Boynton Beach shooting death of Lantana man
description: On March 22, 2026, investigators said three men arranged a drug deal with 20-year-old Hakeem Reynolds and lured him to the 2000 block of Northwest 2nd Street in Boynton Beach for an intended armed robbery. During the robbery, investigators said Ja'Quan Jeudi shot Reynolds twice in the back, killing him. Jamarrion Moore was arrested on March 26 with assistance from the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office TAC Unit. Jeudi and Javonte Sheppard were arrested on March 29 with assistance from the U.S. Marshals. Authorities also determined that Jeudi and Moore were involved in another armed robbery several hours before Reynolds' killing.
Charges: Ja'Quan Jeudi: premeditated first-degree murder; robbery with a firearm Jamarrion Moore: resisting arrest; obstructing justice; probation violation; premeditated first-degree murder; robbery with a firearm Javonte Sheppard: premeditated first-degree murder; robbery with a firearm

Title: Lake Worth Beach man facing charges for using AI video to make false police report in Seminole County
description: On March 24, 2026, Alexis Martínez-Arizala allegedly approached a Seminole County deputy at an Academy Sports store in Lake Mary and showed the deputy a three-second AI-generated video falsely depicting two men entering and stealing the deputy’s patrol vehicle. The deputy confirmed that no one had entered the vehicle and that the video and accompanying report were fabricated. A warrant was signed for Martínez-Arizala on March 27. He was later arrested in San Juan, Puerto Rico, and charged with offenses involving fabricated evidence, false reporting, unlawful communication-device use, and providing false information to law enforcement. Authorities said he was expected to be extradited to Florida.
Charges: Tampering with or fabricating physical evidence; unlawful use of a two-way communication device; false report of a crime to law enforcement; knowingly giving false information to a law enforcement officer concerning the alleged commission of a crime

Title: BODYCAM: Man accused of striking deputy, reaching for crowbar outside Florida Publix
description: On July 28, 2026, Hillsborough County deputies responded to a Publix parking lot in Lutz after receiving a report of a man looking inside vehicles. Deputies approached 22-year-old Gonzalo Cabrera near the store entrance and questioned him. According to the sheriff’s office, Cabrera refused to identify himself and resisted attempts to detain him. A struggle followed as deputies tried to take him into custody. Investigators said Cabrera struck a deputy while attempting to escape and continued resisting after being taken to the ground. Deputies also alleged that he reached toward a concealed crowbar in his waistband before they handcuffed him. No serious injuries were reported.
Charges: Battery on a law enforcement officer; resisting an officer with violence; resisting an officer without violence; possession of burglary tools; loitering or prowling; trespassing; disorderly conduct

Title: Bodycam shows man refusing to drop stick, claiming he owned golf course before arrest
description: On June 10, 2026, staff at Sailfish Sands Golf Course in Stuart, Florida, called authorities after reporting that Augustin Esquivar Saah was swinging a golf club and threatening people. When deputies arrived, Saah reportedly had a stick and continued behaving aggressively. Deputies repeatedly ordered him to drop the stick, but he refused and claimed that he owned the golf course. He also told deputies to leave him alone and challenged them to arrest him. After a final warning and countdown, deputies physically intervened and restrained him. No injuries to deputies or bystanders were reported. Saah was subsequently arrested and charged.
Charges: Disorderly conduct; resisting an officer without violence

Title: Lake Worth Beach Man arrested after interfering with deputies, spitting at paramedic
description: On February 19, 2026, Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office deputies were assisting with an active arrest near 118 North A Street when Dawayne King approached the scene on a skateboard. Deputies said King ignored repeated commands to move away from the patrol vehicle and continued arguing with officers. Deputies attempted to detain him, resulting in a brief struggle before he was handcuffed. While being evaluated by Palm Beach County Fire Rescue personnel, King reportedly spit toward a paramedic, with the spit landing near the paramedic's boots. He was transported for booking on multiple charges following the incident.
Charges: Interfering with a first responder; two counts of resisting without violence; assault on EMS personnel

Title: Towel, tequila and trouble: Jupiter man accused of bizarre early morning break-in
description: On July 23, 2026, Geoffrey Bartimus allegedly entered a neighbor’s home in Jupiter, Florida, during the early morning hours. The resident woke around 6:30 a.m. after her dogs began barking and encountered Bartimus heading toward the back door. Police allege he had previously tried the front door while carrying beer. After entering through an unlocked sliding door, he allegedly drank vodka and tequila, cut a lime, and wore a towel around his head. He apologized when confronted and fled over the back fence. A police K9 tracked him to his nearby residence. Officers later arrested him after he resisted entering their patrol vehicle.
Charges: Unarmed burglary of an occupied dwelling; petit theft from a dwelling; resisting an officer without violence

Title: 3 arrested after dozens of 911 calls lead to struggle with deputies in West Palm Beach
description: Serge Alexis, 39, was arrested after Palm Beach County sheriff’s deputies responded to a West Palm Beach residence following approximately 60 allegedly unnecessary 911 calls over 24 hours. Deputies found Alexis still speaking with 911 dispatchers and arrested him for misuse of 911 services. According to the arrest report, Alexis violently resisted custody by punching, kicking, pushing, and grabbing deputies. He allegedly damaged a deputy’s watch and shoulder-mounted flashlight and kicked one deputy after being handcuffed. Deputies used a hobble device before placing him in a patrol vehicle. Alexis was medically cleared and booked into the Palm Beach County Jail.
Charges: Battery on a law enforcement officer; resisting an officer with violence; resisting an officer without violence; misuse of 911 services; criminal mischief causing $200 to $1,000 in damage

Title: VIDEO: Man accused of threatening PSL business, exposing himself, running from cops
description: On June 6, 2026, Port St. Lucie police responded to a business after Alec Perkey allegedly threatened employees and customers while intoxicated. Police said Perkey had been asked to leave after making a female customer uncomfortable. He allegedly threatened the business and employees, retrieved a baseball bat from his vehicle, exposed himself, and engaged in lewd behavior. When officers arrived, Perkey reportedly fled into a wooded area. Officers established a perimeter and ordered him to surrender. After continued attempts to evade police, officers pursued him on foot and deployed a Taser. He continued resisting and was eventually taken into custody and medically evaluated.
Charges: Two counts of lewd and lascivious exhibition; four counts of assault; disorderly intoxication; resisting an officer without violence

Title: Guest’s bizarre behavior sparks police standoff at five-star Palm House Hotel
description: On June 26, 2026, Palm Beach police responded to the Palm House Hotel after staff requested assistance removing Samuel Liu, a 27-year-old Virginia man, from the property. Police said Liu had displayed unusual behavior and had previously requested a room change because of an odor. After staff decided to evict him, Liu allegedly barricaded himself inside his room, slammed the door, locked the deadbolt, and made incoherent statements. Officers repeatedly ordered him to open the door. When officers attempted to enter, Liu allegedly prevented them from accessing the room. Police eventually forced entry and took him to the ground. Liu resisted while officers handcuffed him.
Charges: Felony criminal mischief causing more than $1,000 in damage; resisting an officer without violence; trespassing

Title: Florida deputies arrest man after undercover cocaine sale
description: Joel Santos Torres, 35, was arrested after Hillsborough County authorities said he traveled from Osceola County to Hillsborough County to sell approximately one kilogram of cocaine to undercover detectives. Investigators arranged a predetermined meeting location where the drug transaction took place. After the alleged sale, deputies arrested Torres. Authorities said the case involved cocaine trafficking and possession with intent to sell. Torres was also accused of using a two-way communication device unlawfully and resisting an officer without violence. The provided report does not describe a shooting, physical confrontation involving firearms, injuries, or a vehicle stop during the investigation or arrest.
Charges: Trafficking cocaine; drug possession with intent to sell; unlawful use of a two-way communication device; resisting an officer without violence

Title: Foot chase onto Palm Beach Gardens High School disrupts sports practices, night school
description: On June 25, 2026, Palm Beach Gardens police encountered 25-year-old Zachary Brian Sisselberger near Holly Drive while responding to a call. Police said Sisselberger ran when officers attempted to stop him, leading to a foot chase. He allegedly jumped a locked fence and entered Palm Beach Gardens High School while football and softball practices and night classes were underway. School officials issued a Code Yellow while officers searched the campus. Police eventually found Sisselberger hiding in the bleachers. He initially did not follow commands but later surrendered and was taken into custody without further incident. Authorities reported no serious injuries.
Charges: Trespassing on school grounds, disrupting a school function, resisting an officer without violence, and misdemeanor battery

Title: Man accused of threatening to torch Swampgrass Willy's, then to kill police officers
description: On March 25, 2026, police responded to Swampgrass Willy’s in Palm Beach Gardens after Vu Van Nguyen allegedly became intoxicated and confrontational. He reportedly threatened to burn the establishment, stole wood from a nearby restaurant, threw rocks, and damaged a vehicle. Police detained Nguyen after he refused to identify himself. He allegedly made threats to kill officers during the encounter and continued making threats while being evaluated at a medical center and later at the police station. The stolen wood was returned, and the restaurant did not pursue theft charges. Nguyen was subsequently accused of multiple offenses and trespassed from the plaza.
Charges: Two counts of corruption by threat against a public servant; disorderly intoxication; disorderly conduct; resisting arrest without violence

Title: Dave & Buster’s employee helps police stop suspected DUI driver in Port St. Lucie
description: On June 29, 2026, police responded to a Dave & Buster’s parking lot in Port St. Lucie after an employee found Anthony Rosales asleep in the driver’s seat of a running vehicle. Officers reported smelling alcohol and seeing an open bottle inside the vehicle. Rosales was reportedly too impaired to perform field sobriety exercises and later provided a breath sample of 0.124. During the investigation, police said Rosales resisted officers, attempted to batter an officer, and repeatedly threatened to kill the arresting officer and the officer’s family. Police also determined that Rosales had a previous DUI conviction earlier in 2026.
Charges: DUI, second offense; resisting an officer with violence; battery on a law enforcement officer; threats against a law enforcement officer; operating a motor vehicle without a valid driver’s license
Comments: Lacking action, and generally it is good to avoid DUI cases.

Title: Officer kicked after alleged $1 tip jar theft at Boca Raton Dunkin'
description: On June 1, 2026, police reported that Tiara Kristin Beasi allegedly took a $1 bill from a tip jar at a Dunkin’ in Boca Raton after ordering coffee. Employees reviewed surveillance footage and contacted police. When officers approached Beasi, police said she became aggressive and attempted to strike an officer by swinging her arm toward the officer’s face. After being handcuffed and arrested, she allegedly continued resisting and kicked an officer in the leg during a search before transport. Police said Beasi later admitted taking the dollar, which officers recovered from her property. She was subsequently transported to jail.
Charges: Petit theft; assault on a law enforcement officer; battery on a law enforcement officer

Title: Man charged after driveway confrontation ends in alleged shooting in Fort Pierce
description: On January 8, 2026, deputies responded to a reported disturbance in a Fort Pierce driveway. Investigators said Donald Barry Green confronted a 48-year-old man who had arrived by bicycle at a woman’s home. Green allegedly ordered the man to stop, get off his bicycle, and lie on the ground. Deputies found Green pointing a firearm at the victim, who reported being shot in the right calf. Investigators said Green fired a warning shot into the ground when the victim did not comply. The victim was treated by St. Lucie County Fire Rescue and transported to a local hospital. Detectives later established probable cause for felony charges.
Charges: False imprisonment; aggravated assault with a deadly weapon; aggravated battery with a deadly weapon

Title: 21-year-old busted after allegedly ramming FHP cruiser during 120 mph chase
description: On January 10, 2026, Florida Highway Patrol troopers say 21-year-old Amari Moore was traveling at 120 mph in a 65 mph zone on northbound I-95 near Hypoluxo Road. Moore allegedly exited the highway and ran multiple red lights while attempting to evade a trooper. Investigators say he then made a U-turn and intentionally rammed his vehicle into the FHP cruiser, disabling and totaling it. The trooper was shaken but not seriously injured. Moore allegedly fled northbound and abandoned his vehicle in Lantana. A witness video and anonymous tip helped investigators identify him. He was subsequently arrested on February 11, 2026.
Charges: Operating a motor vehicle without a license; fleeing with disregard for safety; aggravated battery on an officer

Title: Man charged after 2-county crime spree ends in downtown Orlando
description: On June 4, 2026, Robert Lee Smith was accused of a two-county crime spree involving Seminole and Orange counties. In Sanford, witnesses said Smith exited a vehicle after a minor collision, displayed a gun, threatened another driver, and pursued him. Later, in downtown Orlando, deputies stopped a red Kia near Colonial Drive and Orange Avenue. Smith allegedly got back into the vehicle and fled, striking other vehicles and an Amazon delivery van. He then attempted to flee on foot but was quickly tased and handcuffed by deputies. Smith was booked into the Orange County jail and faced charges for fleeing and eluding, resisting arrest, and driving without a license.
Charges: Fleeing and eluding, resisting arrest, and driving without a license

Title: New Smyrna Beach man arrested for brandishing handgun while intoxicated
description: On April 28, 2026, police responded to a report of a suspicious intoxicated man yelling in the street in the 300 block of Palm Street in New Smyrna Beach, Florida. Officers reported hearing what sounded like a firearm being cycled and saw Brian Birdsong emerge from behind a vehicle holding a silver handgun. He initially refused repeated commands to drop the weapon but eventually placed it on the ground. Police said he continued ignoring commands, concealed his hands, and moved toward the gun, leading officers to restrain and handcuff him. A loaded magazine, ammunition, and alcohol were found in his vehicle.
Charges: Resisting an officer without violence; using a firearm while under the influence of alcohol; disorderly intoxication; improper exhibition of a firearm or dangerous weapon

Title: Family considering legal action following use of K-9 during Brevard County man's arrest
description: On June 2, 2026, Brevard County deputies pulled over a vehicle near Cocoa that James Corona, 27, was riding in. Corona was wanted on a warrant for violating probation from a previous reckless-driving conviction involving alcohol. During the arrest, a K-9 deputy repeatedly ordered Corona to exit the vehicle with his hands raised, warning that the dog would be released. The arrest video appears to show Corona with his feet and arms outside the vehicle before the K-9 was released. Corona said he was cooperating when the dog attacked him. He received hospital treatment for his injuries before being taken to the Brevard County Jail.
Charges: Violation of probation; resisting arrest without violence

Title: Victim runs mile for help after being held at gunpoint for sex in Orlando; 2nd victim comes forward within hours
description: Tony Andesron Jr., 38, is accused of using a firearm to threaten two separate victims at his Orlando residence and attempting to force them into sexual activity. According to Orange County Sheriff's Office documents, the first victim escaped after being pushed onto a bed and threatened with a gun, eventually running about a mile to a business for help. A second victim, a 20-year-old woman, reported being forced onto a bed and threatened with a firearm before escaping. Deputies later attempted to arrest Andesron, who allegedly resisted for about 40 minutes and damaged a deputy's vehicle while trying to drive away during the confrontation.
Charges: Attempted sexual battery with force; kidnapping with intent to commit a felony; aggravated assault with a firearm; criminal mischief; false imprisonment with a weapon; grand theft; resisting an officer

Title: I had to': Man attacks Orlando Chinese restaurant, staff with shovel
description: Richard Jarvis, 43, was arrested after deputies responded to an aggravated battery at Pearl's Chinese restaurant in Orlando, Florida. According to the arrest affidavit, Jarvis attempted to enter through the restaurant's back door while threatening people inside. He later entered through the front door, went into the kitchen, threw food, and damaged restaurant equipment with a shovel. When the restaurant owner attempted to flee, Jarvis allegedly struck him in the back with the shovel and threatened to kill him. Deputies detained Jarvis at the scene. The incident involved an alleged physical attack, property damage, and unlawful entry while Jarvis was carrying a weapon.
Charges: Aggravated battery, criminal mischief, and burglary of a structure with a weapon

Title: Tampa police reclassify fatal hit-and-run as homicide, arrest warrant issued
description: Early Sunday, June 7, 2026, a security guard outside the Vale nightclub on North Armenia Avenue was struck by a vehicle following an altercation inside the club. Police said Jose Zamora Valdes, 32, was asked to leave after a dispute with a woman he knew. While being escorted out, Valdes pushed the woman, causing a brief confrontation. He then went to his vehicle and intentionally drove into the security guard. The guard suffered fatal injuries, while a friend with him sustained minor injuries. Valdes fled the scene, and police later impounded the vehicle. An arrest warrant was issued, and authorities began searching for him.
Charges: Murder; aggravated battery with a deadly weapon
Comments: Lacks police intervention, and case is still ongoing.

Title: St. Pete police force way into home to save kidnapping victim: affidavit
description: On April 26, 2026, Michael Warren, 36, was accused of kidnapping a woman in St. Petersburg. According to the arrest affidavit, witnesses saw Warren push the victim and his girlfriend against a vehicle in an alley behind their home. He allegedly pulled the victim's hair, picked her up, and slammed her to the ground before carrying her inside the home. When St. Petersburg police arrived, officers heard the victim crying inside, but no one answered the door. Officers forced their way inside and found Warren. He refused verbal commands and attempted to retreat into a bathroom before officers used a Taser and took him into custody. The victim suffered bruising.
Charges: Kidnapping; domestic battery; resisting an officer without violence

Title: Woman charged with arson after lighting ex-boyfriend's home on fire: GPD
description: Jessica Batts, 34, was arrested after allegedly setting her ex-boyfriend’s apartment building in Gulfport on fire. Police said Batts arrived at the building on 49th Street South at approximately 4:38 a.m. after receiving a trespass warning for the location. A friend of the victim reportedly saw Batts use a butane torch to ignite the northeast side of the structure. After the friend confronted her, Batts allegedly fled on foot. At approximately 5:15 a.m., a Gulfport police officer found Batts walking north on 49th Street and discovered the butane torch in her possession. When the officer attempted to take her into custody, Batts allegedly resisted and bit the officer on the forearm.
Charges: Arson; battery of a law enforcement officer; resisting arrest without violence; aggravated stalking

Title: VIDEO: Edgewater police stop fleeing burglary suspect after pursuit
description: Jarkvis Peoples, 28, was wanted in connection with a residential burglary when he allegedly fled from Volusia County Sheriff’s Office deputies attempting to arrest him. He later entered Edgewater, where Edgewater Police officers located his vehicle and attempted to stop it using a PIT maneuver. The first maneuver damaged a rear tire, but the vehicle continued. A second PIT maneuver at Old Mission Road and Massey Drive successfully stopped the vehicle. During the pursuit, Peoples lightly struck a civilian vehicle, but no injuries were reported. After his arrest, officers discovered that Peoples’ 11-year-old daughter was inside the vehicle. He subsequently faced an additional child abuse charge.
Charges: Child abuse; fleeing law enforcement; residential burglary

Title: Man charged with attempted murder re-arrested in Oviedo; three teens arrested after ‘drug deal gone bad’
description: An attempted armed robbery in the Live Oak Reserve neighborhood of Oviedo led to a car crash, a gunshot, and an alleged effort to dispose of a firearm. A 17-year-old reportedly approached a vehicle carrying a concealed firearm, leading to a struggle with the 16-year-old driver. The driver accelerated, causing the vehicle to crash into a tree. After the crash, the suspects fled. Police allege the 17-year-old and a 15-year-old later gave the firearm to Darren Salazar to dispose of it. Salazar was subsequently located in an apartment complex and arrested on evidence-tampering and contributing-to-delinquency charges.
Charges: Tampering with evidence in a criminal proceeding; contributing to the delinquency of a minor fleeing
Comments: Lacks police intervention during the incident.

Title: 6 kids caught after New Year’s car chase near Orlando, deputies say
description: On New Year’s Day, a deputy attempted to stop a Toyota Corolla after it ran a red light near Silver Star Road and Hiawassee Drive. The vehicle fled, leading to a lengthy pursuit tracked by a helicopter. Deputies later observed the Corolla stop at a residence and allegedly drop off guns before continuing to flee. The vehicle eventually stopped on Errol Parkway, where seven occupants exited and ran. Authorities arrested 18-year-old Tyrone Henderson. Six other juveniles were detained and released. Henderson was charged with fleeing or eluding a law enforcement officer and possessing a weapon during the commission of a felony.
Charges: Fleeing/eluding a law enforcement officer; possession of a weapon in the commission of a felony

Title: Man accused of making threats at a Gainesville Burger King arrested
description: Timothy Jordan, 34, was arrested after allegedly making threats at a Burger King in Gainesville on Saturday evening. Police responded around 6:10 p.m. to the restaurant at 6123 W. Newberry Road following reports of a suspicious person. Officers learned Jordan was allegedly armed with a black handgun and threatening people inside. An employee said Jordan entered the restaurant, screamed a threatening statement, and grabbed the handgun from his waist. Jordan told officers he was speaking with his sister and did not intend to threaten anyone. Police initially believed he had barricaded himself in a restroom, but searches found no one. He was later located elsewhere in Alachua County.
Charges: Aggravated assault

Title: Mother accused of stomping, beating her 2-year-old daughter to death, police say
description: Jessica Wilson, 29, is accused of beating and stomping her 2-year-old daughter, causing severe injuries that ultimately resulted in the child’s death. Deputies responded Thursday to a medical emergency after the toddler became unresponsive. The child was hospitalized with skull fractures and bruising to the head, chest and back. A witness said Wilson handed her unresponsive daughter to her and CPR was started. Wilson allegedly told the witness she had beaten the child. During a police interview, Wilson reportedly admitted hitting the toddler with a belt, punching her and stomping on her back because the child was not listening. Wilson allegedly acknowledged that she had gone too far.
Charges: Second-degree murder

Title: Man accused of shooting 70-year-old woman at Orlando bus stop pleads not guilty
description: Kevin Millares, 27, is accused of shooting a 70-year-old woman three times in the back at a bus stop in Orlando’s Azalea Park neighborhood. The victim was taking her morning walk near the 1000 block of Egan Drive when she noticed Millares approaching. After she turned away, the suspect allegedly walked behind her and fired. After she fell, he allegedly shot her twice more. The victim was critically injured and underwent surgery. Investigators identified Millares through surveillance footage and evidence found at his nearby residence. He fled the Orlando area and was later arrested by the U.S. Marshals Service in New York.
Charges: First-degree attempted murder with a firearm

Title: Florida Keys man drove drunk with unbuckled child, threatened to sexually assault deputy's family, MCSO says
description: Deputies responded to a welfare-check report involving Jamie Allan Koval, who was reportedly drinking alcohol and smoking marijuana while responsible for a six-year-old child. Deputies located Koval driving a Chevrolet pickup truck on Key Deer Boulevard in Big Pine Key. The child was inside the vehicle without a seatbelt, and deputies reported that Koval appeared intoxicated. Koval allegedly refused to exit the truck and failed field sobriety exercises. Investigators also said he threatened a deputy and threatened to sexually assault the deputy’s family. He was arrested and taken to jail, while the child was placed with family members.
Charges: DUI with a person under 18 in the vehicle; resisting arrest; child neglect; threatening a law enforcement officer; threatening a law enforcement officer’s family; refusal to submit to a breath test

Title: Police arrest a North Miami Beach man in connection to fatal triple shooting at Taste of Miami Karnival in Little Haiti
description: Jamesly Mezime, 22, was arrested in connection with a fatal triple shooting at the Taste of Miami Festival in Little Haiti. Police said the shooting happened after a fight between Mezime and 23-year-old Kitchner Cyrille near the festival’s main stage. Surveillance video allegedly showed Mezime produce a firearm and shoot Cyrille, who was also robbed. Cyrille died, while his cousin was shot multiple times and an unidentified woman was shot in the leg. Detectives conducted surveillance at Mezime’s home and later arrested him near Biscayne Boulevard and 38th Street. Police said Mezime cooperated and confessed at the station.
Charges: Second-degree murder; two counts of attempted murder
Comments: Lacking police in action during the incident.

Title: Lyft driver speaks out after he said he was held at gunpoint, forced to drive 2 men to Miami Beach
description: Ashton Montanez, 22, was arrested after a rideshare driver reported that two men entered his vehicle and forced him to drive to Miami Beach. The driver said one of the men had a gun and that he felt the weapon against his back. Miami Beach police located both men near the 1400 block of Ocean Drive. Jefferson Mesidor was arrested immediately, while Montanez allegedly barricaded himself inside a building, prompting a SWAT response. Montanez was initially charged with kidnapping, but a judge found no probable cause for that charge. The charge was downgraded to resisting officers without violence, and bond was set at $500.
Charges: Resisting officers without violence

Title: A Broward man blames being off his mental health medication after deputies say they found Molotov cocktails, guns, and ammunition in his apartment
description: Justin Messingham, 47, was arrested after deputies responded to a reported shooting near his apartment. Deputies later found him in the road, screaming and acting erratically. According to the arrest report, he ignored commands to get down, was tasered and arrested. Deputies found shell casings outside his apartment, multiple guns and ammunition inside, and several explosive devices, including Molotov cocktails. Investigators said some explosives appeared ready for use. A bullet reportedly entered a neighbor’s apartment. Messingham was charged with multiple counts related to obstructive devices and resisting an officer. He was released on bond with restrictions on weapons and explosives.
Charges: 15 counts of making or attempting to make an obstructive device; resisting an officer without violence

Title: South Florida man punched, choked girlfriend and waterboarded her dog, threatening to kill them, officials say
description: Kevin Anthony Monasterio, 24, was arrested after authorities alleged he attacked his girlfriend and abused her dog during two incidents at their home. Investigators said he punched the dog, threw it against a wall, and later sprayed it in the face with a water hose. He allegedly punched and strangled his girlfriend twice, restricting her breathing and causing bruising to her neck and arms. Before leaving, he allegedly threatened to kill the woman and her dog if she left without telling him. The victim contacted police after going to a family member's home. Monasterio denied the allegations.
Charges: Domestic battery by strangulation Battery Animal cruelty Assault

Title: Florida man armed with sword threatens neighbor during argument, police say
description: Police responded to the 1800 block of Everest Parkway just before 7 p.m. Wednesday after a disturbance involving a weapon was reported. Authorities said a dispute between neighbors escalated when Raul Elosegui Fernandez, 41, grabbed a sword from his truck and threatened a neighbor. The sword reportedly had a tan handle and an approximately 3-foot metal blue blade. Fernandez allegedly raised the sword above his shoulder and approached the victim while making threatening statements. The victim went inside his home and called police. Officers later located Fernandez's white Chevrolet pickup at his home, found the sword inside, seized it as evidence, and arrested him.
Charges: Assault with a Deadly Weapon

Title: Man accused of assaulting woman with umbrella in Overtown
description: On August 6, 2026, Richard Kenneth Hughes Jr. allegedly attacked a woman in Miami’s Overtown neighborhood. According to police, the woman was walking to work when Hughes approached her, followed her, and became verbally aggressive before charging at her. Police said Hughes grabbed an umbrella from her and repeatedly struck her in the face, causing a deep facial laceration requiring medical treatment. A witness reportedly saw Hughes continue striking the woman while she was on the ground. Surveillance footage allegedly captured the attack and showed Hughes later throwing a large rock toward the victim, narrowly missing her. Police arrested Hughes, and the motive remained unclear.
Charges: Aggravated battery with a weapon or firearm causing great bodily harm; aggravated assault with a deadly weapon

Title: Miami police: Video captures man punching woman with disability in Allapattah
description: Charles Anderson is accused of assaulting his girlfriend, a woman with a disability who is unable to walk, in the Allapattah area of Miami. Police said surveillance video showed Anderson approaching the woman while she was seated on her assistive walker and punching her repeatedly in the face with closed fists without apparent provocation. The victim reportedly told police Anderson had asked her for money to buy gas, and she refused. She was found bleeding and was taken to Jackson Memorial Hospital, where she received stitches for a laceration beneath her chin. Anderson allegedly confessed during police questioning and was subsequently arrested and booked.
Charges: Aggravated battery with great bodily harm; aggravated abuse of a disabled adult

Title: Fitness influencer faces charges in Broward dating violence case, records show
description: Westley “Wes” Watson, 42, is accused of attacking a woman during a dating violence incident in Hallandale Beach. Police said Watson physically restrained the woman, shook her, applied pressure to her neck, threw her to the ground, dragged her by her hair, and struck her repeatedly, including slamming her head into a table. The woman suffered facial cuts, scratches, and bruises. Police said Watson prevented her from leaving his home and threatened to kill her and her family. His friend allegedly checked her phone while his security guard prevented her from leaving. Officers arrested Watson near Holiday Drive and Layne Boulevard.
Charges: Robbery by sudden snatching; felony battery; aggravated assault with intent to commit felony; false imprisonment; hindering, delaying, or preventing communication to a law enforcement officer

Title: Bodycam video shows unresponsive 6-year-old with autism receiving CPR in North Miami Beach
description: Daniel Eduardo Romero, 34, was accused of severely abusing his girlfriend’s 6-year-old autistic son at a home in North Miami Beach. Police said the child suffered extensive injuries, including bleeding and swelling in his brain, injuries to his liver and kidney, spleen lacerations, a fractured shoulder, and bruising. The child went into cardiac arrest and had no detectable pulse when officers arrived. An officer performed CPR until firefighters restored his pulse. Romero allegedly gave investigators conflicting explanations, initially claiming the child fell and later saying he fell from a bicycle. Police determined the injuries were inconsistent with an accident and arrested Romero during the investigation.
Charges: Aggravated child abuse causing great bodily harm, child neglect causing great bodily harm, and providing false information to law enforcement.

Title: Pursuit of man who struck cruiser in Hallandale Beach ends in crash in Hollywood, police say
description: On August 8, 2026, a Hallandale Beach police officer was patrolling the 1700 block of East Hallandale Beach Boulevard when he noticed a vehicle parked near a closed business. When the officer approached, Mohammad Chehade entered the driver's seat, backed up, struck the police cruiser, and fled. The officer was not injured, but the cruiser sustained approximately $5,000 in damage. Police pursued the vehicle into Hollywood, where Chehade allegedly attempted to strike the cruiser. The pursuit ended after the vehicle crashed on North Ocean Drive. Chehade fled on foot but was detained several blocks away. He faces several charges.
Charges: Aggravated battery on a law enforcement officer and several other charges

Title: Man accused of striking parking enforcement specialist with vehicle while fleeing citation in Doral
description: Ronald Ebrain Hernandez-Belisario was arrested after police said he struck a parking enforcement specialist with his vehicle while attempting to leave without receiving a parking citation. The specialist found his gray Honda parked in a marked pay zone in downtown Doral and discovered that payment had not been made. When she began issuing a citation, Hernandez-Belisario allegedly drove away and struck her with the vehicle’s passenger-side mirror. The specialist was not seriously injured and declined medical treatment. Police later located Hernandez-Belisario at an address associated with the vehicle. He was identified by the victim, arrested, and transported to the Turner Guilford Knight Correctional Center.
Charges: Aggravated battery on a police officer, firefighter or official

Title: Man accused of beating roommate to death in Pompano Beach
description: Shenard Jennings, 33, was arrested after authorities accused him of beating his roommate, Karim Shouman, 39, to death during an argument inside their home in Pompano Beach. According to the Broward Sheriff’s Office, the argument stemmed from an ongoing dispute and became physical when Jennings punched Shouman. Jennings allegedly continued beating him, ultimately causing his death. Deputies and Pompano Beach Fire Rescue personnel responded to the residence shortly before 1 a.m. after receiving a report of a deceased person. Shouman was found dead in the kitchen and was pronounced dead at the scene. Jennings was transported to the Broward Sheriff’s Office Main Jail.
Charges: First-degree murder

Title: Miami-Dade felon charged with murder, armed robbery in fatal bus stop beating, deputies say
description: James Thompson, 57, was arrested and charged after investigators said he beat a man to death at a bus stop in southwest Miami-Dade. The confrontation reportedly began at a market over a monetary debt connected to a previous narcotics transaction. Thompson allegedly followed the victim to a bus stop at Southwest 173rd Street and the South Dade TransitWay, where he repeatedly punched the victim, causing him to fall from a bench. Investigators said Thompson continued kicking the victim in the face and upper body after he became unconscious. Thompson then allegedly searched the victim’s backpack, took an unidentified item, and fled. The victim later died at a hospital.
Charges: Second-degree murder; armed robbery with a weapon; illegal possession of a firearm as a post-convicted felon; possession of cannabis with intent to sell while illegally armed; resisting an officer without violence; violation of house arrest

Title: Naked man resists arrest in North Bay Village, urinates in squad car, police say
description: Bryton Facen, 30, of Miami Gardens, was arrested after police said he was found naked in the roadway near the 1400 block of Kennedy Causeway in North Bay Village. According to police, a physical struggle occurred when officers attempted to detain him. Authorities said Facen punched, kicked, bit and spit at officers, forcing them to use a Taser and multiple sets of handcuffs to restrain him. Police said he later urinated inside the back of a squad car. Medics eventually subdued him with ketamine, and he was taken to Jackson Memorial Hospital for treatment and evaluation. Facen was subsequently booked on multiple felony and misdemeanor charges.
Charges: Four counts of aggravated battery on a law enforcement officer; four counts of resisting an officer with violence; one count of indecent exposure

Title: Man, 53, arrested for punching 70-year-old at North Miami Beach supermarket
description: On April 27, 2026, police responded to Presidente Supermarket at 450 NE 125th St. in North Miami, Florida, after a 70-year-old man reported being punched in the face. The victim told officers that the suspect, identified as 53-year-old Sosthene Gregoire Pervil, punched him once, causing substantial pain, facial swelling, and redness. The victim declined medical treatment at the scene. Officers used the victim’s description to locate and detain Pervil near 590 NE 125th St. at approximately 8:08 a.m. The victim later positively identified Pervil during a show-up identification procedure. Pervil was subsequently arrested and charged with battery involving a person aged 65 or older.
Charges: Battery on a person 65 years of age or older

Title: Miami man charged after allegedly attacking security guard with perfume bottle
description: On June 7, 2026, shortly after 4 a.m., Jairo Antonio Osoriobenavides allegedly became involved in a confrontation with a uniformed security guard near Northwest Seventh Street and Northwest 17th Court in Miami, Florida. Police said the security guard was attempting to escort Osoriobenavides from the property because he was allegedly intoxicated and acting aggressively. After an argument outside the establishment, Osoriobenavides allegedly threw a perfume bottle that struck the guard in the head and caused a laceration. The two then fought, with the security guard using his baton. Miami Fire Rescue treated both men, and both were transported to Jackson Memorial Hospital with injuries. Osoriobenavides was arrested.
Charges: Aggravated battery and battery on a security officer

Title: Miami Beach man accused of brutal attack on woman who gave him shelter
description: Yunior Suarez, 47, is accused of entering a Miami Beach woman’s apartment without permission after she had allowed him to stay temporarily for about a month. Police said he locked the door, punched the woman in the head, slammed her head against the floor multiple times, and strangled her until she nearly lost consciousness. He allegedly struck her dog during the confrontation. The woman grabbed a kitchen knife in self-defense, causing Suarez to leave. Police said he took her cellphone, driver’s license, and vehicle keys. He was later found sleeping inside the apartment and arrested without incident.
Charges: Burglary with assault or battery; robbery; battery by strangulation; tampering with a victim

Title: ‘I planned this completely’: Miami Beach man confesses to random stabbing, having child porn on his phone, police say
description: On January 11, 2026, Sebastian Tomas Datorre Rodriguez, 21, allegedly stabbed a sleeping man in the neck at Soundscape Park near Lincoln Road and Washington Avenue in Miami Beach. Police said the victim suffered heavy bleeding and required emergency surgery, later being listed in stable condition. Datorre Rodriguez reportedly fled the scene and went directly to the Miami Beach Police Department, where he confessed and surrendered. Police said he had been thinking about stabbing someone for several days and randomly selected the sleeping victim.
